items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is Rs 15,000 crore
items.quote: The CAPEX guidance for FY 26-27 is Rs. 15,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected between Rs 7,500-10,000 crore; 9M spent Rs 5,428 crore
items.quote: For the full year, initial guidance was Rs.7,500 and then final guidance is Rs.10,000 crores. It will be anything between these two.

items.statement: January price increases: long products +Rs 2,000-2,500/t, flat products +Rs 3,300-3,500/t; further increases expected in February-March
items.quote: the real increase of around, say, Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 2,500 was reflected in January in long and around, say, Rs. 3,300 to Rs. 3,500 in flat in January so far as sales price is concerned.

items.statement: Domestic steel consumption grew ~7% YoY in 9M FY26; market stability from December; Q4 uptick expected post monsoon/festive season
items.quote: Indian steel industry continues to enjoy robust demand for steel, with consumption during nine-monthly FY25-26 grown by almost 7% over CPLY.

items.statement: Semis share down to 10%; targeting near-zero via DSP 1Mt TMT mill (18-24 months) and conversion contracts
items.quote: right now, semis percentage is 10%. If you compare the previous years it is less because our focus is on having finished products more than the semis.

items.statement: Debt reduced ~Rs 5,000 crore in 9M FY26; additional ~Rs 2,000 crore in Jan; momentum continuing Feb-Mar
items.quote: Reduction in debt is close to Rs 5,000 crores in nine-monthly, and in January alone, we have again reduced by around Rs 2,000 crores, and momentum continues for February as well as March.

items.statement: Interest cost down Rs 500 crore in 9M; expect another Rs 500 crore reduction in Q4; FY26 total ~Rs 1,000 crore lower
items.quote: in 9 monthly, our interest cost has come down by Rs. 500 crores. We expect that another 500 crores reduction in inventory will additionally happen in Quarter 4. So, overall, for the year, the interest cost reduction could be around Rs. 1000 crores.

items.statement: RE power sourcing yielding structural power cost savings; further improvements underway
items.quote: we are trying to reduce our power cost by sourcing it from RE power sources. So, we have taken certain actions in different plant units and that has given rise to some savings.

items.statement: Target FY27 volume growth similar to FY26, contingent on industry growth, using headroom at Surat, Udaipur, Jhajjar, Cuttack
items.quote: So even next year also, we see a similar kind of growth, of course, contingent to the industry growth. But we see a similar kind of growth even next year.

items.statement: Pet coke/coal cost seen rising to Rs 1.58-1.60/kcal in Q4 as existing stock exhausted and new buying at higher rates
items.quote: Pet coke, coal prices, it's going up. I think definitely it will go up because whatever we have in stock, that we have almost exhausted. Now, new buying is also happening. It will go up by at least 1.58 to 1.60, that is what we see in our case.

items.statement: Blended cement share 62% in Q3; target 67% to improve clinker factor (CC ratio 1.44 currently, was 1.54 in FY21-23)
items.quote: I think our effort is to take this blended cement from 62% to about 67%. To that extent, our CC ratio will improve.

items.statement: Conveyor belt project stalled due to land issue; Rs 170 cr already incurred plus balance included in Rs 3,300 cr presentation figure
items.quote: No. That is not going on. That is stalled because of this issue of the land, as we have been talking of. So, that includes the expenditure already incurred plus the balance to be incurred, which is about Rs. 170 odd crores.

items.statement: Railway siding Phase 2 completion by March 2028
items.quote: As far as the railway siding is concerned, the second phase that is expected to be completed by March '28.

items.statement: Q4 and Q1 EBITDA margin expected around 20%, could reach 20-25% if tariff reduces to 25%
items.quote: So we think in Q4 and Q1, the margin should remain around 20% or so depending on the product mix, but we expect to that range. But if any good things from Supreme Court of U.S.A. or any trade deal happens even to 25%, which we are hearing. This is all like all in public this thing. So there might be a removal of 25% ag

items.statement: Expect 15-20% CAGR sales growth next year even if 50% tariff persists
items.quote: Still we will maintain a growth of 15%, 20% because we'll not hold inventory in our warehouses. We will do whatever sales naturally happening, which is at the rate of 15% to 20% CAGR, right?

items.statement: TPU manufacturing line to be commissioned by October 2026, 25% capacity earmarked for new generation products
items.quote: The upcoming TPU manufacturing line, which will be commissioned by October 2026, will further strengthen our backward integration and innovation capabilities with 25% of the capacity earmarked for new generation products.

items.statement: Order book remains robust; orders for current and next quarter are sufficient to run factories at optimal levels
items.quote: However, factory is continuously producing as per the requirement because we only produce against the orders, and we have enough orders for this quarter and going forward.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 18.9%, down 118 bps YoY; contained tariff impact via cost optimization and product mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 18.9%, down only 118 bps year-on-year, maintaining a healthy level despite tariff headwinds, which have primarily been driven by cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Sun Control segment strong demand; architectural film expanding rapidly in Middle East and India; PPF demand strong in India, Middle East, Europe, South America offsetting US challenges
items.quote: Our Sun Control segment witnessed a strong demand. Our architectural film business continued to expand rapidly in all geographies, including Middle East and Indian markets, backed by focused marketing initiatives and premium product launches.

items.statement: US inventory at 100 days vs normal 60-75 days; holding bonded warehouse stock to benefit from potential tariff reduction
items.quote: Right now, if you add everything, so this goes almost, I can say, around 100 days. I mean it's like you can just see 60 days versus 100 days. So there is like 30, 40 days more inventory is lying with us in the warehouse.

items.statement: Middle East sales doubled in 1 year, grew 3-4x in 3 years; China partnerships underway; US order flow strong despite tariffs
items.quote: So first and foremost, we have grown really well in Middle East region. So I mean, the sales, which was last year versus this year has doubled. If we see last 3 years, 2 years, where tariff was not seen, but if we compare versus 2 years to now, the growth has been almost 3x to 4x, right, in terms of sales from that par

items.statement: Board approved INR 775 crore for 50 KTPA precipitated silica expansion at Cuddalore and INR 135 crore for 350 KTPA dense ash plant at Mithapur
items.quote: Board in its meeting on November 21st, 2025, also approved 50 kilo tonne per annum precipitated silica expansion at Cuddalore at an investment of INR 775 crore, and a 350-kilo tonne dense ash plant in Mithapur with an investment of INR 135 crores

items.statement: Kenya 50 KTPA electric calciner soda ash plant operationalized, to be fully stabilized by March 2026; adds capacity with lower carbon footprint
items.quote: 50 KT electric calciner soda ash plant in Kenya was operationalized and will be fully stabilized by March 2026

items.statement: US export volumes to Southeast Asia to decline temporarily as company stops taking orders below contribution margin
items.quote: you would see in the coming quarter, us not delivering the volume, sort of going down on the volume because it doesn't make any sense to be selling in those markets at negative contribution

items.statement: US domestic soda ash realizations down ~$5/tonne vs prior year; export prices to Southeast Asia sharply lower, causing margin pressure
items.quote: Overall, I would say that there's been about $5 drop in realizations on the domestic market

items.statement: India soda ash prices declined marginally by INR 500-600/tonne in Q3; other product prices held steady
items.quote: prices have sort of gone down by about INR 500 or INR 600 a tonne in soda ash. But otherwise, other products have held more or less up

items.statement: Publication segment revenue expected to grow ~15% in FY27 due to curriculum changes in Maharashtra (4 grades) and Gujarat (2 grades)
items.quote: Overall, with these grades changing, we feel around 15 -odd percentage revenue growth we will achieve in publication segment for FY '27.

items.statement: Domestic stationery business targeting 15-20% growth in FY27 driven by non-paper stationery expansion and new marketing team
items.quote: And in stationery, of course, it is just now not the paper stationery. We have already come out with a lot many other non -paper stationery products also. And we have set up a fresh new marketing team also for the same. And with that, overall, both put toge ther, we will see at least 15% to 20% growth in stationery bus

items.statement: UAE manufacturing facility capex of ~INR30 crores for machinery only (no land/building), operational by Q2 FY27
items.quote: Yes. So around INR30-odd crores, we are investing ther e. Balance, as I said, partly we are shifting -- additionally, partly we are shifting from India.

items.statement: UAE facility expected to generate INR50-55 crores revenue with 8% EBITDA in FY28, scaling to INR90+ crores with 12% EBITDA in FY29
items.quote: So basis of our calculation today, it would be between INR50 crores to INR55 crores of revenue with around 8% of EBITDA next year. And in the subsequent year, that may figure -- FY '29, I'm saying, it will reach around INR90 -odd crores with the same facilities and EBITDA would be around 12%.

items.statement: Export EBITDA margin compressed from 15-16% to 4-5% due to 10% discount offered to US customers to absorb tariff impact
items.quote: At present, we are realizin g INR90 instead of INR100. And this INR90 automatically, whatever our EBITDA was around 15%, 16% in exports, that has come down to 5%.

items.statement: Domestic stationery EBITDA margin dropped to 5-6% from higher levels due to initial expenses for non-paper stationery expansion and manpower costs
items.quote: Domestic also, it has come down to 5%, 6%. And reason I did mention that since we are growing our non -paper stationery business, and we have -- there are initial expenses that we are incurring, including the manpower cost for which -- against which we have not yet received the good revenue.

items.statement: US customers accepted 10% discount to continue sourcing from Navneet; pricing on FOB basis; UAE pricing to match India pricing as customers set international prices
items.quote: Immediately, in the week when the new tariffs were announced, proactively, my team sat in front of them physically and did say that we want to continue thi s business with you for very, very long. And for that, we did offer them 10% discount.

items.statement: US consumption down 10-15% due to inflation; developing new categories (files/folders, metal, canvas) to offset volume decline; total addressable market for files/folders >$500M
items.quote: And because of that, the consumption at the U.S. also has gone down by 10% to 15%. Now that is likely to impact our volumes for sure. And therefore, as a strategy, we are developing newer and newer categor ies so that value-wise, at least we match up to what we have been doing so far.

items.statement: Targeting 20% of domestic stationery revenue from non-paper stationery by FY28; UAE facility initially for paper/plastic blended products only
items.quote: FY '28, if you're asking, then we would like to 20% of our revenue -- domestic revenue to come from non-paper stationery.

items.statement: Navneet AI platform built on 110,000+ digital resources for teachers; no additional opex (INR1 lakh license costs only); using existing Bangalore team; awareness creation for 1 year
items.quote: Now Navneet AI platform that we have created, first of all, we have not invested in manpower also, whatever manpower that we had through them only, we have created this platform. So there is no additional opex that we are spending to create this platform.

items.statement: K12 Techno Services stake revalued at INR6,550 crores valuation; Navneet stake to dilute to ~13% after March funding round; open to partial sale
items.quote: So the value was -- one of the shareholders sold off their part equity at INR6,550 crore s valuation. And therefore -- and there was some primary infusion at the same rate also in the company. And therefore, we had to revaluate it.

items.statement: Domestic stationery capex halted except Southern Gujarat facility capitalized in current quarter; all new expansion directed to UAE
items.quote: So whatever capex that we were to put in India as far as the machineries are concerned, that we have halted for a while, except the plan that we had already put up last year. And in the current quarter, we have capitalized the same, which is in Southern Gujarat.

items.statement: Expect domestic stationery margins to recover by FY27 as non-paper stationery scales; UAE facility margins lower than India due to higher labor costs
items.quote: Yes, yes, yes. We can expect that.

items.statement: FY26 AUM target INR33,000-34,000 cr; FY27 target INR43,000-44,000 cr; FY28 target revised to INR55,000 cr from INR50,000 cr
items.quote: So I think we have said that this year, we will continue to deliver a growth AUM to be in the range of about INR33,000 crores to INR34,000 crores, and we are on that track. Already, we achieved INR30,400 crores this 9 months period. And we will continue to grow. Next year, we have revised our guidance to deliver anythi

items.statement: Target ROE 16%+ and ROA 4-4.25% by FY28
items.quote: Our aim will be to deliver ROE in the range of about 16% plus and ROA anything between 4% to 4.25%.

items.statement: Spread guidance of 7.2% maintained for Q4 FY26
items.quote: And I think we've given a guidance of 7.2%, which we hope to deliver that.

items.statement: Micro LAP AUM target INR3,000 cr in 2.5-3 years from INR650 cr currently; yield 23-24%, ticket size INR5 lakh, GNPA 0.9%
items.quote: Micro LAP average ticket size is about INR5 lakhs. It is collateralized by security. The yield is in the range of about 23% to 24%. And currently, AUM is about INR650 crores from the 151 branches. In next 3 years' time from now, we intend to have a loan book of about INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Gold Loan demand shifting from informal to organized sector; expect decent growth despite price volatility
items.quote: So even though some price correction, which we've already seen happening, but on ground, there is still the larger market of the gold loan is still exist in the informal segment with the small money lender and the small jewellery shop who also do the lending activity. That market is continuing to shift to the organized

items.statement: Co-lending to stay at 22-23% of AUM; highly ROE accretive; no intention to grow further
items.quote: I think Co-lending will remain largely in the current range of between 22% to 23%. We do not intend to grow it further from this level. And we are able to maintain, this is a very good level to have it. It's very, very highly ROE accretive.

items.statement: Board approved INR230 crore for 41.1 MW AC captive solar (33 MW open access at Jodhpur, 8.1 MW at Chittorgarh) operational by Q2 FY27
items.quote: The Board has approved an additional capex of INR230 crores for captive solar power capacity of about 41.1megawatt AC, out of which 33 megawatts will be under open access at Jodhpur District and additional 8.1 megawatt of solar power capacity within our Chittorgarh unit premises.

items.statement: Fabric expansion (35 mn meters woven, yarn dyeing, printing, coating) to commission from Jun-Jul, production from Oct-Nov, full ramp by FY27 end; spinning by Nov-Dec 2025
items.quote: First of all, the fabric capacity should be there in the early second half of this year -- of next financial year. We should be -- we are going to commission the things from June, July onwards and expect the production to start somewhere from October, November onwards.

items.statement: Hybrid power purchase agreement of 18 MW started partial supply, full operational in Q1 FY27; 4.6 MW solar plant expected operational in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The hybrid power purchase agreement of 18 megawatts announced in quarter 2 has started partial power supply, and it is expected to get fully operational in the Q1 of the FY '27.

items.statement: Current yarn spread ~INR99/kg (realization INR250, cotton cost INR151); good-time spread INR115-120
items.quote: Yarn realization for this quarter was around INR250 a kg and cotton cost was around INR151. So the spread is around INR99.

items.statement: Expect demand stabilization and improvement with US tariff reduction and EU/UK FTA implementation; knitting utilization at 40% to recover
items.quote: going forward, we expect the demand to normalize. And in the meantime, we have already seen some capacity shutting up. So it will be a stable kind of demand , were the margins should also stabilize and improve going forward.

items.statement: Fabric expansion to shift woven:bottom-weight ratio from 65:35 to 50:50; adding yarn dyeing, printing, finishing, coating
items.quote: Now the ratio we are expecting is 50-50. At the moment, it is about 65-35. Now it will become 50-50 after this expansion.

items.statement: Domestic cotton at premium to international prices after 11% import duty restored; export competitiveness needs duty-free import policy
items.quote: At this point of time, the Indian cotton prices, if we consider without duty, then definitely, they are expensive than the international prices. But with duty -- with whatever the duty impact, which is there, 6%, 7%, then I think Indian cotton is still cheaper than the international prices.

items.statement: Existing weaving capacity at 90%+ utilization; new fabric capacity expected 80% utilization in FY28; EU/UK FTA opening new export customers
items.quote: We're already running our existing capacity on 90% plus site. And the new capacity which is going to come in, we are expecting that next -- we should be able to ramp it up to at least 80% capacity in the next financial year, '27-'28.

items.statement: US knitted fabric exposure was 3-4% direct + 7-10% indirect; tariff reduction to restore this business
items.quote: Basically, we had an exposure of our knitted fabric business in U.S. and which contributed to about 3% to 4% of our export sales. That was the direct sales. And apart from this, there was indirect sales of about 7% to 10% to our customers in India who used to export to U.S.

items.statement: No impact from Bangladesh cheaper yarn imports issue; business continues as is
items.quote: At this point of time till now, there is no action has been taken on that side, and the business continues as it is.

items.statement: No definitive garmenting plans; first priority is fabric capacity ramp-up; open to inorganic growth if right fit found
items.quote: As of now, we do not have any definitive plans to get into the garmenting.

items.statement: Expect presales to be around FY25 levels in FY26 and aim to exceed it; target 15% YoY presales growth over time but FY27 visibility depends on approval timelines
items.quote: Yes, with the expectation that the launches would come in, we should be around last year's number in terms of overall sales and ideally breaking past that as well.

items.statement: Real estate EBITDA margin expected to improve to ~20% from Q1/Q2 FY27 as newer higher-margin projects get recognized
items.quote: I think from Q1, maybe Q2, we should start seeing higher margins in the real estate segment, maybe closer to 20%.

items.statement: Commercial lease revenue to reach upwards of INR2,000 crores upon stabilization of pipeline assets by 2030-31
items.quote: So, as we see, once these assets sort of are leased out and stabilized, the overall lease revenue will be upwards of INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Commercial capex: INR600 crores in FY26 and INR800 crores in FY27; Hospitality capex: INR800 crores budgeted for FY27
items.quote: So, in FY '26 for the commercial division, about INR600 crores is what we expect to spend. And the year after in FY '27, about INR800 crores.

items.statement: Residential launch pipeline of ~12 million sq ft over next 4 quarters; Q4 FY26 target 4.3 million sq ft with GDV ~INR5,400 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have a strong pipeline with approximately 12 million square feet of launches planned over the next 4 quarters.

items.statement: Commercial office: 2.5 million sq ft to get OC in FY26; 4.2 million sq ft launches planned over next 4 quarters
items.quote: We have also mentioned that in FY '26, we've launched about 1.2 million square feet. And upcoming launches will also account about 4.21 million square feet.

items.statement: Leasing segment EBITDA margin sustainable at 70% (lower blended due to facility management at 15-20% margin)
items.quote: EBITDA margin 70%. So, it's slightly lower because we include facility management as well, which has just a margin of maybe15% to 20%.

items.statement: Target 5-7% YoY like-to-like price hikes in Bengaluru and Chennai; average realization up 16% YoY to INR13,142/sq ft in Q3
items.quote: In our own portfolio, about 5% to 7% is what we would like to take year-over-year and what we've been doing in the past.

items.statement: Approval delays of 3-4 months in Bengaluru due to regulatory changes (BBMP to GBA transition) caused launch slippage from FY26 to FY27
items.quote: We've faced delays of about 3 to 4 months in some of these projects. And it's primarily due to some of the changes that took place in Bengaluru.

items.statement: Brigade Morgan Heights sales halted due to Chennai regulatory issue affecting 1 lakh+ properties; court hearing expected this month with positive verdict anticipated
items.quote: We are expecting the hearing to happen in a couple of weeks' time. So, we are quite hopeful that it should be done by this month itself, and we should be able to restart by the end of the month.

items.statement: Net debt INR1,887 crores (Brigade share INR1,273 crores) as of Dec'25; avg cost of debt reduced 115 bps to 7.61%; 92% debt backed by commercial rental income
items.quote: Consequently, the company's net debt outstanding as of 31st December ' 25 was INR1,887 crores, out of which Brigade share of the same is INR1,273 crores.

items.statement: Land bank addition: INR2,100 crores spent in 9M FY26 for 14 msf developable area, GDV INR16,000 crores (54% Bengaluru, 30% Hyderabad)
items.quote: In the last 9 months, we have incurred about INR2,100 crores towards our land bank with a developable area of 14 million square feet and GDV of INR16,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects motorcycle industry to grow 12-15% in immediate term with 3-4pp difference between bottom and top half
items.quote: we could be looking at something like 12% to 15% growth over the next few months

items.statement: Targets 200,000+ monthly export run-rate in Q4 FY26 and sustained growth tempo
items.quote: we expect hopefully that we will turn in a 200,000 unit plus performance

items.statement: Anticipates 50-60bps material cost inflation in Q4; priced for half, watching balance with currency tailwind
items.quote: At the start of the quarter, we had anticipated an impact of anywhere between 50 to 60 basis points for which we have taken certain pricing actions across the portfolio to offset about half this impact so far

items.statement: EV portfolio now 25% of domestic revenue; both e-2W and e-3W crossed INR1,000cr quarterly revenue each
items.quote: At an aggregate level, our EV portfolio comprising both electric 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers now contributes to a staggering 25% of domestic revenues

items.statement: Overall EV business delivers double-digit EBITDA margin while improving unit economics
items.quote: More importantly, the EV business now delivers double-digit EBITDA margin while improving unit economics as the portfolio continues to scale

items.statement: Last capital infusion of INR300cr into BACL in October; no further investment needed
items.quote: The last infusion we did into BACL was in October of about INR300 crores. And that we think is absolutely the last of it that is needed

items.statement: Exports crossed 600,000 units/quarter after 15 quarters; top 30 markets grew 15% vs industry 10%
items.quote: The BU crossed the 200,000 average per month sales level in October '25 after nearly 40 months and maintained this level through the remainder of the quarter, surpassing the 600,000 units mark after 15 quarters

items.statement: Deferred all pricing actions in Q3 despite commodity inflation; absorbed 50bps margin hit to protect volume
items.quote: given the beat on volumes that we saw through the festive season, we chose to defer all pricing actions to the start of this current quarter, essentially January and therefore, taking none to cover the inflation last quarter

items.statement: KTM AG turnaround plan underway: liquidity secured, top management in place by Apr 1, cost reduction workstreams active
items.quote: With actions in these 3 areas, the turnaround of KTM AG is truly on its way

items.statement: Domestic 3W ICE segment turned from -4% to +4-5% growth post-GST; electric 3W growing 50%+
items.quote: The Electric segment continues to drive the 3-wheeler industry by growing at about 50% plus

items.statement: Joint KTM-Triumph showrooms to expand from 50 to 100+ by March 2026
items.quote: We currently have about 50 KT showrooms operational and plan to expand these to over 100 by March

items.statement: Riki e-rickshaw seeding in 40 towns; scale-up from Apr-May after playbook validation; no FY27 target yet
items.quote: we would start to scale up, let's say, from April-May onwards, start to get into more cities and more dealerships

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected to fall 8-10% below FY25; FY27 revenue growth targeted at 15% over FY26
items.value: -8% to -10% YoY for FY26; +15% YoY for FY27
items.quote: FY'26 probably based on current order book and the way the projects are moving, new projects having started a bit late, we believe that we may probably not be able to achieve last year's revenue and we'll be probably short by approximately 8% to 10%. But going ahead for FY'26-'27, we definitely believe that 15% growth

items.statement: FY26 order intake target INR3,000-3,500 cr in last 2 months; FY27 order intake vision INR11,000-12,000 cr across all sectors
items.quote: For FY '26, we are typically looking at order book intake in the next 2 months to the tune of around INR3,000-INR3,500 crores. And based on budget promises which have been made, definitely we will look overall order book intake for the next year to the tune of around INR11,000 to INR12,000 crores we generally keep as a

items.statement: Q3 FY26 capex INR15 cr; Q4 FY26 expected INR25 cr; full-year FY26 capex INR75-80 cr
items.quote: So, for Q3, the capex was approximately INR15 crores. We expect another INR25 crores in Q4 to take it around INR75 crores to INR80 crores for the year.

items.statement: HAM equity investment balance INR320 cr (INR220 cr for Bowaichandi, INR100 cr for Tumkur-Shivamogga III/IV); phased investment INR180 cr by Jun'26, INR72 cr FY27, INR72 cr FY28
items.value: 320 cr total; 180 cr by Jun'26; 72 cr FY27; 72 cr FY28
items.quote: Approximately INR320 crores is balance, of which largely INR220 crores is for the new HAM project Bowaichandi and balance is for the TS III and TS IV that is Tumkur-Shivamogga III and IV, which will be invested in the period of INR180 crores by March '26 , March '26-'27 INR72 crores and March'27-'28 INR72 crores.

items.statement: Chennai ORR monetization discussions ongoing; Jaora-Nayagaon retained with strong revenues, open to dialogue if good interest arises
items.quote: Chennai ORR, we continue to pursue seller. On the Jaora-Nayagaon we are still holding it in our books as an investment. The revenues are strong and if any good interest comes, we would be telling and doing a dialogue.

items.statement: Targeting quarterly revenue above ₹800 Crs in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, up from current ₹700+ Crs run-rate
items.quote: Now is about in between Q4 and Q1. How do we go above ₹800 Crs. revenue? That's what all of us as leadership team are working.

items.statement: On track to achieve ₹200 Crs Purple Fabric revenue for full year FY26
items.quote: Mihir, we are on track for what we are forecasting for the 200 Crs. number. I think we're reasonably confident of coming close to that number for the year.

items.statement: Targeting 20%+ EBITDA margin for full year FY26 despite incremental investments
items.quote: Pavan, that's what Vasudha just now also confirmed that we're driving towards 20% plus margin for the full year.

items.statement: LTM EBITDA margin at 23.8%, confident of similar full-year margin
items.quote: if you look at our LTM EBITDA, it has fetched us about 23.8%. So, going by that yes, we are very highly hopeful that we'll also end up in a similar number as we close this financial year.

items.statement: Incremental investment of ₹10-15 Crs in Q3 FY26 for Purple Fabric, distribution, and delivery capacity
items.quote: last quarter we said we made an incremental investment of ₹15 Crs. and similarly this quarter also we have made similar investments between ₹10 to ₹15 Crs.

items.statement: North America revenue approaching ₹1,000 Crs LTM with multiple growth levers firing
items.quote: I think I want to maybe just quantitatively share one more forward thing I think across North America I'm not far from start touching ₹1,000 Crs. revenue.

items.statement: No material headwinds or tailwinds; balanced portfolio across geographies and products provides downside protection
items.quote: There are always headwinds of you hear the noise of politics and different things we got to deal with that. That's what we design business for. So, there's nothing right now material of headwinds or material tailwinds.

items.statement: Signed one large global system integrator and 14 value discovery partners for Purple Fabric ecosystem
items.quote: In this last quarter, we have signed one large global system integrator for our AI proposition is taking out to the market as well as 14 value discovery partners to evangelise and help us take this to more clients across the board.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with global mainframe infrastructure leader for mainframe-to-cloud migration using eMACH.ai
items.quote: On momentum we are in advance discussion with a global mainframe infrastructure leader to jointly transition monolithic banks to eMACH.ai based architectures from the mainframe architecture.

items.statement: CentralOne Forge acquisition already profitable at single-digit margins, better than initial margin-neutral expectation
items.quote: We are already making profit on CentralOne, the single digit profit that we are making. In fact, initially we said it's going to be margin neutral, but we are making some profits out of it.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped to 54% in Q3 due to capacity building for future deals; expected to return to 57% trend
items.quote: If you if you look at our trend maybe again in the last 12 months and then even in the previous last 12 months it was hovering around 57%.

items.statement: Board approved appointment of D. Shivakumar as independent director for five-year term subject to shareholder approval

items.statement: Alu-Zinc coating technology upgrade commissioned in Q3 FY26, increasing capacity by 36% to 180,000 tons per annum

items.statement: Signed 15,000+ new seats in Q3 FY26 and ~57,000 since Dec 2024; 80+ GCCs contributing 21% of space revenue
items.quote: On the demand side, we signed contracts for 15,000-plus new seats in Q3 FY26 and roughly 57,000 new seats since December 2024, reflecting a well-diversified revenue base.

items.statement: 12 GCC deals closed in 9M FY26, 11 more to go live Jan-Jun 2026; India adding 20-30 first-time GCCs per quarter
items.quote: During nine months FY26, we closed 12 deals with GCCs and 11 more already logged in to go live between January to June 2026.

items.statement: Transform revenue expected to settle at ~20% of total revenue (currently 17%)
items.quote: So, roughly about 20% of the revenue is expected from the construction fit-out business. Currently, the split is about 83-17, but roughly this will settle in somewhere around 80-20 kind of a number.

items.statement: Transform segment impacted by GRAP-IV pollution norms and lower managed aggregation seat additions; fixed cost nature causes margin dip when revenue falls
items.quote: Q3 FY26 was impacted, as we said earlier, due to the GRAP restrictions in North and had three large client projects that obviously led to a revenue dip.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue expected to be better than Q3; similar YoY growth trajectory targeted for FY27
items.quote: I can say that our fourth quarter is going to be better than our third quarter and we are looking at similar kind of growth that we had this year, next year as well.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting from 70% aerospace/defence, 30% non-aerospace to 50-50 split in FY27
items.quote: Moving forward, we are going to be approximately 50% aerospace and defence and 50% non-aerospace and defence. So that's how our revenue split is going to be moving forward, 50-50, approximately in that range.

items.statement: Sustainable profit margin target of 17-22% in short to medium term as programs move to production and scale increases
items.quote: But in this industry, we are looking at anywhere between 17% to 22% moving forward.

items.statement: Confirmed POs on hand over INR750 crores executable over 2 years; strategic agreements over INR2,500 crores over 3-5 years
items.value: 750 crores confirmed POs; 2500 crores strategic agreements
items.quote: today our confirmed POs on hand would be over INR750 crores and our strategic agreements would be over INR2,500 crores

items.statement: Leasing additional 210,000 sq ft facility in Bangalore from April 1, 2026 to meet demand
items.quote: we are planning to take a building on lease from the first of April of the year 2026 -2027 of around 210,000 square feet to fuel our growth and our expansion plans

items.statement: Planning QIP of up to INR300 crores for capacity creation, infrastructure, plant tooling, machinery, training
items.quote: We are looking at raising up to a maximum of INR300 crores and it is primarily to fuel our future growth, for expansion in our facilities for infrastructure, plant tooling, machinery, training and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Semiconductor and space programs are high-volume, low-mix vs aerospace/defence low-volume, high-mix; semiconductor revenue >INR10 crores in first quarter post-qualification
items.quote: Our entry into the semiconductor equipment manufacturing segment is scaling rapidly, generating over INR10 crores in revenue in the very first quarter after qualifications

items.statement: COGS increase due to product mix shift; space and semiconductor have higher material cost than defence but compensated by volume
items.quote: If you look at it from the space side and from the semiconductor side, the material cost is much higher than the defence side. So that's why we're seeing a skew in our COGS. But like I said earlier, our profit margin will always be consistent in the range of 17 to 22.

items.statement: 99% export revenue currently; focusing on domestic Indian defence market for growth
items.quote: When it comes from a revenue perspective, 99% of our revenue is all export. So that's our company is an export-oriented unit

items.statement: Delivered EBITDA and PAT profitability in Q3 FY26 as committed for H2 FY26
items.quote: I am delighted to report that we have delivered both EBITDA and PAT profitability in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Financial services gross profit Rs 37 cr, up 405% YoY and 45% QoQ; lending margins stable in 3-4% range
items.quote: gross profit for financial services at INR 372 million or Rs. 37 crores, which is up 405% year-on-year and 45% quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Payments GMV hit all-time high of Rs 481 bn, up 63% YoY and 11% QoQ; UPI transactions grew 220% YoY to 3.2x
items.quote: GMV - which is basically the total value of payments processed - rose to an all-time high in this quarter for Rs. 481 billion

items.statement: FLDG share 80% of disbursals, distribution 20%; personal loan disbursals ~Rs 900 cr, ZIP EMI up 126% YoY
items.quote: the FLDG or DLG led business is 80% of the current quarter's disbursal and 20% is the distribution led risk-free business

items.statement: Merchant acquiring burn ~Rs 13-15 cr per quarter; expected to breakeven in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: merchant business that I just described, which we are trying to build, merchant offline devices and online merchant, I think put together would be around Rs. 13-Rs.15 crores of burn every quarter

items.statement: Risk-first approach in lending; lending expenses down 57% YoY; credit quality and collection efficiency improved
items.quote: Lending related expenses came down 57% year-on-year and this is our approach that we obviously want to continue growing digital lending, but we will be taking risk first approach

items.statement: UPI and Pocket UPI not yet monetized; revenue from wallet MDR, convenience fees, bill payments; Zaakpay share 30-50% of MobiKwik gateway volume
items.quote: for the UPI transactions, we are still not making money. So, we do expect that for UPI transactions, also, we will start getting the benefit over the next few quarters

items.statement: No specific quarterly profitability improvement guidance; focus on revenue growth with stable margins; merchant lending to scale in FY27
items.quote: I do not think we should expect significant more improvement in margins per se. It will be more about growth and growth of revenue and maintaining and growing the margins slowly

items.statement: Bond product experiment with expected realization 0.5-1.5%; Rentpay category shut down per RBI directive
items.quote: we do see the revenue realization will be between 0.5% to 1.5%

items.statement: Expects to exit FY26 with EBITDA better than negative 9% YTD.
items.quote: So I do believe that by the exit of FY '26, we will be better than negative 9% because the recent quarters, we've been performing better.

items.statement: Plans to open 700 stores by end of FY26.
items.quote: We closed Q3 with 600 stores open pan India and we are very much in line for opening 700 stores by the end of this fiscal.

items.statement: EL platform scheduled for launch later this year.
items.quote: EL is scheduled for launch later this year, and the launch of EL, that is leading into your second question.

items.statement: Announced INR3,000 price hike in Q4.
items.quote: In fact, even in the start of this quarter, Q4, we have announced a INR3,000 price hike.

items.statement: Commodity inflation poses a few percentage points of risk for the rest of the year.
items.quote: I think it will be a few percentage points of risk this coming – for the rest of the year, something hopefully we will be able to work with given our increasing scale.

items.statement: Expects 10-20% long-term cost reduction potential in cost structures.
items.quote: I feel there is like a 10%-20% long-term potential still easy in the cost structures.

items.statement: EV two-wheeler industry growth expected to improve as sub-1 lakh segment stabilizes.
items.quote: I do believe that from an industry's perspective, now there are good products priced fairly there, which means that segment's growth will also now be incremental.

items.statement: EL platform to enable entry into INR1-1.25 lakh price segment.
items.quote: But there are price segments, particularly in the INR 1 to INR1.25 lakh, where including the price of our ProPack today, we practically don't have a product.

items.statement: Non-vehicle revenue expected to compound with fleet size, material upside in 3-4 years.
items.quote: But if you take a three -four year view, I think there's a lot of juice in the non -vehicle side for the company.

items.statement: International expansion to be a mid-to-long term growth driver, not in next 12 months.
items.quote: So think of that as a more mid to long term growth lever.

items.statement: ProPack attach rate at 91% in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Very strong performance in Q3 with 91% attached rate for the software products.

items.statement: BOM reduced by 8% from FY25 to 9M FY26.
items.quote: a BOM has reduced by roughly about 8%, roughly about INR10,000 from an average … weighted average BOM of INR1.2 lakh to roughly about INR1.1 lakh, INR1.11 lakh by now.

items.statement: Cell cost below 20% of total BOM.
items.quote: But at a cell level, the total cost of cells as a function of the total bill of material is below 20% now.

items.statement: Charging network reached 5,000 points as of Dec 31.
items.quote: Ather runs the largest fast charging network for electric two wheelers in the country, with our total network size reaching 5,000 charging points as of 31st December.

items.statement: Targeting steady double-digit revenue growth (~12%) and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins of 11-12%
items.quote: We want to be a steady double-digit growth and EBITDA 11%-12% steady, sorry, the pre Ind AS margins.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at INR 320-330 crores, up from typical INR 150-225 crores, driven by aggressive store expansion and renovations
items.quote: This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores.

items.statement: Store pipeline of ~300 identified locations; expect ~150 net store additions in FY26 and another significant expansion year in FY27 with ~120 stores already in pipeline
items.quote: We've added about 50 plus stores in this quarter. Our sense is that we should add another 90 plus net stores in the next quarter. So that would make the overall addition to about INR150 stores this year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 18.4%; Lifestyle Brands EBITDA margin at 20.6%, highest in 4 years excluding one-offs
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 180 bps from 16.6% in Q3 FY25 to 18.4% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Emerging Businesses profitability improved 790 bps YoY; Van Heusen Innerwear losses halved, on track for break-even; Reebok strong profitability improvement
items.quote: Profitability improved by 790 bps YOY, reflecting positive operating leverage, and continued improvement in Van Heusen Innerwear business.

items.statement: GST rate changes (below INR 2,500: 5%, above: 18%) result in small net negative blended impact; Innerwear GST benefits passed to consumers
items.quote: Overall, it's a small net negative, but not a significant one.

items.statement: October-November strong; December moderated due to wedding calendar shift (last wedding 5 Dec); encouraging second half of January; momentum expected to continue through Q4
items.quote: October, November were strong demand months. December, the wedding calendar was such that the last of weddings was on, I think, 5th December.

items.statement: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle) expected to become 1/4 of ABLBL business in 4-5 years; Reebok network doubled to 200+ stores, targeting 230+ by FY26 exit
items.quote: This portfolio is expected to be one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4-5 years.

items.statement: No fresh borrowing; INR 500 cr NCD issuance approved only to refinance repaid debentures; net debt reduced to INR 800 cr from INR 1,000 cr in Sept, targeting further INR 75-100 cr reduction
items.quote: The INR500 crores debentures which we repaid recently in the month of January, we intend to raise it and to refinance the existing, the debentures repaid. There is no fresh borrowing.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands 6th consecutive quarter of positive LTL (5% in Q3); retail LTL 10% YTD; small towns LTL 13-14%; wholesale/e-commerce corrections largely done
items.quote: This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of sustained like-to-like growth.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin guided at 22%-23% for next several years
items.quote: we are confident of keeping the operating EBITDA in the range of 22% to 23%.

items.statement: R&D spend guided at 10%-11% of revenue for next several years
items.quote: And the R&D spends, again, to be around 10% to 11% of revenue for the next several years.

items.statement: Pithampur facility validations on track for mid-CY2026, commercialization expected Q1 CY27
items.quote: At Pithampur, we are on track to operationalizing, kind of doing all the validations by mid of 2026 calendar year, we should be able to complete that and we expect commercialization in quarter one of CY '27.

items.statement: Gross margin pressured by higher-than-planned outsourcing due to strong demand; tactical measures being evaluated to improve gross margin in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: This has put pressure on the GM but the root problem is, it is a good problem to have because we are having more than anticipated demand and we had to actually do more outsourcing than what we had actually envisaged at the start.

items.statement: Confident of returning to 67%-68% gross margin range as Pithampur ramps up and outsourcing reliance reduces
items.quote: we are confident of going back to our earlier gross margin range of 67%-68%.

items.statement: Demand stronger than anticipated; sales ramp-up above expectations across specialty and non-specialty products
items.quote: for the demand which we had anticipated, actually our demand has even been more than what we have envisaged.

items.statement: Specialty share of gross profit increased to 31%-32% in Q2/Q3 FY26 from 26.9% in FY25; pipeline shifting toward specialty, drug-device, and branded products
items.quote: the specialty share of gross profit has remained in Q2 and Q3 at 31% to 32%. This is higher than 26.9%, which was there in the full year of FY '25.

items.statement: Regulatory, competition, and supply chain uncertainties factored into conservative business planning; R&D productivity improvement from 3.3x to 5.7x provides comfort
items.quote: we factor in conservatism from all the external variability factors, regulatory being one, but it could be competition, it could be change in the FDA guidelines.

items.statement: Board composition updated: Dr. Pradnya Saravade appointed Independent Director; General Atlantic nominee Anand Agarwal stepped down
items.quote: we have appointed Dr. Pradnya Saravade as an Independent Director. And one nominee, General Atlantic, Director, Mr. Anand Agarwal, has stepped down.

items.statement: FY27 target: minimum 1 GW each for solar panel, inverter, and battery.
items.quote: We will do minimum 1 gigawatt each solar panel, inverter, and battery.

items.statement: Ratlam new lines to contribute revenue from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Yes. Q1 FY27, yes, new Ratlam lines will contribute definitely for revenue contribution.

items.statement: Ratlam capacity utilization: at least 50% next year, 100% in second next year.
items.period: next year and second next year
items.quote: I think what I can say, definitely, at least 50% we would utilize in next year and 100% in second next year.

items.statement: Ratlam capex Rs. 272 crores excluding land; machinery Rs. 159 crores split across module, inverter, battery.
items.quote: So, Anuj, the overall size excluding land, it is around Rs. 272 crores. Specifically if we ask, out of these Rs. 272 crores, Rs. 159 is for machine.

items.statement: Dadri solar cell plant completed at Rs. 300 crores vs Rs. 400 crores budget.
items.quote: we had targeted total budget of solar cell line was around Rs. 400 crores, while we completed this line in around Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by scaling benefits and backward integration; 0.9% sequential gross margin improvement.
items.quote: So, when we talk on the sequential basis of quarter two versus the quarter three, so we have around 0.9% as a percentage of revenue our margin increase due to our scaling benefits.

items.statement: Raw material price changes (increase or decrease) passed on to customers.
items.quote: Increase or decrease, all will be passed to the customers, sir. Any increase or decrease in price will be passed to customer.

items.statement: Price hikes passed gradually, e.g., Rs. 0.25 per week over two months.
items.quote: So what we start, we start with Rs. 0.25 per week increase. So that in two months we can pass total price hike to customers.

items.statement: Rooftop solar market expected to grow at 40-43% CAGR, supported by government.
items.quote: Actually, there is a historical CAGR of 45% and the upcoming industry expectation is also 40% to 43% CAGR.

items.statement: Solar panel contributes 45-47% of total revenue.
items.quote: So in terms of value, out of our total revenue, generally it amounts to 45% to 47% out of Rs. 100.

items.statement: DCR implementation by June 2026 may shift by a few months; company sees it as positive.
items.quote: We expect that this timeline will be shifted by a few months. And even if it does not shift, it's good for Indian industry maybe because capacity is in the pipeline and the pipeline will mature faster.

items.statement: Current debt level around Rs. 470+ crores including term loan, working capital, vendor finance.
items.quote: Yes, it's around Rs. 470-plus crores.

items.statement: Solar cell plant utilization at 40% now, expected to reach 80% by end of quarter.
items.quote: Yes, yes. We are now about around 40% at this time. And at the end of this quarter, we are expecting up to 80% basically.

items.statement: 9M FY26 solar panel sales 460 MW vs 255 MW last year; inverter/charger/UPS 900 MW vs 508 MW.
items.quote: For the nine months, we sold around 460 megawatts of solar panels. And for the similar period in last year, we sold 255 megawatts of solar panels.

items.statement: Core business top-line growth expected at high single digit to early double digit for FY27
items.value: high single digit to early double digit
items.quote: I can see the market will give us opportunities to grow at a very high single digit to early double digit for sure.

items.statement: Planned equity infusion of INR 1,400 cr for lithium-ion and ~INR 500 cr for lead-acid core business in FY27
items.quote: INR1,400 crores equity we have planned for lithium. And we'll have about another INR500 crores roughly for lead acid core business.

items.statement: Data center pipeline very strong with quarterly revenue of INR 75-100 cr currently
items.quote: Data center revenue at this moment, as I said, in a quarter, it will be about, let's say, INR75 crores to INR 100 crores, only data centers. But the pipeline is very strong.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 11.7% YoY in Q3; sequential gross margin expansion of 175 bps and EBITDA margin expansion of 220 bps
items.quote: Despite this, the company was able to maintain the year-on-year EBITDA margin at 11.7% for Q3, buoyed by strong volume growth, improved product mix, better realization and benefits accruing from the various cost excellence projects.

items.statement: 2% price hike taken in January 2026; further staged increases planned as commodity and currency pressures persist
items.quote: But in January, we have taken one round of price correction, we had to take because otherwise, this currency and these commodities were killing us. So we took it in January, and we hope to take stage by stage as the situation develops, we'll see what next to do.

items.statement: Auto OEM up 25% YoY, 2W/4W replacement double-digit growth; momentum expected to continue into Q4
items.quote: Auto OEM and Domestic 2W/4W replacement demand was robust - both these verticals hit their highest ever quarterly revenue in Q3. Auto OEM was up +25% YoY, while 2W/4W replacement market continued its double-digit growth. This momentum is expected to spill over into Q4 as well.

items.quote: INR98 crores. Pravin Saraf: Yes. So it is INR100 crores right now. Yes, in the first 9 months.

items.statement: Roha to reach full capacity utilization in four years; original plan stands.

items.quote: Yes, around Rs. 130 crores are standing in CWIP.

items.quote: We do expect that our peak demand will be in the 270-280 gigawatt range, and we can expect a very large increase in the demand of power in the coming months.

items.quote: We will be spending close to 15,000 crores-20,000 crores -25,000 crores of CAPEX every year.

items.quote: Yes, in my view, this quarter, unless there are again any external events or hopefully no climate change impacts but other than that, it should be a pretty strong quarter from a volume perspective. You are right, in Decoratives.

items.quote: Decorative alone, I think it was fantastic news to see the volume coming back. We grew at 8%.
