items.statement: BP parent forming JV with investor, BP retaining 35% stake; transaction subject to approvals.
items.quote: BP has signaled that they will form a joint venture with an investor, where BP will remain a 35% shareholder and the investor will take 65%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 expected to be better than last year by 5-10% in industry volume; revenue will depend on product mix
items.quote: Looking forward, the next quarter, which is this quarter, which is typically again a very high quarter in the financial cycle for the several past years, the momentum is going forward. So we are expecting it to be better than last year, at least by 5% to 10%.

items.statement: FY27 outlook uncertain; Q1 FY27 expected flat, Q2-Q4 FY27 dependent on OEM outlook
items.quote: Based on the order book, we think that this quarter is going to be stable and the next quarter will be probably a little bit flat, just like any other earlier years. But the Q2, Q3, Q4 of FY '27, we're still waiting for the OEMs outlook so that we can align our capacities and supply chain to that requirement.

items.statement: Capacity expansion starting Q1 FY27, completing by Q3 FY27 to meet ~500k M&HCV segment demand
items.quote: We are investing it and starting from Q1 FY '27 and by Q3 FY '27, we would have added all the capacities that is required for the outlook of somewhere around 500,000 M&HCV segment.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.9% in Q3 FY26, up 52 bps QoQ and 93 bps YoY; sustainable with favorable product mix
items.quote: Our expense structure has been fairly stable over the past, and we have been kind of closed all our expenses at about INR507 crores, leaving us with EBITDA of INR725 million or INR72.5 crores, which is at about 12.9%.

items.statement: Product mix shift toward tandem axles and MS185; bus segment impact due to low-floor mandate from Oct 2026
items.quote: The shift in the heavy-duty or high tonnage vehicles, multi-axles into tractor trailer, tandem into tractor trailer, that's going to stay. Now where will it reach as a peak? That's anybody's guess today.

items.statement: Strong demand post-GST rate cuts from all OEMs; OEM inventory at healthy levels; tipper segment improving with new launches
items.quote: After September, post the GST rate cuts, there was real traction in terms of demand, and this came from almost every OEM that we are partnered with and which translated into a very strong quarter in terms of the volume.

items.statement: COGS improvement trend to continue via supply chain optimization, lighter designs, and high-tech products over 2-3 years
items.quote: We have been always focusing on that, optimize our supply chain, developing innovative designs, lighter designs so that we can always continue to improve in that. So that trend will continue.

items.statement: Bus axle potential 3-5% penetration of customer portfolio if current product meets low-floor mandate
items.quote: The expected penetration with our largest OEM may be 3% to 5% because that is the only gap we see. It's 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization ~80%; no capacity constraints for current demand
items.quote: Our current capacity utilization is around 80%. Again, our capacity is going to go up and down depending upon the product mixes and then different configuration and it keeps changing almost on a weekly basis.

items.statement: Exceptional item of INR12 crore for new wage code effective Nov 21, 2025 impacted PBT margin by ~2%
items.quote: In this quarter, there is an exceptional item of about INR12 crores, which was an impact on the wage code that we had to take. The new wage code came into effect on 21st November.

items.statement: Target 580-630 restaurants by 2027
items.quote: We remain on track to reach our 580 to 630 restaurants by 2027.

items.statement: Plan to open 20-25 restaurants in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Yes, we do foresee that we will open around 20 to 25 restaurants this quarter, which should be able to compensate for whatever was happening in October, November, December.

items.statement: Positive same-store sales growth in January with mid-single-digit guest count growth
items.quote: This positive momentum extended into January, where we reported positive same-store sales growth supported by healthy mid-single-digit guest count growth.

items.statement: Restaurant operating margin improved 150 bps YoY; EBITDA margin improved 70 bps YoY in Q3
items.quote: Restaurant operating margin improved 150 basis points year-on-year, while operating EBITDA margin improved 70 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: INR 99 everyday value meal launched in West, not margin dilutive due to mix and supply chain efficiencies
items.quote: We realized that it is not a worse or we will not take a margin hit when we do this INR99, and we have rolled it out in a certain manner so that it's accretive as far as the business is concerned.

items.statement: Third-party aggregator volatility impacted off-premise; one platform had deep decline, working on partnership recovery
items.quote: We had a deep run on one of the platforms. One of the other platforms was okay. We are working with them to get the relationship right and to be able to create a plan by jointly working on sustainability.

items.statement: Royalty rate base reset; current quarter reflects new agreement, no further drop expected
items.quote: This year would be the right base to look at it. I think we continue to work with our partner in terms of our royalty structure. And we've come to an agreement in terms of what the base should be.

items.statement: McCafé at 100% penetration; launched subscription plan; focus on making coffee a daily habit
items.quote: We are at 100% penetration in terms of McCafe. And now the main job that we're doing is to ensure that people try our coffee and our beverages.

items.statement: Gratuity-related one-time exceptional expense in Q3; no other known normalizations
items.quote: Gratuity was the only exception which we had on the P&L.

items.statement: Protein Slice launched globally first; Chicken Surprise brought front and center in value proposition
items.quote: The Protein Slice is definitely a great introduction. It's the first of its kind globally, and it's allowed us to continue to expand our offerings to be in the consideration set of customers.

items.statement: Phase 1 ABS expansion capex approximately INR350 crores, to be completed in H2 FY27, funded by internal accruals and possibly a capex loan.
items.quote: overall capex for Phase 1 is approximately INR350 crores and which will spill over this year and next year, most of them. And we will finance them with internal accruals as well as maybe a capex loan, which we have yet not taken and have funded it through internal accruals only.

items.statement: Thailand breakeven capacity utilization 65-80% depending on product mix.
items.quote: the breakeven or the EBITDA positive scenario will depend a lot on the product mix that we are able to achieve in Thailand. So that number can range anywhere from 65% to 80%.

items.statement: Thailand inventory losses due to price falls; more than 75% of Q3 loss from inventory valuation.
items.quote: more than 75% of the losses are on account of inventory valuations, which have taken a dip in the last quarter, when we have sold the product.

items.statement: Raw material and finished goods prices fell 20-25% from peak, causing inventory losses.
items.quote: when the inventories were at the peak to when they came down, I think the gap could have been as high as about 20% - 25%.

items.statement: ABS demand in India 350,000-370,000 tons; domestic production less than 50%, net importer.
items.quote: ABS demand is higher than about 350,000 tons or even probably closer to 360,000, 370,000 tons this year as against which the domestic production, if I exclude Supreme so far, is still less than 50%.

items.statement: Power cost reduction from hybrid power agreement to accrue from Feb/Mar 2026.
items.quote: That agreement will come into effect only in this month or the next month, so February or March. So we will see those benefits only accruing now in the coming few quarters.

items.statement: Thailand business almost entirely on formula pricing, very little spot.
items.quote: Thailand, again, a lot of the business, I would say, practically all of the business is on formula. Very little business is on spot.

items.statement: Phase 1 ABS expansion first year utilization could be 60-70% in FY28.
items.quote: I believe that would be possible. I think once the capacity comes on stream, we should be able to achieve fairly high capacity utilization numbers.

items.statement: Backward integration at Kakinada expected to lift annualized fertilizer EBITDA from INR5,500 to INR6,500 per ton on full capacity
items.quote: As against the current annual average EBITDA of INR5,500, we should be able to increase it to INR6,500 on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Backward integration project for sulfuric and phosphoric acid at Kakinada commissioning in Q4 FY26; granulation expansion in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Our backward integration project at Kakinada for sulfuric acid and phosphoric acid are progressing very well as per the timelines and will be commissioning during this quarter. The granulation train expansion is also on track, and it will be commissioned in the third quarter of the financial year 26-27.

items.statement: Mancozeb capacity expanded 20% in Q3 FY26; further 30% expansion planned
items.quote: We have expanded 20% and now we are planning to expand another 30%.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection EBITDA margin at 20% in Q3 FY26 (9M: 18%); confident of sustaining or improving
items.quote: In the case of CPC business of Coromandel, our margins are doing good and it is in the range of 20% - we are confident of sustaining or improving it. For the quarter, we achieved 20% and cumulative 9 months is 18%.

items.statement: NACL EBITDA margin improved to 9-10% post-acquisition; further upside pending Dahej utilization and mix improvement
items.quote: They've already moved up EBITDA percentage to 9% - 10%, which they should be able to sustain and grow further. They are also looking to improve the product mix and bring in new products.

items.statement: Fertilizer prices raised 3-4% in Q3 to offset input cost inflation and rupee depreciation
items.quote: Also, we took some price correction during this quarter by 3% to 4% to offset the impact of increase in input prices and currency depreciation.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid price at $1,290/t in Q3; industry resisting further increases
items.quote: Currently, the $1,290 remains - industry is not keen to increase this price any further. Industry will be pushing for cost reduction in phos acid price.

items.statement: Unique fertilizer grades share improved to 36% in Q3 (from 33%); SSP unique grades at 47%
items.quote: Our share of unique grades has improved from 33% to 36% during the quarter. Also, we took some price correction during this quarter by 3% to 4% to offset the impact of increase in input prices and currency depreciation. In SSP, Coromandel continues to do well and is market leader led by differentiated products such as

items.statement: Sulphur price spike to $550/t seen as temporary; expected to retract in Q1 FY27 as supply-demand balances
items.quote: We do feel that the sulphur price increase is not sustainable. Sulphur always used to be a disposal issue. I think it is a phenomenon of short supply and excess demand, which should get moderated as we move into first quarter of next year.

items.statement: NACL completed rights issue; proceeds used to retire high-cost debt and fund capex for cost reduction
items.quote: During the quarter, NACL has successfully completed rights issue, the proceeds of which will be used to retire all high-cost debt and also used for creating capex, which can help in reducing costs and improving operational efficiencies for NACL plants.

items.statement: Targets cumulative cost savings of Rs. 200 crores over next two years from company-wide cost optimization drive.
items.quote: we are targeting cumulative cost savings of Rs. 200 crores over the next two years, which we expect to translate into visible improvement in profitability over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expects Aquapharm volume growth of at least 20% next year.
items.quote: On the Aquapharm side, I think we should be comfortably looking atleast a 20% volume growth next year.

items.statement: Domestic tyre market demand expected to grow 5-6% next year.
items.quote: we expect to leverage the growth, which we are expecting from the domestic tyre market which will be around 5-6% growth next year as well.

items.statement: International market volume growth expected high single digit in FY27, not double digit.
items.quote: We are targeting double digits, but I think in FY '27, it will be a very high single digit.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton for carbon black expected to reach Rs. 24,000-25,000 in next five years.
items.quote: we should be reaching some where near Rs. 24,000-25,000/ ton in next five years.

items.statement: No change to FY29 PAT guidance of Rs. 2,500 crores.
items.quote: No, we don't want to make any changes in our long -term guidance now because all the levers which we built into our numbers for FY29, those work in progress, very much work in progress.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected around Rs. 550 crores; FY27 sub Rs. 400 crores.
items.quote: FY26, it will add up to about Rs. 550 odd crores. So, far, we have spent about Rs. 400 crores. There's one specialty line which is under way currently, but that's the number for the current year. Next year, it should be somewhere around Rs. 300-400 odd crores.

items.statement: Nanovace commercial plant capex estimated at $25-30 million, to be commercialized by end FY28.
items.quote: On the full-scale, our current estimate gives us a number of about between $25-30 million.

items.statement: Received formal allocation from P&G for GLDA in MENA and Europe; to initiate supplies to Henkel from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: For GLDA, we received a formal allocation from P&G (MENA and Europe for the first time) and we are also on track to initiate supplies to Henkel from Q1 FY '27 in Europe.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA per ton for carbon black was Rs. 13,800; 9-month FY26 was Rs. 15,300/ton.
items.quote: Well, third quarter, we had Rs. 13,800 EBITDA per ton. And this number is for 9-months Rs. 15,300/ ton.

items.statement: US tariff reduction to 18% expected to improve margins and volumes; effective tariff around 8-9% due to CBFS offset.
items.quote: This 18% also will see the effective rate being less, maybe around 8-9% or so. So, we definitely, see margin improvement happening.

items.statement: Domestic tyre demand robust with 5-6% growth; international volumes to grow as trade deals improve competitiveness.
items.quote: As I said, the domestic tyre market demand is robust. We should be expecting single -digit growth, but strong single-digit growth, I would say between 5-6%.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black volumes up 17% YoY to 16,700 tons in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: specialty sales volumes were up by 17% YoY to 16,700 tons.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, tariffs, and trade barriers impacted Q3 performance and near-term profitability.
items.quote: our Q3 performance has been shaped by geopolitical developments and volatile market conditions across segments. While this has put pressure on near -term profitability, the underlying fundamentals of our business remain strong an d unchanged.

items.statement: FY26 reported revenue expected broadly in line with FY25 despite Inbrew transition
items.quote: Despite this transition, the company remains confident of maintaining FY '26 reported revenues broadly in line with FY '25.

items.statement: Target 30-35% YoY volume growth for proprietary IMFL brands
items.quote: We continue to target 30% to 35% year-on-year volume growth, aided by an improving brand mix and premiumization trends.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue growth >25% YoY expected to achieve full-year flat revenue
items.quote: Yes, yes. Because we are -- generally, Q4 is the best quarter for us. So we are expecting that to achieve that, yes.

items.statement: Total malt plant capex ~INR100 cr, INR60-65 cr already invested, balance for cask procurement
items.quote: So on an overall front, we will be doing a capex of around about INR100 crores, out of which around INR60 crores, INR65 crores we've already invested. And the balance which would be done would be in purchase of maturation of casks.

items.statement: INR6 cr spent on cask procurement in Q3 FY26, will continue as per operational needs
items.quote: During Q3 FY '26, we incurred INR6 crores towards the casks procurement, and we will continue to procure casks as per the operational requirement.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 16% (+700bps QoQ) driven by raw material softening and proprietary brand mix
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR42 crores, representing an increase of 73% quarter-on-quarter with an EBITDA margin of 16%, improving by 700 basis points from Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Proprietary IMFL EBITDA margin 21% in 9M FY26, highest contributory segment
items.quote: Basically, IMFL Proprietary brand is the highest contributory segment, which is giving a 21% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: RTD Kultur launch on track for H2 FY26; tequila & brandy planned for Q1 FY27 aligned with excise renewal
items.quote: Our RTD product Kultur remains on track for the launch in H2 FY '26. Within our Prestige & Above portfolio, tequila and brandy are planned for the launch in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Malt maturation started; first single malt super-premium product expected in 1-1.5 years (Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28)
items.quote: our maturation has already started. It's been almost 2 months our maturation has already started. So probably within a year, 1.5 years, our first single malt super premium product would be available in the market.

items.statement: Proprietary IMFL volume grew 32% YoY to 1.7M cases in 9M FY26; licensed IMFL down 27% due to Inbrew model change
items.quote: For 9 months FY '26, IMFL proprietary volume stood at 1.7 million cases, representing a growth of 32% on year-on-year basis. IMFL licensed volume stood at 1.02 million cases with a decline of 27% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Ethanol oversupply persists (25% blending capacity vs 20% mandated); exploring private sales and ENA capacity expansion
items.quote: See, right now what the supply of ethanol is, is equivalent to 25% of blending of ethanol. And government has approved only 20% of the blending of ethanol, okay? If in future, the blending percentage goes up, then the ethanol requirement will go up. as we already said, supply is higher than the demand.

name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Ltd

items.statement: Expects Q4 disbursements to be better than Q3 across all businesses.
items.quote: So, quarter 4 will be better than quarter 3 in terms of overall disbursement and across all the businesses, we are seeing the disbursements are up.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-22% for current year.
items.quote: So still, we hold a 20% to 22% AUM growth for the current year.

items.statement: Expects 5-10 bps cost of fund reduction next quarter, flowing to NIM.
items.quote: These two will still give us another 5 to 10 basis points on the cost of fund reduction in next quarter is what we are working on, which should at least to a large extent, flow through to the NIM.

items.statement: Q4 NIM expected around 8.1%, full year slightly below 7.9%.
items.quote: No, no, all put together only income, so 8.1% would be the quarter 4 number. So overall, we should end the year with around shade less than the 7.9% we are talking here.

items.statement: NIM expected to hold at current levels next year absent macro shocks.
items.quote: I expect it to hold next year to a large extent unless there is some drastic increase. I don't see any reduction coming through beyond current levels.

items.statement: Vehicle finance credit costs to moderate in Q4; early delinquencies improving.
items.quote: On the vehicle finance side, the credit costs have stabilized, and we are looking at a reasonable moderation in Q4.

items.statement: CSEL NCL expected to fall below 5% next financial year.
items.quote: 6.4% is very high. And it can come down definitely below 5% in next financial year.

items.statement: Home loan NCL to be maintained at 0.5% going forward.
items.quote: So, we'll maintain the NCL as 0.5 going forward.

items.statement: SBPL credit cost peaked; expected to stabilize and decline from Q4/Q1.
items.quote: For SBPL, the credit cost for Q3 may look higher, but it has basically reached a peak. We don't see any more increase as far as credit cost is concerned.

items.statement: Home loan AUM growth guidance of 28-30% for next 2 years.
items.quote: we have always maintained that the book growth -- AUM growth will be around 28% to 30%, and we see that coming for the next 2 years.

items.statement: CSEL targeting 3.5% ROA next financial year.
items.quote: he will deliver 3.5% ROA, which is normally we targeted in the next financial year.

items.statement: Overall PBT ROTA target of 3.5% reiterated.
items.quote: Those two will be the contributing factors to reach the 3.5% pretax ROTA.

items.statement: Vehicle demand improved post-GST cut; expects Q4 to be very good.
items.quote: So, we are expecting quarter 4 of the vehicle finance is going to be very good and then they are going to maintain it in the next financial year.

items.statement: LAP yields sustained via higher-yield small LAP and geographic expansion.
items.quote: LAP has introduced a small LAP and that small LAP has now started getting the momentum. So, the amount of volume they are generating like INR8,000 crores, in that around 20% is coming from small LAP, which has got high and therefore, they are able to maintain the yield.

items.statement: Iron ore volume target for FY26 is 20-22 million tons, aiming to exit with 20+ million tons.
items.quote: We are very confident of achieving 21. That's why we have given a confident -- a guidance of 20 to 22 million tons for the year.

items.statement: Thriveni FY27 revenue guidance of INR10,000+ crores.
items.quote: FY '27 revenue guidance of INR10,000 plus.

items.statement: Thriveni FY26 revenue guidance of INR7,500+ crores.
items.quote: FY '26 we are looking at a revenue guidance of around INR 7,500 plus crores.

items.statement: Thriveni FY27 EBITDA expected close to INR3,000 crores.
items.quote: FY '27 the EBITDA of Thriveni should be close to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Thriveni FY26 EBITDA guidance of INR2,000-2,200 crores maintained.
items.quote: We stick to the guidance.

items.statement: Capex outlay of INR14,000 crores over this year and next, funded 6,000 crores debt, rest internal accruals.
items.quote: the capex outlay is around INR14,000 crores from this year and the next year. We would be around -- we intend to do around INR6,000 crores from debt and then the balance should be from the internal accruals.

items.statement: Second slurry pipeline capacity increased to 16 million tons, total cost INR8,000 crores, first phase INR2,000-2,500 crores.
items.quote: the total cost envisaged is around INR8,000 crores on this particular project, but we will be doing it on phase wise. So, the first phase of up to Chandrapur will be around INR2,000 crores -- INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Second pellet plant commissioned in Q2 FY27, 1.2 million ton wire rod mill by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: The second pellet plant is now commissioned in Q2 FY27 and the 1.2 million ton wire rod mill by Q4 FY27.

items.statement: BHQ plant expected commissioning by December 2027.
items.quote: we are hopeful of getting it commissioned by December '27 or so.

items.statement: Copper cathode margins anticipated at 30-32%, contributing INR500-700 crores next year.
items.quote: the margins that we anticipate are approximately 30%, 32%. So that gives that INR500 crores, INR700 crores that we're talking about next year.

items.statement: BHQ royalty savings offset processing costs; premium of INR1,400 per ton on higher grade output.
items.quote: The premium that we would get on this output of product if I were to sell all the ore would be around INR1,400 a ton also.

items.statement: Iron ore and pellet demand strong in domestic and international markets; expect buoyancy to continue.
items.quote: On the demand side, both Iron Ore and pellets have witnessed strong demand in the domestic as well as international market, and product has been very, very well accepted.

items.statement: Value-added products accounted for ~35% of standalone revenues in 9M FY26, improving margin stability.
items.quote: For 9 months FY '26, value-added products accounted for roughly 35% of standalone revenues.

items.statement: Logistics is the main challenge for iron ore volume growth, not mining or marketing.
items.quote: the problem is not in the marketing of it, the problem is not in the mining of it. The area that we are right now focusing on solving the problems are on the logistics side.

items.statement: Confident of achieving INR 4,000 crore revenue and 20% EBITDA margin by FY27, ahead of prior FY28 target
items.quote: So, when we say INR 185 crores this quarter, INR 187 crores last quarter, and also the topline is going to close to INR 900 crores, INR 860 odd crores or even if you take 15% growth we are pretty comfortable to reach that level, not even FY'28, in FY'27 that one.

items.statement: 20%+ EBITDA margin sustainable due to diversified four-segment portfolio absorbing segment volatility
items.quote: Yes, it's going to 100% sustain because now you see we have four segments. So, even if there is small issue in one segment, other segment is able to absorb those things. We are very confident to sustain these things.

items.statement: Low capex needed for existing business; free cash flow and warrant proceeds (25% remaining in 12 months) to fund organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: We are going to generate good free cash flow next year, looking at our current debt INR 200 odd crores is nothing actually for this Company. Then even if you look at it INR 800 crores EBITDA there is a lot of free cash generates, we don't need much CAPEX for existing business whatever API.

items.statement: Merger synergies of INR 50-60 crore from network optimization tracked over 12-18 months; interest burden to reduce as debt declines
items.quote: We also explained 50 crores-60 crores it takes 12 months-18 months, it's tracking very well, that 50 crores-60 crores, 18 months start from maybe now 3 months over another 15 months.

items.statement: API growth was low single-digit due to timing of CDMO contracts shifting to next quarter; no structural demand issue
items.quote: API, one of the reason is a little bit timing issue. Last quarter we had a few CDMO contracts. Okay that's pushed to next quarter. This quarter it was less but it's a simple timing issue.

items.statement: Warrant proceeds of 25% remaining to be called in 12 months; debt at INR 200 crore; free cash flow generation to support acquisitions
items.quote: I put a money, 25% remaining, I am going to do 12 months, so all this going is going to come. It's a reasonable size to do entire organic and also some acquisitions.

items.statement: Expects 8,000-9,000 tons monthly trajectory by calendar year end as Jagriti stabilizes.
items.quote: So you know we're looking at about 8 to 9000 ton trajectory in the next you know like I would say by the calendar year end.

items.statement: PM4 to contribute 3,500-4,000 tons; current machines around 4,000 tons.
items.quote: Going to be about 3 1/2 to 4000 tons from PM4. The current paper machines produce around 4000.

items.statement: Jagriti capex about 500 crores, majority in CWIP, 16 crores creditors outstanding.
items.quote: So, the Jagriti Capex at present is about 500 crores and of which majority is actually in the C WIP and we just have about 16 crores which is the creditors outstanding.

items.statement: Total Jagriti spend 515 crores: equity 198, banks/loans 308, creditors 8.
items.quote: The total spend is 515, the total equity invested 198, banks and loans 308, creditor, there's two account balance, 8CR.

items.statement: Equity gap about 60 crores to be funded via internal accruals and promoter equity by Feb-March.
items.quote: So, we are looking at a gap of about 60 CR in the equity side and. Yes, we will. We plan to fund this through internal approvals and the equity from the promoter side.

items.statement: Quarterly EBITDA about 20 crores available; operational and loan interest 3-4 crores.
items.quote: If I look at, even if I keep the performance at say this quarter's level, we would be having about 20 CR of EBITDA avai lable with us. The operational interest and the loan interest would be about 3 or 4 CR and then the balance is available for investment.

items.statement: Guatemala project paused; about $5 million spent, board capped at $10 million.
items.quote: So about five, four to 5 million USD is what has been spent. Our board had anyways restricted us to go beyond 10 million there.

items.statement: Guatemala team to be let go by Jan 31; Rolando retained as legal representative on retainer.
items.quote: We basically informed them that 31st January is going to be the last working day. We will not be paying salaries.

items.statement: Delivery range priced at 25-30% premium vs existing; restaurants can pass on packaging charges.
items.quote: Right. So again, like I said, if you compare Apple to Apple, we're looking at around 25 to 30% premium.

items.statement: B2C revenue up 80% YoY; higher gross margins, adding 5 channels in Q3 and 5 in Q4.
items.quote: Oh, one very, very positive indicator is our growth on B2C side. The revenue has increased 80% year over year.

items.statement: Delivery range launch with 8 machines, each ~400 kg/day initial output.
items.quote: In terms of scale, we will be starting with approximately 8 machines which will be each producing close to 400 KG a day of product.

items.statement: Market resistant to cost increases; refocusing on applications like teabags and back-in-box.
items.quote: So, we are continuing to work on it. We have kind of refocused our energies towards applications like teabags, back in box, etc.

items.statement: PM4 commissioning expected Q1 next year; Jagriti stabilization July 2026.
items.quote: That's what. So that'll be July 26. That's what we declared in the last the board meeting as well.

items.statement: Promoter considering share investment; believes share price heavily undervalued.
items.quote: We have very deep belief in the organization, so we would do whatever we feel is the best possible number. We find that the share price is heavily undervalued right now.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to reach 20% by FY28 driven by chrome ore acquisition, economies of scale, value addition and improved product mix
items.quote: We are positive that the EBITDA margins will continue to get to the 20% level by FY28 which we have been targeting.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 180-190 crore planned for FY26 including DMSO and South Africa mine investment
items.quote: Regarding CAPEX, this year, I mean, we still have a quarter to go. We are going to do about 180 to 190 crores of CAPEX. This includes DMSO and our investment into mine in South Africa.

items.statement: DMSO capacity of 10,000 tons in phased manner (5,000 tons first phase), chrome oxide 20,000 tons at Vizag, chrome metal 6,000 tons
items.quote: For DMSO, we are going to come up with a capacity of 10,000 tons, but it will be in a phased manner. The first phase will be operating at 5,000, and thereafter to 10,000. And chrome oxide, we are going to come up with a capacity of 20,000 tons in Vishakhapatnam. And chrome metal capacity would be 6,000 tons.

items.statement: Strong order book for Barium Carbonate with improved margins after EU imposed 84% anti-dumping duty on Chinese imports
items.quote: So, what I can say is that we are seeing a very strong order book with improved margins and we will see how things progress in the Quarter 1 FY27.

items.statement: Achieved 10-15% price increase for Barium Carbonate, will take further increases in tranches aligned to application market
items.quote: And we have already managed to get 10% to 15% price increase, and we will take one step at a time on what needs to be done and not to do it in a very hurry.

items.statement: US tariff reduction on chrome chemicals expected to restore export volumes; targeting North America revenue share of 14-15% from current 9% over 1-2 years
items.quote: We are confident that our share in North America over the year or two will go up to 14% to 15% in overall revenue of Vishnu Chemicals.

items.statement: Domestic market remained resilient with market share gains in electroplating, wood preservative and pigment sectors despite soft macro
items.quote: In terms of volume, we have managed to increase market share both in electroplating, wood preservative, as well as pigment sector.

items.statement: Capex funding through combination of internal accruals and debt
items.quote: It's a combination of internal accruals and debt.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA growth guidance revised to ~25% from earlier 15-20%
items.quote: you can take it from our side that the guidance gets revised for this year at approximately 25% or so

items.statement: Long-term volume growth guidance of 15-20% annually maintained
items.quote: we are confident that on a yearly basis, we will be growing at 18%, 20% volume growth. So that remains intact

items.statement: Net debt guidance of INR1,250 crores by March 2026 maintained
items.quote: our guidance was INR1,250 crores at the end of -- as at 31st March '26, we have given a guidance of INR1,250 crores

items.statement: Small pack capacity expansion planned for sticks/sachets running at full capacity
items.quote: sticks and pouches, we are almost running at full capacity. And in glass jars and cans, we are at 50% to 60% of capacity utilization. So there is some way to go, and this we are going to expand in the near future

items.statement: New capacity additions to be evaluated after 1.5-2 years when utilization reaches 80-85%
items.quote: by the end of 2 years from now, let's say, we are looking at an 85%, 90% kind of a capacity utilization. And that's the time we'll see that going forward, how do we want to build capacity

items.statement: EBITDA per kg at INR135-140 levels, target to maintain
items.quote: We have now improved our EBITDA per kilo. It's now at INR135, INR140 levels, and we'll continue to maintain -- try and continue to maintain at these levels

items.statement: Volume growth of ~20% in Q3 FY26, 9M volume growth 18-20%
items.quote: out of this 38%, the volume is close to 20% or so. There is another 18% to 20% of value growth that we've got for this quarter

items.statement: Branded retail sales growing 40-50% YoY, targeting INR430-440 crores for FY26
items.quote: We are growing at almost 40%, 50% this year. And this year, we are likely to close at around INR430 crores, INR440 crores of only branded sales

items.statement: Small packs (sticks/sachets) at full capacity, glass jars/cans at 50-60% utilization
items.quote: sticks and pouches, we are almost running at full capacity. And in glass jars and cans, we are at 50% to 60% of capacity utilization

items.statement: Experimenting with traditional snacks under Malgudi brand, micro-launches in Hyderabad
items.quote: we have started experimenting with some traditional snacks under the brand name Malgudi, which goes with traditional ethos of the country

items.statement: Plant-based snacks category shut down due to poor market evolution
items.quote: that category itself, if you see around you, has kind of -- has not done well. In fact, the whole category is almost on a shutdown basis

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR1,448 crores (Dec 2025) from INR2,000 crores a year ago
items.quote: The gross debt, which used to be around INR2,000 crores a year ago, has come down to INR1,448 crores as at 31st December '25

items.statement: Targets double-digit growth for brands, with 8-9% for slower brands, driven by GST cut and rural revival.
items.quote: So our endeavor is always to get to double -digit growth. Of course, some of our brands are seasonal. A lot depends on that. But nevertheless, every brand has got a lot of opportunity because penetrations are still on the lower si de for most of our brands.

items.statement: Expects double-digit top-line growth in Q4 FY26, with caveat on extended winter and summer loading.
items.quote: That is what we expect that hopefully, we should get to double-digit growth. The only caveat is winter is extended, and we have to get to the summer.

items.statement: Expects 8-10% growth if season favorable, focusing on rural sachets.
items.quote: If the season is with us, then I don 't see any reason why should we not get to close to 8% to 10% growth.

items.statement: Digital brands to sustain robust 31% growth in coming quarters.
items.quote: And this growth in the coming quarters, we expect to sustain this robust growth.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 70.6%, up 30 bps, due to cost discipline, price hikes, input stability.
items.quote: On the financial front, gross margin expanded to 70.6%, an improvement of 30 basis points, underscoring our rigorous cost discipline, judicious price hikes and benefits of input price stability.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 33.4%, up 110 bps.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR384 crores, growing by 13%, while EBITDA margins improved to 33.4%, an expansion of 110 basis points.

items.statement: Rural demand improving, expects 8-9% growth for brands previously growing 4-5%.
items.quote: So brands which were growing to -- at 4%, 5%, they should get to about 8%, 9% growth. That is the first target that we have.

items.statement: Rural offtake split is 48-52% in favor of rural; rural growth double-digit this quarter.
items.quote: About -- it's about 48-52 split in favor of rural from an offtake perspective.

items.statement: Quick commerce doubled sales, now 20% of e-comm; organized channels 32% YTD, up 280 bps.
items.quote: Our omnichannel strategy continues to perform well with quick commerce doubling its sales and now contributing 20% to our e -comm business.

items.statement: Summer season uncertain due to erratic weather; trade cautious on stocking.
items.quote: But this year, we have slightly challenged that our winter is extended, and they are being a little cautious.

items.statement: Board declared second interim dividend of INR6 per share for FY26; total INR10 per share in 9M FY26.
items.quote: I'm also delighted to announce that our Board of Directors have declared a second interim dividend of 600%, amounting to INR6 per share for FY '26.

items.statement: Tax rate to reduce to ~25% for standalone from FY27; consolidated tax rate ~20%.
items.quote: Further, I would also like to inform you that as per the recent proposed amendments in the union budget, our applicable income tax rate for the stand -alone entity would reduce to around 25% from 35% for FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Annual consolidated gross margin expected at 66-67% excluding seasonality
items.quote: So keeping aside the seasonality, on an annualized basis, you can assume it about 66%, 67% on a consolidated basis on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Comfort Click targets 14%+ EBITDA margin; base business targets 16-18% EBITDA margin over next 1-2 years
items.quote: Comfort Click, we are looking at continued growth of top line in good double-digits, as we have mentioned. And hopefully, with that business operating between 14% plus kind of EBITDA margins. Our base business, we are where it was, and we are looking at taking it to 16%, 17%, or 18% levels, which is work in progress.

items.statement: RiteBite Max Protein revenue aspiration of INR500 crores potentially achievable in 2 years
items.quote: Hypothetically, yes. I can't comment on the specifics. But yes, of course, it's possible. There is a good potential in this.

items.statement: Current financial year expected to be bottom for PAT; next financial year onwards EPS accretive including acquisitions
items.quote: So as we talked about this earlier also, maybe the current year current financial year will be the bottom. And from next financial year onwards, we'll have even EPS accretive P&L even for the new entity newly acquired entity.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery outpacing gradual urban improvement; consumption trends steady in Q3 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, consumption trends remained steady, led by sustained recovery in rural demand, which continued to outpace the gradual improvement in urban markets.

items.statement: Comfort Click expanding in Europe (Poland, Finland, Portugal) and US; RiteBite Max Protein now in 9 countries; Cuticolor launched in organized channel
items.quote: WeightWorld brand advanced its European expansion by entering Poland, Finland, and Portugal, strengthening Comfort Click's regional footprint and unlocking access to fast-growing Wellness markets in Europe. RiteBite Max Protein expanded into 2 additional international markets, taking its presence to 9 countries within

items.statement: Key input costs largely under control except milk ahead of upcoming season
items.quote: On the raw material front, except for milk, other key inputs remained largely under control ahead of the upcoming season.

items.statement: Comfort Click employs ~340 people, largely Indian residents based in Hyderabad and Baroda
items.quote: About 340, 300 plus, largely Indian resident, large offices between Hyderabad and Baroda.

items.statement: Constant currency growth reporting for Comfort Click to start from next financial year
items.quote: From maybe next year onwards, we'll start reporting constant currency growth also.

items.statement: MAT provisions impact under evaluation; analysis to be disseminated within a week
items.quote: Our team is working on finalizing the impact on the of this revised MAT as well as evaluating the setup of the MAT as per the new regime. And our team will be ready with the analysis in about a week's time.

items.statement: Early season demand (first 30 days) in line with expectations; real season starts March-April
items.quote: Overall, I mean, early days to say, everything is in line. This I mean, 30 days, the real season starts from March-April. So these 30 days, yes, we are it's in line with our expectation, but that's it.

items.statement: Improved segmental disclosures targeted by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: Over the next few months, by end of the year, we'll come back and work on some of these things so that we can give you a better visibility.

items.statement: Expects to return to 13-14% EBITDA margin in Q4 FY26, and 16-17% in H2 FY27.
items.quote: So, you will find that those margins of 16%, 17% should be looking very likely in the second half of next financial year. But we should be back to that 13%, 14% level in Q4 itself.

items.statement: Full year FY26 revenue growth expected at 7-8%.
items.quote: And we should be ending the year as we projected in the earlier con-call by roughly 7% to 8% on an overall full year basis.

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth in Q4 FY26 and next financial year.
items.quote: So, we now anticipate that going forward we should be able to maintain this momentum of double-digit growth in Q4 as well as in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Announced price increase of 4% for Sanitaryware and 11% for Faucetware.
items.quote: The kind of indication that we have given to the market is on an average it will be 4% for Sanitaryware and 11% for Faucetware.

items.statement: Price increase sufficient to cover cost increases to date.
items.quote: Yes, the price increase will be sufficient to cover the kind of increases which have happened till date.

items.statement: FY26 capex outlay around INR13.2 crore by end of December 2025.
items.quote: Our capital expenditure plan for financial year '26 remains measured with an outlay of around INR13.2 crore by end of December '25.

items.statement: Faucetware brownfield expansion from 4 lakh to 6 lakh units can be done in 3-4 months when demand sustains.
items.quote: So, with these, whenever we feel that the demand is sustained and that we will be able to keep on having a kind of sustained production requirement we can go from 4 lakhs to 6 lakhs within a span of, you can say, 3 to 4 months because only balancing equipment needs to be done.

items.statement: New Sanitaryware plant construction decision to be taken at end of Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The land is already purchased, but we have not commenced the construction activity for the plant. That we are going to take a view at the end of Q4, depending upon the market situation at that point of time, whether we need to start construction immediately or defer it even further.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin declined to 10.2% due to trade discounts, brass costs, publicity, and pre-operating expenses.
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 10.2% in Q3 FY '26 as compared to 13.2% in Q3 FY '25. This decline was primarily driven by an increase in trade discounts and elevated brass input costs impacting both manufacturing and procurement.

items.statement: Demand improving with 11.1% growth in Q3 FY26, driven by actual demand not pre-buying.
items.quote: So, there is an actual improvement in demand. If you look at our growth even in Q2, we have grown by 5% to 6%. In fact, the price increase has happened only yesterday.

items.statement: Senator and POLIPLUZ sales expected at INR20 crore for FY26, revised down from INR40-45 crore.
items.quote: And we had earlier projected something like INR40 crore for the full year, but we would like to revise that we should be ending at more like INR20 crore for the current year because the stores have been taking some time to get ready.

items.statement: Senator and POLIPLUZ expected to achieve INR100-120 crore revenue next year.
items.quote: So next year, we should be able to do once the scale-up is complete, more in the region of, you can say, INR100 crore to INR120 crore.

items.statement: Brass prices increased 12% in Q3 and further in January, posing cost pressure.
items.value: 12% increase in Q3, from INR640 to INR800 per kg in January
items.quote: In Q3, it has risen by something like 12%. In January, again, it has gone up significantly. If you look at the entire purchase of the 9 months of the financial year, from March -- April to December, you will find that the average price was something like INR640 for brass per kg, which has gone up to something like INR8

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 102% for Faucetware and 82% for Sanitaryware in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: During the quarter, capacity utilization stood at 102% for Faucetware and 82% for Sanitaryware.

items.statement: Europe revenue to grow 20%+ over next few years, with margin improvement.
items.quote: I'm not just looking at top line growth, but we should look at Europe over the next few years as growing at 20% plus in revenues.

items.statement: Europe revenue can reach INR400-500 crores by FY28 or FY29.
items.quote: Yes, yes. We can expect that. We can.

items.statement: India business to grow double-digit, but not confident about 15%.
items.quote: So I do feel confident for a double-digit. I'm not so confident about the 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to stabilize at 13-14% in next couple of years, then improve.
items.quote: I feel in the next couple of years, we would be stabilizing at around 13, 14. And a couple of years after that, we should be able to pitch for much better margin.

items.statement: API business to ramp up in 8-10 months as Auric site starts high revenues.
items.quote: But I'm sure that in another 8 to 10 months, we will start getting high revenues from Auric site also and then we can really ramp up our API business.

items.statement: FPP to launch at least five new products in FY27.
items.quote: We have right now visibility for '26 -'27, where there is expectation that at least five new products should be launched out of our own portfolio.

items.statement: No further capital expenditure planned; maintenance capex INR35-40 crores per annum.
items.quote: Around 35, 40 max per annum would be the maintenance capex required.

items.statement: Other expenses to be controlled at INR150 crores consolidated, excluding one-time costs.
items.quote: But otherwise, we are confident to keep it at INR150 crores on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: One-time costs of INR8-9 crores in Q3 from remediation and penalties.
items.quote: Around INR8 crores to INR9 crores.

items.statement: Technology transfer costs ~INR20 crores annually for second site supply.
items.quote: So, I think we can roughly quantify that on an annual basis we would have spent around INR20 crores?

items.statement: Europe Q4 to be much better due to resolved MMP issues and new sites.
items.quote: And in the new sites are all coming in, we expect the fourth quarter to be much better for Europe.

items.statement: US sterile sales from Goa lines to contribute meaningfully in Q4.
items.quote: Yes. We have seen some upside in the present quarter. I'm hoping we'll be able to keep that run rate. If that happens, Q4, you will see some meaningful contribution.

items.statement: Total debt ~INR900 crores; long-term debt to reduce to ~INR550-555 crores by year-end.
items.quote: So our total debt right now sits at around INR900 crore s. INR700 crores in the main business and INR220 crores in WRPL.

items.statement: Africa EBITDA margin expected to reach 10% in H2 FY27, 7-8% in H1 FY27.
items.quote: I am expecting Africa's EBITDA margin for next financial year, that is FY '27, by the second half of that year, cross 10% easily, maybe even stay at an average of about 10% in '27 based on the order volumes that we anticipate.

items.statement: India margins to stay flat until US tariff corrects; Q4 similar to Q3.
items.quote: So my India business, if the reciprocal tariff remains at 50%, the India business margins will remain where they are.

items.statement: Africa bottomed out; margin improvement from Q4 onwards.
items.quote: So in some ways, you could say that region has bottomed out and performance will improve from Q4 onwards.

items.statement: US tariff burden of INR40.2 crores shared with customers in Q3; will persist while tariff remains.
items.quote: The whole U.S. tariff burden is that is the burden that we -- is the impact that we've had during this quarter. And that amounts to about INR40 crores, INR40.2 crores.

items.statement: Total penal tariff impact ~INR60 crores, offset INR20 crores from supply chain.
items.quote: The total impact of the penal tariff was closer to INR60 crores, and we set off about INR20 crores of it from our supply chain.

items.statement: No ability to raise prices amid high tariffs; will continue discounts to US customers.
items.quote: I don't see any ability for us to increase prices in the interim, with high tariffs as well as the expectation of inflation in U.S., et c., our ability to increase prices is next to zero.

items.statement: Good order book visibility for India and Africa; Q4 and Q1 FY27 order book robust.
items.quote: For the quarters ahead, the company has the visibility of a good order book for both India and Africa business.

items.statement: European revenue rising from 13% to 16-17%; adding new EU customer.
items.quote: We were at about 13%. Now we are further increasing it going forward, about -- we'll be about 16%, 17%.

items.statement: Two India units (Bhopal phase 2, Karnataka) to start commercial production next financial year.
items.quote: These 2 units are in advanced stages of execution completion, and we expect the commercial production to happen in the next financial year.

items.statement: Kenya capacity expansion to come on stream in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: That will also come on stream in the next financial year in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Invested INR175 crores in BRFL via OCDs and INR72 crores for 19% stake; acquisition expected Q2 FY27.
items.quote: So far, I think we have invested in OCD to the extent of about INR175 crores in BRFL. We've also bought 19% stake in the company, paying about INR72 crores.

items.statement: AGOA restoration clarity expected within a month; would be massive tailwind for Africa.
items.quote: My sense is it will -- we will get to know within a month as to the status of AGOA. Month of February, we will have a clarity.

items.statement: India-EU FTA opens significant market; implementation likely 2027.
items.quote: In the long-term, the recently announced India-EU FTA will open access to a significant market, placing Indian exporters at par with key competing countries like Bangladesh, Vietnam and a 12% duty advantage with China.

items.statement: Africa EBITDA margin expected to reach 10% in H2 next financial year, with H1 at 7-8%.
items.quote: So, Africa for next financial year, we are anticipating at least in the second half going to 10% in the first half, staying at between 7% and 8% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Aim to push African revenues to US$120-125 million next financial year.
items.quote: Our endeavour for next financial year is to try to push African revenues to 120 US$ million, 125 US$ million or thereabouts next financial year.

items.statement: Additional India revenue potential of INR500 crores from Bhopal, Jharkhand, and Karnataka units, but ramp-up delayed due to tariffs.
items.quote: So these 3 entities put together can contribute about INR500 crores annually.

items.statement: India margins to remain at current levels until U.S. tariffs persist.
items.quote: India margins will stay where they are until the U.S. tariff remains.

items.statement: U.S. demand growth expected to stay muted in 2026 due to inflation and geopolitics.
items.quote: I wouldn't say there is going to be a demand upswing. On the contrary, demand growth will stay muted till this geopolitics plays out in 2026.

items.statement: Intention to increase European business share from 14-16% to 20-25% of total revenues.
items.quote: today, European business is closer to about 14% - 15%, 16-odd percent of our total revenues. Intention is to take it up to 20%, 25%.

items.statement: If 50% tariff on India continues for long, brands may diversify sourcing away from India.
items.quote: if 50% tariff doesn't change soon, change in the next several months, we may have brands looking at options to diversify their sourcing.

items.statement: Hedged USD receivables at INR88.5-89, while spot is INR91, providing potential upside.
items.quote: our hedge rate for Q3 was about INR88.5 or thereabouts.

items.statement: No duty refund expected if AGOA is restored; benefits will be prospective only.
items.quote: AGOA, no, no, no. So all that will be prospect. I don't think we'll get a duty refund for past, yes.

items.statement: Export incentive budget allocation for RoSCTL and duty drawback reduced, but no scheme changes announced.
items.quote: the allocation to RoSCTL and duty drawback has reduced compared to the actual spend in 2025-'26.

items.statement: Expects FY27 defence performance to be very good with gradual quarterly improvements; formal guidance to be shared at start of FY27
items.quote: In FY27, we are likely to perform very good. And the total expectations, we will share at the start of the financial year 2027.

items.statement: Expects to sustain consolidated EBITDA margins around 27-28% over next 3-5 years driven by defence and international growth
items.quote: We are confident that we should be able to maintain the EBITDA margins around 27%-28 % as we move forward also.

items.statement: International explosives revenue crossed Rs 1,000 crore in Q3 (+35% YoY) driven by strong commodity demand (gold, copper) across Africa, SE Asia, Turkey
items.quote: Our international business has crossed 1000 crore revenue in this quarter which is a significant increase of 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: Domestic mining demand flat in 9M FY26 due to heavy monsoon and economic slowdown; expects 6-7% annual commodity demand growth and 10-12% volume growth long-term
items.quote: If you look at India business definitely in the first 9 months, the demand was greatly impacted due to heavy monsoon and some slowdown in the economy.

items.statement: Defence revenue hit record Rs 702 crore in Q3 (+72% YoY); Pinaka rockets to start shipping in Q4; 155mm artillery shell commercial production to begin Q4
items.quote: Defence revenue was quarterly highest till date at Rs. 702 crores versus Rs. 409 crores up by 72% showing a wonderful fix in the defence business.

items.statement: Capex update to be shared with Q4 results; ~Rs 2,500 crore guided for FY26
items.quote: We can share the total CAPEX update on the Q4 numbers, please.

items.statement: Key strategic challenges: adopting new technologies, developing products, maintaining stakeholder relationships across expanding defence zones
items.quote: As we are expanding in defence in various zones or areas, it will be a challenge for us to maintain the relationship and strong connect with all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Forex exposure cost normal at ~Rs 20 crore; operating in multiple currencies across geographies
items.quote: So, it's approximately around Rs. 20 crores odd which is very, very normal cost.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected flat in value terms; volume decline but will recover in FY27
items.quote: Current year, I think we will be flat, flat to positive, but yes, flat. That is what I can tell you. It is in value terms.

items.statement: Target revenue of INR 6,000-7,000 crores by FY29 or latest FY30
items.quote: by FY '29 or latest by FY '30, we should be somewhere between INR6,000 crores to INR7,000 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity INR 5,000-5,500 crores; can reach INR 5,500-6,000 crores with tweaks; land acquired in Indore and Palwal for future expansion
items.quote: our current capacity is upwards of INR5,000 crores. I think a little tweak here and there, it can go to INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores.

items.statement: Defense orders of ~INR 500 crores in hand; expect INR 150-200 crores execution in FY27
items.quote: currently, we have orders of approximately INR500 crores in hand, which have to be executed.

items.statement: Construction equipment EBIT margin at ~20% in Q3, near peak; agri EBIT margin dropped to ~1% due to provisions, target 12-15% over time
items.quote: construction equipment, this quarter, we are already at close to about 20% EBIT level, which I think is one of the best in the country

items.statement: Price increases across all non-agri categories accepted by market after 8-10 months; gross margins 32-34% sustainable due to pricing power and cost efficiencies
items.quote: Now I think it is 9 months down the line, 10 months down the line. Now it has totally flown into customers.

items.statement: Shift to higher-tonnage new-gen cranes and tower cranes driving margin improvement; tower crane volumes up 8-9% YoY to ~900 units in FY26
items.quote: Tower cranes closer to about 800 last year. This year, it will be closer to 900.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on Chinese crawler/truck cranes recommended by DGTR in Sept but not notified by Finance Ministry; PLI scheme (CIE) expected in 2-4 months as alternative
items.quote: Finally, duty was recommended on the Chinese cranes in the month of September. Unfortunately, for some good-bad reason, it has not been notified by the Finance Ministry.

items.statement: Exports targeting 7% of revenue in FY26 (up from 4%); defense targeting 2% in FY26, 4-5% in FY27; combined target 10-15% by FY27
items.quote: Our plan was 10% to 15%. The first benchmark, hopefully, we should be reaching in FY '27.

items.statement: Electric cranes ready for commercial sale within Q4 FY26 after ARAI battery approval
items.quote: Within this quarter, the electric cranes will become ready for commercial sale

items.statement: Tower crane capacity at 800-900 units, currently at ~80% utilization; planning new plant in Palwal to expand to ~1,100 units in FY27
items.quote: In the next year, we will try and expand our capacity for tower cranes. Because our current capacity is 800-900, we are doing a small rejig so that our capacity comes closer to maybe 1,100 units

items.statement: Backhoe loader volumes at 800-900 units annually; target 3x growth over 5 years; gaining market share as domestic market contracted 10% but ACE flat
items.quote: We feel that even in the coming year from this 800, 900 units, we should easily go to 1,300, 1,200 units, that's a 30%, 40% increase.

items.statement: Targets 8-10% SSSG, at least 50% revenue growth, and 150 new store additions in FY27
items.quote: We guide for 8% to 10% SSSG for next year, and at least a 50% revenue growth, and adding at least 150 new stores.

items.statement: Targets blended sales per sq ft of Rs 1,000 in FY27 despite 50% area expansion
items.quote: So, if you talk about company blended level, we are targeting it to maintain at a Rs. 1,000 per square feet, even when we are adding 50% more area every year.

items.statement: Capex per store ~Rs 1.1 cr; inventory investment ~Rs 1.3-1.4 cr; total ~Rs 2.4-2.5 cr per store
items.quote: The CAPEX per store is around Rs. 1.1 crore and the investment in inventory for that store is around Rs. 1.3 crores. Total investment is Rs. 2.4 crores to Rs. 2.5 crores.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of Rs 400 cr to fund new stores, working capital, and regional warehouses over next 12 months
items.quote: So, that is why most of the proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes. So, that is a mix of new capital allocation for the new stores. That is a mix of additional working capital required. That is also some investment in the regional warehouses and hub-and-spoke model that we are doing.

items.statement: Targets gross margin 28-29%; EBITDA margin expansion via operating leverage and higher sales per sq ft
items.quote: So, going forward also, we target a gross margin of 28% - 29%. And all the margin expansion should happen from operating leverage and from higher sales per square feet.

items.statement: Targets cost of retailing ~Rs 180 per sq ft in near future (from ~Rs 195 in Q3)
items.quote: I think we can target Rs. 180 in the near future.

items.statement: Full-price sales 92% in Q3; no significant increase in industry discounting observed
items.quote: We also sold more than 92% of goods at full price in this quarter. So, in fact, our full price sales have been increasing. But we have not seen at the industry level also like other retailers...

items.statement: Demand momentum unchanged in Q4; wedding season and potential GST/consumption boost supportive
items.quote: So, the momentum has been the same. We are seeing the same kind of footfalls and demand in the fourth quarter. And that is why the next year guidance is also the same.

items.statement: Women's wear (kurti) growing fastest; no structural mix shift expected over next 3 years

items.quote: Another important project is Rishikesh-Karnaprayag, where work is going on full swing, and our target which is to achieve the completion of the project in December 2028.

items.statement: Signed MOU with Visakha Port Authorities for infrastructure development.
items.quote: We have also signed an MOU with Visakha Port Authorities for development of various infrastructure projects in that port.

items.statement: Internal KPI: revenue growth plus EBITDA growth combined around 45%, with margin expansion.
items.quote: Our internal KPI is that both of these areas have to grow on an average of about over 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Model company at 19-20% revenue growth; internal push 20-25% across revenue and EBITDA.
items.quote: When you model our company at a round 19% to 20% growth rate, that is a sensible way to model us, because internally, I am pushing for around 20% to 25% growth across these metrics, which our team has been consistently achieving and is still hungry to push for more.

items.statement: Model 18-20% revenue growth and 23-25% EBITDA growth.
items.quote: If you are modeling our company for growth, modeling it for around 18% to 20% revenue growth and around 23% to 25% EBITDA percentage growth would be sensible.

items.statement: Q4 revenue could be slightly below to slightly above Q3; normal scenario slight dip.
items.quote: Given that context, it could range to slightly below Q3 to slightly above Q3, but we should be very resilient in Q4.

items.statement: OCF to PAT expected 85-95% for the year; collection days to normalize in Q4.
items.quote: We believe that we will be achieving in the range of around 85%-95% OCF for this year also.

items.statement: Data and inventory cost increase is investment in verticalization for international markets; will continue for a few more quarters.
items.quote: This is something that we will continue to do for at least a few more quarters till we can unlock the full potential of all the industry verticals that our platforms can serve in international markets.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected faster than revenue growth, leading to margin expansion.
items.quote: Therefore, the EBITDA growth would be faster than the revenue growth in most cases.

items.statement: Opex will not grow in line with revenue, driving operating leverage and margin expansion.
items.quote: The efficiencies will be realized even more on the EBITDA level, because our opex is not going to grow at pace with that.

items.statement: CPCU rate increased due to verticalization and premium user targeting, enabling higher pricing.
items.quote: Consequently, because of this verticalization strategy, as well as with the ability to target premium consumers in a deeply intelligent way, with personalization of those personas relevant to that industry vertical, these two factors are allowing us to charge a higher price.

items.statement: India growth resilient and diversified; iOS and CTV are key growth anchors.
items.quote: Earlier, our growth in India was anchored on Android. Now we are also doing really well on iOS.

items.statement: CTV contributing meaningfully to shifting advertiser budgets to CPCU model.
items.quote: Therefore, the CTV business is contributing meaningfully to this expansion of growth of the advertisers’ budget towards the CPCU business model.

items.statement: RMG ban caused INR 10-12 crores revenue loss in Q3, but broad-based recovery in India.
items.quote: You can assume about INR 10 crores to INR 12 crores of revenue on the base effect for the Q3 of the last year, which has not occurred in this quarter.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic acquisitions; shortlisted from 12 to 4 companies, targeting one meaningful deal in 2026.
items.quote: We have shortlisted from 12 to 4 and hopefully from 4 to 1 in the near term.

items.statement: Focus on verticalization across EFGH categories; E and F strong, G pulled back, H doing well, healthcare needs more investment.
items.quote: In category G, we saw some pullback. In category H, hospitality and travel is doing well while in healthcare, we need to double-up and we need to do more.

items.statement: Board approved INR 700 crore fundraise via QIP/preferential; promoter to maintain >50% stake.
items.quote: the board yesterday has agreed to a fundraise of INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Target to expand bed capacity from 700-800 to 2,000-2,300 by 2029.
items.quote: We are looking to increase our bed capacity from our existing 700 to 800 that we have today to 2,000 to 2,300 by 2029.

items.statement: Raipur 300-bed hospital capex INR 100 crores, funded by accruals and IFC funds.
items.quote: our capex for Raipur is all done and it is at INR 100 crores for 300 beds.

items.statement: Raipur hospital to start operations from April-May 2026.
items.quote: We are on track with the commissioning of our new 300-bed super specialty hospital in Raipur, which is expected to begin operations from April-May 2026.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement as costs ease and occupancy rises to 68-70%.
items.period: end of FY26 or early FY27
items.quote: By the end of this financial year, or the beginning of the next financial year, we should be hovering around 68%-70% is one thing.

items.statement: ARPOB to grow 4-6% YoY long-term, driven by mix and medical value travel.
items.quote: we are going to maintain the increase in the ARPOB trend the way we have managed. 4% to 6% year-on-year

items.statement: South Delhi 650-bed hospital capex INR 75-80 lakhs per bed; construction to start April-May 2026.
items.value: INR 75 to INR 80 lakhs per bed
items.quote: Cost per bed would be in the range of INR 75 to INR 80 lakhs per bed

items.statement: Raipur ARPOB to start at INR 30,000-35,000, ramping to INR 40,000-55,000.
items.quote: we are expecting an ARPOB of INR 30,000 to INR 35,000 to start

items.statement: International patient revenue grew 34.9%, contributing 34% of total revenues.
items.quote: Our international patients revenue grew by 34.9%, contributing to 34% of our total revenues.

items.statement: Employee cost peak is one-time; annual appraisal impact 4-5% going forward.
items.quote: There will be an annual appraisal impact of 4 to 5%.

items.statement: Debt to be reduced to INR 250-280 crores maximum after fundraise.
items.quote: The maximum debt we will be at any point will be less than INR 300, INR 250 to INR 280 crores.

items.statement: Gurugram expansion to 1,000 beds with capex INR 60-65 lakhs per bed.
items.quote: around 60, 65 lakhs per bed is what I would say.

items.statement: Raipur hospital expected to break even in 18-24 months.
items.quote: Yeah, 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20% CAGR over next 2 years with EBITDA margin improving to 20-23%
items.quote: This robust platform supports our revenue growth target of 20% CAGR. Moreover, as higher value pursuing contracts gain traction and rising demand for scientific -based remediation and circular economy solutions, we anticipate an improved margin profile of a round 20% to 23% going forward as well.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at 15-18% based on executed contracts and current run rate
items.quote: The revenue growth for the next year based on the Atkoli and maybe incremental capex should be in the range of 15% to 18% for us.

items.statement: Two BMC C&T contracts worth Rs.1,330 crores over 7 years via 51% owned subsidiary consortium
items.quote: These contracts carry a combined revenue potential of approximately Rs.1,330 crores over a 7-year tenure, enhancing long-term revenue visibility and providing annuity-like cash flow.

items.quote: Our subsidiary, Antony Lara Enviro Solutions Private Limited secured a 10 -year DBOT concession from Thane Municipal Corporation to set up and operate a 600 to 800 tons per day municipal solid waste preprocessing and stabilization facility, backed by a fully reimbursable capital outlay of Rs.67 crores.

items.statement: Two Andhra Pradesh WTE projects (Kadapa & Kurnool) each 750 TPD, 15 MW; total capex Rs.600-650 crores at 75:25 debt/equity; EBITDA margin >40%; revenue from FY29
items.quote: Total project capex is expected to be around Rs.600 crores to Rs.650 crores with debt/equity ratio of around 75 -25. The EBITDA margin would be similar to our PCMC site, which is upwards of 40%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.4% impacted by annual appraisal/incentive cycle and manpower additions; 9M FY26 margin 21.4% per guidance
items.quote: For the quarter, the company reported an EBITDA of Rs.50 crores with margins at 18.4%. The operating margins were impacted by higher employee cost, a normal occurrence in Q3 due to the annual appraisal and the incentive cycle.

items.statement: PCMC WTE tipping fee escalated from Rs.505 to Rs.656/ton (cumulative 3-4 years); future annual escalation 3-5%
items.quote: With escalation, our current tipping fee is about Rs.656 per ton, which will get escalated every year. There was a cascading effect of 3 to 4 years cumulatively, so that's why the first escalation was at a higher rate. But going forward, anything between 3% to 5% is a fair assumption.

items.statement: Live WTE tender in eastern India; more tenders expected in Tamil Nadu post state elections in next 2 quarters
items.quote: As we speak, there is one live tender in the eastern part of the country and a few more on the drawing board stage. We are expecting a few more tenders in South India, especially Tamil Nadu in the next 2 quarters after the elections in Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: C&D waste recycling contribution currently 5% of revenue; expected to at least double in FY27 due to policy changes
items.quote: As of now, the contribution of C&D business is 5%. We expect this to at least double in the next financial year.

items.statement: DSO elevated at 114-115 days but improved to ~96 days after collection efforts; municipalities remain tough paymasters
items.quote: We know that the days sales outstanding remained elevated at approximately 114-115 days during the period, which continues to be a key area of focus for us. Encouragingly, subsequent collections efforts have yielded positive results, bringing the DSO down to around 96 days.

items.statement: Post AP WTE commercialization (FY29), expect Rs.90-140 crores annual revenue in first years, scaling to Rs.130-140 crores
items.value: Rs.90-140 crores initial; Rs.130-140 crores steady
items.quote: So post the AP project commercial operation, we expect close to around Rs.90 crores to Rs.140 crores of annual revenue to start in the first couple of years, and that will scale up to around Rs.130 crores to Rs.140-odd crores going forward.

items.statement: Merger of AG Enviro Infrastructure Projects with parent completed Dec 31, 2025 post NCLT approval; streamlines operations, optimizes cash flow, strengthens balance sheet

items.statement: BMC C&T contracts already awarded; new standing committee expected to improve execution speed and reduce administrative delays in payments
items.quote: Collection and Transportation contracts are already bid out, and they already have been awarded. So, with the new standing committee and other general body coming in, we expect decision -making to be faster and execution should be smoother.

items.statement: Broking business growth expected at 10-14%.
items.quote: overall, like, growth would be there in tune of 10 % to 14%

items.quote: We plan to grow at around 20% - 25% for next couple of years in terms of AUM. So, if I give a number to it, we can reasonably expect it to close above Rs. 6,000 crores at the end of FY’27.

items.statement: Micro LAP portfolio to increase to Rs. 125 crores by March end FY26.
items.quote: Currently, we stand at Rs. 80 crores of Micro LAP portfolio and we plan to increase it to Rs. 125 crores by March end, FY’26

items.statement: Expect 15-20 bps reduction in cost of borrowing over next six months.
items.quote: I expect another 15 to 20 basis point reduction in the next six months

items.statement: AUM growth to regain traction after strategic shifts stabilize.
items.quote: Once these strategic shifts stabilize, we expect AUM growth to regain traction

items.quote: in totality, around 70% of business comes from online

items.quote: approximately 21% of net inflows come from SIP and interesting data point is, out of total AUM of ours, 80% is equity

items.quote: we have already taken 15.25% GST impact. So, we are already impacte d, but we are already stabilize our business model this quarter only.

items.statement: STT increase in budget may impact broking; focus on cash and commodity.
items.quote: we have to see even in this budget the STT has been increased. So, our major focus would be there in increasing cash market business and the commodity business in time to come.

items.statement: Discount broking in gestation period, spending on marketing to open 12,000 accounts monthly.
items.quote: We are opening around 12,000 accounts per month , a nd for that, we are spending a lot on marketing.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 to be better than Q3 with volume growth and pricing recovery; full-year FY26 EBITDA growth above 8% YoY
items.quote: we will maintain that kind of run rate and we will continue to give the volume growth. The pricing as of now looks like we have hit the bottom and we will see some recovery. So definitely, this quarter should be better than the previous one

items.statement: Multi-year EBITDA CAGR aspiration of at least 20%
items.quote: if you take a multiyear average, our EBITDA at least at 20% CAGR. So that is the trajectory.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR500 crore, funded by internal accruals
items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan to invest approximately INR500 crore in 2027, which will also be supported by internal accruals.

items.quote: We have incurred year-to-date capex of INR366 crore. The majority of this spend was directed towards the upcoming CDMO agro plant at Bharuch and the construction of our new multipurpose facility at Gajraula.

items.statement: 16 molecules confirmed with peak potential of INR1,400 crore; 7+ in advanced discussions with INR900 crore potential; total funnel 100+ opportunities with INR3,500 crore peak potential

items.quote: Our quarterly EBITDA margin for the segment remained stable, sustaining a trajectory above 25% with absolute EBITDA reported at INR116 crore.

items.quote: However, margins are expected to improve in the coming quarters as prices recover and the share of cosmetic and food grade products increases in the overall product mix.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals mix improving with higher fine chemicals and CDMO share; Nutrition mix shifting toward cosmetic and food grade from feed
items.quote: the mix of our Specialty Chemical business is also improving because the share of fine chemicals and CDMO in specialty is increasing and those are high-margin growth driver segments for us

items.statement: Renewable power share increased to 34% in Q3 from 28% in Q2; power and fuel expenses down 10% YoY and 3% QoQ
items.quote: the successful commissioning of renewable O2 power at our Bharuch site, which has taken Ingrevia's renewable power share to 34% in Q3 as against 28% in Q2

items.statement: Interim dividend of 250% (INR2.5 per share) recommended by Board
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board has recommended an interim dividend of 250%, translating to INR2.5 per equity share.

items.statement: Beauty EBITDA margin can sustainably improve going forward, but no specific guidance given.
items.quote: I don't want to guide towards any direction, but I think it can sustainably improve going forward.

items.quote: But I mean, I'm not guiding towards that, but I think it remains a market opportunity.

items.quote: And this is also something that is, I would say, it can be quickly expanded given its low CapEx and low fixed cost model.

items.quote: We've entered into a deep strategic partnership with Nike to run Nike's official direct-to-customer, D2C digital commerce platforms in the country.
