items.quote: Yes, there are no one-off items, but it has a mix impact. So mix impact sometimes pulls something down, and it also has a service ad income impact.

items.statement: India-U.K. and EU trade deals may lower import tariffs, potentially reducing costs and consumer prices.
items.quote: So, there is a chance that if the tariffs are lower, they could even pass some of that advantage on to the consumer in terms of bringing the price multiplier down and making the products more, I would say, equitable on price to what it is in the U.S. and European markets.

items.statement: E-commerce beauty category growing strongly as offline GT/MT sales shift to quick commerce.
items.quote: I think the category growth has been strong and category growth is also increasing in terms of category growth through e-commerce is increasing because a lot of offline sales through GT/MT are moving to e-commerce through the quick commerce model.

items.statement: Fragrance market expected to evolve with higher share of luxury fragrances over time.
items.quote: So this is where we do believe that over time, India's fragrance market will continue to evolve to get to a higher share of mix from luxury fragrance brands.

items.statement: Nykaa Now not dilutive to overall profitability; may lower AOV but increase frequency.
items.quote: So this is not a very dilutive. This is not dilutive currently nor do we envisage this to be dilutive to overall profitability in a meaningful way.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 19-20%, implying revenue of $119-120 million.
items.quote: overall, for this year, I would say we are on track to deliver revenue growth of bet ween 19% to 20%. So we should end the year with revenue between $119 million to $120 million.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expected around 24%, in line with prior guidance.
items.quote: On a full year basis, we expect that our EBITDA would be closer to about 24%, right, which is in line with what we had guided earlier in the year.

items.quote: The trajectory that is called for to get to that $200 million number would require close to a 30% kind of a growth, right? items.quote: But on an ongoing basis, the restructuring of compensation will mean that there will be an impact of between 10 to 15 basis points on our earnings going forward.

items.statement: Vertical mix shift: financial services and consumer goods to grow; technology to become smaller share.
items.quote: I would say that over the next couple of years, financial services and consumer goods will become larger shares of the revenue right that we'll be delivering. And tech will become slightly smaller because of some of the issues.

items.quote: But FY '27, INR10,000 crores seems to be now kind of number, which we may not be able to achieve, maybe it may go to FY '28, but we would suddenly be into a striking distance of this number.

items.quote: So these all put together, NPD will be roughly around INR500 crores or something in that range.

items.quote: But 15th November onwards, we found that rural market started giving us much more consumption. And there was a demand that we can -- we could see clearly, and this demand continues even till today.

items.statement: Alternate channels growing 35-40% vs 5-8% in general trade; quick commerce up 65%.
items.quote: And you can say around 35%, 40% is the average growth rate of alternate channel versus 5%, 7%, 8% in general trade.

items.statement: Focus on distribution expansion and alternate channels for Foods business growth.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance to be shared by end of March or April call
items.quote: For the next year, we'll give you more accurate numbers probably by end of March or in the April call, rather than giving it now.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 9-10% for FY26
items.quote: So guidance of margin, we are still maintaining 9% to 10%.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at INR130-150 crore, INR120 crore spent so far
items.quote: So we have, I think, done almost close to INR120 crores so far. And we are looking at a INR130 crores to INR150 number by March end in CapEx.

items.statement: FY27 capex still under evaluation, to be finalized by April
items.quote: FY27, we are still studying the situation. So, it is still a little dynamic. But by April, I think we'll give you a more accurate number.

items.statement: AC division running at full capacity for next few months; refrigeration capacity also fully booked for season
items.quote: Over the next three, four months for the current season, we are running on full capacity, or we have an order book which expected to run on full capacity for the next few months.

items.statement: Compressor division at 50-60% utilization in Q3, targeting 60%+ post-April with 60-70% capacity booked for calendar year
items.quote: For this quarter, we are looking at a 50% to 60% capacity utilization. And post-April, we are looking at a 60% plus capacity utilization.

items.statement: AC share to decline to 60-65% of revenue in FY27 from current ~60-64%, other products to contribute 30-35%
items.quote: We believe AC in the overall revenue will go down, will be about 60% to 65%. And 30%, 35% will come from the other products.

items.statement: Most customers on conversion pricing model passing through metal costs; quarterly pricing for others corrects within a quarter
items.quote: So maximum customers, we are on a conversion pricing model. So there, the cost is transferred and the impact to us is minimal.

items.statement: Demand improved QoQ; Q4 and Q1 FY27 expected to continue strong, dependent on summer season
items.quote: Yes, quarter-on-quarter, of course, numbers are also depicting it. So the demand has gone up. And fourth quarter and Q1 next year, I see, I mean, I see the demand to continue.

items.statement: Compressor capacity expansion to 7.5-7.8 million units contingent on government QCO decision in March
items.quote: Based on that, we will decide on a quick ramp up to add another five-odd million capacity. So we want to scale up to 7.5 million if the direction from the government is in line with whatever we expect.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected below Rs.500 crores, lower than FY26.
items.quote: So, next year CAPEX is probably, below Rs.500 crores would be our estimate.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guidance of 5-7% annually, not double digits.
items.quote: I think 5 % - 7% is a reasonable number to project out if you are thinking about building a model. I would not go more aggressive than that , definitely, not double digits, I would keep it to single digits.

items.statement: Noida EBITDA loss may have peaked; no breakeven timeline guided.
items.quote: I hope so that we have seen the peak of the losses.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions can add 496 beds with minimal incremental capex.
items.quote: We continue to have meaningful headroom for growth within our existing network, with the potential to add 496 beds through Brownfield expansions, including 193 beds at Lucknow, 81 beds at Patna and 222 beds at Noida. These additions are expected to drive near to medium -term growth with minimal incremental capex.

items.statement: Mature hospital margins expected to stabilize in 22-25% range, no structural change.
items.quote: This number is a fairly balance d range, 22%, 23%, 24%, 25% this number is a very balanced range.

items.statement: Aiming for a couple hundred basis points of efficiency from the system.
items.quote: So, there will be some up and down across cost items, but overall, I think that we will be looking at trying to see whether we can get a couple of hundred basis points of efficiency out of the system as well.

items.statement: CGHS rate revision gave Rs.7-10 crores benefit in nine months; full impact not yet played out.
items.quote: That is right. I think it is somewhere in the range of Rs.7 to 10 crores of impact in nine months.

items.statement: Insurance contracts renewed after 2-3 years, positive tariff benefit expected.
items.quote: So, I think, probably when we come to maybe June or September of next year, you will see more of a realistic picture of a full year of pricing impact across GGHS, our increases and insurance negotiations.

items.statement: Noida ramp-up in line with expectations; strong positive momentum expected.
items.quote: I do not know when that breakeven will happen. But, we are not worried that it is all slipping south or something like that. It is very much as per our expectations on how the ramp up of these units will do.

items.statement: War for clinical talent expected to persist for years, impacting costs.
items.quote: But I do believe that given the talent is scarce, this is something that the industry and the country will face for some years to come. I do not think this is something that is going to get solved in the next quarter.

items.statement: Increasing cancer/daycare and robotics work to support ARPOB growth.
items.quote: So, I think that these things are actually in favor of ARPOB growth because ARPOB is a derived metric.

items.statement: Net cash position of about Rs.600 crores as of December.
items.quote: We have a loan of about Rs.600 crores and a cash position of over Rs.1200 crores, so, net cash is about Rs.600 crores.

items.statement: Noida bed addition will continue without waiting for cost breakeven.
items.quote: So, we would not stop the build out is the answer to the question.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin for 9M FY26 at 24.9%, closer to lower end of guidance
items.quote: Accordingly, the adjusted EBITDA margin for 9 months '26 is 24.9%, which is closer to the lower end of our EBITDA guidance.

items.statement: R&D expense for Q3 FY26 at 2.9% of sales, within full year guidance range of 2.5%-3%
items.quote: The R&D expense for Q3 '26 remains within the range of 2.5% to 3% of our guidance for the full year FY26.

items.statement: Gross margin increased 170 bps YoY to 72.6% in Q3 FY26 due to price increases, mix and inventory accrual release
items.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter has increased by 170 basis point year-on-year basis to 72.6% from 70.9% in Q3 '25.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined 170 bps YoY to 25.9% in Q3 FY26 due to higher R&D and employee costs
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA margin for the quarter is 25.9% as compared to 27.6% in Q3 '25. This decline of 170 basis points is largely attributable to increase in R&D cost by 70 basis points, and the balance is due to higher employee costs.

items.statement: Domestic pharma revenue grew 11.1% YoY in Q3 FY26 with 9.1% organic growth excluding OTC
items.quote: In quarter 3 financial year '26, our domestic revenue grew 11.1% year -on-year to INR3,046 crores, supported by strong organic growth of 9.1%, excluding OTC.

items.statement: Chronic therapies outperformed IPM: cardio 1.2x, antidiabetic ex-GLP1 2.2x; chronic contribution up 200 bps to 36.7% in 9M FY26
items.quote: In 9 months financial year '26, our chronic contribution increased by 200 bps year -on-year to 36.7% versus 34.7% last year, primary led by continued outperformance of 1.2x vs IPM ex GLP-1. We outperformed IPM by 1.2x in cardio and 2.2x in antidiabetic ex GLP-1.

items.statement: In-licensed/specialty portfolio less than 2% of overall sales mix
items.quote: Tushar, as of now, the portion of specialty portfolio or the in-licensed portfolio, in particular, is quite negligible. It is less than 2% or so in the overall sales mix.

items.statement: GLP-1 launch on track for day-1 participation around March-end
items.quote: So it's a currently innovator market, and we are on track for a day 1 launch. It would be around March, somewhere around March end. So we are on track, and we expect to be a participant in the launch in day 1.

items.statement: OTC revenue grew 5.2% YoY in Q3 FY26; expect double-digit growth next year after stockist rationalization and channel shift
items.quote: We hope that going forward next year, good double-digit growth would be there.

items.statement: Finance cost decreased to INR157 crores in Q3 FY26 from INR170 crores in Q2 FY26 due to CP repayment of INR1,500 crores
items.quote: The finance cost for Q3 FY'26 has decreased to INR157 crores from INR170 crores in Q2 FY'26. This reduction is primarily driven by repayment of last tranche of commercial papers worth INR1,500 crores in October 2025.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR4,294 crores; net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.3x from 1.4x QoQ
items.quote: In line with our prudent financial strategy, we continue to strengthen our balance sheet and have reduced our net debt to INR4,294 crores as of 31st December 2025, resulting in the net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 1.3x in Q3 '26 on a trailing 12 months basis, which has improved as compared to net debt to adjusted E

items.statement: Management expects unit volumes to be flattish in FY27 with revenue growth driven by price increases of 20-30% on laptops/desktops and higher on components.
items.quote: demand unit-wise, in my view, would be flattish. It may not degrow because India digitization, PC penetration is still very, very low. And the higher selling price will help us to get the revenue.

items.statement: Laptop and desktop prices have risen ~20% already with similar hikes expected over next 2 months; component prices (RAM, SSD) up 50-100% or 2-3x.
items.quote: Currently, about 20% price hike has already happened. And next 2 months, similar trend will continue on the hike on the overall product cycle, I mean, from laptop and desktop perspective. Whereas on other components the price hike is already 50%, 100% or even 2x already.

items.statement: Q3 saw channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes; from January, tertiary/consumer demand picked up as buyers preponed purchases to avoid further increases.
items.quote: Q3, you are right, it was more inventory piling up at the channel level. But however, now the price increase implementation has already happened. And now virtually every consumer -- potential consumer and corporate knows of this impending price hike. So if they were to buy in March to -- before the year-end, they are n

items.statement: Q3 consolidated PAT margin was 1.85%; management expects similar margin trend to continue with no major variation.
items.quote: Currently, business market size trend, average selling price, all 3 are in the similar mode. So our expectation is that it will be the similar trend only. We are not seeing any major variation.

items.statement: PES (branded PCs) share rose to 56% of revenue in Q3 FY26 from 51% a year ago; LIT (components/essentials) at 44%.
items.quote: However, in the current Q3 of 2025, the PES business has gone up and now it is at 56%. So there is a 5 percentage basis point increase in the PES business in terms of ratio.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue growth of 5% achieved without any large project orders vs INR 2,000 cr of project revenue in 9M FY25; pipeline is decent but execution slowed by supply/price volatility.
items.quote: on a 9 months to 9-month basis, our revenue growth is 5%, but all this growth, even bigger 5% growth is without any project order. So last year, we had almost INR 2,000 crores of project order vis-a-vis this year, it is nil.

items.statement: Added 55th branch in Solapur; network now spans 55 towns with 700+ locations and 10,000+ distribution partners.
items.quote: In addition, we also launched a new branch in Solapur, which is now our 55th branch in India, an unprecedented network of branches, service center and warehouses spread across 55 towns of India.

items.statement: Micron's Crucial consumer brand EOL will dent revenue next fiscal year; Micron enterprise supply continues.
items.quote: next financial year, crucial definitely will be a dent, but we will continue to do Micron business, which is more enterprise class.

items.statement: Base business (ex-large deals) grew ~24% in 9M FY26 vs prior 15-20% guidance; management expects similar trend to continue in Q4.
items.quote: our guidance was always 15% to 20%, but because of the price increase shortage and hence, because of a little bit extra stocking, this business has done a little bit more than what we had anticipated, and it should continue in the coming quarter as well.

items.statement: Potential risk of excess inventory and lengthened debtor days if affordability worsens; management monitors daily.
items.quote: There is a potential risk of having excess inventory or there is a potential challenge of lengthened debtors. But all our eyes are on it. Our ecosystem, we are monitoring on a daily basis.

items.statement: Domestic PC market shipments grew >10% YoY in Q3; India outperforming global recovery driven by enterprise refresh, Windows 10 EOS, AI device adoption.
items.quote: The domestic PC market delivered one of its strongest quarter ever in this quarter with shipments growing upwards of 10% year-over-year.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary set up for SAARC execution (material pickup from Dubai/Hong Kong); business expansion to follow once operations established.
items.quote: at this moment, it is more for execution purpose. Once we set up the operations and start expanding, then we'll look at the business angle.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target revised upward from INR1,710-1,720 crore to ~INR1,900 crore (~30% growth)
items.quote: Instead of INR1,710 crores, INR1,720 crores, I think we will touch probably INR1,900 crores this year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue projected at ~INR2,100 crore, exceeding prior 20% growth target on FY26 base
items.quote: We are building up enough capacity that we should cross that figure next year from INR1,900 crores to go up, maybe we'll cross INR2,100 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected around INR1,900 crores, surpassing earlier INR1,700 crore target
items.quote: we would be easily surpassing that and most likely if we maintain the current quarter momentum, it would be around INR1,900 crores for this year

items.statement: Order book at INR1,685 crores as of Q3 FY26, Q3 inflow ~INR570-575 crores, 9M inflow ~INR1,600 crores
items.quote: SoT think our turnover is INR523 crores plus we've added INRS0 crores. So you can say about INRS73-575 crores in the quarter

items.statement: Pipeline 1 at ~INR1,200 crores (6x monthly avg), Pipeline 2 at ~INR1,000 crores (6-7x monthly avg), hit rate 21-22%
items.quote: our pipeline, which is about 6x of our monthly average order booking. That is our pipeline 1 that we call. And our pipeline 2, which is a little longish kind of gestation period is about another 6x to 7 of our average monthly order book

items.statement: Data centers and multi-story commercial/institutional buildings now ~15% of pipeline; heavy structure capacity doubling to 45,000 tons
items.quote: our pipeline do consist at least 15% of the data center and the multistory steel buildings in that space currently

items.statement: Cautious on order book growth to avoid overbooking beyond delivery capacity; reputation risk if delivery fails
items.quote: We can't take everything. But yes, I think it should be a little better than what it is. Gradually, we'll keep improving it, increasing the order book based on our capacity

items.statement: Zero debt, cash ~INR200+ crores; no bill discounting, clean collections; net working capital ~34 days
items.quote: It's INR200 crores plus and no borrowings. We have no debt

items.statement: Total addressable market estimated at 100x current size; PEB capacity to reach 240,000 tons by Q2 FY27, 280,000+ tons with sixth plant
items.quote: the total addressable market is maybe 100x of what the market size is today right now. So there is enormous, enormous market

items.statement: Management targets 28% revenue growth for FY26 and maintains 20-25% growth guidance for FY27 and beyond.
items.quote: So, to be specific, I think this year we are targeting to grow around 28%. And next year onwards, again, we are still targeting to grow 20% to 25%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to sustain between 17% and 19% in coming quarters and year-end.
items.quote: Yes, it will be. Margins will be stable around 17% to 19% in the coming quarters also year-end.

items.statement: Phase 2 of Chennai plant expansion to commence in Q1 FY27 with estimated investment of Rs 9-10 crore.
items.quote: At Chennai, to complete the phase two, we will be incurring approximately Rs. 9 crores or Rs. 10 crores approximately, which we already planned in our IPO.

items.statement: 1.8 MW solar power plant under open access model for captive consumption with total capex of Rs 6.2 crore, expected completion within six months.
items.quote: The total CAPEX for the project is estimated at approximately Rs. 6.2 crore including one-time statutory approval.

items.statement: Current order book stands at approximately Rs 85 crore, expected to grow at 20-25% annually.
items.quote: Normally, we have order book of around Rs. 85 crores as of now. And normally, we see this order book to keep on growing at a growth rate what we are projecting for next year, for example, 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin expanded to 13.12% YoY (+387 bps) driven by exchange gains and lower personnel cost; 9M margin at 16.07% (-110 bps).
items.quote: EBITDA margins responded to 13.12% improving by 387 basis points supported by favorable exchange gains on imports aided by reduction in personal costs as a percentage of sales.

items.statement: SFS segment grew 149% YoY in Q3 driven by wallet share gains, new products from existing customers, and new customer additions.
items.quote: For the nine month segment revenue grew 108% year-on-year while the 3rd Quarter revenue increased 149% year-on-year reflecting sustained demand momentum and improving capacity utilization.

items.statement: No demand slowdown in automotive; absolute growth continues but share declining due to faster growth in renewable and industrial segments.
items.quote: Automotive as an absolute value, the business is growing. But I think because of much higher growth, which is coming in industrial and renewable, because of India and Europe, the percentage share of automotive or mobility is reducing in our business.

items.statement: US Section 232 tariffs (50%) on springs and fasteners remain unchanged; no relief from recent reciprocal tariff reductions.
items.quote: But the point is the products what Gala is manufacturing are springs and fasteners, which fall under section 232 of the US trade law. And in this section, there is no relief given as of now. So, currently, these products which fall under section 232, if they are imported in US, our customers to pay actually 50% tariff.

items.statement: SAP HANA migration planned with implementation starting Q1 FY27, go-live targeted Q3 FY27; 5-year subscription fees of Rs 3.48 crore.
items.quote: We have finalized five year license agreement with SAP India and plan to commence implementation by Q1 of FY'27. With the target to go live in Q3 of FY'27, we have committed a five year subscription agreement with a total fees of Rs. 3.48 crore.

items.statement: Solar project expected to reduce power costs by 15-20% annually and support carbon neutrality goals.
items.quote: Well, the overall benefits in the power cost will be reduction on an annual basis, it will be 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Seat retractor springs (circlip tractor springs) completed testing and validation; pilot lots expected this quarter with ramp-up in Q1/Q2 FY27.
items.quote: And now we are expecting pilot loaders from customer in this quarter. And slowly we may start ramp up month on month in Quarter 1, Quarter 2 after supplying this pilot lot, which is expected to be supplied in this quarter end or early next quarter.

items.statement: Chennai facility generated Rs 11 crore revenue in Q3; price agreements signed with 4 leading wind turbine OEMs for new bolt products.
items.quote: The plant generated approximately Rs. 11 crore of revenue in the 3rd Quarter making steady progress in building scale at the new facility. During the period, we concluded a price agreement with four leading wind turbines OEMs for new bolt products to be manufactured at our Chennai facility.

items.statement: Inventory days on reducing trend but will take a couple of quarters to stabilize after Chennai ramp-up.
items.quote: Now, it is on the reducing trend, but it will take another couple of quarters to actually stabilize.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow growth target of 10%-14% on Rs 1 lakh crore addressable market; revenue growth target 20%-25% for next couple of years
items.quote: Next year again, I said, 12 months we have a good Rs. 1 lakh crores of, tendering opportunity, which we will look at a 10% to 12%, maybe even 13%, 14% order intake. And our growth, as we had already planned, we are looking at 20%-25% growth going forward in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book Rs 14,733 cr; effective order book including L1 Rs 18,216 cr; 57% domestic, 43% international; 90% T&D
items.quote: As of December 31st, our unexecuted order book stood at Rs. 14,733 crores, and including L1 our effective order book stands at Rs. 18,216 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at 11.5%-12% despite Rs 17 cr one-time labor code provision
items.quote: Rs. 17 crores have been provided, and we still don't change our EBITDA profile. I think this is something which is part of the change which happens in a normal course of business and we are comfortable to maintain our EBITDA profile of 11.5% to 12%.

items.statement: Q4 execution risk from ROW/forest clearance delays in domestic and international projects; conservative guidance accounts for this
items.quote: We have some ROW issues, some forest issues in projects in domestic and some issues on ROW in international. So, we are giving you a conservative guidance.

items.statement: Debt increase marginal; CAPEX funded by internal accruals and IPO proceeds; long-term borrowing ~Rs 90 cr, short-term ~Rs 750 cr
items.quote: As we are going to incur the CAPEX, some part of the borrowings will increase. But it is not going to be very substantial because the CAPEX was funded by internal accruals and money received from the IPO as well.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 83 days (9M FY26) from 91 days (FY25); focus on net working capital control
items.quote: Our working capital days improved to 83 days compared to 84 days in H1, FY '26 and 91 days in FY '25, reflecting better working capital management.

items.statement: Middle East (Abu Dhabi, Oman, Jordan) bid pipeline Rs 10,000-15,000 cr; targeting T&D margins similar to Africa
items.quote: Middle East, we are not in Saudi. So, we are in 3-4 countries there. Principally, we are in Abu Dhabi, Oman, Jordan. And we feel that this potential will be Rs. 10,000 crores to Rs. 15,000 crores, which we will try and bid.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth revised to mid-teens (15-16%) from earlier 20%+; EBITDA and PAT growth guidance maintained at 20%+
items.quote: In terms of revenue growth, it will be in the mid-teens around 15% to 16% is what we will be anticipating to end the year with. But our margin guidance of 20% plus on EBITDA and PAT remains intact

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 41.5% in 9M FY26 driven by backward integration eliminating China sourcing; full impact baked in
items.quote: What had happened over the course of this financial year is, we have completely discontinued China supplies because now we manufacture the intermediate in-house by procuring the raw materials, so we are completely backward integrated, and hence that shift is seen in the material margin improvement

items.statement: Destocking by customers largely complete; seeing recovery in RFQs and biotech funding environment improving
items.quote: We are seeing an improvement in environment. A lot many requests for RFQs have come in the last one quarter. Suddenly, it wasn't looking so healthy for a while now, but it is turning around

items.statement: Four new product approvals in FY26 with peak market potential ~$10B; ramp-up expected over 2-3 years as Big Pharma acquisitions may accelerate volumes
items.quote: Roughly, peak market sales roughly is about $10 billion. I haven't checked any changes on the analyst estimates for these four end molecules in this course of the last 2-3 months

items.statement: Peptide facility (16 KL) at Neo Anthem commissioned; total investment ~Rs 200 crore including utilities; supports 8-9 innovator programs and GLP-1 generic supply
items.quote: We currently work with innovator peptides, close to about 8-9 programs are there on innovator peptides, which are under development. From lab scale, now we have expanded into a full-blown 16 kiloliters commercial scale manufacturing facility at Neo Anthem

items.statement: Pipeline remains robust with 130-140 early-stage molecules; 5-6 Phase 2 programs expected to move to Phase 3 in 18-30 months; 6 Phase 3 molecules unchanged
items.quote: With respect to early phase molecules, we still have similar numbers, about 130 to 140 numbers, which are there on the pipeline side. I think on the Phase 2 programs, it will be about 5 or 6 of them, which would be in the Phase 2 side

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (US-India trade) caused customer destocking and inventory reduction; easing trade relations now providing tailwinds
items.quote: There has been some definitely because of the general geopolitical tension that we have seen in the last one year where we have been in loggerheads with a major trading partner, United States. It has put a lot of anxiety in the mind of big pharma

items.statement: FY27/FY28 outlook positive; expects CAGR similar to last 5 years but no specific near-term guidance; visibility improves as year progresses
items.quote: If you're saying in the next five years, will we have a CAGR of what we have had in the last five years? I expect so. But will it be immediately next year? I can't say till I am a little bit into that year

items.statement: Reiterates FY26 guidance of around 18% gross sales growth and 20-22% PAT growth YoY.
items.quote: We reiterate to all of you our FY'26 guidance of around 18% gross sales growth and 20 %-22% PAT growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Confident of achieving around 20% gross sales and 20-22% PAT growth for FY26.
items.quote: We still are confident of achieving our stated goals of around 20% on gross sales and 20% to 22% on a PAT growth on a year -on-year basis for FY '26 as compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Expects Q4 PAT of Rs 43-45 crores, implying 20% YoY growth.
items.quote: we are looking at anywhere around Rs. 43 crores to Rs. 45 crores of PAT for this period.

items.statement: Current qualified pipeline stands at Rs 4,500 crores, up from Rs 2,500 crores last quarter.
items.quote: We are currently sitting on a strong pipeline of Rs 4,500 crores, which we believe will be closed in near future.

items.statement: Cybersecurity accounts for Rs 1,800-2,000 crores of the Rs 4,500 crores pipeline.
items.quote: out of the Rs. 4,500 crores, we have close to around Rs. 1,800 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores of it would be cybersecurity for us, the funnel which is there.

items.statement: Renewal business EBITDA margins are at least 1-1.5 percentage points higher than normal business.
items.quote: our EBITDA margins will be significantly higher for our renewal business. It will be higher by at least 1 to 1.5 percentage points as compared to our normal business.

items.statement: Targets 15 basis points of operating leverage every year.
items.quote: if we are able to achieve 15 basis points of operating leverage every year, that would be the right number for us.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY26 to contribute close to 60% of full-year PAT.
items.quote: H2 will contribute north of 60% or close to 60% of our PAT for the full year.

items.statement: ALM segment likely to bounce back to 70-75% of budget in Q4 after underperformance.
items.quote: in Q4 we are likely to bounce back at close to about 70%-75% of our budget.

items.statement: Win rate traditionally around 30-35% on pipeline.
items.quote: traditionally the win rate has been around 30 %-35%, if you see it.

items.statement: Working capital days stable at 51 days.
items.quote: We are at around 51 days as of 31st December, 2025.

items.statement: No forward guidance for FY27; opportunities look bright.
items.quote: As an organization, we don't give a forward -looking guidance for such a long period.

items.statement: 4 GW module capacity to be commissioned by end FY26, commercial production from Q1 FY27 with 3-4 month ramp-up.
items.quote: Our greenfield integrated project in Odisha remains on track with 4 GW of module capacity scheduled for commissioning by the end of FY26 and 4.8GW of cell capacity scheduled for FY27.

items.statement: 4.8 GW cell capacity commercial production expected around October 2026 (H2 FY27).
items.quote: Cell installation, machines will also start around the same time. But cell takes little more time to stabilize and ramp up the efficiencies. So we expect the commercial production from the second half of next financial year. So assuming around October is the timeline which we are planning for commercial production of o

items.statement: Capex for cell plus module project is INR1,850 crores, with cell portion INR1,350 crores.
items.quote: So the capex for cell plus module is about INR1,850 crores. And for cell part is INR1, 500 crores. Sorry INR1,350 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at over 5 GW, translating to about INR6,500 crores.
items.quote: So if you see our order book, we have executed close to a gigawatt in this quarter, but we have also added new orders, and today our order book is over 5 GW, which translates to about INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: 13% EBITDA margin is realistic expectation for the year; Q4 should show positive impact from commodity price pass-through.
items.quote: So Prakhar, if you see, even in our guidance we have said that 13% EBITDA is a realistic expectations for the year. However, if you see for the year we are at 16%.

items.statement: Target to increase non-module business (EPC, pumps, inverters) to 15% of revenue in next couple of years.
items.quote: So our solar module versus the rest of the business this year expected to be 95 % and 5%. But as we are expanding into EPC business, pump, inverter, this year the target for going forward is to make it to 15%, which we are trying to achieve in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Module prices dipped in Q3 but returned to original levels; silver now ~25% of module price vs 15-16% earlier.
items.quote: As I said the prices fluctuates up and down due to all these factors and since there has been lot of fluctuation in the silver prices, silver prices used to be about 15%-16% of the module prices, today it is close to 25%.

items.statement: India solar installations expected to exceed 50-55 GW this year, driving demand; no overcapacity seen.
items.quote: If you see this year also last year about 32 GW to 34 GW installation happened. This year itself the pace which is going on I think India should be over 50- 55 GW already.

items.statement: US trade policy details still awaited; 18% duty from 50% seen as positive, pursuing US market for cells and modules.
items.quote: So we are still evaluating the policy, trade policy, but it is a very welcome and a positive step. 18% from 50% is definitely good for us.

items.statement: Net debt at INR749 crores including term debt and working capital; interest cost spike temporary, to normalize by March.
items.quote: Today is INR749 crores to be precise.

items.statement: DCR sales currently 3-4% of monthly sales; value unlocking from cell manufacturing and DCR expected next year.

items.statement: Plans to reduce Stage 2 by 2-2.5% annually, aiming below 2% in 1-2 years.

items.quote: Most probably in couple of weeks’ time we will roll out NCD of about another Rs.100 Crores to Rs.125 Crores

items.statement: Karnataka disbursements impacted by e-Khata issue, expected to resolve by March.
items.quote: I think by March, the e-Khata issue should get sorted out.

items.statement: DSA sourcing share increased to 50% from 35% last year.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of 20% this quarter, total 45% for FY26 vs 40% last year.
items.quote: our Board has declared interim dividend of 20% again. Totally this current financial year so far, we declared dividend of totally 45% as against 40% in the last financial year.

items.statement: Has Rs.1000 Cr unutilized sanctions from banks, sufficient for 6-7 months.
items.quote: Off the balance sheet we are having close to about Rs.1000 Crores unutilized sanctions from at least 6 or 7 banks , which will fuel my growth and funding requirement for at least another six or seven months

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: TCNS to add 50-60 stores next year; expansion agenda starts Q4 this year.
items.quote: I expect that we'll add between 50 to 60 stores next year in TCNS, something that we had held back so far.

items.value: mid- to high single-digit LTL, double-digit overall
items.quote: So we are looking for mid- to high single-digit growth in Pantaloons for LTL and double-digit growth at an overall level, yes.

items.statement: Pantaloons to add about 20 stores in FY27, with larger store sizes.
items.quote: I think about 20 stores is what we would say we need to build in because Gaurav, as Sangeeta had explained, a lot of our premiumization strategy was building around aspirational and experience premiumization, not necessarily significant shift in pricing.

items.statement: OWND! to open 40-50 stores next year; may scale beyond 50 once model is right.

items.statement: ABFRL ex-TMRW to start making pre-Ind AS profit from next full year, growing thereafter.

items.statement: TMRW expected to breakeven by FY29.
items.quote: We expect TMRW, as we have mentioned in our various sort of presentations, including investor presentation, to be somewhere between FY '29 is when TMRW should breakeven.

items.quote: But on an annualized basis, our breakeven will probably be next year. So as Tasva scales a little bit, Tasva intrinsic margins are very good.

items.statement: Capex across business for 9 months was about INR300 crores including security deposits.
items.quote: Capex across business for 9 months is roughly INR300 crores, including security deposits.

items.statement: Ethnic business margin expanded 350 bps YoY to 22.7% in Q3, eighth consecutive quarter of expansion.

items.statement: ABFRL excluding TMRW margin at 20% in Q3, up 70 bps YoY.
items.quote: If we see ABFRL, excluding TMRW, overall margin stood at 20% in this quarter, up 70 basis points versus last year.

items.statement: Pantaloons average selling price increased 2-3% due to premiumization shift.
items.quote: But in terms of our average selling price, we've seen about a 2% to 3% increase because of the shift and because of our premiumization.

items.quote: Looking back at the quarter, the overall demand environment remained mixed with consumption largely centered around festive and wedding-related shopping.

items.statement: TCNS leadership transition: Anant transitioning out, Sooraj taking over with 3-4 month handover.
items.quote: And as Anant transitions out of it, first of all, he's spending next 3, 4 months with our next leader who is Sooraj, who has been in this ethnic business for the last 2, 3 years, was responsible for growing and building Tasva business, looking after Jaipur.

items.statement: Leverage to settle at 4x-4.5x long-term, expected around 2030.
items.quote: As our cost of funds reduce, as the ratings probably improve, the leverage, which is about 2.2x, should settle in the range of 4x to 4.5x. That is the go-to long-term for the company, which I believe we should be hitting sometime around 2030.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio of 30-40% over longer term, starting in about a year.
items.quote: Conservatively, we believe that we should be in the 30% to 40% sort of dividend payout ratio over a longer-term, basis all the calculations of RoA and capital that we have simulated.

items.statement: Annualized credit cost of 100 bps for core mortgage product.
items.quote: So as far as our core mortgage product is concerned, we are fairly optimistic of running it at about 100 basis points of annualized credit cost.

items.statement: Cost of funds to drop by 270 bps by end of March 2027.
items.quote: On an overall stock basis, we would expect that in about 9 months to 12 months, the cost of funds should go down by about 270 basis points.

items.statement: Borrowing cost to fall below 8% after investment comes through.
items.quote: Right now, we are borrowing at, give or take 9%. And we expect, as I said, a movement down to below 8% quickly right after this investment is to come through.

items.statement: Net recoveries of about INR4,500 crores over next 3 years from legacy book.
items.quote: On a net basis, over the next 3 years, once we are done with all of these provisions and the legacy book has run down, we should be able to cash recover about INR4,500 crores.

items.statement: Quarterly recoveries of INR400-500 crores from legacy book.
items.quote: So we do recover about INR400 crores to INR500 crores per quarter.

items.statement: Co-lending volumes to return to original levels by May or June 2026.
items.quote: We have done it with a few banks where we are already technically integrated and business volumes have started in the month of Jan itself, and they will pick up month-on-month to come back to original levels by about May or June of this year.

items.statement: Expect 15-18% opex cost saving from co-lending technology integration.
items.quote: And once all of the tech kicks in, we expect on an operating basis, something like a 15% to 18% cost saving in the business that we do on an opex basis.

items.statement: PIL matter sub judice; no financial loss expected to company.
items.quote: No financial loss, this is again very, very important, is possible as an outcome of this PIL to the company, which is Sammaan Capital, given the regulatory closures, loan repayments, and the fact that the company has already earned over INR3,000 crores of interest and has no principal exposure outstanding to any of the

items.quote: as of now, I feel it should be close to 7,500 site tenancies for this year

items.quote: we will not maintain ₹240 crores for this year, since the rollout is not done by both the major operator.

items.statement: EBITDA margin sustainable at 68-70%, PAT margin at 30-32%.
items.quote: it will still sustain the 68%, 70% of EBITDA margin with close to 30%, 32% of PAT margin.

items.statement: Revenue per tower expected to reach ₹32,000-33,000 in next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: I'm very confident it will reach to level of ₹32,000, ₹33,000, which I've been declaring from past quarter in coming one or two quarters itself

items.statement: Plans to add 8,000 towers for 10,000 tenancies in FY27, reaching 13,500-14,000 towers.
items.quote: We will add another 8,000 towers for 10,000 tenancies.

items.statement: No immediate fundraise; may consider in FY27 after Q1 based on rollout.
items.quote: as of now, no immediate plans for fundraise. But yes, once we have a successful Q1, then we can take a call on fundraise.

items.statement: Vodafone plans 13,000-15,000 sites in Q1 FY27; Suyog is preferred partner.
items.quote: They are planning around 13,000 to 15,000 sites in Q1 of next financial year.

items.statement: BSNL allocated ₹28,000 crores for 23,000 4G sites in FY27.
items.quote: India has allocated ₹28,000 crores for BSNL only for FY 2027.

items.statement: BSNL rollout may be delayed due to material availability from Tejas.
items.quote: BSNL I am not committing right now because still we have not got confirmation from which quarter they want to start the rollout.

items.statement: Data centre project worth ₹35 crores expected to complete by Q4 or mid Q1.
items.quote: it should get completed by Q4 or mid of Q1.

items.quote: Two years ago, we were doing almost 80%-85% in bulk and 10%-15% in consumer packs. Today, we are doing almost 50%-55% in consumer packs, and the rest is in bulk. Going forward, we are planning to do 70% in consumer packs and 30% in bulk.

items.statement: Strong order book: Q4 FY26 sold out; additional 4,500 MT capacity largely confirmed via quantity commitments from existing and new customers

items.quote: We are planning to initiate the additional 5,500 metric tons in phase 2 likely by mid/end of FY27.

items.quote: Yes, 11% revenue growth, that will lead to the revenue of around INR3,600 crores in the financial year '27. And with the EBITDA of around 20.5%, then EBITDA will be in the range of around INR730 crores, INR740 crores.

items.statement: Expects 3-4% sequential tonnage growth in Q4 FY26, with realizations maintained at current level.
items.quote: Fourth quarter, we are expecting a tonnage growth of around 3% to 4% on a sequential basis.

items.quote: So total capex we are expecting next year around INR350 crores.

items.quote: It is for the current calendar year ‘26 , calendar year of 2026, till December 2026, what we planned.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin around 20% in FY27, supported by fixed cost leverage and fuel cost savings.
items.quote: Yes, around 20% definitely.

items.statement: No further price hikes planned; realizations to be maintained at current level unless substantial cost changes occur.
items.quote: No, right now, no. And unless there will be substantial change in the cost structure.

items.quote: No, see around 1% or 2%, you can assume not beyond that.

items.quote: Our daily tonnage has crossed 10,900 -plus tons during the quarter, reflecting improving demand trends.

items.statement: Focus on adding 20-ton vehicles over larger 28-ton due to better payload efficiency; scrapping older larger vehicles.
items.quote: So considering these factors and considering the return load factor also, we are focusing to add lesser tonnage ve hicles the 28-toner vehicle have been wherever the major maintenance or something like that, then we are scrapping those vehicles.

items.statement: Employee cost rose to 18.1% of income due to annual increments; no further increments expected until March 2027.
items.quote: The employee cost as a percentage of total income increased from 16.6% in Q3 FY '25 to 18.1% in Q3 FY '26 on account of annual increment.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR5 per share.
items.quote: Considering this improvement in cash profits, the Board of Directors have approved an interim dividend of INR5 per share to reward to the shareholders.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR272 crores as of Dec 2025 from INR304 crores in Sep 2025.
items.quote: Net debt stood at around INR272 crores as of December ' 25, down from INR304 crores in September '25, reflecting healthy cash generation.

items.statement: No incremental liability from new Labour Code; salary structures already compliant.
items.quote: We are happy to say that there will not be any incremental liability on the company to comply this new Labour Code.

items.quote: Well, we have always said that double-digit growth in India is not impossible, and we would continue to stick to that. We see no reason why we should not achieve it this year.

items.statement: India margin guidance remains 22-23%, hopes to maintain close to current 26%.
items.quote: Realistically, if we can maintain margins anywhere close to the current levels, we would be very happy. But our guidance has always been 22% - 23%, has never been higher than that.

items.statement: Snacks business expected to grow to close to $100 million with high teens growth.
items.quote: We think this is going to go close to a $100 million business, and this is not an unforeseen number that can happen with two of these three territories.

items.statement: Expects better season with favorable weather, volume growth to cover upsizing impact.

items.statement: Capacity added 40-45% in last two years, 50% more available than used this year.
items.quote: Between the last 2 years, we have added close to 40% - 45% capacity. So that capacity is available with us.

items.statement: Cash to be used for Twizza acquisition, brewery setup, and potential dividend increase.

items.quote: What we expect and we are very much on target to achieve that, is that by the end of the financial year, this growth rate should be much higher than what it is reported for the first nine months, more or less in line with what we had stated in the previous calls.

items.statement: Bavla site revenue to reach about INR 250 crores by end of FY26.
items.quote: But yeah, it should be closer to about INR 250 crores by the by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: India business revenue target of INR 500 crores in next 12-18 months, then INR 800 crores in 3-5 years.
items.quote: So overall, our first target is to get to INR 500 crores of revenue, which should happen in the next 12 to 18 months is what our expectation is. And then the next target is to get to INR 800 crores of revenue coming out of India’s side.

items.statement: RFP's worth INR 1,200 crores submitted; expect 30-35% conversion into orders.
items.quote: And in terms of value, this would be close to about 1,200 crores worth of RFP’s that have been given out. We expect that at least 30%, 35% of this should get converted into orders, and that gives us the confidence.

items.quote: So, as you look into the future for this particular segment, and more specifically cholesterol and vitamin D analogs, we would keep on seeing the margin improvements, where our target is to first get to the 20% margin and then take it up to 25%.

items.quote: So, what we are expecting is that in the next financial year, we should be breakeven in that particular facility with both the manufacturing lines.

items.quote: Again, I can repeat that we are on track, and this should be finished in about one and a half years.

items.statement: Expect significant ramp up in India assets due to RFP conversions and new orders.
items.quote: So we do expect a significant ramp up as far as the India assets are concerned, because now that the capacity is already created, it is all about filling up these capacities with this new RFP.

items.quote: We actually expected the revenue to be higher by about INR 20 odd crores in this particular quarter. items.statement: FY27 revenue from French subsidiary expected around EUR 18 million.
items.quote: So that should be closer to about 18 million.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target 19.5-20%, with first nine months at 19.4%.
items.quote: So, we could be ending the year with anywhere between 19.5% to 20%.

items.statement: Target to reach 25-26% consolidated EBITDA margin within two years, then 30% by 2030.
items.quote: our target is to get as quickly as possible to the 25%, 26% consolidated margin that we were doing prior to March of 2020. So that's the first target to be achieved over the next two years and then get to the 30% EBITDA margin mark by the end of 2030.

items.statement: India site production capacity utilization to increase 2.5x in next three years.
items.quote: India should be able to easily make a 2.5x of what it is doing today as far as the production capacity utilization is concerned.

items.statement: Shanghai facility utilization to increase from 50% to around 75%.
items.quote: we do expect that the utilization should go up from the current 50% to around 75%.

items.statement: Development revenue from Swiss entity targeted to double in next five years.
items.quote: the target is that in the next five years, we should be able to double the development revenue from what it is right now

items.statement: Plan to pay down India debt of ~INR 750 crores to zero over three years using internal accruals.
items.quote: So India debt is today roughly about 750 crores. So ideally speaking, we would want to make the India debt zero.

items.statement: Net debt at CHF 150 million; may consider fundraise at right valuation but focus on operational cash flow.
items.quote: we are at close to about CHF 150 odd million of net debt.

items.statement: Fair visibility on revenues from Japanese customer for next three years; co-investment to ramp up supplies.
items.quote: We have a fair visibility on the revenues coming from this particular customer over the next -- at least for the next three years, and that is the reason why we are doing the co-investment along with the customer.

items.statement: ADC linker and payload constitute max 1.5% of final product price; company supplies ~60% of that.
items.quote: if you talk about the ADC, that would be close to about, say, maybe 1.5% at max of the final product price that the customer is realizing.

items.quote: the nature of our business is such that it is very difficult to have a linearity in the margins every quarter, because it all depends upon whether -- I mean, what is the composition of revenue that is driving the margins in that particular quarter.

items.quote: we see that with the customers that are very, very keen to ship their manufacturing from China to India.

items.statement: No major tariff impact on pharmaceuticals; fine chemicals may benefit from India-Europe FTA.
items.quote: On the fine chemical part, personally I see a big chance because there they are falling on the tariff regimes, but if we have now a free trades agreement between Europe and India, there's absolutely the chance that we can produce more in India and export it to Europe

items.quote: So we don't give -- we are not yet ready to give a guidance for the growth business. We will do it along with our decision on ibuprofen.

items.quote: We expect to have this -- the results of an analysis to be part of our Q4 results. That will give a clear direction to the company.

items.statement: Debt to be reduced to sub INR500 crores by May 2026 after final rights issue call money.

items.statement: OneSource product approval and launch expected in FY27.

items.statement: Growth API capacity utilization currently a little over 70%.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR146 crores (19%), including INR113 crores from rights issue and INR33 crores from operations.

items.statement: One-time INR6.7 crores impact from new labour code on gratuity and leave encashment.

items.statement: Developed markets contribute 75% of overall sales.

items.statement: Target to grow 15-20% ahead of market, at least 4-5% ahead.
items.quote: I think we mentioned earlier also, our target is to grow between 15% to 20% ahead of the market, at least 4% to 5% ahead of the market.

items.statement: Plan to invest ~INR 150 crores in land for greenfield facility near Pune.
items.quote: So we plan to invest close to about INR 150 crores in land, yes, of course, greenfield facility near Pune, in Pune.

items.statement: Next year capex could be INR 300-350 crores, moderating to INR 250-300 crores in outer years.

items.statement: 9M FY26 net new business wins with annual peak revenue potential of INR 20,636 million.

items.statement: India EBITDA and PBT strong at 11.9% and 7.6%, grew YoY and sequentially.

items.statement: India margin improvement sustainable with flexibility of 0.2-0.3% variation.

items.quote: Expansion at Mehru is also progressing well with equipment being commissioned in a phased manner. items.quote: By the way, domestic B2B delivered mid-teens growth. I think it is part of our commentary as well somewhere but we delivered mid-teens growth.

items.quote: At present, we are incurring a cost of about 2.5 to 3 crores per month which can again optimize over a period, as I said.

items.statement: Marketing spend to be 7-10% of topline on regular basis.
items.quote: Going forward, for the regular advertisement and other things, as usual, like other parks, about some 7% to 10% of our topline will be the marketing spend on a regular basis.

items.statement: Demand for Chennai Park is strong with good buzz.
items.quote: Demand is strong. It's a new park, and we have been able to create a lot of buzz. So, I think we are on a good track.

items.statement: Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar parks affected by heavy rains.
items.quote: Like this year, all the parks which are on the eastern side, Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar both got affected by a lot of rains.

items.statement: Company plans to announce 1-2 new parks in next 3 years, evaluating Vishakhapatnam and Goa.
items.quote: We will definitely sign minimum one, maybe two or three at more locations.

items.statement: Expect commercial vehicle segment growth to continue in Q4 FY26 and H1 FY27 driven by regulation changes, infrastructure upgrades, and trade growth
items.quote: We expect the commercial vehicles also to continue growth in the next Q4 as well as in the first half of next year.

items.statement: Lifetime order book of INR 2,000 crores for Q3 FY26 and INR 7,000 crores for 9M FY26 across product categories
items.quote: We have also registered a lifetime order book of INR 2,000 crores with multiple orders across product categories within the organization.

items.statement: Committed capex of INR 400 crores for FY26, INR 276 crores spent in 9M FY26, INR 100 crores planned for Q4 FY26
items.quote: From a capex perspective, during the year, we have committed to spend close to about INR 400-odd crores. We have already spent about INR 276 crores for the 9M ended FY26, and we plan to spend another INR 100 crores in the coming quarter as well.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 11.8% in Q3 FY26 (up 30 bps YoY), 11.6% for 9M FY26 (up 26 bps YoY); target 12.5%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 11.8% in Q3 FY26, registering a growth of 30 bps year-on-year.

items.statement: Flash Electronics EBITDA margin sustainable at 16-17%, Q3 FY26 at 18.4%
items.quote: So the margins are again going to be in the same level that we have shown in the last two or three quarters, which is somewhere about 16% to 17%.

items.statement: Switch business SOP Q2 FY28 with 2-year ramp-up; sunroof SOP Q1 FY27 with ramp-up over few quarters; lifetime orders typically 4-5 years
items.quote: So we expect one year from here and the production to start. And yes, the orders that you mentioned are lifetime. So they will take about two years to ramp up and then subsequently, it will move forward.

items.statement: Exports returning to normalcy in Q3 FY26 after 4-5 subdued quarters; Europe and US picking up across divisions
items.quote: But this quarter, we have seen coming back to normalcy where our exports to the Europe as well as to U.S. port are picking up, and it is across the divisions that we have.

items.statement: Commodity cost pass-through with quarterly true-up; indexed cost arrangements with vendors and customers; lag of one quarter
items.quote: There should be a lag of a quarter or so while we do the true-up with our vendor and pass those on to the OEM.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet supply issue resolved; developed magnetless and rare earth-free motors; benefiting from new budget magnet corridor
items.quote: That is behind us. The overall industry, I think, has figured out multiple ways, so have we. And plus now with the new budget and the overall magnet corridor that is being created, a lot of efforts have been done.

items.statement: R&D spend ~4% of revenue (opex + capex) consistently for Q3 and 9M FY26
items.quote: For by and large, as I mentioned, we spend about 4% of our revenue in R&D.

items.statement: 4-wheeler EV kit value potential INR 50,000-60,000 (components) up to INR 90,000-1,00,000 (6-in-1/7-in-1 system solutions)
items.quote: You can typically put somewhere about INR 50,000 to INR 60,000. However, if I club products and make it a system solution into 6-in-1 or 7-in-1, that could even go up to INR 90,000 or INR 1 lakh.

items.statement: ADAS focus on component-level entry (not system) for passenger vehicles; 2-wheeler ADAS system solutions already developed and under customer testing
items.quote: Our focus here across the ADAS as a product is to enter from the component side and not the system when it comes to the passenger vehicle or others.

items.statement: Launched residential wires in select markets within 6-7 weeks, targeting Rs36,000-37,000 crore market with right to win
items.quote: Crompton is launching a range of residential wires. This is a large and attractive market. There is clear adjacency with many of our products and we have a strong right to win in this market.

items.statement: Solar rooftop order book of Rs500 crore to be executed over 9-12 months; Rs18-19 crore revenue recognized in Q3
items.quote: The expectation, is that this order book will be executed over approximately the next 9 to 12 months. As I already said, this last quarter, we have already executed about Rs.19 crores of solar rooftop sales.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 10.3% in Q3 (+18.5% QoQ); Butterfly EBITDA margin up ~100bps YoY to 8.2%
items.quote: Consolidated revenue was Rs.1,898 crores. EBITDA grew 18.5% QoQ and EBITDA margin expanded to 10.3%.

items.statement: Milk prices expected to remain elevated near-term; further price hikes planned to offset inflation
items.quote: we foresee that in the near-term, the milk prices are going to remain at an elevated level. And we will take due precautionary action when it comes to passing on the pricing cost push

items.statement: Gowardhan Ghee price increased in February to offset milk inflation
items.quote: from February, we have increased our prices in branded Cow Ghee, which is Gowardhan Ghee to a certain extent to take care of the inflationary impact

items.statement: Gross margin maintained sequentially at 25.9% despite 6.5% QoQ milk price increase; down YoY from 27.2% due to 20% milk inflation
items.quote: while the milk prices inched up 6.5% sequentially, the company has been able to maintain a similar gross margin sequentially at 25.9% for Q3 FY 26 versus 25.8% for Q2 FY25

items.statement: EBITDA margin 7.6% in Q3 FY26 vs 9% YoY and 8.9% QoQ; 9M EBITDA 8.1% vs 8.7% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 FY 26 is 7.6% versus 9% last year and last quarter, it was 8.9%

items.statement: Core categories (ghee, cheese, paneer) grew 12% volume in Q3; new age business grew 123% YoY crossing INR100 cr quarterly revenue first time
items.quote: During Q3, these categories recorded a 12% volume growth. And together, they contribute to 64% of the total revenue

items.statement: New age business now 9% of revenue (up from 6% YoY); Avvatar Protein Wafer Bar contributes 8% of brand revenue and scaled nationwide
items.quote: On a year-to-date basis till December FY26, the new age business now contributes to 9% of our overall revenue, up from 6% in the same year last year

items.statement: Thorandale plant at Manchar commissioned; capex funded through internal accruals; no significant debt increase planned
items.quote: We have commissioned a new plant as well, Thorandale plant, which is at Manchar only. So there was a separate staffing for that

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from INR615 cr (Mar'25) to INR483 cr (Sep'25); net debt INR435 cr; NCD of INR150 cr taken in 2021 now INR81 cr outstanding
items.quote: as on 31st March 2025, our gross debt was around -- on a consolidated basis was around INR615 crores, which as on 30th September is INR483 crores

items.statement: Marketing spend at 3.5-4% of revenue; Avvatar whey protein prices raised to pass on milk cost inflation despite in-house production
items.quote: in marketing, we spend around 3.5% to 4%. Last year also was around 4%

items.statement: FTA risk minimal as dairy excluded from free trade agreements; global protein shortage supports pricing
items.quote: even FTA, the dairies are not included. So dairy is isolated from FTA. So there is no risk, I would say, that one

items.statement: Volume guidance for FY26 maintained at ~5.3 million tons including clinker; Q4 cement volume growth expected at 8-10% YoY
items.quote: Yes, I think about 5.3 million tons remains intact and it also has clinker.

items.statement: Depreciation to remain at Rs 30 crore per month (Rs 90 crore per quarter) in FY27 as Silchar plant commissioning offsets reduction
items.quote: Depreciation will remain the same. 30 crores per month, 90 crores per quarter. That will be more or less the same.

items.statement: Capex incurred in 9M FY26: Rs 431 crore; Q4 FY26 planned capex: Rs 150 crore; FY27 capex to be finalized
items.quote: So vitally we have till now incurred about 431 crores of CAPEX and in Quarter 4 we plan to incur about 150 crores of CAPEX.

items.statement: Total capex for 4 projects (Bihar 2mt grinding, Rajasthan 3mt clinker + 5mt grinding, Umrangso 3mt clinker + 2mt grinding) estimated at Rs 4,800 crore over 3-4 years
items.quote: So, the overall CAPEX for these four projects is about 4,800 crores.

items.statement: Rajasthan project (Nimbol 3mt clinker + 3mt grinding + Haryana 2mt grinding) estimated at Rs 2,400-2,500 crore with 10% deviation possible
items.quote: So, I think the cost that we have and that may change and I think the broad cost that we have taken out is about 2,400 to 2,500 for the clinker plant and the integrated grinding unit along with the grinding unit in Haryana.

items.statement: Silchar grinding unit (2mt) to be commissioned by end of February 2026; Jorhat grinding deferred to align with Umrangso clinker plant
items.quote: The timeline for Silchar is this month. I think by end of the month we will be commissioning a plant so between 20th to 27th is when we think of commissioning the plant and Jorhat would be, I think we have deferred Jorhat and we have preferred to put in Bihar rather than Jorhat.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA/ton at Rs 1,600 vs Rs 1,000 YoY; 9M FY26 at Rs 1,677 vs Rs 1,005 YoY; steady state EBITDA/ton for Star Cement overall expected at Rs 1,300-1,400
items.quote: On the per ton EBITDA front, it is 1,600 during this quarter as against 1,000 per ton same quarter last year.

items.statement: East region EBITDA/ton at Rs 600-700, could reach Rs 800 with price improvement; Rajasthan steady state EBITDA/ton modeled at >Rs 1,000 but lower initially due to ramp-up and branding costs
items.quote: I think the EBITDA per ton that we earn in East is about Rs. 600 to 700 and I think with some price betterment I think it can reach to about Rs. 800.

items.statement: Freight cost increase in Q3 due to one-off strike in Meghalaya (Oct) forcing rail transport; normal sequential increase Rs 60-70/ton; no material impact expected in Q4
items.quote: So, Harsh, because December quarter and March quarter is a natural cycle. There is a slight increase over the second quarter because second quarter is not an oxy gen period. So, there is hardly a Rs. 60 -70 per ton increase.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth expected similar to FY26; FY28 hard to predict; clinker sales of ~0.65 lakh tons/quarter expected to continue
items.quote: In the coming year I think the volume growth would be similar to the volume growth that we experienced in FY26 so I don't see FY27 to be very different to FY26

items.statement: Non-trade share increased to 22% in Q3 FY26 from 19% YoY; premium cement 17.1% of trade sales vs 12% YoY; OPC/PPC blend 18%/82%
items.quote: So, non -trade in Quarter 3, we had sold 22% of our overall volume. So, this has increased compared to last year's same quarter, which was 19%.

items.statement: No impact from Meghalaya illegal mining crackdown as coal sourced via Coal India FSA, spot and biomass; no Bangladesh exports from Silchar due to logistics and Rs 2,000/ton customs duty
items.quote: No, I don't think our coal supply is really linked to the Meghalaya coal illegal coal . So, I don't think there will be a big impact of that.

items.statement: Target net debt/EBITDA <1.5x; QIP to be done before reaching threshold; no immediate fundraising planned
items.quote: So, ideally we'd want to keep our debt to EBITDA ratio to be less than 1.5X EBITDA and so I think that is what we are targeting and then we will make sure that whenever we are reaching the threshold or before that we will do a QIP to fill in the gap.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences targets FY26 EBITDA breakeven and ~INR5bn revenue; FY27 revenue growth target ~15% with CDMO leading growth
items.quote: We had said we are targeting ourselves to be EBITDA breakeven this year. I think that guidance stays for us. I think we're pretty confident that we should be able to pull that off.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil FFB tonnage growth expected at 12-15% CAGR over long term driven by acreage expansion and farmer productivity programs
items.quote: I think the business is slated for FFB tonnage growth of I think a good healthy teens in terms of anywhere between 12% to 15%.

items.statement: New CPO processing plant in Khammam to go live in 2 months; downstream refinery for value-added products (cocoa butter substitute, CPKO refining) to commission in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our new CPO processing plant on the upstream in Khammam will go live in a matter of 2 months and our downstream refinery will also go get commissioned by somewhere in the first quarter of the coming year.

items.statement: Animal Feed underlying EBIT/ton improved to INR2,020 in Q3 FY26 from INR1,937 in Q3 FY25; cattle feed salience ~54% of volumes
items.quote: Underlying EBIT per metric ton improved to INR2,020 per metric ton in quarter 3 fiscal year '26 from INR1,937 per metric ton in quarter 3 fiscal year '25.

items.statement: Crop Protection domestic margins targeted at 28-30% range; in-licensing and in-house portfolio ~60-65% of revenue
items.quote: We are pretty confident of holding on to the range of 28%, 30%.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil Q3 pricing impact negative YoY as lower CPO prices offset higher PKO prices; PKO premium to CPO driven by coconut oil supply constraints
items.quote: Actually if I were to see in Q3 over Q3 last year, year-on-year, actually pricing overall in fact is a negative one, right? Because while the palm kernel oil prices were higher than last year, the CPO prices were lower than last year.

items.statement: Foods branded salience rose to 81% in Q3 FY26 from 77% YoY (Yummiez ~28%, RGC ~52%); strategy to become pure-play branded retail over 5 years
items.quote: The business continued to advance its strategic shift towards value-added offerings with branded salience rising to 81% in quarter 3 from 77% last year.

items.statement: Dairy margins under pressure (EBITDA INR11cr, 3% margin) due to 10%+ milk procurement cost inflation driven by global butter exports; structural cost improvements absorbing impact
items.quote: Profitability, however, remained under pressure with EBITDA declining to INR11 crores and margins softening to 3%, primarily due to higher milk procurement cost and a shortfall in revenue growth.

items.statement: Pet food plant ready for commissioning within a month
items.quote: The pet food business is that we have put up the plant for the pet food business of the group and that plant is ready to get commissioned in a matter of a month or so from now.

items.statement: Consolidated 9M FY26 revenue INR7,900cr (+9% YoY), PBT before exceptional items INR482cr (+17% YoY)
items.quote: For the 9 months ended 31st December 2025, the company reported consolidated revenues of INR7,900 crores, an increase of 9% year-on-year. Profit before tax, excluding non-recurring and exceptional items, for the period was INR482 crores marking a healthy 17% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Aims to touch INR 10,000 crore order book by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: we should be able to try and touch INR 10,000 crore by about Q1FY27.

items.statement: FY26 revenue to grow double-digit year-on-year.
items.quote: our overall FY26 is definitely on a double digit, aiming to have a double-digit growth in revenue vis-a-vis quarter – vis-a-vis FY25.

items.statement: FY27 to be a year of disruptive growth across all parameters.
items.quote: FY27 is going to be a year of disruptive growth.

items.statement: Maintains red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT margins on half-yearly or annual basis.
items.quote: our red line is 20% EBITDA margins. And we will try and definitely maintain that on an half yearly or an annual basis

items.statement: Export margins to settle around 13% on annual or half-yearly basis.
items.quote: this is the broad range where on an annual or a half yearly basis, the export margin would settle down.

items.statement: Export order book at INR 1,700 crore as of Dec 31; INR 1,900 crore including January order.
items.quote: This INR 1,700 is as of 31st December. This order of about INR 180 odd crores has come in Q4 in January.

items.statement: RITES Videsh order book at all-time high of INR 2,150 crore.
items.quote: we have an order book of INR 2,150 crores, which includes the INR1,700 crores of export.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue to be much higher than Q3, with export and turnkey execution picking up.
items.quote: quarter four, whether it is the export execution or the turnkey execution, quarter four, we are poised to be much higher than quarter three.

items.statement: Turnkey execution to grow double-digit sequentially in Q4 vs Q3.
items.quote: Q4 you will see definitely a double-digit, uptick vis-a-vis Q3, etc.

items.statement: Export revenue to step up by at least INR 120 crore in Q4 with four more locomotives shipped.
items.quote: at least a step up of another about INR 120 crores minimum export revenue should be there in quarter four.

items.statement: Consultancy plus export to contribute about 70% of revenue annually; leasing 5%; balance turnkey.
items.quote: on an annual basis, consultancy plus export would contribute about 70% odd, and the leasing in about 5% odd and the balance from about turnkey.

items.statement: Consultancy segment aims to touch 10% growth over next two to three years.
items.quote: we will aim to try and touch 10% odd in terms of growth in consultancy.

items.statement: High dividend payout policy to be maintained.
items.quote: our broad policy of giving a high dividend payout would definitely be maintained.

items.statement: No working capital constraint in export segment; orders covered by advances.
items.quote: There is hardly any working capital requirement. Most of it, we covered by advance.

items.statement: Confident of delivering FY26 organic growth guidance of 12-13% and expanded margins.
items.quote: we remain confident of delivering on our guidance of 12% to 13% organic growth rate and expanded margins for FY '26

items.statement: Expects to hit higher end of 12-13% organic growth bracket for FY26.
items.quote: the estimate for this year was 12% to 13%, and we would like to hit the higher end of the 12% to 13% bracket that we have been talking about it.

items.statement: Core Diagnostics expected to achieve high single-digit EBITDA margin in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The margin for Core Diagnostics is expected to meet the stated guidelines of high single-digit as an exit run rate for quarter 4 FY '26.

items.statement: Expects 70-100 bps organic margin improvement for FY26, continuing in coming quarter.
items.quote: at the beginning of the year, we have made an estimate of 70 to 100 bps improvement in the margins, and we stay put with that. You can see that coming in the coming quarter as well.

items.statement: Estimated FY26 capex of INR 55-60 crores for network, IT, and equipment.
items.quote: Estimated capex for the year is INR 55 crores to INR 60 crores.

items.statement: 9-month capex at group level close to INR 40 crores; full year likely INR 60 crores.
items.quote: The 9-month period is about close to INR 40 crores at a group level. And we think that for the full year basis, this could be something close to INR 60 crores.

items.statement: Aspires for 7-8% patient volume growth in near future.
items.quote: 7% to 8% volume growth has always been our aspirations in the near future, and we are working towards it

items.statement: Market conducive for price increase; will use price levers at appropriate time.
items.quote: We see the market is definitely may be able to absorb some price increase and the environment is conducive. But we are delaying it, deferring it for the reasons I've already mentioned.

items.statement: No material impact from US tariffs; reagents mostly EU/Japan-based, minimal exposure.
items.quote: we don't anticipate anything. But look, I mean, if the rupee runs away like crazy, there is obviously always a chance that vendors can come back and potentially talk about renegotiations.

items.statement: Board approved bonus issue in ratio 3:1, subject to approvals.
items.quote: the Board of Directors has approved the issue of bonus shares in the ratio of 3:1, that is 3 fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 2 each for every 1 existing equity share

items.statement: Labor Code impact: INR 9 crores one-time at group level; recurring INR 5-6 crores.
items.quote: On a recurring basis, I think the amount would be around INR 5 crores to INR 6 crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Company remains net debt-free with cash reserves of INR 127 crores.
items.quote: the company remains net debt-free with a current cash reserves of INR 127 crores.

items.statement: Order book is about INR 450 crore; no new orders last quarter, update next quarter.
items.quote: The order book is about INR 450 crore, and then there is some more business that we are acquiring at the moment.

items.statement: INR 450 crore order book to convert gradually over next two to three years.
items.quote: There will be some gradual ramp-ups. The INR 450 crore will come gradually over the next two to two and a half or three years.

items.statement: New project production start mostly towards end of the year.
items.quote: Mostly towards the end of the year.

items.statement: Long-term vision revised to INR 3,000-3,500 crore in next four to five years.
items.quote: The estimation should be about INR 3,000 crore to INR 3,500 crore in the next four to five years.

items.statement: Approved INR 80.49 crore capex for NDR Hayashi JV; timelines to be shared later.
items.quote: That is the capex that we have approved for the JV. We are currently acquiring a lot of businesses for the JV. We will share the timelines slightly later, towards the end of the year.

items.statement: Margins not significantly impacted by OEM volume swings; impact limited to 0.5-1%.
items.quote: There should not be a significant impact in our margins. It should not be more than 0.5% or 1% compared to the volume going up or down.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain similar, around 6-7%.
items.quote: Margins are expected to be similar.

items.statement: Maruti EV production scale-up: some in Q3 FY26, larger in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So Q3FY26 had some scale ups, Q4FY26 should have a larger scale up.

items.statement: Premiumization to increase revenues more than volumes for NDR and Bharat Seats.
items.quote: Yes, definitely. In addition to that we are also expanding our market share.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 80-85% across all plants; no capacity constraint.
items.quote: Current capacity utilizations are about 80% to 85% across all our plants.

items.statement: Two-wheeler revenue about INR 25-30 crore in 9M FY26; focus remains passenger vehicles.
items.quote: Two-wheelers should be about INR 25-30 crore in the 9 months.

items.statement: JV asset turnover expected at 3 to 4 times.
