items.quote: The asset turnover should be about 3 to 4.

items.statement: Tire and wheel assembly business growth expected next year.
items.quote: That has come last year. We have got a little bit more business for tire and wheel. That should come sometime next year.

items.statement: Vande Bharat seat program remains minor; not a focus area currently.
items.quote: That remains a minor part of it, and we are currently not focusing too much on that.

items.statement: Management expects volume and value growth every quarter going forward, with EBITDA margins improving gradually and better numbers from H2 FY27
items.quote: The way things are going with the changes in tariff structure in US and signing of trade agreements, we are fairly confident that the worst quarter is behind us and now every quarter we will see volume and value growth happening.

items.statement: Target to increase export revenue share from 9% to as high as 50%
items.quote: Obviously, our target is to go much, I mean, from 9%, we want to go up as high as 50% on exports.

items.statement: Dimer acid segment currently at marginal profitability, just keeping heads above water
items.quote: No, at this stage, it is, I mean, we are just keeping our heads out of water. It is very marginal.

items.statement: Current demand for isosteric acid is above average with no major upswing or downslide
items.quote: Currently, it is going on. No, we do not see any major upswing, but at the same time, there is no downslide. So, I mean, it is above average. I would say above average.

items.statement: Animal feed plant ready, awaiting GMP certification; new product equipment expected in production by Q3 FY27
items.quote: Animal feed plant is ready. Yes, the plant is ready and for which we have already applied for the GMP certifications. Once the GMP certificate comes, we will start the plant.

items.statement: Maximum quarterly volume capacity is double current 9,850 tonnes; could achieve ~Rs 900 crore revenue at current realizations
items.quote: Double than what we did, double.

items.statement: Raw material (vegetable oil) imported at 16.5% duty vs finished dimer acid at 7.5% duty creates structural disadvantage; Chinese dumping with export incentives adds pressure
items.quote: The raw material is having higher import duty, but the finished product is having lower import duty. So, that is getting affected, that is really the crux, and second thing is, China is giving export incentives to dimer manufacturers there, and so they are in turn doing dumping.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased 25% in last two months; prices 10-15% below FY22 peak levels
items.quote: In last two months, they have gone as high as 25%.

items.statement: Paint sector demand lower due to new entrant competition; customers asking for lower prices; company developing alternative applications for linoleic acid
items.quote: Because of the competition, they are obviously asking for lower and lower prices. So, that is the reason we have started looking at other applications, which we can use.

items.statement: Tocopherol business (100% US export) at zero for two quarters; US customers may have switched suppliers; revival needed
items.quote: Tocopherol business, basically 100% of our material is getting exported to US, so it is, since two quarters our business has been zero.

items.statement: Buyback executed to increase promoter holding; no cash flow pressure as volume growth to come from existing capacity
items.quote: No, there is no pressure in cash flow. In fact, the complete volume increase, which is going to happen in the next two years, is going to come from the current capacity only.

items.statement: Management refuses to reinstate Rs 1000 crore revenue / 23% EBITDA margin guidance; says 'we will be back to good old days'
items.quote: I mean, it is not advisable to give any forward-looking statements. We never do exactly in figure terms what we say. We will be back to good old days. That is the most I can say.

items.statement: Base business (ex-B2C, ex-Rajasthan) targets higher teens annualized revenue growth
items.quote: we try to achieve revenues in the higher teens is what we are aspirational, and that's what we are currently focusing. If you leave aside the seasonality factors, but on annualized basis, that is what the number we expect to achieve.

items.statement: Rajasthan project expected to contribute ~INR200 cr annualized revenue in FY27
items.quote: Rajasthan revenue should be able to contribute approximately around INR200 crores of annualized revenue.

items.statement: Full annualized revenue potential of Rajasthan expected by end of FY27
items.quote: by -- end of FY '27, we should be able to achieve the full annualized revenue that we are targeting from Rajasthan.

items.statement: Retail (RPL) business targeting breakeven in Q4 FY26
items.quote: we are in line with the quarter 4, where we'll be looking for breakeven for the RPL business.

items.statement: Apulki Hospital mature revenue expected ~INR20 cr in 2-3 years
items.quote: we expect the revenues -- mature level revenues to be in the range of around INR20-odd crores, which we believe it will take around between 2 to 3 years to come to a mature level.

items.statement: Rajasthan rollout: ~20 labs installed, ~300 collection centers, rest in progress; completion targeted by Q4 with spillover to Q1
items.quote: we have around 20 labs currently, which have almost been installed and about 300 collection centers and the rest are in progress. So hopefully, by Q4, majority of them should be done. And by Q1, there might be some spillover

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 26% (normalized 27%); Rajasthan cost absorption a timing issue, aim to maintain margins in FY27
items.quote: directionally, as I said, technically, it should have an impact in the first year, but we are trying to ensure that at least even if it doesn't go upward, but we'll be able to maintain at least the same level of margins.

items.statement: GST rationalization positively impacted consumable costs in Q3, expected to continue
items.quote: there has been some impact for us, positive side on the GST where we were able to also control our consumable cost, and we hopefully see that continuing in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Q3 seasonally soft; temporary operational pauses to accelerate government receivable recovery impacted volumes
items.quote: Q3 is a seasonally softer for the diagnostic industry. This year, the impact was accentuated by lower seasonal volumes and temporary operational pauses undertaken to accelerate recovery of our long pending government receivables.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting: pathology share expected to rise to 65-70% in FY27 from ~50% currently due to Rajasthan and Maharashtra projects
items.quote: Once Rajasthan triggers in and also the Maharashtra project, if it comes in, we expect overall pathology to have a higher share in the revenue, which, in my opinion, could be in the range of around 65% of pathology, 70 pathology and the rest of radiology.

items.statement: No major PPP contracts nearing expiry; receivable recovery progressing in Himachal (INR40 cr received) and Karnataka (confirmations received)
items.quote: As of now, there are no major contracts which are nearing expiry to just confirm that to you.

items.statement: Rajasthan project debt facility from ADB in final stages; debt is project-specific, not company-level
items.quote: for Rajasthan, we have currently, as we disclosed in the previous quarters as well, we have availed a certain facility from ADB, which is in the final stages of completion.

items.statement: Retail network expanded to 3,000+ touch points; retail revenue grew 8x YoY, contributed ~8% of 9M FY26 revenue
items.quote: retail revenue grew by nearly 8x year-on-year and contributed approximately 8% to the overall group's revenue contribution in 9MFY26. Our retail network has expanded to over 3,000-plus touch points

items.statement: Management refrains from providing quantitative revenue or margin guidance for any vertical, focusing on long-term execution instead.
items.quote: As you are aware, we refrain ourselves from giving future guidance, either overall revenue-wise or bottom line-wise or even vertical-wise breakup.

items.statement: Plant 6 mechanical completion expected by end of FY26 with INR50-60 crore capex, ~INR10 crore remaining; maintenance capex INR15 crore annually.
items.quote: Plant 6 mechanical completion is expected to be completed by end of FY '26. On which the expected capex is about INR50 crores to INR60 crores. Most of it is already incurred in coming period, about INR10-odd crores should get added.

items.statement: Plant 6 commercialization expected in H1 FY27 after quality validation and customer audits; partial contribution may start earlier.
items.quote: In first half of FY '27, we should be ready to also do the commercialization. Exactly when is what we are figuring out.

items.statement: Revenue capacity to reach INR1,000 crore from oral solid plants (ex-injectables) plus INR100 crore from injectables after current capex.
items.quote: With this, we would reach INR1,000 crores revenue capacity from all the plants, excluding injectables. And from injectables, we are talking about INR100 crores additional.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA INR79 crore (reported) and INR89 crore (ex-ESOP) at 13.3% margin; Q3 FY26 EBITDA INR24 crore (reported) and INR32 crore (ex-ESOP) at 13.6% margin.
items.quote: Excluding the impact of ESOP expenses, EBITDA for 9-month FY '26 was INR89 crores, 13.3% of revenue and PAT INR60 crores, 9%.

items.statement: Indian pharma market grew 11.8% YoY in Q3 FY26 with 1.6% volume growth; Windlas delivered 20% YoY revenue growth in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: The Indian pharma market grew 11.8% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY '26 with volume growth of 1.6%. Against this backdrop of modest industry volume growth, Windlas Biotech delivered another strong and consistent quarter, achieving record revenues with Y-o-Y growth of 19% in 9 months FY '26 and 20% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: CDMO growth driven primarily by volume; injectable facility and Plant 2 extension contributing; mix of complex and simple products maintained.
items.quote: Most of our growth comes from volume, right? Because we are a cost-plus business and API prices are not increasing. So the growth is primarily volume oriented. And for sure, there is improved contribution from our injectable facility as well as from our Plant 2.

items.statement: Schedule M enforcement driving industry consolidation; Windlas sees no strategic ceiling but emphasizes capability building over speed.
items.quote: Any fragmented industry having a strong regulatory pressure, it's like a textbook case for consolidation. So how does it play out? We don't know. But yes, the -- any fragmented industry with a strong regulatory pressure, quality or regulatory pressure is bound to have a pressure for consolidation.

items.statement: Company is debt-free but not risk-averse; will use cash and debt for strategic acquisitions if fit is right, maintaining financial discipline.
items.quote: We like to be cash rich, but we are not risk-averse. So in past, we have taken several debt for working capital and for capex and for -- whenever we see an opportunity, so like if I have to do an acquisition, it's a very good strategic fit, I won't be shy in using my cash and also taking a debt.

items.statement: ESOP expense for ~100 employees not expected to reduce regular salary increments; employee costs per se not expected to decline.
items.quote: We don't think that we would see reductions there. And with the additional production impact -- so we don't expect employee cost per se to go down.

items.statement: No net new Pizza Hut units in calendar 2026; store count broadly in line with Dec 2025.
items.quote: our plan is not to add any net new units in the brand for 2026. However, we will ensure that the overall store count remains broadly in line with December 2025 numbers.

items.statement: KFC India plans to add 110-120 stores every year; this stays.
items.quote: we plan to add about 110 to 120 stores every year for KFC. That stays.

items.statement: Corporate G&A guidance for FY27 is 5%.
items.quote: For let us say for 2026-27, you can take a 5% G&A.

items.statement: Gross margin profile to be broadly maintained, varying by some basis points.
items.quote: broadly we will be able to maintain the gross margins profile. I mean, it could be vary by some basis points, but largely the gross margin profile will be maintained.

items.statement: Confident KFC can deliver prior brand contribution margins at ADS of INR 105,000-110,000 vs earlier INR 125,000.
items.quote: the brand contribution margins that KFC used to deliver at INR 125,000 ADS, in the current scenario we are very confident that we will be able to deliver those kind of brand contribution margins at about INR 105,000 to INR 110,000 kind of ADS numbers.

items.statement: Hopeful of maintaining EBITDA numbers, supported by Biryani by Kilo breakeven and better KFC SSSG.
items.quote: we are hopeful that we should be able to maintain the EBITDA numbers.

items.statement: Positive SSSG across all brands in January 2026 except Pizza Hut; too early to conclude sustainability.
items.quote: We have seen positive SS SG across all our brands in the month of January except Pizza Hut where the losses are being contained.

items.statement: Early signs of consumption recovery in some sectors due to government support and fiscal measures.
items.quote: On the macro front, we are beginning to see some early signs of consumption coming back in a few sectors in the broader economy , thanks to the government support and fiscal measures.

items.statement: KFC store expansion has caused some cannibalization; differentiated online/offline strategy being developed.
items.quote: if you are opening stores at that pace, there will be some amount of cannibalization which will seep in.

items.statement: Pizza Hut turnaround will take a couple of years to fully sort out loss-making stores.
items.quote: It will take a couple of years to finally sort it out, but we have absolutely started this exercise.

items.statement: Merger synergies estimated at INR 210-225 crore annually; no material timeline deviation expected.
items.quote: the estimated annual merger synergies of approximately INR 210 crore to INR 225 crore will allow us a greater headroom to invest in India and grow the business.

items.statement: Technology transition from Yum! to DIL will take about a year.
items.quote: all of these initiatives will transition from Yum! to us. Now that is going to take about a year.

items.statement: Biryani by Kilo achieved breakeven brand EBITDA ahead of guidance.
items.quote: we have achieved break -even brand EBITDA results for Biryani by Kilo much ahead of our target as guided earlier.

items.statement: Leadership transition: Manish Dawar becomes President & CEO from April 1, 2026; Anupam Kumar becomes CFO.
items.quote: Manish Dawar shall get elevated as President and CEO for DIL with effect from April 1, 2026.

items.statement: Optimistic about stronger revenue growth in FY27 and beyond due to capacity expansion and new products.
items.quote: With capacity expansion, steady demand for existing products and a gradual scale up in volumes for the new product categories, we are optimistic about delivering stronger revenue growth in FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: New cell culture and bioprocess capacity to ramp up over 3-4 years, reaching 15-20% in first year, 30-35% in second year.
items.quote: I would believe from 0 to 100, we would get to the installed capacity maybe in -- within 3 to 4 years at even levels, maybe 15%, 20% capacity going in the first year, 30%, 35% by year 2 and so on.

items.statement: Panchla facility breakeven at INR 70-75 crores revenue, cash and EBITDA positive.
items.quote: once the entire Panchla facility has been somewhere close to $8 million to $9 million overall as a facility, not only in bioprocess containers, so about INR 70 crores, INR 75 crores in revenue, we should be in cash positive, EBITDA positive numbers.

items.statement: Bioprocess containers capacity can generate over INR 150 crores revenue at full capacity.
items.quote: I believe that at full capacity, most of these bioprocess containers, what we've set up in our new facility, could generate revenues of in excess of INR 150 crores.

items.statement: New cell culture and bioprocess products to have similar material margins of 68-70% gross margin as existing products.
items.quote: Material margin-wise, it would be similar to what we currently work at. We work at about 68% to 70% gross margin across product lines, with the exception of a few which could be lower, and the exception of a few which could be higher.

items.statement: Domestic pricing under pressure due to aggressive competitor pricing; growth is volume-led.
items.quote: On competition, intensity in the domestic market is moderately increasing with several competitors adopting aggressive pricing strategies, which has kept pricing under pressure.

items.statement: Domestic demand picking up with increased order inflows; operating at near full capacity.
items.quote: In the domestic market, demand for our products has begun to pick up, reflected in increased order inflows for plastic labware products. We have been operating at near full capacity over the past few months in the existing plants, and are actively working to expedite the ramp-up of new capacities.

items.statement: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) procurement system negatively impacting government business growth.
items.quote: I think the government business has taken a big setback over the last 3 to 4 years since GeM is getting more and more stronger each and every year.

items.statement: Equity infusion in Singapore subsidiary to service loan obligations for German acquisition, not for expansion.
items.quote: This investment of equity is basically related to the loan which we have taken in Singapore entity for the acquisition of German entity. We need to serve the EMI obligations and the loan obligation from India.

items.statement: International markets expected to be growth driver due to new products and India's nascent market share.
items.quote: For now, yes, because we are building products where India is still a nascent user of those products, and the world is a more mature user of those products and India accounts for 2.5%, 3% of the world market.

items.statement: India-U.S. FTA could significantly benefit exports if executed, reducing tariffs from 50% to 18%.
items.quote: But the U.S., if executed perfectly, and if the executive order is signed, it could be a big benefit because 50% coming down to 18% gives us a new lease of life and would definitely help expand our business in America.

items.statement: Nerbe growth flat due to challenging European economy; no significant investments post-acquisition.
items.quote: Nerbe overall has been just a marginal growth from last year. It's a very challenging economy. 2025 calendar year was a very challenging time for the European economy, especially the German economy.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 growth expected ahead of YTD FY26 growth of 11.1%
items.quote: We believe that with all the plans that we've got in motion, our Q4 growth will be ahead of the YTD FY26 growth that we've delivered, which is of 11.1%.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance maintained at INR 60-70 crores
items.quote: Our YTD FY26 capex this year is running close to INR 60 crores. And we've given out a guidance that we intend to keep our capex in the range of INR 60 crores to INR 70 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 57 bps YoY to 11.3%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded by 57 basis points to 11.3% in Q3.

items.statement: COGS program well institutionalized, creating headroom for growth investments
items.quote: Our COGS program is now well institutionalized and is helping create the headroom for growth investments.

items.statement: Air purifier demand expected to stay strong and broaden geographically beyond North markets
items.quote: Going ahead, given the worsening air quality across the country and in most metros, we see this demand staying strong and becoming more geographically broad-based beyond the North markets.

items.statement: Water purifier category to see sustained tailwinds from growing awareness of water contamination
items.quote: We believe that the EWP category will see sustained tailwinds as consumer awareness grows about the hazards of drinking untreated and impure water.

items.statement: Q3 slowdown was a one-off aberration due to unanticipated post-festive slowdown and elevated e-commerce inventory
items.quote: Q3 was clearly a one-time aberration on account of very temporary channel-specific issues leading from the unexpected, unanticipated post-festive slowdown.

items.statement: Service AMC bookings grew double-digits for third consecutive quarter in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our AMC bookings growth trajectory continued strongly, making Q3 as a third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

items.statement: Non-AMC filter aftermarket initiative expected to impact revenue from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: We expect this to start having some impact from Q2 of next year onwards.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected slightly over 10% with Q4 continuing same run rate; PAT targeted around INR145 crores
items.quote: We had, Saket, said that we will be in terms of growth a little over 10% overall. This Q4 should also continue the same run rate with maybe a little bit marginal improvement, so let's see. That's what the guidance was. We are, I think, on track. We should be okay.

items.statement: FY27 guidance to be given at Q4 FY26 annual results call
items.quote: However, we would prefer to give our overall guidance for FY '27 at the time of quarter 4 FY '26 annual results call.

items.statement: China expansion expected to double current revenue at full maturity; 40%+ of investment is infrastructure
items.quote: We are looking at the 2x overall revenue in China when the full maturity of all this capacity takes place.

items.statement: Advantek total investment expected ~INR250 crores by end FY26; incremental plant & machinery ongoing; peak revenue 2x of plant & machinery investment
items.quote: It's an ongoing thing, but yes, we expect it to end this year around INR250 crores-plus.

items.statement: Consolidated capex INR32 crores in Q3 FY26; cumulative INR100 crores in 9M FY26
items.quote: We have incurred capex of INR32 crores in the last quarter and cumulative capex of around INR100 crores in the last 3 quarters in the current financial year.

items.statement: New product development strong: 123 SKUs in Q3, 382 SKUs in 9M FY26; new supply agreements signed across segments
items.quote: Pace of new product development continues to be strong at around 123 SKU up to quarter 3 or only in quarter 3, resulting at 382 SKUs for the 9 months for the period ending December '25.

items.statement: India Engineering normalized EBITDA margin 23.8% in Q3 (reported 21.7% after INR5.97 cr one-time labour provision); target sustainable range 22-23%
items.quote: If we normalize the effect of onetime exceptional provision, then our India Engineering business operating EBITDA margin has shown a healthy 23.8%, though the reported EBITDA is at 21.7%.

items.statement: Advantek Q3 loss INR3.7 crores; loss to reduce in Q4 but not breakeven; breakeven expected FY27
items.quote: We expect a much stronger revenue performance in Harsha Advantek subsidiary in quarter 4, which should increase the EBITDA and reduce the Q4 loss in Advantek subsidiary.

items.statement: Raw material pass-through lag ~4 months (3-month review + 1-month lag); copper price spike hurt Romania Q3; India margins tracked on absolute basis
items.quote: Usually, we decide as a 3 months is the period and with 1 month as a lagging. 4 months total lag.

items.statement: Bronze Bushing 9M revenue INR92 crores (30%+ YoY growth on track); Large cages 9M INR39 crores vs INR31 crores; Stamping 9M INR41 crores; Japan customers 9M INR51.5 crores (flat)
items.quote: Bronze Bushing business has continued its strong growth trajectory, reaching a sales revenue figure of about INR92 crores in 9 months, ending in December '25. Thus, as per our earlier estimate, we are on track to achieve about 30%-plus growth Y-o-Y basis in this segment.

items.statement: Commodity volatility remains risk for Romania; pass-through mechanism exists but quarter-to-quarter impact persists
items.quote: There is a lot of volatility in the commodity market. We do have a pass-through mechanism. We have a quarter-to-quarter impact and correction. I mean, not knowing future, but what we have seen so far so there's a significant volatility. That there is a risk and a concern remains.

items.statement: Solar division Q3 revenue INR59.7 crores, EBITDA 9%; order-driven, positive contribution expected full year
items.quote: Solar business, as mentioned, has achieved a revenue of INR59.7 crores with an EBITDA of INR5.5 crores.

items.statement: Expect bromine production north of 18,000 tons in FY27, targeting 18,000-25,000 ton run rate
items.quote: I'm reasonably confident that I think we should -- we are -- we have solves on most of this implemented now. There is clearly a road map to get to that 17,500, 18,000 number. As I mentioned to the earlier -- to Vinay earlier that we are -- a simple answer, we will be north of 18,000 tons next year.

items.statement: Elemental bromine order backlog at ~6,500 tons after shipping ~2,500 tons in Q3; minimal cancellations
items.quote: So we have still around 6,500 tons in backlog. We've not seen a significant amount of cancellations there.

items.statement: Bromine price increases pressuring derivative margins; not all cost increases passed through to customers
items.quote: The increase in bromine prices obviously sprint cost pressures on our bromine derivatives business. And what I mean by Sanjesh, obviously, is that given the specific products we are making right now and the way the contracts are, not all of the cost increase is something we're able to pass through to our clients.

items.statement: SiCSem semiconductor project: 25-acre site allotted in Bhubaneshwar, groundbreaking done Nov 2025, land levelling complete, fiscal support agreement with ISM underway
items.quote: The 25-acre site in Info Valley, Bhubaneshwar has been allotted, and we held a groundbreaking survey on that at the site in November 2025. Land levelling is complete, and we are right now going through topographical survey and soil testing right before we start any construction activity.

items.statement: Flame retardant bromine project under detailed evaluation; timeline of 12-18 months from Q2 FY26 (end FY27) still holds
items.quote: We are in the project evaluation phase there, and we'll provide a more detailed update on that as we make progress. Current market environment is kind of mixed there. So we are trying to evaluate the feasibility of that business and how quickly we can scale that -- scale volumes up.

items.statement: Rampraveen Swaminathan appointed Managing Director; Ranjit Pendurthi shifts to strategic role focusing on new initiatives
items.quote: Further, the Board has appointed Mr. Rampraveen Swaminathan as the Managing Director of the company. We would like to welcome him to the Archean team.

items.statement: FY26 launch guidance of INR170bn; expect to exceed INR150bn
items.quote: Overall, we started the year with a guidance of about INR170 billion worth of launches. I would say, we'll be range bound to that with our launches definitely exceeding INR150 billion.

items.statement: FY26 presales guidance gap expected to narrow significantly in Q4
items.quote: So, I think we will largely cover the gap between the guidance numbers and the actual performance for this year.

items.statement: INR6.7bn used for land acquisition from JDA partners and INR0.7bn for approvals in 9M FY26
items.quote: We've added stroke, bought some land from our JDA partners, wherein -- which happened where we used about INR6.7 billion and another INR0.7 billion went in terms of approvals for forthcoming projects.

items.statement: Expect price growth in late single digits (not double digits) for next 18-24 months
items.quote: I expect price to move up in late single digits rather than going up in double digits for the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Demand steady but not euphoric; 40-50% offtake at launch, balance over project life
items.quote: So, within 6 months, let's say, we are able to sell 50% to 60% of those number of units is more like what one would relate to. And that's the current scenario where demand is steady but not euphoric.

items.statement: Construction delays due to heavy monsoon and pollution (GRAP) impacted collections and revenue recognition in H1 FY26
items.quote: On the construction front, this year, we had like a very heavy monsoon season and then immediately backed by a very heavy pollution season in the Delhi NCR. And we've actually lost significant number of days during the current year on the construction front.

items.statement: Land cost + approvals ~15% of topline; historical land cost 10-12%
items.quote: But land approvals put together, I think an assumption of about 15-odd percent of top line is a fair assumption.

items.statement: Targets consolidated revenue growth of around 9-10% for full year FY26.
items.quote: For the full year, we are targeting consolidated revenue growth of around 9%, 10%

items.statement: Targets 10-12% revenue growth in IFM segment.
items.quote: We are targeting a 10%, 12% revenue growth in the IFM segment, supported by a strong favorable long -term industry outlook in India.

items.statement: Expects consolidated EBITDA margin to stabilize around 6%.
items.quote: So, we believe that these margins should be stable in this ballpark. So, in the 6% ballpark.

items.statement: Denave margins at 4%, expected to remain stable; no further decline.
items.quote: Margins in that business in Denave right now are approximately around 4%. And on a 9-month basis, we don't see this going down further.

items.statement: Athena margins at 20%, expected to stabilize at this level.
items.quote: So, if you look at a 9 -month to 9-month number, our margin percentage is still at about 20%.

items.statement: Plans to deploy cash of INR2,053 million for value-accretive acquisitions.
items.quote: Apart from the organic growth, we also have cash of about INR2,053 million on our books, which we plan to deploy towards value -accretive acquisitions.

items.statement: Took provision of INR230 million for Avon logistics receivables; operations halted.
items.quote: Over the last 2 quarters, Avon, one of our subsidiaries had taken a total prov ision of approximately INR230 million relating to receivables from its logistics and brokerage business

items.statement: Full pass-through of statutory wage revisions in contracts protects margins.
items.quote: Importantly, we have always operated with a full pass -through of statutory revisions in our contracts, ensuring that any change in minimum wages or any change in statutory regulation will flow through the pricing, supporting revenue visibility while protecting margins.

items.statement: IFM revenue growth back on track with 14% YoY growth in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: I'm happy to share that the IFM revenue growth is back on track in Q3 FY '26 with the segment delivering a growth of 14% year on year.

items.statement: Denave demand generation business grew mid-teens excluding large client.
items.quote: Excluding this large client, our demand generation business recorded mid-teens revenue growth, indicating strong interest from other marquee customers.

items.statement: Denave shifting to technology-led model; expects margin impact in 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: However, we do ex pect in another 2 to 3 quarters, we will start seeing impact of that at a scale level.

items.statement: AI and automation pose both opportunity and threat to BSS, especially Denave and Athena.
items.quote: AI is something which is both an opportunity and a threat in some of our businesses.

items.statement: DSO increased but expected to improve with customer term revisions and collections.
items.quote: So that is now getting pretty much resolved and we should start seeing DSO come down.

items.statement: Added 13 new logos in IFM segment during Q3 FY26.
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 13 new logos in the IFM segment, including a few marquee names.

items.statement: Plans to add 17 hotels with 672 keys over next 14 months, reaching 3,219 keys and 56 hotels by FY27.
items.quote: In total, we will add 17 hotels totaling to 672 keys over the next 14 months, taking our overall room count in '26-'27 to 3,219 keys with 56 hotels.

items.statement: Plans to add 438 keys in FY27, entirely under management contracts plus 85 keys from Mumbai property.
items.quote: During ’26-'27, we plan to add 438 keys.

items.statement: Plans to add 6 hotels with 234 keys in Q4 FY26 across multiple locations.
items.quote: During quarter 4 this year, we plan to add 6 hotels totaling to 234 keys with properties opening at Vizag, Darjeeling, Katra, Kochi, Goa, and Dharamsala.

items.statement: Plans to open 16 Flurys stores in Q4 FY26, reaching about 120 stores.
items.quote: So, during quarter four now we plan to open 16 stores to take the number to about 120 stores with high revenue growth and then go on a faster and an accelerated pace as India's story improves.

items.statement: Plans to reach 150-160 Flurys stores by FY27, with 30-40 cafes opening in FY27.
items.quote: Number of stores we plan to take the number of stores from current which will we will conclude at 120 stores we plan to take it to about anywhere between 150 to 160 stores.

items.statement: Plans to reach 200 Flurys stores by 2028 and 450-500 stores by FY30.
items.quote: Till 2028 we will be at the 200 mark. And we remain committed to our overall plan of having 450 to 500 stores to be precise by '29-'30.

items.statement: Total capex of INR 1,570 crore, including INR 950 crore for new hotels and INR 330 crore for acquisitions.
items.quote: Our total capex of this becomes INR 1,570 crore.

items.statement: Annual operational capex of INR 40 crore for renovations and Flurys expansion.
items.quote: Average capex per year which we do is INR40 crore for operational capex, which is like 100 rooms going every year and Flurys about INR 180 crore to INR 200 crore over a period of top 5 years.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin was 35.3% with revenue INR 200 crore and EBITDA INR 71 crore.
items.quote: During Q3 FY '26, consolidated revenue stood at INR 200 crore, while EBITDA was at INR 71 crore, translating into an EBITDA margin of 35.3%.

items.statement: ARR and RevPAR increased 11% and 9% year-on-year in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: This performance was supported by industry-leading occupancy levels of 90%, along with year-on-year improvement in ARR and RevPAR of 11% and 9%, respectively.

items.statement: Healthy mix of corporate travel, weddings, and leisure demand supported Q3 performance.
items.quote: A healthy mix of corporate travel, weddings and leisure demand supported performance during the quarter.

items.statement: F&B retail space experiencing slowdown, with competitors shutting stores, impacting Flurys expansion pace.
items.quote: Also, at the same time because of India's growth story has slightly slowed down, particularly you would know that the F&B retail space is experiencing a slight slowdown particularly many of the competitor stores of even international brands as you are based in Mumbai, you would know that they have been shutting down.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at 0.11, targeting 0.1-0.2 range; gross debt INR 236 crore, net debt INR 154 crore.
items.quote: Currently it is at 0.11 and we would like to be in this kind of range only from 0.1 to 0.2 in our entire cycle of this growth.

items.statement: Sale of serviced residences at The Park Unizen to add INR 300-350 crore cash flow over three years.
items.quote: The sale of these serviced residences over the next three years will add INR 300 crore to INR 350 crore in cash flow and will further strengthen the balance sheet of Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 PAT of INR140-160 crores.
items.quote: We are giving an expectation of quarter 4 '26 PAT of between INR140 crores to INR160 crores.

items.statement: Expects FY27 credit cost at 1.7-1.8%.
items.quote: In the coming year, we expect the credit cost given where our SMA book is and given the amount of provisioning we have done to be in the 1.7% to 1.8% range.

items.statement: Expects FY27 ROE of 14-15%.
items.quote: I would expect next year, our ROE to be around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Expects FY27 NIM of 7-7.1%.
items.quote: Our NIM should be about 7% to 7.1%.

items.statement: Expects FY27 ROA of 1.5-1.6%.
items.quote: And the ROA should be about 1.5% to 1.6%.

items.statement: Expects GNPA to remain flat at INR830-850 crores in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We expect that to remain flat. That is between INR 830 crores to INR 850 crores in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Expects SMA to decline to 4% by March 2026.
items.quote: we expect it to be at 4% when we finish the year.

items.statement: Expects cost-to-income ratio to normalize to 60-62% by Q2/Q3 FY27.
items.quote: cost income ratio should be around 60% to 62% when it normalizes.

items.statement: Expects NIM to improve further in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We will see further NIM improvement even in quarter 4.

items.statement: Expects SMA and slippages in March 2026 to be lower than March 2024.
items.quote: SMA and slippages from March '26 will be lower than March '24.

items.statement: Expects CASA growth of 25-30% going forward.
items.quote: if we continue doing the 25% to 30% as we go ahead, I think it will keep us probably at 2.5x, 3x of the industry growth rate

items.statement: Expects Micro LAP growth to reach 20% next year.
items.quote: I do see Micro LAP to reach the 20% growth rate in the following year.

items.statement: Two unnamed deals to start contributing revenue in Q4; Femwell and StrideCare in Q1.
items.quote: Two of those deals that are unnamed are actually kicking into Q4 itself. And the other two deals, Femwell and StrideCare are expected to start kicking into revenue in Q1.

items.statement: StrideCare to go live entirely by end of Q1, perhaps early Q2.
items.quote: StrideCare should go live entirely by the end of Q1, perhaps early Q2.

items.statement: Femwell's 800+ providers to go live over six-to-nine months starting Q1, spanning Q1 to Q3.
items.quote: The Femwell deal, which is, you know, their base of 800-plus providers, is likely to go live across that 800-provider base over the six-to-nine-month duration starting in Q1. So it'll basically go from Q1 to Q3.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain in early-to-mid 30s range, within 100-150 bps.
items.quote: And, you know, we stay consistent with what I have said is that this is the EBITDA range that we feel relatively comfortable with. And by that, I don't mean 35%, but this range within the next within say 100 to 150 bps.

items.statement: Full year effective tax rate expected around 21%.
items.quote: For the full year ETR please expect ETR to be around the same 21% number.

items.statement: R&D investment to continue increasing, currently at 4.7% of revenue.
items.quote: As you've seen our R&D investment this quarter is up to nearly 5%, 4.7%. I think it's about INR39 crores, give or take. And so we intend to continue to expand our R&D investment

items.statement: Net economic value add model: Palomar deal generated $3 million in first year, recovering $16.5 million advance.
items.quote: In the first year itself, which by the way took us more than 6 months to implement the platform in the first place, maybe even close to 8 months by the time the full platform was implemented, in the 4 months of full go-live, we've already been able to generate $3 million of net economic value add.

items.statement: Refinanced term loan from $146 million to $50 million, triggering one-time non-cash write-off of INR12.7 crores.
items.quote: We, of course, continued to pay that down and we have now refinanced that term loan to a $50 million term loan. Of course, the refinancing triggered an accelerated amortization of the setup cost of the original loan. The INR12.7 crores number is that one-time non-cash write-off which is also sitting in the PAT numbers.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR322 crores (~$35 million).
items.quote: We ended the quarter at INR322 crores or approximately $35 million in net debt.

items.statement: Hedging policy covers 50-60% of net forex exposure.
items.quote: It's 50% to 60% of our net forex exposure, that's what we hedge.

items.statement: 85-90% of growth expected from existing customer expansion.
items.quote: And we still continue to maintain that in most healthy growth years, somewhere between 85% to 90% of our growth is going to come from existing customer expansion versus new customer addition.

items.statement: Acknowledges potential hiccups in revenue due to dynamic US regulatory environment.
items.quote: So if your question is, does this create unpredictability in the market and could there be hiccups? Absolutely. I mean, hard for me to tell.

items.statement: Medicare Advantage rate pressure seen as tailwind for value-based care offerings.
items.quote: So when you really think about it, the more the pressure on these risk-bearing entities or providers, the more attractive our value-based care portfolio becomes to them. And so I fundamentally look at it as a macro tailwind for the value-based care business.

items.statement: Priorities: pay down $50 million debt quickly, then growth and acquisitions.
items.quote: And of course what the $50 million of debt that we still have, is of course something that we want to pay that down pretty quickly. So those would be priorities in the near term.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated top line expected around INR5,700 crores with double-digit EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Yes, so FY '27, with everything put together, we will be looking at a top line of close to 5,700 and a double-digit EBITDA on that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA expected INR90-100 crores, revenue around INR1,200 crores.
items.quote: Q4, we are looking at anything between INR90 crores to INR100 crores consolidated EBITDA.

items.statement: Technical textile yarn capacity at Silvassa doubling from 9,000 to 18,000 MTPA, commissioning in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: This expansion will double our installed capacity from 9,000 metric tons per annum to 18,000 metric tons per annum in Q1 FY '27, strengthening our presence in the high-value technical textile and supporting long-term margin improvement.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 1 polymerization capacity to reach 700 TPD by end of Q4 FY26; currently at ~575 TPD.
items.quote: As of today, the production has reached approximately 575 metric tons per day and we remain on track to achieving Phase 1 polymerization capacity of 700 metric tons per day by the end of Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 2 expansion to 950 TPD, fully operational in FY28; capex INR125-150 crores.
items.quote: So it's only a small capex maybe about INR150 crores or INR125 crores to INR150 crores which will add up to adding that additional 200-odd tons per day.

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh cotton yarn project capex ~INR400 crores, commissioning in H2 FY28.
items.quote: Overall, what we will be spending on -- not on the maintenance, but what we will be spending now will be about INR100-odd crores for the second phase at Punjab and we will be doing spending about 400 and odd crores at the cotton facility for Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 margins expected to return to Q2 levels as QCO impact normalizes and raw material benefits flow in.
items.quote: So definitely we will see a better number this quarter going forward and we will be like the Q2 numbers.

items.statement: Gross margin expected around 31% in coming quarters.
items.quote: So we can expect a gross margin at anything around 31%-odd in the coming quarters?

items.statement: Cotton spreads improving and expected to move up further; polyester margins to follow from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Yes, you're right. The cotton spreads have improved and we personally feel that yes, it's on a good wicket and it's going to move up further.

items.statement: Punjab facility all filament yarn; Silvassa revenue mix: ~INR400 crores cotton, ~INR100 crores technical textiles, rest filament.
items.value: 400 and odd crores, 100 and odd crores
items.quote: So, effectively on our Silvassa facility of where the top line is close to INR3,000 crores, we do about 400 and odd crores revenue comes from the cotton side and about 100 and odd crores comes from the technical textiles and the balance comes from the filament yarn.

items.statement: Inverted duty structure increased working capital blockage, but refunds expected faster.
items.quote: Yes, I mean there are no challenges. Except that yes, we have a larger blockage of funds because of the larger inversion. Earlier we had an inversion from 18 to 12. Now we have an inversion from 18 to 5, so there's a little more money blocked.

items.statement: Promoter holding at 78%, will reduce to 75% per SEBI regulation over time.
items.quote: So as per the SEBI regulation, we have to bring it down to 75%, but we have some time on that, so we will look at it as we go across the journey.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps YoY to 11.2%; PAT margin rose to 7.9% from 5.5%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR545.7 million, with EBITDA margin expanding to 11.2% from 9.2% in Q3 FY'25, translating into a strong 200 bps increase.

items.statement: IDC estimates 2026 new PC shipments could decline up to 8.9% due to memory shortages and rising prices, driving higher refurbished PC acceptance
items.quote: According to IDC, global new PC shipments stood at about 284.7 million units in 2025. Against this backdrop, IDC estimates that shipments in 2026 could decline by up to 8.9% due to memory shortages and rising prices.

items.statement: DDR5 8GB RAM prices rose 270% from $23.35 to $86.61 (Oct 2025 to Jan 2026); DDR5 16GB rose 3.4x from $54.85 to $189.99
items.quote: To put this into perspective, as DDR5 8GB RAM prices increased from $23.35 on 1st October 2025 to $86.61 by 1st January 2026, nearly a 270% increase. Similarly, DDR5 16GB RAM prices rose from $54.85 to $189.99 over the same period, a 3.4x increase.

items.statement: New PC prices increased ~20% so far; further increases expected, expanding refurbished PC addressable market
items.quote: We are already seeing the impact. New PC prices have increased by roughly 20% so far and we expect further increases ahead.

items.statement: Management sees potential for further margin expansion beyond current 11-11.5% EBITDA margin due to inventory positioning and rising new PC prices
items.quote: If your question is around, is there a possibility and we have the environment available for the same, the answer is positive. Yes.

items.statement: Expanded facilities in India (Navi Mumbai), UAE (now 8 facilities from 3), and US; headcount grew from 1,194 to ~1,900 including 600+ engineers
items.quote: We have now around eight facilities in the UAE from three what we had earlier. And we have now taken one bigger facility adjacent to our existing facility in Navi Mumbai. And we are increasing our space in the US market as well.

items.statement: Signed strategic partnerships with world's largest tech distributor and India's 2nd & 5th largest distributors to expand reach in Tier 2/3 cities
items.quote: We have partnered with one of the world's largest technology distributors and the second largest distributor in India, and separately partnered with fifth largest technology distributor in India.

items.statement: Net debt INR 466 cr, gross debt INR 557 cr as of Dec 31, 2025; full-year finance cost expected similar to last year (~INR 38 cr) despite higher inventory
items.value: Net debt INR 466 cr; Gross debt INR 557 cr
items.quote: The gross debt is INR557 crores, and the net debt is the quarter end net debt is INR466 odd crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 volume: 186,000 units (83% laptops, 17% others); 9M FY26: 487,500 units (73% laptops, 27% others)
items.quote: The volume for this quarter was about 1,86,000 units which was spread across laptops and others in the proportion of 83% and 17%.

items.statement: Laptop ASP rose ~INR 1,000 QoQ to ~INR 28,800; non-laptop ASP rose from ~INR 17,900 to ~INR 18,200; blended ASP ~INR 26,200 vs INR 25,200 YoY
items.quote: For this quarter our average selling price for ASP for laptops is almost INR28,800 odd. Now the same in the previous quarter was about INR1,000 lower.

items.statement: 9M FY26 volume grew from 401,000 to 488,000 units YoY (~22% growth); Q3 FY26 volume 186,000 vs 143,000 in Q3 FY25 (~30% growth)
items.quote: Volume growth has increased from 4,01,000 to 4,88,000 in terms of total units in the nine month period.

items.statement: Working capital days at 120-130 range, stable YoY and improved sequentially by a couple of days
items.quote: The working capital days are in the 120 to 130 day odd range on an overall basis. Sequential quarter-wise there's actually been an improvement in of a couple of days.

items.statement: No dividend policy framed yet; business needs capital for growth, will remain fluid on capital returns
items.quote: At this point of time business requires fuel and we need to grow. I guess, we remain fluid in this and we will keep sharing our thoughts on this.

items.statement: Plans to increase private label contribution to 22% from current 17% over next two years.
items.quote: The company plans to increase private label contribution to 22% from current 17% over the next two years.

items.statement: Plans to open 10-15 stores per year, reaching 60-65 stores by FY27.
items.quote: We plan on opening 10 to 15 stores every year that's just because we don't want to open the store test the waters if it's not working shut it down that's the waste of the capex that goes within it is just a depreciating model . Whenever we try to open a store we try to do it the right way -- so Yes so 10 to 15 stores i

items.statement: Retail store capex is INR1,500 per sq ft; average store size 5,000 sq ft.
items.quote: So capex for the retail store is almost INR1,500 per square foot and on an average we have a 5,000 square foot store size.

items.statement: No manufacturing capex needed for next 2-3 years; existing capacity sufficient.
items.quote: But aside from that , whatever work we are doing right now we have enough capacity to cater for the next two three years.

items.statement: Secured INR22 crores export order, manufacturing own products like atta, spices, peanut.
items.quote: INR22 crores of export business yes.

items.statement: Same store sales growth is 8% year-on-year, blended across products.
items.quote: 8%. The same store growth is 8% for year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Private label growing 17-20% year-on-year in retail stores.
items.quote: We are growing almost in the range of 17% to 20% and it is growing year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Indian Chaska brand did INR8 crores revenue this year; plans 15-20% month-on-month growth.
items.quote: We did an exceptional revenue of around INR8 crores this year and we plan to grow on 15% to 20% month on month.

items.statement: Private label supports higher gross margins and better inventory control.
items.quote: The company has set priority to increase private label contribution as private label supports higher gross margins, better inventory control and strong brand equity.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility is managed by research and in-season procurement; impacts industry equally.
items.quote: See the volatility and the change in the commodity price is something that we cannot control right all we can do is keep a keen eye on the demand and the supply that is been seen in the market right.

items.statement: Inventory level is INR210 crores; targeting to maintain same ratio.
items.quote: So the current level of inventory considering the size of the company is almost INR210 crores and we are targeting to maintain more or less the same inventory ratio.

items.statement: Export credit days increased due to longer transit to US, UK, Europe, Australia, Canada.
items.quote: Now we are now – now majority of our export operation is in U .S, U.K, European countries, Australia, Canada where the transit is more than 45 days, 50 days, 60 days depending on the vessel and depending on the geopolitical situation what route is open, what route is not open because we see consistency in this market r

items.statement: Export revenue diversified: UK 20%, Canada 15%, US 11%, Australia 10%, Sri Lanka 10-12%, Saudi 10-12%, Oman 5-6%.
items.quote: Australia contributes 10%, US does 11%, Canada does 15%, UK does 20%. There's Sri Lanka as well who does around 10 % to 12%, there's Saudi Arabia who contributes around 10% to 12%, there's Oman who contributes around 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow high single digits in FY27, with moderation in second half due to high base.
items.quote: So overall, the industry for the next financial year is likely to grow in high single digits.

items.statement: January price increase of INR300 per vehicle taken to mitigate commodity inflation.
items.quote: The price hike we've taken in January was INR300 is what we've taken from 1st of January per vehicle, INR300 per vehicle.

items.statement: Commodity inflation impacted Q3 by 40-50 bps; prices continue rising in Q4.
items.quote: So your first part of the question was how much is the impact coming from the commodity in the previous quarter was approximately 40 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: May take further price increases during the quarter if required, given strong market conditions.
items.quote: I also would like to add that the market conditions are strong, and we'll be taking adequate price increase if required during the quarter.

items.statement: ICE business EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 17% on pricing, LEAP savings, operating leverage.
items.quote: ICE business EBITDA margin expanded by 100 bps year-on-year to 17%, driven by pricing, LEAP savings and operating leverage.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin improved 20 bps to 14.7% after EV investment of INR208 crores.
items.quote: During the quarter, after taking into account the investments behind EV business, approximately INR208 crores, the overall EBITDA margins improved 20 basis points to 14.7%.

items.statement: Margins to hold; growth to drive overhead dilution and expansion.
items.quote: On the margins, I think with the growth, we will get overhead dilution, and we will see expansion there.

items.statement: Positive demand trend expected to continue; January retail grew 21% YoY.
items.quote: Post festive demand continues to stay strong with January '26 retail growing at 21% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q4 and Q1 expected strong, especially rural, aided by wedding season and early festives.
items.quote: We also expect that as we see the wedding season unfolding from February onwards, some early festives that set in from March, we expect quarter 4 also to be strong

items.statement: Scooters, EV, and premium expected to grow faster than other categories.
items.quote: Some segments are likely to grow faster as Harsh said, scooters, both ICE, EV and premium we are -- we expect a faster growth than the rest of the categories.

items.statement: EV capacity expansion expected to see marked increase in FY27.
items.quote: So we are looking at F '27 as the year in which we would be able to see a marked increase on this front.

items.statement: ABS regulation timelines uncertain; company ready to comply with any guidelines.
items.quote: There are different options being discussed -- and we are awaiting further guidelines, if any, when they come. But we will be ready to fulfil those guidelines, whichever guidelines come.

items.statement: Interim dividend announced on back of strong festive season.
items.quote: You've all seen the interim dividend getting announced. This was on the back of a strong festive season.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 volumes of 9-9.5 million tons, with demand momentum continuing through March.
items.quote: I can easily and with a great deal of confidence, say that within this quarter, we will do 9 million to 9.5 million tons.

items.statement: Expects FY27 industry demand growth of 7.5-8%, with Shree growing in line or better.
items.quote: So next year, I expect the demand to be around 7.5% to 8%.

items.statement: Guides FY27 capex at INR500 crores, excluding any new cement capacity additions.
items.quote: So I am giving a guidance of next year capex at INR500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex to be INR2,000 crores, with INR1,500 crores already spent.
items.quote: This year I'll be doing INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Plans to expand RMC plants from 19 to 45 by September 2026.
items.quote: We intend to take it to 45 within next 6 to 8 months, means you can easily assume that by September'26, the number of plants will increase to 45 from 19.

items.statement: Narrowed price gap with UltraTech from INR30 to INR15 per bag; expects further improvement.
items.quote: If you will notice by restraining our volumes, we have narrowed the gap from about INR30 a bag to about INR15 a bag.

items.statement: Expects to restore EBITDA per ton premium of INR100-150 over competition.
items.quote: Otherwise we had always maintained a INR100 to INR150 delta plus side. And I expect to catch that up.

items.statement: Fuel cost at INR1.56 per kilocalorie, lowest in industry; may rise in Feb-Mar but stay below INR1.80.
items.quote: As on date, we are at 1.56 per kilocalorie. It may remain same for January, but it may go up in February and March. In any case, I don't think it should increase to1.80, which is my peer group fuel cost.

items.statement: No let-up expected in demand through March due to government budget spending.
items.quote: We don't find any let up in February and March because the central government budget has to be spent by 31st March, so I don't think there will be any let up in volumes.

items.statement: Premium cement share at 21-22%; expects to maintain same run rate this financial year.
items.quote: And at the moment with the current demand scenario we are at 21%-22%, and we expect to maintain the same run rate for this financial year.

items.statement: Dividend payout for FY26 expected to be materially better than FY25.
items.quote: But I expect the dividend payout for FY ‘25-‘26 to be better than FY ‘24-‘25. And it is not a differential of INR5 rupees kind of a thing.

items.statement: 80 MT capacity target by FY29 may be deferred depending on demand.
items.quote: I had hinted that 80 million tons by FY '29 may get deferred or may culminate is completely dependent on how the demand pans out in FY '26-'27.

items.statement: Depreciation expected at INR1,600-1,700 crores next year.
items.quote: Depreciation should be about INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: MCA investigation under section 210 is routine; information shared, no report yet.
items.quote: It is a routine inquiry. They have asked for information; the information has been shared. Now, they have not come up with any report.

items.statement: FY27 double-digit earnings growth seen as realistic, driven by GDP and currency tailwinds.
items.quote: But if you look at our macroeconomics, GDP growth at about 7-7.5%, currency by about 2-3%, I think 10% is a given. So, a double-digit growth, I think from a business perspective, seems very realistic.

items.statement: Travel segment to maintain 4%-plus margin trajectory.
items.quote: But broadly, the guidance that we have given is that we will continue our trajectory on the 4 -plus percent as far as the Travel segment is concerned.

items.statement: Forex segment to continue 40%-plus margins.
items.quote: Yes, Mr. Varma. We will continue to be in that trajectory. I think that's what we have been delivering year-on-year. And I don't think there's anything that should be less from that part. The 40-plus percent will see.

items.statement: Sterling H2 FY26 to outperform H1; margins 32-35% EBITDA.
items.quote: These factors for H2 FY26 outperform H1.

items.statement: Sterling to add minimum ~15 hotels/resorts in 2026, asset-light model.
items.quote: And this year as well, we are looking at a similar number minimum.

items.statement: DEI to fully implement WeC by Q1 FY27, benefits from Q2.
items.quote: By the quarter one of 2027, we should see WeC in full implementation. By April or May is when we see the full implementation. We should be seeing some benefit in quarter two of that coming through.

items.statement: Investments directed at technology and upscaling for customer obsession; no acquisitions or shareholder returns currently.
items.quote: But currently, our investments are directed on technology and upscaling to the mandate of getting customer obsessed and making the journey seamless for them.

items.statement: Forex EBIT margin expanded to 41.5% in Q3 FY26 from 38.7%.
items.quote: Correspondingly, our EBIT margins expanded to 41.5% from 38.7% last year, reflecti ng a disciplined execution and operating leverage.

items.statement: Travel EBIT margin 3.1% in Q3 FY26 vs 2.9% last year.
items.quote: EBIT margins for the segment stood at 3.1% versus the 2.9% last year.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin 36% in Q3 FY26, 4pp above H1 average.
items.quote: EBITDA margin was sustained at a healthy 36% , which is a 4% over H1 average.

items.statement: Short-haul travel leading growth; long-haul Europe sluggish due to rupee depreciation.
items.quote: Early indicators for the summer 2026 reflect continued customer interest with short -haul travel continuing to lead growth. Long haul, specifically Europe remains slightly sluggish owing to the steep rupee depreciation against the euro.

items.statement: Inbound India business Q4 FY26 better than Q3; pipeline building.
items.quote: So what I'm saying is that if you look at our inbound business, which is typically, as you know, this is the season running from October to March, while the first quarter, which is the October-December quarter didn't pan out very well, or the second p art of the season seems much better than the first part.

items.statement: Shift from long-haul to short-haul travel; short-haul 9M growth 23% vs long-haul 5%.
items.quote: This is clearly evidenced by our performance, which indicates a 23% increase on our short haul on a 9 -month basis versus a 5% increase in long haul.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and travel advisories impacted Middle East and US DMS businesses.
items.quote: Two of our units and namely that was in U.S.A. and Middle East, which is Desert Adventures that we operate in the Middle East market, we had subdued growth. And obviously, in the case of Middle East, it was more the macro driven by the geopolitical tension that we were going through.

items.statement: India Q4 realisations to rise ~Rs 2,300/t QoQ; HRC spot up ~Rs 3,500/t.
items.quote: I think the guidance we are giving is, India prices on QoQ will be about Rs. 2,300 /t higher, and on a spot basis of course , hot rolled will be much higher, but I think when you look at the mix and you look at some of the contracts that we have, we see an improvement of about Rs. 2,300/t.

items.statement: Netherlands Q4 realisations to fall €30-33/t QoQ due to mix, but EBITDA to expand on cost savings.
items.quote: In Netherlands, on a spot basis it is going to be higher on the hot roll coil, but because of the mix issues that K oushik referred to, and the fact that the packaging contracts are getting renegotiated, we are seeing a QoQ reduction of €30-33/t per ton from 3Q to 4Q.

items.statement: UK Q4 realisations to rise ~£5/t QoQ; EBITDA to improve slightly.
items.quote: In UK, it's going to be about £5/t higher or so.

items.statement: Overall Q4 EBITDA to be better than Q3; volumes up ~0.5 Mt QoQ.
items.quote: So overall we expect EBITDA to be better in 4Q compared to 3Q, and volumes to be almost half a million tons better in 4Q compared to 3Q.

items.statement: Coking coal consumption cost to rise $15/t in Q4; purchase cost up $22/t.
items.quote: Coking coal, like I said, on a consumption basis will be about $15 /t higher in 4Q compared to 3Q.

items.statement: NINL expansion to take 35-40 months; FID in next couple of months.
items.quote: So, I guess it will take about 35 -40 months when we get into the execution level. I think it is also important to mention that we will get to the FID in the next couple of months.

items.statement: UK EAF project progressing; electricity connection from National Grid critical for commissioning.
items.quote: Major demolition work has been completed and securing access to high power electricity is critical for our plan ned transition. We are working with the Electricity System Operator and National Grid for the new electrical infrastructure which remains critical for the project commissioning.

items.statement: Europe steel prices expected to rise towards US levels due to CBAM and safeguard quotas.
items.quote: But, because of these actions, we expect that prices in Europe will move away from Asian prices and move towards the US steel prices. It may not reach the levels of US steel prices but certainly will move closer to that.

items.statement: UK needs spread expansion of ~£100/t to become profitable.
items.quote: So, I'm saying that, wherever the spread is today, that spread has to expand by about £100/t to make it a profitable entity.

items.statement: India demand strong; no major impact expected from European exports returning.
items.quote: I don't think that volume will be so significant as to make an impact in the domestic market in India , because the demand is pretty strong in India.

items.statement: Focus on increasing market share in attractive segments to 2x overall share; downstream expansion in tubes, wires.
items.quote: Generally, in Tata Steel, we always look at whether our market share in attractive segments be twice our overall market share. So, if we are a 15-20% market share player, then in the attractive segments, we should be at least 40% or more .

items.statement: UK EBITDA losses to continue until government policy support on imports or steel prices rise.
items.quote: It is still there, and we expect it to keep improving because of the actions we are taking, but it will not become positive till there is some action from the UK government on the imports or if the steel prices go up in UK.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA to remain below 3x; capex calibrated to balance sheet.
items.quote: I think we've said that broadly we would like to be up to about 3x Net debt to EBITDA. And sometimes when you have cyclical issues, we move to 3.2 x, and when in better times or when we are able to generate more cash flows, it comes down , as you see now, we are at 2.6x.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected flattish; Q4 to show growth.
items.quote: But on a yearly basis, we are of the opinion it should be flattish year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin decline of 100-110 bps expected.
items.quote: So in overall annual basis, we are expecting a similar decline 100-110 bps.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable gross margin guided at 38%.
items.quote: And going forward, I am of the opinion that 38% gross margins are sustainable in the long term.

items.statement: MPP-2 plant capex expected at Rs 60-70 crores.
items.quote: And the MPP-2, we are expecting a CAPEX in the range of Rs. 60 crores to Rs. 70 crores.

items.statement: Dahej operations targeted EBITDA positive in FY27 with 80% capacity utilization.
items.quote: We are working for making Dahej operations EBITDA positive in FY'27 and try to reach 80% capacity utilization of the existing plant.

items.statement: Three new product launches planned for FY27: two fungicides and one spray enhancer.
items.quote: So we have lined up three new launches for next year, out of which two would be fungicides and both of them would be 9(3) first time introductions.

items.statement: Bayer products FY26 revenue expected around Rs 30 crores, lower than earlier Rs 40 crores.
items.quote: It would be significantly lower than Rs. 40 Cr. Maybe around Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Technical sales expected to grow 10-20% next year.
items.quote: Technical sale would be sort of in line with this current year, maybe 10%-20% growth.

items.statement: Regulatory changes on four biostimulant products caused Rs 49 crore impact in 9M FY26.
items.quote: this year the impact in our Q3 is around Rs. 15 crore and 9 month is the impact of Rs. 49 crore on account of these four products biostimulant stock sale basically.

items.statement: Three biostimulant product approvals expected this quarter, launches by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: we are hopeful of getting out of our, at least 3 products approval in this quarter, so that we can launch by Q1 ending.

items.statement: China export rebate changes may raise some commodity prices but no material sourcing impact; costs to be passed on.
items.quote: At Dhanuka, we kind of significantly follow this practice of passing on the increased cost as much as possible downstream.

items.statement: Q4 started well; Rabi harvest and Kharif outlook positive but too early to guide Kharif.
items.quote: So, Q4 has really started well. January has done well for us.

items.statement: Cash on books more than Rs 250 crore.
items.quote: It is more than Rs.250 crore.

items.statement: New Pune assembly business to add ₹250-300 crore over 3 years, with ₹70-75 crore in FY27.
items.quote: this capex that we talking about should bring in this assembly business with four or five projects over a 3-year period. It could be in the in the range of 250 to 300 cror es. With the first year this FY27 being about 70-75 crores out of that
