items.quote: the practical capacity of this plant is around 350 million, okay? And we have given a very bold statement of 20% to 30% utilization. Right now we are around 60 million, 70 million type of number we are hitting.

items.statement: BIS certification for flashlights expected to support organized players from next year, closing price gap with unbranded.
items.quote: Regulatory developments such as mandatory implementation of BIS certification are expected to support medium-term growth for organized players by accelerating formalization within the category from next year.

items.statement: Alkaline volume share reached almost 19% in December 2025, growing 72%.
items.quote: Alkaline volume shares continued its upwards trajectory, reaching almost 19% in December '25.

items.statement: Rural demand stable, urban selective; discretionary spends measured.
items.quote: Urban consumption remained selective, while rural demand remained relatively stable, supported by post-monsoon cash flows, improving agri realizations and festive season spillovers.

items.statement: Zinc prices and dollar strength caused input cost pressure; gross margin fell 150 bps YoY.
items.quote: Zinc prices moved higher and the U.S. dollar strengthened, leading to elevated input cost pressures across the manufacturing sectors.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR317 crores; net working capital contained below 15% of revenue.
items.quote: During the quarter net debt reduced to INR317 crores post investment of INR167 crores in the Jammu alkaline facility.

items.statement: Jammu plant breakeven from day 1; 10% operating margin improvement from domestic manufacturing vs imports.
items.quote: the plant will be a breakeven from the day 1 because we will also be manufacturing some other products there to ensure that we don't lose the leverage on the production from the day 1.

items.statement: Jammu plant investment INR180 crores approved, 90% already spent.
items.quote: we have approval around INR180 crore, 90% odd has already been done.

items.statement: Closing order book will be larger than opening each quarter; order intake not an issue.
items.quote: Each quarter my closing -- our closing order book will be larger than the opening order book. And each quarter our supplies are increasing. In spite of that our closing order book would be more.

items.statement: Current order book 6.4 GW; book-to-bill 1.9x; 51% C&I, 36% bidding, 13% PSU.
items.quote: Yet again, highest ever order book of 6.4 gigawatt reaffirming our market leadership, powered by over 3 gigawatt new order wins in this financial year itself, resulting in book-to-bill ratio of 1.9x.

items.statement: 3-4 GW non-bidding order discussions ongoing.
items.quote: The order pipeline is strong. as we speak today, we are now clearly talking about three to four gigawatts non bidding route of discussions are happening.

items.statement: OMS EBITDA margin at 40%; AI expected to help sustain or increase it.
items.quote: Second thing is today I am at 40% EBITDA margin, plus how do I not just sustain can I increase this margin. This is what AI would help me.

items.statement: Establishing three new AI-enabled smart blade factories.
items.quote: We are also establishing three new AI-enabled smart blade factories, further expanding our footprint.

items.statement: India wind installations to surpass 10 GW over next 2 years; 100 GW by 2030.
items.quote: Industry is well positioned to move to higher installation year-after-year with a clear trajectory to surpass 10 gigawatt over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Execution delays due to land, ROW, grid connectivity; expects Q4 jump.
items.quote: We are reasonably confident that by end of this year especially in the quarter 4 you will see a significant jump in terms of our execution.

items.statement: Working capital to remain high due to public sector projects; development company to help from FY28.
items.quote: working capital requirements today Sudhanshu as long as we keep doing this public sector projects these projects would continue to be at a high level. It may not significantly increase but will remain at this levels.

items.statement: 5 MW turbine in proto stage; 3.3 MW introduced with lower LCOE.
items.quote: our 5 megawatt turbine is now getting into the proto stage and that will come at appropriate time. But the thing let me tell you is that the in spite of the fact there is a 5 megawatt turbine launched, our 3.15 megawatt is going significantly.

items.statement: Exports: orders expected next financial year, revenue from FY28; US market wait and watch.
items.quote: you will see some traction some terms of orders getting announced in the next financial year, but the supply starting and the revenue flowing in will be in FY28.

items.statement: Deferred tax assets: INR1,100 crores remaining; no cash tax on INR4,400 crores cumulative profit.
items.quote: Even as on today, we still have INR1,100 crores more deferred tax assets sitting in our bank. Even if we don't recognize anything further up to INR4,400 crores of cumulative profit from now on what we get we will not pay single rupee of tax.

items.statement: Plans to open about 150 screens next year, gross additions with negligible exits.
items.quote: And next year, we are looking at about 150-odd screens to open.

items.statement: Capex outlay for next year between Rs. 350-400 crores, including new screens, renovations, and maintenance.
items.quote: Yes, it will be between Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores of CAPEX outlay that we are planning for next year, all inclusive, including new screens plus renovations and maintenance.

items.statement: On track to add nearly 100 new screens in FY2026.
items.quote: Year-to-date, we have added 62 new screens and exited 11 loss-making screens, and are on track to add nearly 100 new screens in FY 2026.

items.statement: Expects slight increase in margins, with bulk already achieved.
items.quote: So I would say that to answer your question straight, in terms of margin there will be a slight increase, but a bulk of the margins is already--

items.statement: Confident that 2026 and 2027 will surpass 2025 performance due to strong content.
items.quote: The kind of content mix we have in Hollywood, Hindi and regional cinema is so strong that we would stick our neck out and say that 2026, 2027 definitely would surpass what we have seen in 2025, 2026.

items.statement: Occupancies are sustainable and best years are ahead.
items.quote: I think these occupancies definitely are sustainable. And the reason we say that is that post-COVID, of course, there were a lot of structural changes, consumption pattern changes.

items.statement: Expects gross debt to fall materially by end of financial year through prepayments.
items.quote: So we are expecting that gross debt levels will also fall materially by the time we finish this financial year.

items.statement: No plans to impair goodwill.
items.quote: No, there are no such plans as of now.

items.statement: No guidance on dividend or buyback at this stage.
items.quote: At this stage, there is no guidance on any dividend or distribution.

items.statement: Promoter pledge levels expected to remain stable.
items.quote: On the promoter pledge, I think the pledge levels have been pretty sort of at the same level for quite some time. We do not expect that to change, or rather we do not expect that to increase.

items.statement: No plans to re-enter film production.
items.quote: At this point, we have no plans to go back to production.

items.statement: Advertising revenue expected to marginally grow over last year.
items.quote: But having said that, we believe that we are on the path of being able to post a marginal growth over last year.

items.statement: Group revenue CAGR target of 12-14% over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Overall, at a group level, we are looking at a 12% to 14% revenue growth in the next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: India operations expected to grow from FY27 onwards due to trade deals.
items.quote: we expect higher volumes, increased sourcing from India and growth in our India operations from 2027 financial year onwards.

items.statement: Bangladesh capacity expansion to complete by Q2 FY27, adding 6 million pieces.
items.quote: Our capacity expansion plan remains on track for completion by second quarter of financial year '27. This will lift the capacity by about another 6 million pieces in Bangladesh

items.statement: Bangladesh capex: INR110 crores allocated, INR66 crores committed.
items.quote: Out of INR110 crores allocated, INR66 crores has already been committed.

items.statement: Sustainable laundry capacity expansion to complete by Q2 FY27, INR90 crores allocated.
items.quote: Construction of the laundry facility is targeted for completion by quarter 2 FY '27 out of INR90 crores allocated, INR51 crores has been committed.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margin at group level next financial year.
items.quote: Next financial year, we are well positioned to achieve this double-digit number.

items.statement: Guatemala losses to reduce substantially and reach breakeven in FY27.
items.quote: Guatemala losses should reduce substantially in FY '27 onwards or it should reach a breakeven in the next financial year itself.

items.statement: Indonesia EBITDA margin expected to become double-digit next year and year after.
items.quote: We expect it to be double digit in the next year and year after.

items.statement: U.S. tariff reduction from 50% to 18% improves India's export competitiveness.
items.quote: A major and long-awaited development was the India-U.S. bilateral trade deal, which reduces the tariff from 50% to 18%, significantly enhancing the India's textile export competitiveness.

items.statement: Discounts given to U.S. clients for tariff will be reversed if tariff is reversed.
items.quote: when the customer had asked for these discounts, we have said that if the tariff gets reversed, then these discounts also will be reversed.

items.statement: U.S. retailers increasing price tickets surgically, not across all products.
items.quote: there is an increase in the U.S. market in terms of price ticket, but it has been done surgically. It is not done across all products across all retailers.

items.statement: Slight decrease in buying numbers as retailers increase price tickets.
items.quote: what we are seeing is a slight decrease in the buying numbers.

items.statement: Bangladesh faces competition as India gains FTA advantages, but no immediate impact.
items.quote: I don't see an immediate impact on Bangladesh, but yes, there will be this competition as these countries like India and all really ramps up there, then definitely, there should be some competition in Bangladesh, but still some time to -- before that.

items.statement: Target to double AUM, income, and PAT over next 3 years, maintaining asset quality below 1%.
items.quote: Over the next 3 years, our objective is clear to double our AUM, income and PAT while preserving best-in-class asset quality.

items.statement: Expects to maintain 25% AUM CAGR over next 3 years with similar profitability.
items.quote: So a combination of all these factors, which is geographical expansion, product expansion and distribution will allow us to maintain our 25% CAGR of AUM expansion over the next three years and also remain a profitable franchise by giving a similar CAGR to all our stakeholders and investors.

items.statement: Adding five new products to existing five, with partnerships including Eicher, Kirloskar, Sterling and Wilson.
items.quote: we are going to be closing this year again by doubling our product suite by adding about five new products on top of the existing five products for which we already have some key institutional partnerships and three big pipeline partnerships with Eicher, Kirloskar and Sterling and Wilson.

items.statement: NIM guidance of 6% for full year already achieved; will maintain same for this year.
items.quote: In terms of our NIM outlook, we had projected and guided for about a 6% NIM achievement on the full year basis. So we have already achieved the same. So we are going to maintain the same for this year.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing target for this year was 10.5%, already achieved at 10.3%.
items.quote: our full year target for this year cost of borrowing, which was given in quarter one of this year was 10.5%. So we have already achieved it and we are at 10.3%.

items.statement: Raised INR 1,885 million at 8.5% via NCDs and CPs; will continue targeting similar instruments to reduce cost of funds.
items.quote: we have been able to raise about Rs.188 Crores last quarter in a mix of NCDs and CPEs at 8.5%, which has been a fairly good achievement for the company.

items.statement: Entire INR 1,885 million raised will be used for portfolio expansion.
items.quote: The entire money raised will go into portfolio expansion.

items.statement: SBI-MSME co-lending partnership start delayed to Q1 FY27 due to RBI guideline compliance; SBI bullish.
items.quote: although we had guided that the new SBI-MSME co-lending partnership shall start from quarter 4, we are still in the process of integrating our systems with their systems and hopefully we should be able to start it in quarter 1 as of now.

items.statement: AI-enabled customer app first phase expected live by end of next quarter (Q3 FY27).
items.quote: The AI-enabled public customer app is under development stage, and the first phase of the app is expected to go live by the end of next quarter 3 of the upcoming fiscal year.

items.statement: Operating leverage to remain similar in medium term, stabilize by end of 3-year roadmap.
items.quote: in the medium term, we have guided that we will be maintaining almost similar operational leverages. And by the time we achieve our three-year strategic roadmap map outlook, we should see stabilization in these levels.

items.statement: Geographical concentration in Delhi, UP, Maharashtra, Haryana, Rajasthan to reduce below 20% each over 3 years.
items.quote: over the next three years, you will see that this strategy will play out well and each trade contributing less than 20% on the overall book.

items.statement: Promoters increased stake by 4.7% this fiscal year, close to SEBI 5% limit; no buyback or bonus planned.
items.quote: the promoters have this year added about 4.7% on a fiscal year basis and 0.5% of that is in Q3 alone. If SEBI allows the promoter to increase their stake by 5% in a fiscal year basis so we are very close to that.

items.statement: FCCB conversion decision lies with investors; management believes investors are bullish and will convert over time.
items.quote: The investors are bullish on the company and will look forward to converting their shares with the passage of time.

items.statement: Gross NPA guided below 2%, currently far below at 0.83%.
items.quote: We have always guided for less than 2% NPA levels and we are far, far below our guided range.

items.statement: CAPEX plan for current fiscal year is Rs. 13,300 Crore and next year Rs. 15,000 Crore.
items.quote: The CAPEX plan for the current fiscal year is Rs. 13,300 Crore and next year , we are planning to spend Rs. 15,000 Crore.

items.statement: Average annual CAPEX will be Rs. 12,000 to 13,000 Crore.
items.quote: Thereafter, on an average, our annual CAPEX will be in the range of Rs. 12,000 to 13,000 Crore.

items.statement: By end of March 2026, additional capacity of 2100 MW to be added.
items.quote: So, by the end of March ’26, we are going to add additional capac ity of 2100 MW.

items.statement: Next year capacity addition will be 2744 MW from hydro.
items.quote: Next year, our capacity addition will be 2744 MW from hydro.

items.statement: Most solar capacity under construction (1,190 MW) planned to be added by end of next financial year.
items.quote: Renewable as CMD sir has shared with you that currently our solar capacity under construction is 1,190 MW and most of the solar capacity , we are planning to add by end of next financial year.

items.statement: Planning to start at least two PSP projects of around 2,000 MW during this calendar year.
items.quote: So, we are planning to start at least two projects of around 2,000 MW out of these four during this calendar year

items.statement: Expect to sign PPAs for 2,000 to 3,000 MW in next 2 to 3 months.
items.quote: But I am still hopeful that in next 2 to 3 months, we may sign PPA of around 2,000 to 3,000 MW also.

items.statement: Targeting commissioning of all remaining four units of Subansiri Lower by December 2026.
items.quote: We are targeting to commission all the remaining four units by December '26.

items.quote: We are hopeful that we will complete this project and commission all the thr ee units by October or November'26 which will add 120 MW to our NHPC kitty.

items.statement: Ratle Hydroelectric Project (850 MW) targeted for completion by November 2028.
items.quote: The overall physical progress of the project is 26% and we are targeting to complete it by November'28.

items.statement: Pakal Dul (1000 MW) and Kiru (624 MW) targeted for commissioning by December 2026.
items.quote: We are targeting to commi ssion all the units by December '26 and considering the current pace of the progress, we are confident that we will achieve this target.

items.statement: Kwar HE Project (540 MW) targeted for completion by March 2028.
items.quote: Its physical progress is around 27% and the targeted date of completion for this project is March'28

items.statement: Teesta-VI targeted for commissioning in 2029.
items.quote: But , we are very much sure that we will achieve the targeted commissioning of 2029 in this project also.

items.statement: Dibang Multipurpose Project (2880 MW) targeted for completion by 2032.
items.quote: All the works are in full swing and we hope that whatever target we have fixed for 2032, we will do our best and make all the efforts to achieve that target.

items.statement: Targets 20%+ revenue growth, aiming to cross INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY27.
items.quote: So we continuously have a target of approximate 20 plus percent in terms of revenue growth. So definitely this year and next year, our vision statement was clear. By 2027, we are crossing INR 1,000 crore of revenue mark

items.statement: Gross margin to be 58-59% with potential 1-5% improvement.
items.quote: in terms of gross margin, 58%-59%, we are operating and this is probably couple of percentage or 5% may improve.

items.statement: Plans to open 75 new stores annually, with average size 1600-1700 sq ft.
items.quote: we plan to open 75 new stores in a year. And the size of the store is increasing because we are opening the average store size of 1600 to 1700 square feet now.

items.statement: Targets 6-7% same store sales growth (SSG) long-term.
items.quote: we are targeting 6%, 5%-6%, which is a long-term sustainable number. Maybe a couple of quarters up and down, but long-term sustainable number is approximately 6%-7%.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin improvement of a couple of percentage points.
items.quote: a couple of percentage of margin improvement in terms of EBITDA is always there. We are targeting that.

items.statement: E-commerce to contribute 8-10% of revenue next year.
items.quote: next year, by the 1000, we are targeting 8%-10%.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve to 12-13%.
items.quote: We are expecting a PAT margin because of GST rationalization and everything. That is 12%. Maybe it is maybe 13%.

items.statement: Passed on GST benefits to customers, supporting demand.
items.quote: we have been passed on whatever the GST benefit has been there to the consumer, right, whatever the inventory we had.

items.statement: GST rationalization boosted consumer momentum, expected to continue.
items.quote: GST rationalization has definitely made the changes in terms of overall business, specifically for retail. So momentum is there and it looks like long term.

items.statement: Family stores have 2% higher EBITDA than men's stores; focus on bigger stores.
items.quote: EBITDA is 2% higher in the family stores than the men's store.

items.statement: Online sales return rate is 32-33%, industry standard around 30%.
items.quote: we also have a return percentage of around 32%-33% and we are trying our best to just get it down around that 50% mark.

items.statement: Inventory days target 110-120 days, working capital 100-105 days.
items.quote: working capital 100 to 105 days and inventory days is in between 110 to 120 days.

items.statement: Repeat customer rate increased from 44% to 50-52% over four years.
items.quote: it started in 4 years back 44% and approximately it is operating as of now 50%-52%.

items.statement: Franchise stores constitute 20% of total stores, with commission 27-28%.
items.quote: The total number of franchisee stores is 131 out of total 646, which is 20%.

items.statement: Order book over Rs. 163 billion, with 64% EPC and 36% O&M.
items.quote: Our order book continued to expand with strategic wins and currently stands at over Rs. 163 billion. It remains well balanced, with 64% EPC and 36% O&M projects, providing strong revenue visibility and deeper client relationships.

items.statement: Preferred bidder in over Rs. 3,000 crores worth of projects.
items.quote: We are a preferred bidder in over Rs. 3,000 crores worth of projects, which also includes projects in the Middle East.

items.statement: Minimal capex, asset-light model with Rs. 5-10 crores depreciation.
items.quote: We hardly have any capex, Kishore. As I said, we are asset light. I mean, Rs. 5 crores to Rs. 10 crores of depreciation is what we do. So hardly any capex.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining EBITDA margin at 13-15% despite commodity price changes.
items.quote: So this gives us confidence that we will maintain it at the 13% to 15%.

items.statement: Strong order pipeline with conversions expected early next year.
items.quote: As far as pipeline is concerned, we see a very strong pipeline. Some of them have only got deferred, which is going beyond this quarter. But early next year, we see many of those prospects converting.

items.statement: International revenue at 50% of total, expected to increase.
items.quote: We are at about 50% right now. And we have already stated that we want to keep expanding globally, and look at improving our international business while continuing to remain a market leader in India.

items.statement: No exposure on states; projects must be multilaterally funded, sovereign backed, or LC backed.
items.quote: We will not take any exposure on the states, and this is a stated position from our side.

items.statement: Norfund investment platform due diligence largely over, definitive agreements in advanced stage.
items.quote: The due diligence is largely over. And we are right now in the process of negotiating the definitive agreements. So in the next couple of months, we are hopeful subject to, of course, you know the multilateral funds or the large funds will have their own internal investment committees, Board procedures.

items.statement: GNN HAM project borrowing to be excluded from books by year-end.
items.quote: Our aim is to do it by the year-end. Of course, as I said, we are at a very mature stage. We should be done with most of the activities, subject to the timelines of the investors' investment committee and Board approving.

items.statement: Free cash generation of about Rs. 300 crores for 9M FY26.
items.quote: For the 9 months, roughly the free cash generation is about Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Net cash position over Rs. 1,000 crores, 12th consecutive quarter net cash positive.
items.quote: Excluding the transient debt under our HAM entity, net cash stood at over Rs. 1,000 crores, a historic high for the group, reinforcing the strength of our balance sheet and capital discipline.

items.statement: Indore terminal to be operational in 2 years with 120,000 TEUs annual capacity.
items.quote: So it should be operational within 2 years, and we're looking at about 120,000 TEUs per year capacity at the terminal.

items.statement: FY27 margins to follow similar trend; volume mix to change with domestic and Ankleshwar.
items.quote: No. See, a similar trend basically, but there will be a change in volume mix with domestic and Ankleshwar and depending on what locations are growing. So it's hard to give it on a per TEU basis right now. But if you look at our percentage margins, we'd like to keep the same trend going.

items.statement: Expects US trade deal to boost exports of handicrafts, textiles, leather, chemicals; awaiting fine print.
items.quote: So, after the announcement of this U.S. trade deal, so we are expecting a major traction, especially in the exports of handicrafts, textiles, leather and chemicals. And right now, we have 25% of U.S. sales of the total volume kitty we have export. So we are expecting that with this deal, the U.S. bound exports, they ar

items.quote: And apart from this U.S. trade deal, we are also hopeful this EU trade deal. So there also, we are having an exposure – about 10% of the exports are going to EU countries from our ICD. So there also, we are expecting increase in the volumes, especially in terms of exports of handicrafts and textiles.

items.statement: DFC JNPT connection expected by end of March; may shift Mundra and road volumes to JNPT.
items.quote: Yes. So the last connection to JNPT DFC corridor is expected by end of March. And once this gets completed, so we are expecting some volume to get moving. So basically, what we are expecting that there will be some shift of Mundra volumes towards JNPT.

items.statement: Snowman able to pass on cost increases; got price hikes in all contracts in last 5-6 months.
items.quote: Yes, we are able to get those price hikes in all our last contracts, which have been done in last 5 to 6 months, we have got the price hike.

items.statement: Dry pallet realizations improved from INR600-700 to INR850-1,000, improving quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: If I say earlier, the dry pallet, we were selling in the range of INR600 to INR700. Today, we sell in the range of INR850 to INR1, 000, and it is improving every quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Jaipur land dispute: INR8-9 crores aggregator land under dispute; INR21 crores owned land clear; INR5 crores with railways.
items.quote: So the owned land by us is about INR21 crores. The aggregator land is about INR8 crores to INR9 crores. And then we've deposited with railways, but then we got the work stopped. So that's -- it's flying with railways about INR5 crores. But in case -- I mean, that's just the project when it goes through, that will be ut

items.statement: Snowman capacity to expand from 155,000 to 200,000 pallets in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Regarding Snowman turnaround, we are focused on top line and EBITDA expansion right now, and we're in still a growth phase where we want to more than -- our capacity is 155,000. We want to take it to 200,000 in the next 2, 3 years, and we want to build on that further.

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Expects adjusted EBITDA margin to improve from 13% to 17% over next 2 years.
items.quote: I expect that to be 17% over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Expects ROCE to reach 14% in 2-3 years as new initiatives break even.
items.quote: I expect around 14% is where we will end up in the business.

items.statement: Maintains 12% CAGR growth guidance with FY24-25 as base year.
items.quote: So FY'24-'25 is the base year, and we will grow at 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Plans capex of EUR2-3 million outside India and Rs.70-80 crore in India over 12-18 months.
items.quote: But out of India, the expected outflow would be in the range of EUR2 million to EUR3 million and India would be in the range of Rs. 70 crore to Rs. 80 crore.

items.statement: Gross margin to improve from Q4 FY26 onwards, currently at lower end of range.
items.quote: We are at 42.4% or something, we are at the lower end of the gross margin range that the business will operate at.

items.statement: U.S. Creative Development Centre secured first customer order, to be executed from Q4 FY26.

items.statement: India demand recovery slower than expected post-GST changes; expects to recover sales momentum shortly.
items.quote: We have not seen that play out. So, we did see some uptick during the Diwali. But after that, we are not seeing a broad-based demand jump as what we were expecting.

items.statement: 85% of products are proprietary, providing good pricing power to pass on cost increases.

items.statement: Debt levels may increase near-term due to strategic initiatives and capacity expansion.

items.statement: Insurance claim of ~Rs.100 crore expected to be settled in 6-12 months.
items.quote: So, we are expecting in and around Rs. 100 crore, and we do not see a risk on that.

items.statement: Higher insurance premium of Rs.13-13.5 crore annually may continue for another year.
items.quote: So roughly around Rs. 13 crore to Rs. 13.5 crore , we are spending higher than normal in a year.

items.statement: Fragrance EBIT margin expected to improve to 13-14% as international businesses ramp up.
items.quote: As outside India businesses ramp up, it will be 13% to 14% EBIT.

items.statement: New Europe facility operational by end of Q4 FY26; India facility by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Quarter 4, the new facility will be operational, maybe end of quarter 4, March is the current expected timeline. So, quarter 1, I expect both the new facility in Europe as well as the new facility in India to be operational.

items.statement: Targets 20% to 25% growth for the next 5 years.
items.quote: Yes, we have already said that for the next 5 years, our target is to achieve 20% to 25% growth.

items.statement: Visa business margins expanded to upwards of 40% in recent years.
items.quote: I mean visa business also, if you see the margin has expanded to upwards of 40% now in the last few years.

items.statement: Digital margins contracted due to Aadifidelis acquisition at 3% to 4% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: As we explained earlier, this is because of the Aadifidelis, the new acquisition we did last year. And there, the margins are around 3% to 4% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Mix expected to be maintained as both visa and digital segments see major growth.
items.quote: So we definitely feel the mix will maintain because we see major growth coming in both the segments of the business.

items.statement: Expects good revenue jump from China operations in future.
items.quote: Yes. We see a good jump in revenue in the future.

items.statement: Growth seen across Middle East, East Asia, India, China, Latin America; trend to continue.
items.quote: We have seen good growth coming in from the Middle Eastern market, the East Asian market, India, China, Latin American countries, definitely, the trend we see continuing.

items.statement: Potential volume recovery from Russia-Ukraine region if war streamlines; pre-war was big volume.
items.quote: Going forward, definitely, the re is some war that is happening between Russia and Ukraine that gets streamlined, which there is hope.

items.statement: Europe-India trade deal could increase volumes in future once ratified.
items.quote: But definitely, there will be a jump in the relationship between Europe and India. And definitely, we see that volumes cou ld increase in the future because of that.

items.statement: Initial investment in new contracts like Slovak Republic, then streamlined with economies of scale.

items.statement: Committed to 20-25% revenue growth over medium term with healthy EBITDA margins and net debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: China iron phosphate prices increased 15-20% due to VAT rebate elimination; supports pricing narrative.

items.statement: Passed on 90% of US tariff impact to customers; no margin dilution.

items.statement: North America expected significant revenue and margin expansion in FY27 due to trade deal and wallet share gains.
items.quote: And if this were to realize, then in FY '27, we'll see, I would say, North America again, significant revenue and growth and margin expansion, all three coming from this market.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients to be key growth driver for next two years; utilization to ramp up.
items.quote: So, we see this segment being a, I would say, key growth driver for the next two years for Su deep.

items.statement: Customer approvals for new facility take 6-12 months; H1 FY27 focused on approvals.
items.quote: I think what happens typically is once we commission the facility, we will have typically a 6 to 12 -month period where majority of the customer approvals will happen.

items.statement: NSS acquisition margin profile now similar to Sudeep; expected to grow 15% annually.
items.quote: NSS has been growing typically, I would say, 15% odd percent historically, and at least for the next year or two that will continue.

items.statement: Expects full-year FY26 production of 28,500-29,500 metric tons.
items.quote: Given our current capacity and a robust demand environment, we have the capability to produce 28,500 to 29,500 metric tons for the full year.

items.statement: Expects similar volume increase in Q4 as seen in Q3.
items.quote: Similar increase we are expecting.

items.statement: Targets 80-85% utilization on 43,000 MT capacity next year.
items.quote: And on this 43 you could probably, 80-85 would be our target, of course, 85%.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton of INR65,000-66,000 is sustainable.
items.quote: we feel the 65, 66, 67,000 number is a sustainable number for us.

items.statement: Phase 2 expansion to complete in 14 months, doubling capacity to 59,045 MT.
items.quote: Once Phase 2 of our expansion is completed in 14 months' time, we would have an installed capacity of 59,045 metric tons, annualized.

items.statement: Spent INR5.4 crores on new machinery in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Additionally, in Q3 FY ‘26, the company spent INR5.4 crores towards the purchase of new machinery.

items.statement: Supplying specialized wires for 37 HVDC transformers over 12-18 months.
items.quote: During the third quarter, we commenced supplying specialized winding wires towards cumulative orders of 37 HVDC transformers received to date.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton for 9M FY26 at INR66,000, sustainable.
items.quote: EBITDA per ton for 9 months of FY '26 was approximately INR66,000 per metric ton, which is almost similar to Q3 FY '25 and up from INR50,000 for 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: Copper prices are a direct pass-through, no exposure.
items.quote: Thus, LME copper prices and exchange rate is a direct pass-through, and we do not take any exposure to short or long-term variations in the copper price.

items.statement: Specialized winding wires ~75% of revenue; focus on higher value-added segments.
items.quote: Specialized winding wires represented approximately 75% of total revenue, excluding other operating revenue in 9 months and Q3 of FY ‘26 and increased 48% and 61% versus a year ago.

items.statement: US duty on value addition expected 18-25%, down from 54%.
items.quote: And now, of course, this is still work in progress because we are hearing conflicting information between 18% to 25%.

items.statement: Repaid INR225.9 crores debt, reducing debt-to-equity to 0.42x.
items.quote: In late December 2025, we repaid INR225.9 crores of long-term and short-term debt, including the term debt taken for financing the Supa Phase 1 expansion.

items.statement: Working capital days 75-80, expected to trend lower.
items.quote: Finally, working capital days remain in the 75-80 day range calculated on a closing balances basis during Q3 FY ‘26, though we expect this to start trending lower incrementally over the next several quarters.

items.statement: Normalized performance more visible in FY27; positive results expected.
items.quote: It would be more visible during FY'27. As we said earlier, we are in the path of normalization. In pockets, there are still some additional corrections which we need to take. And therefore, by FY'27, we should start seeing positive results.

items.statement: Improvement starting Q4, substantial improvement next year.
items.quote: The improvement you'll see starting with the fourth quarter. But next year should be showing a substantial improvement because all those corrective actions which we are talking about, by doing that, your cost is coming down, and therefore, your margin obviously improves.

items.statement: Price increase of 2-5% effective Feb 1, 2026 to cover commodity inflation.
items.quote: Yes. We took -- we have already announced a price increase ranging from 2% to 5% from -- with effect from 1st of February.

items.statement: Expect to cover bulk of commodity inflation with price increase and VA/VE.
items.quote: We expect to cover bulk of the commodity inflation with this price increase. Plus, at the same time, we continue to do activities around VAVE - value engineering and value addition.

items.statement: Lighting Solutions EBIT ~7% vs 2% last year, confident to continue momentum.
items.quote: Against the H1 revenue growth of 6%, we have accelerated our growth to 9% this quarter, owing to high mix towards focus categories like ceiling and outdoor lights, which has also helped achieve EBIT of close to 7% versus last year of 2%.

items.statement: Consumer Products EBIT negative due to operating deleverage.
items.quote: The EBIT margins were negative owing to operating deleverage.

items.statement: Channel inventory normalization to continue; healthy in a quarter or so.
items.quote: We expect the normalization process to continue; in a quarter or so, we should be in a healthy place.

items.statement: Summer product channel inventory still high; normalization as season picks up.
items.quote: There are still certain pockets, especially the summer -related products, where the channel inventory remains high, and we look forward to its normalization as season picks up.

items.statement: Entered switchgear, solar, wires; building integrated portfolio for long-term growth.
items.quote: As part of this strategy, we initially entered the Switchgear segment in Q2, followed by the announcement of our foray into solar solutions in Q3 and, more recently, the launch of wires this month.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 211 crores; cash balance INR 620 crores.
items.quote: A part of this is already getting reflected in this quarter' s cash flow from operations, where we have generated operating cash flow of INR 211 crores and ended the period with a cash and cash equivalent balance of INR 620 crores.

items.statement: Consumer Products channel inventory days down 30%.
items.quote: So if I have to elaborate from the number of days, we just want to give you a fact that in Consumer Products, it is down by 30% in terms of number of days.

items.statement: Summer season did not meet expectations, leading to high channel inventory.
items.quote: If I look back at the year so far, we have seen that the summer season did not pan out as per the expectations. And owing to that, the channel was carrying a significant amount of inventory.

items.statement: Working on 3-year plan for new categories; numbers not yet finalized.
items.quote: As of now, we are working on 3 years plan. We will not be able to reveal numbers till we finalize that with the Board.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on channel stocking, dependent on summer season.
items.quote: So going forward, we remain cautiously optimistic that there would not be any resistance from the channel partners or distributors in stocking up. Of course, it is dependent on how the season pans out and how the summers pan out.

items.statement: Expects 5-6% higher crushing this season versus last year.
items.quote: As highlighted in our opening remarks, we expect a 5% to 6% increase in crushing this year compared with last year.

items.statement: Full-year sugar cost of production expected around INR 37.5 per kg.
items.quote: So for the full year, we are expecting in the region of around INR 37.5 per kg.

items.statement: FY26 ethanol sales expected between 26 and 27 crore liters.
items.value: 26 crore liter to R27 crore liter
items.quote: Looks like between 26 crore liter to R27 crore liter.

items.statement: Hopes to crush over 10.5 crore quintals this year, ~6% growth; facilities can handle 11.5 crore quintals.
items.quote: We are hoping to crush over 10.5 crore quintals this year which represents an increase of about 58 to 60 lakh quintals over last year, translating to nearly 6% growth. With the capex already completed, our facilities can very comfortably handle 11.5 crore quintals.

items.statement: PLA project cumulative expenditure INR 1,421 crore as of 31 Jan, funded by INR 790 crore debt and internal accruals.
items.quote: As of 31st January, cumulative project expenditures stood at INR 1,421 crore, funded through a combination of INR 790 crore in debt and the balance through internal accruals.

items.statement: February UP sugar prices INR 41-41.5/kg; expects gradual increase as year progresses.
items.quote: In February, sugar prices for UP mills, including our factories, ranged between INR 41 and INR 41.5 per kilogram . We believe prices may gradually inch upward as the year progresses.

items.statement: UP cane prices raised by INR 30, adding cost pressure.
items.quote: In UP, cane prices have been raised by INR 30.

items.statement: Ethanol prices under B-heavy and juice routes unchanged for three years despite 16.4% FRP increase.
items.quote: Despite a 16.4% increase in FRP and rising operating costs, ethanol prices under the B-heavy and juice routes have not been revised for the past three years.

items.statement: Sugar consumption estimated 288-290 lakh tonnes; no inventory addition, marginal depletion expected.
items.quote: Consumption estimates range between 288 and 290 lakh tonnes. Therefore, without going into minor variations of 1 or 2 lakh tonnes, the broad assumption is that there will be no addition to inventory and, in fact, a marginal depletion.

items.statement: Diverted one distillery unit to C-heavy to maximize sugar production due to no ethanol price hike.
items.quote: So what we have done pursuant to the fact that government did not increase price, we have already diverted one of our units to C-heavy.

items.statement: No ethanol price revision indicated; prices across C-heavy, B-heavy, and juice likely unchanged.
items.quote: Hence, prices across all products — C-heavy, B-heavy, and juice — are likely to remain unchanged.

items.statement: Recovery improvement now expected only 0.10-0.15% due to poor sunlight, down from earlier 0.2-0.3%.
items.quote: Therefore, an improvement of 0.2 % to 0.3 % may now be difficult, but an improvement of around 0.10% to 0.15% could still be possible.

items.statement: Labour code impact of INR152 crores consolidated and INR138 crores standalone accounted in Q3 as exceptional item.
items.value: INR152 crores consolidated, INR138 crores standalone
items.quote: The impact on a consolidated level is INR152 crores, which has been shown an exceptional item in the consolidated as well as INR138 crores in stand-alone financials.

items.statement: January was a good month for jewellery, but volatile gold rate makes it too early to guide for Q4.
items.quote: For the fourth quarter, we've just seen a month gone by and I'd like to leave it by saying it's been a good month.

items.statement: Introduced 18-carat traditional gold jewellery in North and East; seeding in West and South.
items.quote: introducing 18-carat traditional gold jewellery also in certain parts of the country where we have seen a greater openness to it.

items.quote: We always had 14-carat jewellery in both CaratLane and Mia, but now we've also introduced that in Tanishq and also up to 9 carat in CaratLane and Mia.

items.statement: EBIT profit growth in absolute amount becoming more important than profitability margin due to rising gold.
items.quote: The EBIT profit growth in absolute amount is becoming more and more important than profitability margin because profitability margin increasingly is becoming challenging in the rising gold environment.

items.statement: No one-offs in Q3; 50 bps margin drop YoY due to mix and gold price impact.
items.quote: No, in quarter 3, there is no one-off. Last year quarter 3, custom duty gain was there, which you remember, which we normalized. And 50 basis point drop is there in quarter 3 compared to last quarter 3.

items.statement: 20-25% of business from jewellery purchase plans; more customers prefer Golden Advantage over Golden Harvest.
items.quote: anywhere from 20% to 25% of our business comes from our jewellery purchase plans, and that's kind of sustained even at this point in time.

items.statement: More than 50% of business has an element of exchange; Q3 saw a good jump.
items.quote: more than 50% of our business today has an element of exchange of either type. And in quarter 3, we saw a good jump in that.

items.statement: International margin was 5-6% in Q3 after adjusting INR200 crores primary sales; expected to improve gradually.
items.quote: international margin had at least onetime this time, this quarter because we had some primary sales of INR200 crores, close to that, and that has -- the -- if you adjust that, the margins are about 5% to 6%.

items.statement: CaratLane expected to stay at low double-digit EBIT margin profile.
items.quote: I think they would stay there, low double-digit margin EBIT profile.

items.statement: Sub-1 lakh studded jewellery under pressure; above 1 lakh different picture; efforts to woo customers back.
items.quote: You're right in saying that we have been seeing pressure sub-1 lakh, not 1 to 2, but sub-1 lakh in studded jewellery but also with gold rate behaving the way they are also in gold jewellery.

items.statement: Expects improved profitability in coming quarters due to U.S. trade deal and other factors.
items.quote: Overall, the company has demonstrated resilient operational progress and basis the recent developments regarding the U.S. trade deal, we are confident of improved profitability in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expects results of initiatives to start showing in FY27.
items.quote: We expect that the result of all the initiatives that we have undertaken on these aspects in last 1 year will start showing in FY '26-'27.

items.statement: Targets increasing specialty share to 70%+ in 3-5 years.
items.quote: We want to take this share up to 70% plus in next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Targets specialty film share from 25% to 50% in 3-5 years.
items.quote: So what we want to do in specialty film share is take this number from 25% to somewhere in the range of 50% over next 3 to 5 years and maybe even more.

items.quote: So Sana, as Vaibhav mentioned, Elite is a key marquee project that we are starting and, as you are aware that the total capex for this project is USD 193 million, which we are planning to fund through our debt and equity.

items.statement: Elite project completion by end of 2027, sales start following quarter.
items.quote: And right now the third strategic priority for us is the successful execution of the Elite project wherein we are expecting to complete the project by end of 2027 and commission the -- or start selling out the product within the following quarter.

items.statement: Nike contract: 3-year take-or-pay for 5,000 tons, may increase to 10,000 tons.
items.quote: So in Nike, we have signed a 3-year contract where Nike is going to buy 5,000 tons of the finished goods from us, which can be -- and it is valid for 3 years post commencement of commercial production.

items.statement: Expects U.S. tariff reduction to boost margins in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: We are still awaiting the clarity from the U.S. customs, but we are expecting it to happen soon, and this shift is expected to boost margins and thereby performance in upcoming quarters.

items.quote: So the spread, which is VA between 12 micron plain film which is the commodity film and the raw material, in January was roughly around INR30.

items.statement: Expects BOPET demand growth of 8-10% annually, exceeding capacity additions.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers expected to grow double-digit YoY for full year and next 3-5 years.
items.quote: On the Specialty Polymer side, we expect a double-digit growth on year-on-year basis for the whole financial year and we would like to keep growing in healthy double digits in Specialty Polymers on a consistent basis for next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Chinese BOPET dumping causing pricing pressure; antidumping investigation ongoing.
items.quote: Chinese price pressure is indeed a pain point in the domestic market. We have seen that the prices of the products coming from China are at a level which has really prevented us from leveraging the demand scenario in India to the fullest extent.

items.statement: Plans to raise 70% debt for Elite project, peak debt around INR1,200-1,250 crores.
items.quote: So Saransh, as we have mentioned that this INR195 million, we are going to fund through a mix of debt and equity. Our target is that we are going to raise 70% of this amount as debt, which amounts to roughly INR1,100 crores.

items.statement: Birla Opus to deliver Rs 10,000 crore revenue in third full year of operation.
items.quote: we continue to guide that we will deliver the Rs.10,000 crores in third full year operation.

items.statement: Birla Pivot to exit FY27 at breakeven.
items.quote: I think from our current estimates, we will exit FY27 at a breakeven level.

items.statement: Paints business targeting profitable #2 position within three years of full-scale operation.
items.quote: Within three years of full scale operation, we are targeting to be able to reach a profitable #2 position.

items.statement: Decorative paints industry expected to grow 5-6% this year, 8-10% in FY27.
items.quote: by FY27, we are hopeful that it will come back to 8% to 10% growth levels.

items.statement: Institutional business share to reach 12-15% by FY27.
items.quote: hopefully by FY27, we should be able to come closer to the industry average between 12%-15% on overall contribution from institutional business.

items.statement: Chemicals renewable energy share to reach over 40% by end FY27.
items.quote: targeting to reach an exit rate of over 40% by end of FY27

items.quote: The capital expenditure spent on YTD basis is Rs.1,310 crores.

items.quote: Focus now remains on phase-1 of Harihar Lyocell project for additional 55,000 MTPA, capacity of specialty fibres.

items.statement: Premium and luxury segments contribute steady 65% of Birla Opus revenue.
items.quote: our growth remains balanced across all categories of paints with premium and luxury segments continues to contribute steady 65% in our overall revenue.

items.statement: Cellulosic fashion yarn business subdued due to cheaper Chinese imports causing oversupply and lower downstream demand.
items.quote: The business performance for the quarter was subdued due to cheaper imports from China, which has created oversupply and lower downstream demand.

items.statement: No significant potential vacancies to report; occupancy remains approximately 99% to 100% of NKP.
items.quote: As of this point, there are no significant potential vacancies to report.

items.quote: Lastly, the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR 15 (150%) per share for FY ’26.

items.statement: Company has approximately Rs. 325 crores cash and bank balance as on 31st January.
items.quote: Approximately Rs. 325 crores.

items.statement: No significant plan or proposal for volume expansion at NKP or other cities currently.
items.quote: Not right now, there is no significant plan or no significant proposal that we are considering at this point.

items.statement: No further updates on restructuring plans; will inform shareholders when definitive decision is taken.
items.quote: there has been no further updates regarding any restructuring plans.

items.statement: Borrowing cost is one month T-bill plus 233 bps, reset monthly; P&L finance cost higher due to Ind-AS security deposit discounting.
items.quote: No, it is one month T-bill, 30 days T-bill plus 233.

items.statement: Company moved to new tax regime from Q2 FY26; tax expense based on new concessional rate.
items.quote: Please note that the company has moved to the new tax regime from Q2 FY ’26 onwards.

items.statement: Defense could rise to 20-30% of overall business from current 10-11%.
items.quote: I think let's look at 20%, 30%.

items.statement: Aerospace segment expected strong growth next year and year after with new programs and capacities.
items.quote: Aerospace segment also we see a very strong growth next year, also year after next because next year we have some new programs and some new capacities coming on line, but significantly larger coming on line year after next.

items.statement: India CV sector for Q4 looks very strong and may continue into first half of next year.
items.quote: The CV sector for Q4 India lo oks very strong and may continue into first half of next year.

items.statement: Exports have bottomed out and gradual improvement expected from here.
items.quote: Exports seem to have bottomed out and we should see a gradual improvement from here.

items.statement: US Class 7,8 truck orders trending up; expects better than last year and stable growth.
items.quote: Well, you've seen the incoming orders in the US for class 7, 8 in the last 2 months, they've been on the upside.

items.statement: Bharat Forge to spend up to INR3,000 crores on Odisha project, starting after next year.
items.quote: So Bharat Forge, we have said up to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: New business worth INR2,388 crores secured last quarter across components, defense, casting, K Drive.
items.quote: In last quarter, the company had secured new business worth INR2,388 crores acros s all key businesses, which includes the component business of INR378 crores, defense of INR1,878 crores, casting INR78 crores, and K Drive INR55 crores.

items.statement: Defense profitability expected comparable to auto on EBITDA basis with better ROCE.
items.quote: Yes, I would expect it to be, profitable equivalent on an EBITDA basis generally speaking.

items.statement: Europe in secular problem; restructuring of European steel business update by end of fiscal.
items.quote: And while we continue to improve our operation, we also continue to evaluate restructuri ng operations for our European steel business and we will update the progress by end of this fiscal.

items.statement: Tariff cost impact of INR31 crores included in Q3 standalone EBITDA.
items.quote: This includes a tariff cost impact of INR31 crores.

items.statement: Premji Invest took 23% stake in JSA at INR1,300 crores valuation.
items.quote: We have now brought in a very high quality investor in the form of Premji Invest, which has invested to take a meaningful stake in the company and it's 23% at a valuation of INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: American Axle acquisition performing well with margins up almost 200 bps.
items.quote: The acquisition has performed well. Our margins have grown by almost 200 basis points.

items.statement: Server business still in development phase.
items.quote: Its still in the development phase.

items.statement: Domestic tractor industry likely to reach new peak of around 11.5 lakh units this fiscal year.
items.quote: Domestic tractor industry is likely to reach a new peak of around 11.5 lakh units this fiscal year.

items.statement: Expect robust growth in Q4 and Q1, but too early to comment on FY27.
items.quote: we see a robust growth in Quarter 4 and also a very robust growth in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Export growth to continue double-digit, though not at 50-60% seen now.
items.quote: we expect it will continue to be double-digit growth in export numbers going forward even from the existing facility.

items.statement: Board approved investment for land acquisition for Greenfield facility; first commercial production planned 2029-30.
items.quote: Right now, what we indicated to the government is to start this somewhere in 2029-30, the first commercial production.

items.statement: Indicative investment of 22.68 million for Greenfield facility, subject to demand.
items.quote: the investment which you have mentioned in the DPR or the project report which has been submitted to UP government is more like indicative.

items.statement: Agri Machinery EBIT margin up 310 bps YoY to 13.5% on easing material costs and operating leverage.
items.quote: EBIT margin for the Agri Machinery business were up by 310 basis points at 13.5% as against 10.4% in the corresponding quarter, led by easing material costs, better operating leverage and cost control measures.

items.statement: Construction equipment EBIT margin at 6.6%, down YoY but up sequentially.
items.quote: EBIT margin for the quarter-ended December 2025 came at 6.6% as against 11% in the corresponding quarter and was up by 280 basis points as against 3.8% in the sequential quarter.

items.statement: Took price increase in construction equipment due to steel price rise; may take similar action in tractors if industry passes on costs.
items.quote: from January itself, I think we have seen the steel prices have gone up. So, which we have taken some price increase in the CE space, but I think the inflation was way more than what we had increased.

items.statement: Construction equipment degrowth narrowing; expect gradual improvement with infrastructure project awards.
items.quote: the level of degrowth in the construction equipment segment is coming down gradually for our volume from around 23.7% in Q1 to 17.8% in Q2 and 13.7% in Q3 and with Jan ending at 3.7%, thus showcasing early sign of stabilization and we expect this gradual improvement to continue

items.statement: Shift towards 45-50 HP tractors due to increased farmer liquidity post GST reduction.
items.quote: over the last three to four months, we have actually seen a shift towards 45-to-50 HP segment. So, that segment in the last four, five months has actually grown.

items.statement: El Nino could impact tractor demand, but better reservoir levels may mitigate.
items.quote: the reservoir levels are better. So, they will help substantially if El Nino actually comes into effect, because the reservoir levels are relatively better because of the last year's rain.

items.statement: New models and upgrades across brands to launch in next 6-8 months; full impact expected by end FY27.
items.quote: In the coming next six-eight months, we will be launching new models and upgrades across all brands to address key product gaps. The full market impact of this refreshed product portfolio is expected in the end of FY27

items.statement: Kubota market share to improve gradually from H2 FY27 with new product launches.
items.quote: we will see a gradual increase in market share in Kubota, I think from H2 onwards

items.statement: Component export to ramp up next year with new transmission line for harvesters.
items.quote: next year almost, we will see probably the good ramp up will happen on the component export.

items.statement: Targets 16-20% organic revenue CAGR, driven by core strengths and new capabilities.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain confident in achieving our targeted growth of 16% to 20% CAGR in organic growth, and this will be driven by accelerating our core strengths, building new capabilities, and selectively expanding into adjacency.

items.statement: Earmarked Rs 500-700 crore for new technologies, product development, and capacity expansion, front-loaded over first two years.
items.quote: Over the coming years, we have earmarked 500 to 700 crores towards new technologies, product development, and capacity expansion.

items.statement: Expects India genset market to grow at 10-12% CAGR over next 5 years.
items.quote: So, the outlook for India's genset market remains robust and we expect a demand growth of 10% to 12% CAGR in the next 5 years.

items.statement: Auto industry expected to grow 6-8% in 2026, supported by GST 2.0 and easing monetary conditions.
items.quote: Here, from a market perspective, the auto industry is expected to grow 6% to 8% in 2026 and it is supported strongly by GST 2.0 and the easing monetary conditions.

items.statement: Diesel to hold 18-20% market share in three-wheelers, gradual decline expected.
items.quote: And we see that diesel will still hold an 18% to 20% market share and it has continued to do so in the first 9 months of this year.

items.statement: Plans IPO of Greaves Electric Mobility with primary raise of Rs 1,000 crore for growth.
items.quote: As regards cash available with the business, that is the purpose of the IPO. And if you have read through the documents, we will be raising approximately a primary of 1,000 crores, which will be utilized for funding the growth aspirations of Greaves Electric Mobility.

items.statement: Excel domestic business grew 17% YoY in 9M FY26, exports impacted by geopolitics.
items.quote: So, like I said, the domestic part of the Excel business, which is nearly two-thirds of the business or a bit more than two-thirds, grew by 17% year-on-year for the first 9 months of this year.

items.statement: Energy solutions 9M FY26 revenue grew 21% YoY, spares and service grew 40%.
items.quote: Energy solutions delivered a 21% year-on-year growth in the first 9 months of this year. And within that, the spares and service actually grew 40% year-on-year.

items.statement: Mobility solutions 9M FY26 revenue grew 15% YoY.
items.quote: So, taking all these developments together for the mobility solutions, our revenues grew 15% year-on-year in the first 9 months of this year.

items.statement: Industrial solutions 9M FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY, muted due to market conditions.
items.quote: This segment, therefore, delivered a more muted 3% year-on-year growth for the first 9 months of this year.

items.statement: Exports contributed 14% of 9M FY26 revenues, international business a key priority.
items.quote: So, exports have contributed to 14% of the revenues in the first 9 months of this year, and this reflects a consistent traction across the global market.

items.statement: Greaves Finance managed AUM crossed Rs 441 crore as of December 2025.

items.statement: Has approximately Rs 250 crore cash on books, confident to fund capex internally.
items.quote: So, if you go through our financial results, we have approximately (+250) crores of cash on the books. And therefore, we are very confident.

items.statement: Expects overall loss ratio to improve to 77-77.5% from 81.1% next year, excluding potential surplus provisioning reversal.
items.quote: Certainly, I think no reason why from an 81.1%, it can't go back to, say, 77%, 77.5% at least. That is very much certainly possible.

items.statement: Sees motor OD loss ratio reducing by at least 3-5% over the next two quarters due to corrective actions.
items.quote: And when it comes to the motor OD, I certainly see a reduction of at least 3% to 5% over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Plans to participate in new 3-year crop insurance tender next year, aiming to regain lost crop business.
items.quote: But now next year, we will have a new season tender, which will be across the country. And for a 3-year tender, the company will be participating and hopes to be back in the crop business units framework next year

items.statement: Plans to increase equity allocation to 10% of investment portfolio from current 6.7%.
items.quote: Our first half would be to take it up to 10% of the portfolio. And then we'll have to see as to where it can go from there.

items.statement: Cautious on 2-wheeler book due to no motor TP premium hike in 4 years and rising severity.
items.quote: The company has adopted a cautious stance with respect to growing the 2-wheeler book, particularly new vehicles in the context of the absence of motor third-party premium increases over the last 4 years.

items.statement: Stepped up motor TP reserving, 12-14% higher than peers, impacting claims ratio by 3.05%.
items.quote: Chola MS continues to be prudent and conservative in its provisioning for motor TP losses with the level of provisioning a good 12% higher than many of its peers.

items.statement: Loss of crop insurance business impacted Q3 GDPI by INR84 crores and 9M by INR467 crores.
items.quote: Chola MS has suffered the loss of crop insurance business consequent to the retender, which impacted the quarter's GDPI by about INR84 crores and cumulatively by INR467 crores for the 9 months.

items.statement: Combined ratio for 9M was 116.2%, or 113% without 1/n effect, including 3.05% from TP reserving.
items.quote: Consequently, the combined ratio for 9 months was at 116.2%, which is 113% without the 1/n effect. The combined ratio of 113% includes the impact of motor third-party reserving, which is 3.05%.

items.statement: ROE for 9M was 7.9% (not annualized), solvency at 2.04x as of December.
items.quote: The ROE for the 9 months was at 7.9%, not annualized. Solvency was at 2.04x as of December.

items.statement: Motor market share 5.25%; composition: 1% cars, 38% CVs, 11% 2-wheelers.
items.quote: In motor, the principal line of business, the market share stood at 5.25%. Within motor, the company had a composition of 1% in cars, 38% in CVs and 11% in 2-wheelers.

items.statement: Secured about 25% of total motor premium from new vehicles in Q3.
items.quote: The company secured about 25% of its total motor premium from new vehicles in quarter 3.

items.statement: Mid-term EBITDA margin target of 16-18%, with gradual improvement expected.
items.quote: I think what we gave and we definitely stick to this as a mid-term EBITDA margin to go back to the 16% to 18% range and we are getting there because especially the latest investments, we already achieved better EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Backlog at INR 2,205 crores, highest ever, 27% higher than previous year.
items.quote: What is also very comforting is that today, our backlog stands at INR 2,205 crores, the highest it has ever been, which is 27% higher than previous year.

items.statement: India improving driven by pharma, oil and gas, nuclear; chemicals weak due to overcapacity.
items.quote: India continues to improve, driven by investments in pharma, oil and gas, nuclear, so we have diversified there. Chemicals remain weak due to over capacity and uncertainties in global trade.

items.statement: Expect Q4 to be strong in India for revenue and shipments, with continued order intake momentum.
items.quote: We expect Q4 to be a strong quarter in India in terms of revenue and shipment and we also expect Q4 momentum to continue with order intake, which then hopefully will put us in a very strong position for next year.

items.statement: AUM growth expected at 40-50% over next 1-1.5 years, provided external and internal factors stay intact.
items.quote: In next 1-1.5 years it will be around 40% to 50% growth.

items.statement: Near-term AUM expansion guidance of 40-50% over one year.
items.quote: our near-term guidance from the perspective of one year AUM expansion should be in the range of 40% to 50% vis-à-vis branch expansion should also be in a similar number which is around 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Branch network to grow 40-50% over next 1-1.5 years; target to add 50-60 branches this year.
items.quote: We will be growing this number by 40% to 50% over the next 1-1.5 years.

items.statement: This year's target is to add 50 to 60 branches as per annual operating plan.
items.quote: This year our target is to add 50 to 60 branches as per our annual operating plan, but again, it depends on a lot of other external factors.

items.statement: NIM expected to contract further as leverage rises, settling at industry range of 11-12% at 3-4x leverage.
items.quote: once we are at an industry average leverage of 3x to 4x, you will see we will be somewhere in the industry range of 11% to 12% of NIM.

items.statement: Target leverage of 4x; current leverage 1.67x with significant headroom.
items.quote: Our next goal and target is to be at 4x.

items.statement: Steady-state on-book leverage target of 3x to 4x, in line with industry.
items.quote: the industry currently is operating anywhere between your 3-4x, and that is where we aspire to be on an on-book sort of an AUM.

items.statement: Co-lending target of 10-15% of overall AUM next year; some traction expected in Q4.
items.quote: our target for the next year would be to have a co-lending proportion of anywhere between 10%-15% of the overall AUM.

items.statement: Borrowing mix to be maintained at one-third/two-third or 60-40 between NCDs and banks/FIs.
items.quote: this is the proportion that we aspire to maintain in the coming years as well, anywhere between your one-third, two-third or 60-40 ratio.

items.statement: To remain a gold NBFC for next five years; diversify only in portfolio mix and risk-adjusted return.
items.quote: we wish to remain as a gold NBFC in the next five years.

items.statement: PL book transitioning from 30-day to 3-6 month EMI product, spreading yield and lowering fee income.
items.quote: our idea is to move the entire PL book from a short tenure 30 days to a 3 to 6 month sort of a book which fairly spreads across the overall fees income that we earn.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing expected to rationalize as AUM grows and credit rating improves.
items.quote: Talking about our cost of borrowings, yes, we do expect some sort of rationalization in our cost of borrowing.

items.statement: ROI charged to customers remains healthy at around 19.5%; no discounting business.
items.quote: our ROI, which is the rate that we charge to our customers, has been very healthy, around 19.5%.

items.statement: Gold loan demand ample; market shift from unorganized to organized to continue; operational excellence key.
items.quote: With respect to demand, the demand is ample enough to survive a large number of players even though there is competition from the outset, you can see that.

items.statement: Emerging market LAP plus merchant lending to grow 20-25%; low-yield portfolio to run down ~15% annually.
items.quote: We have given a guidance on how much in terms of percentage our emerging market LAP plus merchant lending business would grow. That would be in the rang e of 20% to 25% and we have said the lower yielding portfolio would run down to the range of around 15%

items.statement: ROA to improve from current levels; quality of ROA to improve dramatically over next 4-8 quarters.
items.quote: we expect ROAs to improve from where they are. But more so, the ROA's contribution from annuity -led spread income would dramatically improve over the next 4 quarters and then 8 quarters.

items.statement: No incremental primary capital required for next 2-2.5 years; growth funded by internal accruals.
items.quote: company for next 2, 2.5 years does not require any further capital because it's retained earn ings coming from profitability is fueling the growth.

items.statement: Quarterly income to remain broadly same for next quarter, but quality to change dramatically.
items.quote: while they will remain more or less same for at least for the next quarter is our assumption, but the quality of that would change dramatically.

items.statement: Earlier 4% ROA target may shift or reduce slightly; new ROA guidance not pinpointed.
items.quote: our view is that while the ROA target of 4% would might get shifted or it might get reduced a little bit. But because the net contribution is now cash generating annuity income, this would be more healthier ROA.

items.statement: Annualized cost rationalization of ~INR220 crores; ~50% achieved, balance under execution.
items.quote: UGRO has undertaken an annualized cost rationalization of approximately INR220 crores. Around 50% of this cost takeout has already been achieved with the balance currently under execution

items.statement: Profectus cost takeout of ~INR120+ crores to flow from Q4 FY26 through FY27.
items.quote: When we acquired Profectus from the portfolio because they were exactly in the similar nature of business we had taken out roughly around INR120-plus crores of the cost. So incrementally, that would flow starting from Q4 to the entire FY27.

items.statement: Portfolio yield to increase by at least 200 bps from mix shift to higher-yield segments.
items.quote: emerging market LAP at an average going forward yield of 17.5% would incrementally increase the total yield on portfolio progressively by at least 200 b asis points.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing improved to 10.24% in Q3 FY26 from 10.37% last quarter.
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing improved to 10.24% during the quarter compared to 10.37% last quarter, supported by easing macro conditions, including the reduction in repo rates.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing reduction of ~75 bps expected over next 8 quarters.
items.quote: we have presumed that even if our cost of borrowing reduction happens to the tune of around 75 basis points over the next 8 quarters, then also the NIM margin and the ROA improvement will be very, very significant

items.statement: Emerging market LAP and embedded finance now ~32% of AUM; share expected to increase steadily.
items.quote: As of December 2025, emerging market LAP and embedded finance together account for approximately 32% of consolidated AUM, and this share is expected to increase steadily as the portfolio mix continues to realign

items.statement: Low-yield intermediated portfolio to run down ~15-20% annually; mix shifting to higher-yield secured assets.
items.quote: the rest of the portfolio is allowed to run down in ordinarily manner at approximately 15% to 20% annually.

items.statement: Dependence on co-lending and direct assignment income to reduce to less than 25% over 8 quarters.
items.quote: More than 50% to 60% of ROA contribution was coming from downselling of the assets under direct assignment or co-lending, which over 8 quarters would materially reduce and would remain less than 25% or even more as we progress further.

items.statement: Profectus standalone annualized profitability was ~INR35-40 crores pre-acquisition.
items.quote: Prior to that, Profectus on a stand -alone basis had a marginal profitability of around -- annualized profitability of around INR 35 crores, INR 40-odd crores.

items.statement: FY27 auto segment growth expected double-digit, possibly 10-12% or 15%.
items.quote: I think the growth will be more than 10%, 12%, if not 15%.

items.statement: Railway revenue target for FY27 conservatively INR60-65 crores.
items.quote: we are committing about INR60 crores -- around INR60 crores this year, INR60-65 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 13% EBITDA margin, clear path but no fixed timeline.
items.quote: We have a very clear path on getting to the margin of 13%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected around INR2,500 crores, slightly below earlier INR2,600 crores target.
items.quote: by the time we close this year, we'll be somewhere around INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: EV plus hybrid share currently ~7%, hoping for double-digit next year.
items.quote: our EV share has gone up, EV hybrid gone up to 9% of our turnover. But now it is in the region of about 7%.

items.statement: Raw material prices indexed with customers, quarterly or monthly, so no margin impact except lag.
items.quote: Our RM prices is indexed with the custom er. And the customer basically invests for the RM prices on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Approaching customers for price revision due to labour code implementation.
items.quote: we will be approaching our customers for a price revision there also.

items.statement: US tariffs fully passed on to customers; any reduction will be returned, no extra profit.
items.quote: we will return whatever tariffs have been lowered, we will return it back to the customer. So there won't be any additional profit because of that

items.statement: Railway revenue target for FY26 missed; will cross INR60-70 crores in FY27.
items.quote: No, no, we are not on track there, but '27, definitely we'll be crossing that.

items.statement: Defense fuse tender withdrawn by government; no direct supplies currently.
items.quote: the government withdrew that tender after almost 3 to 4 years

items.statement: Q4 FY26 expected promising with new program launches.
items.quote: we are confident enough that the Q4 will also be very promising for us going forward.

items.statement: 9-month FY26 EBITDA margin around 9.6-9.7%, impacted by higher aluminum prices.
items.quote: EBITDA margins are hovering at around 9.6%, 9.7%.

items.statement: Tax rate expected around 25% after shifting to new regime.
items.quote: overall it will be in and around 25% because we have shifted to the new regime.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR3,000 crores plus may be exceeded.
items.quote: That is what we will plan for the next 3 to 4 years. And those are the figures we have quoted on there, but a lot has changed and let's see what happens, and I think we might do even better.

items.statement: Bharuch plant utilization to exceed 50% by Q1 FY27, ramping up from ~30%.
items.quote: So that at least we had in a sizable percentage more than -- a little more than 50% utilization by then.

items.statement: Jamshedpur rail capex of INR120 crores to go live by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: So that project, we are expecting to go live towards the end of this calendar year, which will be Q3 of financial year ''26-'27.

items.statement: FRC line investment of INR35 crores on track, equipment installation by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: And that's an investment of, for FRC line, very close to INR35 crores. So we are on track in terms of that investment, in terms of that project.

items.statement: Bharuch ramp-up costs to moderate, supporting gradual margin normalization.
items.quote: So as the new capacities and stabilization and utilization improves for our new manufacturing plant, ramp-up costs are expected to moderate, so which is going to support the gradual margin normalization.

items.statement: CV segment demand accelerating, momentum expected to continue in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So we see a little acceleration in the commercial vehicle segments. And that's something which is reflecting in our revenue as well.

items.statement: Rail business Q4 FY26 expected to be strong, historically strong quarter.
items.quote: And historically, if we look at it, the rail per se, the quarter 4 of the financial year is always going to be a strong quarter.

items.statement: Trade deal fine prints being evaluated; no concrete impact on exports yet.
items.quote: So again, we need to wait and watch. So there is no kind of concrete answers, whether that's something which is going to have a direct impact on our exports, but these are all the directions in the positive way.

items.statement: Bharuch ramp-up cost impacted PBT by ~170 bps in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So that has impacted in terms of the basis point very close to 170 basis point impact because of the ramp-up cost for the quarter.

items.statement: Labor Code impact on PBT ~60 bps in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Then on top of that, we had the Labor Code impact, which was very close to 60 -odd basis points.
