items.statement: Unfavorable mix and improved leverage net impact on gross margin ~1.5% in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So the net impact of the gross margin because of the unfavorable mix and the improved leverage is very close to 1.5%.

items.statement: GGB annual revenue run rate expected INR50-55 crores.
items.quote: I would say somewhat close to INR50 crores, INR55 crores. They will also have their seasonality. So I would say somewhere close to INR50 crores, INR55 crores range.

items.statement: Linear motion products actively discussed as low-hanging fruit for India.
items.quote: Yes, linear motion certainly is a low -hanging fruit for the -- for both Timken India Limited in this year and for the parent company as well. So debates and discussions are very actively going on.

items.statement: Solano Gardens GDV over INR 1,000 crores, to be launched and completed in phases over 5 years.
items.quote: The project has received strong market response with the GDV potential of over INR 1,000 crores for the overall development, the project will be launched and completed in phases over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Imperia Phase 2 revenue of INR 299 crores to be booked over next 4 quarters.
items.quote: I mean, we're basically going for the INR 299 crores.

items.statement: Stable EBITDA margin around 30%, next year slightly higher due to Imperia Phase 2.
items.quote: Generally, about 30% to 35% would be a fair assumption on a blended basis over many years. Coming year, I think it will be a little higher.

items.statement: Construction spend for 9MFY26 was INR 116.5 crores, up 11% YoY.
items.quote: Construction spend for the quarter was INR 39.9 crores, up 11% from last year. And for the 9MFY26 stood at INR 116.5 crores, reflecting consistent execution across projects.

items.statement: 9MFY26 booking value INR 361.2 crores, up 29.1% YoY, surpassing full FY25.
items.quote: The booking value for the quarter stood at INR 52 crores. And for 9 MFY26, booking value stood at INR 361.2 crores, up 29.1% year -on-year.

items.statement: Lucknow real estate in multiyear up cycle, no slowdown, organic demand.
items.quote: So, we look forward to consistent and strong growth over the next many years. It's a multiyear up cycle that Lucknow is in.

items.statement: Average realization INR 6,500 per sq ft this year, significant CAGR, but may stabilize.
items.quote: And this year, we are averaging about INR 6,500. So, it's a very significant CAGR year-on-year. I do not foresee it to be continuing like this forever.

items.statement: Commercial projects less than 10% of total area, residential dominant.
items.quote: In fact, they constitute less than 10% of our total area under development. Predominantly, our portfolio is still residential at the moment.

items.statement: Risk of overpricing beyond affordability could hurt market.
items.quote: The only pitfall is that one should not overprice the product and go beyond the affordability of the common man.

items.statement: Piramal loan of INR 110 crores for land acquisition and construction finance.
items.quote: It's a combination of land acquisition and construction finance.

items.statement: Launch pipeline includes 6 projects besides Solano Gardens, enough for 1.5 years.
items.quote: So, enough pipeline for the next year, 1.5 years.

items.statement: Bareilly project investment fully recovered with interest.
items.quote: We successfully recovered our entire invested amount in the Bareilly project along with interest during this quarter.

items.statement: Solano Gardens launch in Q4 FY26, strong response, INR 350 crores booked as EOI.
items.quote: In Jan’26, which is after the close of Q3, we launched the first phase of Eldeco Solano Gardens comprising villas and plots. The project has received strong market response with the GDV potential of over INR 1,000 crores for the overall development, the project will be launched and completed in phases over the next 5 y

items.statement: FY26 expected to be a growth year; medium-term growth preordained for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: We expect FY '26 to be a year when we see growth and we continue to be optimistic about the future, given the potential that our business holds.

items.statement: Potential for 20%+ CAGR over 2026-2036 if plans fall in place.
items.quote: I think if you look at 2026 to 2036 I think there is a potential for a business like this to grow at 20-plus CAGR, but that requires I think, a sequence of right plans to fall in place.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin of ~30% is fair representation of business capability.
items.quote: We've also indicated earlier that if you see the EBITDA margins that we've had in FY '24, which is around 30%, is a fair representation of the kind of margins that this business is capable of.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin is an outlier; last 2-3 quarters better represent steady gross margin.
items.quote: What I can assure you is that the gross margin that you've seen in this quarter is more of an outlier or an aberration for multiple reasons that it is not a steady gross margin going forward.

items.statement: Peptide manufacturing facility to be ready for commissioning in July.
items.quote: But that would be a good outcome for us having set up this large peptide certainty, which will be ready for commissioning in July.

items.statement: Ramp-up of new Unit 3 capacity and new CMS molecule to pick up over 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: It is going to take maybe another one or two quarters to really pick up so that's with regards to the capacity that was created in Unit 3 and how it's being utilized.

items.statement: Paliperidone shipment delay due to customer operational issues; resolution next financial year.
items.quote: I think it will be next financial year.

items.statement: Peptide business seeing traction; aim to secure at least one commercial peptide NCE arrangement in FY27.
items.quote: I think it would be ideal for Neuland in FY 27 if we were able to secure at least 1 commercial manufacturing arrangement for a peptide NCE

items.statement: US intent to secure API manufacturing locally remains a potential concern despite trade deal.
items.quote: I think the U.S. India trade deal does not really alleviate that that potential concern. So, we'll have to just monitor and also probably strategize accordingly.

items.statement: Working capital at 145 days; inventory days expected to reduce to ~90 days over next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: So what will typically happen is over the next two or three quarters, you will see that it will come back to something like 90 days from the current 124 and you can already see it because inQ1FY26 it was 149 days, then it was 123 and it's 124.

items.statement: Net debt negative INR202.6 crores; free cash flow negative INR9.2 crores for the year.
items.quote: Our net debt stood at negative INR202.6 crores.

items.statement: Management targets 12-13% margins in medium to long term, not impossible to achieve.
items.quote: Yes, we can target that level of margin, but see the 12%, 13% that we saw, post-COVID impact that we have seen. But the way we are also trying to devise or improve the margins, not impossible to get to those levels of margin in the medium to long term, I would say.

items.statement: Capex expected to remain INR100-150 crores, for expansion/replacement of facilities.
items.quote: But okay, keeping aside the lease part, our capex is typically in the range of maybe INR100 crores to INR150 crores, expected to remain in the same kind of range.

items.statement: January price hike of 9-12% is work in progress, realization to be seen at quarter end.
items.quote: But yes, what we drive at an individual customer level to start with is 9% to 12%.

items.statement: E-commerce light surface and surface expected to be growth drivers, growing faster than other products.
items.quote: Volumes, yes, the e-com light surface as well as surface have been the growth drivers, so while the other products will also continue to grow. But largely, we see these growing faster than the other products.

items.statement: Ground share increasing, with B2B ground at 28.6% and total ground at 42% of revenue.
items.quote: This was B2B only. Including B2C, it would be about 42% share of ground revenue, and air will be about 53%. So you can see that the share of ground is slowly increasing.

items.statement: Margins expected to be maintained or improved, with no significant impact from seasonality.
items.quote: And yes, as I said, since this is going to be -- expected to be the growth driver, we will work towards keep maintaining or improving the margins.

items.statement: GST cut impact not significantly continuing beyond a couple of months.
items.quote: But otherwise, I mean, we don't see significant impact continuing after maybe a couple of months.

items.statement: Air volumes more or less stable, positive but not declined.
items.quote: Not really. air is more or less stable, I would say. It's positive, but not declined.

items.statement: Pallet utilization at 85-90% for volumetric weight.
items.quote: So our pallet utilization remains at around 85% to 90% for a volumetric weight kind of level.

items.statement: Daily air cargo capacity 450-550 tons per day, flexible.
items.quote: See, daily cargo capacity, theoretical, given the number of hours we are flying and the theoretical capacity that we have, it would be moving between 450 to 550 tons per day, depending on which routes and which flights we operate.

items.statement: E-com light surface grew 26% in shipments, 25% in revenue; surface grew 22% in shipments.
items.quote: So like I mentioned, the e-com light surface would have grown by about 26% in terms of shipments or 25% in terms of revenue and surface at about 22% in terms of shipments.

items.statement: No significant impact from IndiGo schedule cuts.
items.quote: Positive impact of IndiGo, yes, there would have been cases where any scheduled flight, if the schedule gets disrupted, then the customers would typically have contracts with different service providers. So they would also be quick enough to shift the load , but not that very significant to kind of to make a big differ

items.statement: Aircraft utilization normalized at 85% from September 2024.
items.quote: But from September '24, I think, the utilization has been at a normalized level of 85% or so at a volumetric pallet utilization level.

items.statement: Consolidation may lead to better pricing opportunities.
items.quote: I think overall, given the consolidation that has happened, there would be a better opportunity to realize better price points to charge for the value being delivered.

items.statement: Expects mid-double-digit revenue growth, similar to last quarter, if momentum continues.
items.quote: We are exp ecting a mid -double-digit growth, just as we have seen in this last quarter, if the momentum continues, which is expected to be more likely.

items.statement: Reaffirms EBITDA margin guidance of 13-15% despite 1-2% raw material increase.
items.quote: Yes, we will because there is a lot of robustness in terms of the OE demand and we are the largest in the truck and bus.

items.statement: Approves INR 1,130 crore capacity expansion across TBR, ASLTR and PCR, adding nearly 7% capacity.
items.quote: the company has decided to further expand its capacities across TBR, ASLTR and PCR categories through expansions at various locations for an aggregate cost of INR 1,130 crores. This will increase our overall capacity by nearly 7%.

items.statement: INR 1,130 crore expansion is part of the INR 5,000 crore five-year capex plan, to complete in 1-2 years.
items.quote: Yes, INR 1 130 Cr is a part of that only and this will take somewhere between 1 - 2 years to complete this project.

items.statement: Raw material basket expected range-bound with 1-2% increase in Q4.
items.quote: In Q4, the raw material price scenario is expec ted to remain range-bound (1 - 2% increase).

items.statement: Margins to stay intact on volume push, premiumization and higher capacity utilization.
items.quote: Raw material basket is expected to remain rangebound as I said and it is expected to be inching up by 1 - 2% going ahead but the margins are going to be intact because there is a lot of volume push in this and our premiumization will also play a key role in the margin expansion.

items.statement: Q4 expected very strong; healthy growth across sectors, momentum continuing into FY27.
items.quote: So, we are entering the Quarter 4, which is expected to be very strong, and we are very confident about the healthy growth coming across the sectors.

items.statement: 16-inch and above PCR tyres rose to 31% of mix from 27% last year.
items.quote: Last year the contribution of 16-inch & above PCR tyres in our mix was around 27% and today we are at nearly 31%.

items.statement: Will undertake necessary price revisions based on demand-supply and market dynamics.
items.quote: Keeping in view the demand supply situation and the overall market dynamics, whatever necessary price revisions may have to be undertaken going ahead will be done.

items.statement: JK Tornel Mexico expects mid-single-digit growth with 1-2% margin expansion.
items.quote: We are looking at the mid-single digit growth.

items.statement: JK Tornel margin expansion expected in the range of about 1% to 2%.
items.quote: We are looking in the range of about 1% to 2%.

items.statement: PCR expansion at Banmore completed, full capacity by July 2026; TBR Laksar by April 2026; ASLTR Mysuru completed.
items.quote: So, our PCR expansion at Banmore is already under ramp up. It is already completed and it’s going to attain its full capacity by July’26 and for TBR capacities at Laksar by April’26. ASLTR expansion in Mysuru has already been completed.

items.statement: Monitoring USMCA revision in July 2026, important for US business.
items.quote: We continue to closely monitor the upcoming revision of the United States -Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) in July 2026, as this will be important for sustaining and strengthening our business with the USA.

items.statement: Good demand across segments; sharp OEM CV demand; truck category to cross FY19 highs.
items.quote: We are witnessing a good demand across the segments. There has been a sharp demand which is coming in from the OEM in the CV s, i.e. in the truck and bus segment.

items.statement: Expects margin normalization in H2 FY26 and further improvement in FY27.
items.quote: We therefore, expect margin normalization as we progress through the second half with further improvement as we enter FY '27.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR629 crores for FY26; INR121 crores pending in India and INR147 crores in Saudi, to be fulfilled in Q4.
items.quote: And we have a capex plan of INR629 crores, out of which substantial portion has already been delivered, more so in the last quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated order book around INR1,800 crores as of Dec 25, with INR1,200 crores executable in FY26.
items.quote: As on December 25, our consolidated order book stood at around INR1,800 crores, out of which around INR1,200 crores are executable in this financial year.

items.statement: Inquiry pipeline expanded to almost INR2,900 crores.
items.quote: Further reinforcing this momentum, our inquiry pipeline has expanded to almost INR2,000 crores, INR3,000 crores, reflecting sustained demand and high customer confidence across all our core markets.

items.statement: Wind EPC business margin guided at 10-12% on YTD basis.
items.quote: So ma'am, you take on a YTD basis, which is we already guided in the past also. The margin in this business is between the range of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Saudi yield is 3.5% plus per month, higher than domestic.
items.quote: Yes, yes. Definitely, is in the range of 3.5% plus per month.

items.statement: Demand robust across infrastructure, renewables, metals, cement, hydrocarbon; no slowdown seen.
items.quote: So demand is very robust, and it's coming from all, infrastructure, renewables, metals, cement, like Mr. Gaurang explained.

items.statement: Aims to maintain parity between crane rental and EPC business mix.
items.quote: And ideally, we would like to maintain the parity what we have in terms of our crane rental and EPC business.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on Chinese cranes could improve margins if implemented.
items.quote: We hope that this can also lead to margins improving.

items.statement: Saudi business expected to breakeven in 12 to 14 months.
items.quote: So as we have repeatedly told in our last meetings also, we are expecting 12 to 14 months, we are expecting for breakeven time for Saudi.

items.statement: Targets 5% market share in Saudi crane rental market in next 3 to 5 years.
items.quote: And just to say that we are eyeing 5% market share in the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Utilization long-term stable range 75% to 80%.
items.quote: We continue to operate within a long-term stable utilization range of approximately 75% to 80%.

items.statement: Expects FY26 revenue growth of 25-30%.
items.quote: I think we are growing at about 30%, so we should end up the year between 25% to 30% for sure.

items.statement: Tractor volumes to exceed 6,000 units in FY26.
items.quote: I'm hopeful that we will cross the 6,000 numbers this year for tractors and the growth will continue.

items.statement: FY27 cash capex expected around INR60 crores.
items.quote: the cash outflow on capex, we expect next year to be around INR60 crores.

items.statement: To achieve 2-3% tractor market share in 4-5 years.
items.quote: we can definitely claim 2% to 3% market share. That is definitely possible in the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Power weeder business to double and continue growing.
items.quote: We will be scaling up the power weeder business considerably. We are almost close to doubling the business from last year. And this growth will continue

items.statement: Power tiller growth to continue due to small farmer demand.
items.quote: we expect this to continue.

items.statement: No price hikes despite copper cost rise; impact immaterial.
items.quote: On ferrous metal the fluctuation has not been very high or the increase has not been very high, so nothing is happening on that front. But on the copper, it has been pretty steep. And in some of the areas, especially radiator, on a particular model that we use our copper radiator, otherwise it's aluminium, only on that

items.statement: Europe operations to start in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Hopefully, first quarter of next year, that should be up and running.

items.statement: US market entry planned for 2027.
items.quote: in 2027, we will enter the U.S. market.

items.statement: Electric weeders and tillers to be seeded from March, scale next fiscal.
items.quote: we would be starting to seed them in this quarter. In March, we should be able to start seeding them in the market and scaling up steadily based on the response from the market in the next financial year.

items.statement: No pressure on margins; comfortable maintaining current levels.
items.quote: there is no real pressure in terms of fighting the Chinese on the price front.

items.statement: Export mix FY26: Europe 90%, Africa 5%, RoW 5%, US zero.
items.quote: FY '26, U.S. is zero. Europe is 90%, Africa would be 5% and Rest of the World, 5%.

items.statement: Marine engine entry is initial; no numbers yet.
items.quote: It's very initial days. So we don't have any numbers as yet, but we feel this is a good opportunity we will pursue going into the future.

items.statement: Hopeful of crossing 6,000 tractor units this year, domestic plus exports.
items.quote: So cumulatively, tractor, domestic plus Export, I have guided anywhere between 6,000 to 6,500. I'm hopeful that we will cross the 6,000 numbers this year for tractors and the growth will continue.

items.statement: Cash outflow on capex expected around INR60 crores next year; commitments larger for long-term projects.
items.quote: See, the cash outflow on capex, we expect next year to be around INR60 crores.

items.statement: Will enter the U.S. market in 2027 as tariffs have reduced and entry is now feasible.
items.quote: So like I have said before, in 2027, we will enter the U.S. market.

items.statement: Europe ground operations base expected up and running in first quarter of next year.
items.quote: So first is, we are establishing our base in Europe. Hopefully, first quarter of next year, that should be up and running.

items.statement: New FENTM tractor series launched in Gujarat; Maharashtra launch at Gudi Padwa, other states next fiscal.
items.quote: We have just launched in one state, which is Gujarat, so now we'll be launching in Maharashtra which is the next place we will be launching at Gudi Padwa, coming next month. And then, go on for launches in all the other states in the next financial year.

items.statement: Revamped ZETOR series relaunch begins in Q4 from March, continuing into next financial year.
items.quote: And now we have a complete revamped product, so that process of relaunch is happening in Q4 to begin with in March and then going forward into the next financial year.

items.statement: Electric power weeders and tillers to start seeding in March, scaling up next financial year.
items.quote: So we would be starting to seed them in this quarter. In March, we should be able to start seeding them in the market and scaling up steadily based on the response from the market in the next financial year.

items.statement: Plans to expand distribution to about 6,000 counters from roughly 1,000 now for small farm machinery.
items.quote: We will have to get to every taluka. That is about 6,000 counters is what we are looking at to begin with. We are roughly at around 1,000 counters at this point.

items.statement: Targets 2% to 3% tractor market share in next 4 to 5 years, up from under 1%.
items.quote: We are less than 1% market share today. But we strongly believe that in the next 5 years, we can definitely claim 2% to 3% market share.

items.statement: VST products are roughly 15% to 20% more expensive than quality Chinese products; no cost parity.
items.quote: It depends on machine-to-machine, but roughly, I can say we would be expensive by 15% to 20% roughly.

items.statement: No real pricing pressure from Chinese imports; comfortable maintaining current margin levels.
items.quote: So there is no real pressure in terms of fighting the Chinese on the price front.

items.statement: Committed to stepping up investments in Data Centers; no capex guidance given at this time.
items.quote: I think, at this point in time, I cannot give you a capex guidance, but clearly you will see us investing more and more behind Data Centers; I think, there is no question about that in my mind.

items.statement: Plan to reach 1 gigawatt Data Center capacity, giving about 25% market share.
items.quote: our sense is that, in the next three to four years, we will have about a gigawatt capacity, which will give us about 25% share, so we are committed to stepping up investments in Data Centers.

items.statement: Current Data Center capacity is about 120 to 130 megawatts with roughly 12% market share.
items.quote: We have about 120 to 130 megawatts of power, so we are in that ballpark

items.statement: Rights issue called because 3-year timeframe ended with no provision to foreclose; funds for long-term value creation.
items.quote: We have already, sort of, given that there was a timeframe of 3 years which is now over, we have no provision to foreclose the call on the rights issue, so we have called it.

items.statement: Progressive dividend policy to continue; rights issue unrelated to dividend at this stage.
items.quote: We have always mentioned that, as far as dividend is concerned, we will see a progressive dividend policy. You have already seen that play out over the last couple of years. You will continue to see that play out

items.statement: Wrote to DoT requesting parity on AGR dues treatment; awaiting response before deciding next steps.
items.quote: We have written a few letters to the DoT, asking for a clarification and basically requesting parity on the treatment of the AGR dues. We are yet to hear from the DoT.

items.statement: Need differential pricing architecture where customers pay more for more, rather than separate 5G/4G pricing.
items.quote: the ARPUs have to move up, we have to keep reading and look at, really, a differential pricing architecture where people pay more for more, instead of looking at differential 5G or 4G pricing

items.statement: 5G slicing and network-on-demand capabilities ready for India; will play out in next few quarters.
items.quote: the new capabilities on 5G, which is linked to slicing, network on demand or other advance features are very much becoming a reality; they are lighting up as capabilities across the world, and it is ready for India as well, so you will see this move playout in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Data Center tax sop expected to fuel demand; Airtel to pursue stepping up Data Center business.
items.quote: the demand for Data Centers, our estimation is that this will certainly fuel that demand, and with the availability of land, green power, which today most of our Data Centers already have

items.statement: B2B underlying business growing at 10%, should show up in coming quarters if execution holds.
items.quote: if I shed that, the underlying business is growing at 10%, which should show up in coming quarters if we do well.

items.statement: B2B digital businesses (Cloud, Security, IoT) growing about 30%, need to accelerate further.
items.quote: The second component of this business is the digital side of the portfolio, which is ,really, our Cloud, Cybersecurity, our IoT businesses, which are now growing at about 30%, but need to accelerate further

items.statement: Wireless market growth averaging about 6%; premiumization drivers remain intact absent tariff repair.
items.quote: Market growth in wireless has been averaging about 6%, and if you strip out tariff repair, the drivers of premiumization continue to be the same as we have always seen

items.statement: Africa investment doubled in value over five to six quarters; currency volatility is the only risk.
items.quote: the stock and the price of the African asset has, more or less, kind of, doubled in the recent, let us say, five to six quarters, so this has been a really, really good asset

items.statement: Stepped-up investment in Data Centers expected over next two to three years.
items.quote: in the next two to three years, we will see a stepped up investment in Data Centers.

items.statement: Radio capex on new site coverage has clearly slowed as most of country is covered.
items.quote: I think the radio capex on coverage, where you are talking about new sites, that has clearly slowed down because a large part of the country is now covered

items.statement: Transport and fiber-to-tower investment will continue to get its fair share.
items.quote: It is just a question of doability; the transport will continue to get its fair share.

items.statement: Rolling out 2 million fiber home passes per quarter, trying to do more.
items.quote: we are rolling out 2 million fiber home passes for the quarter, so we are really stepped up on our fiber home passes every quarter, and we are trying to see, can we do more of this.

items.statement: India broadband homes to grow from 45-46 million to 100 million in 4-5 years.
items.quote: Today, the total number of broadband homes are about 45-46 million, one day, not in the very distant future, could be about maybe 4 years or 5 years, this will be 100 million

items.statement: Will look at consolidating fragmented industry at right value and partner; also B2B opportunities.
items.quote: Obviously, we will be keen to look at where there are opportunities to consolidate a fragmented industry, it has got to be at the right value, it has got to be done with the right kind of partner

items.statement: Committed to dramatically stepping up Cloud investments; seeking MeitY sovereign cloud certification.
items.quote: we have already made a reasonable investment, and we are committed to dramatically stepping up investments if needed, and this is an area that we are again doubling down on

items.statement: Currency volatility is the only risk in Africa; long-term assumes 5-7% annual devaluation.
items.quote: So currency volatility is the only risk in Africa, but if you take a long-term view over a 10-12 year period, you typically factor in, let us say, a 5 to 7% devaluation per year

items.statement: Africa growing 20%+ on constant currency for several quarters; reported growth now higher.
items.quote: We have been consistently growing now for several quarters at about 20% plus, and in fact now, with the currency having stabilized, particularly the Naira, and in fact hardened a little bit, that is also showing through now in reported numbers

items.statement: Fiber-first strategy; FWA augments, UBR to be brought in judiciously as required.
items.quote: Our approach is fiber first; we believe that is the best experience for the customer and we want to have as many customers as possible on fiber. FWA augments this, and wherever we have had supply gaps, we have augmented with 5G and FWA rollout.

items.statement: Industry seeing lower 4G/5G net adds due to tariff hardening and SIM consolidation.
items.quote: with some of the tariffs hardening over last two cycles, I think there have been a little bit of sim consolidation that has happened in the industry, but the organic rate and the funnel that is there in terms of now bottom end feature phones, etc., has come down

items.statement: Hexacom FWA household penetration aspiration of 30-35% in its two circles.
items.quote: I would hazard a guess anywhere between 30% to 35% penetration of households should be something which we can easily aspire to.

items.statement: Hexacom may see bigger FWA-led homes capex; balance sheet allows faster growth.
items.quote: you may see, driven primarily by the homes, FWA-led Wi-Fi penetration in these two circles asking for bigger capex

items.statement: Hexacom B2B not an option as large enterprises are not headquartered in its two states.
items.quote: bulk of the market is restricted to the top 500 companies, and none of them have their head office in either of these two states, so B2B clearly is not an option there.

items.statement: Expects annual EBITDA margin around 30% plus/minus 200 bps, not quarterly run rate.
items.quote: So it will be an annualized number that we are looking at 30% give or take plus/minus 200 basis points.

items.statement: Incremental HFC capacity up to 15,000 MTPA of R32 to be commissioned in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: Additionally, the CAPEX for incremental HFC capacity equivalent up to 15,000 MTPA of R32 is progressing as planned and is expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Chemours project on track for completion in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: On the Project front, the Chemours Project is progressing well and is on track for completion in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Debottlenecking of MPP capacity at Dahej expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: Further, the de-bottlenecking of MPP capacity at our Dahej facility is expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY27, which will further enhance our capabilities.

items.statement: cGMP-4 engagement provides strong revenue visibility over next three years.
items.quote: This engagement provides strong revenue visibility over the next three years.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals outlook strong with order visibility for Q4 and beyond.
items.quote: The outlook remains strong and encouraging, supported by strong order visibility for Q4 and beyond.

items.statement: CDMO inching closer to aspirational $100 million revenue mark.
items.quote: And with CDMO, obviously, with every month going by, we are getting closer and we are inching closer to our aspirational number of 100 million.

items.statement: Input costs like sulfur and fluorspar increasing; pricing decisions reflect this.
items.quote: So the only issue, and I am sure you guys know it, the price of sulfur keeps increasing, the price of fluorspar is increasing. So, there are input costs that are going higher.

items.statement: Export realizations for R-32 better than domestic.
items.quote: I just stand corrected, our export realizations are better than the domestic ones.

items.statement: CDMO portfolio balanced 50-50 between early and late-stage to commercial molecules.
items.quote: If I remember correctly, it is largely a 50-50 split, which is a great place to be in because every late and commercial stage molecule that we are working on, has the potential to quickly convert into revenues, depending on readouts, etc.

items.statement: Employee costs to be 7-8% of revenue going forward.
items.quote: But, I think a safe bet is to look at what we are saying, 7%, 8% percent of revenue as our employee costs.

items.statement: Agrochemical sector outlook better with volume uptick expected next year.
items.quote: So the next year seems to be an outlook where people are saying, there will be a volume uptick.

items.statement: Pricing pressure in agrochemical business will always remain.
items.quote: Is the pricing pressure always going to be in the agchem business? It is always going to be there.

items.statement: Gross margin fell ~4% YoY on high maize and rice production costs not passed to farmers; expects normalization to 45-48%.
items.quote: But if the costs are stable, then anyway we will increase the prices to some extent that can be absorbed. So it will normalize to what it used to be earlier between that 45% to 48%.

items.statement: Expects major growth in spring maize in Bihar, UP, Punjab and summer millet in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Western UP next quarter.
items.quote: During the next quarter, we are expecting major growth in spring maize in Bihar, UP and Punjab. Similarly expecting growth in summer millet in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Western UP.

items.statement: Maize volumes expected to remain healthy as acreages and usage rise despite low maize prices.
items.quote: We think maize volumes should remain good and healthy and because the acreages are going up and the usage is also going up.

items.statement: Cost of production flat to down YoY; plans to raise prices somewhat as costs stabilize.
items.quote: Basically, when you compare to year -on-year basis, compared to last year to this year, the cost of production has not gone up. In some cases, it has in fact gone down when compared to the previous years.

items.statement: New cotton hybrids performed well; expects good revenue growth starting June 2026.
items.quote: Our products have really done well, performed well, and we will see that good set of growth numbers coming in the next couple of years starting from '26, '27. I mean to say like June '26.

items.statement: Exports grew 86% in Q3 and expected to keep improving every year absent major disruption.
items.quote: Exports have witnessed steep growth of 86% in the revenue during the current quarter and continue to grow and every year would be better than the previous year unless there is going to be any major unforeseen disruption in these markets.

items.statement: R&D spend currently 5-10% of revenue; expected to stabilize lower as most capex is done.
items.quote: As of now, our spend is in between 5% to 10% of our total revenue, both including revenue and capex. Going forward, they should stabilize at decently lower than what we have spent in the last year because most of the capex is already done there.

items.statement: Illegal cotton seed at same level as last year and increasing, impacting cotton sales.
items.quote: See, that it will be in the same level as what it was in last year and increasing now.

items.statement: Cotton inventory of 8-9 million packets sufficient through next season; new hybrids have 3-5 year life.
items.quote: As of now, we are having enough stock till the end of the season, I mean to say by next year’s season will be in between 8 million to 9 million packets for us, which is in line with our anticipation.

items.statement: Open to inorganic growth; buyback decision to be taken in Q1 or follow-up quarter.
items.quote: So that we are open for inorganic growth even as of now. But in terms of the buybacks that have a meeting in the first quarter or the follow-up quarter, then we'll decide about the buyback thing.

items.statement: Three income tax appeal cases pending 2.5-3 years; outcome expected in next six months; no provisions made.
items.quote: Basically, there are three cases pending at the appeal stage. It's been almost like two and a half, three years there. Most probably it should come back in the next six months or so because the hearings are going on.

items.statement: Receivables rose to ~Rs 250 crore from ~Rs 175 crore YoY, expected to normalize to Rs 80-90 crore by year-end.
items.quote: Usually, what, at the year -end, the outstanding are in between RS. 80 crores to RS. 90 crores or something like that, it should come back to those levels.

items.statement: Mustard and wheat drove 59% growth in other crops segment; expects sizable mustard business in couple of years.
items.quote: The increasing areas of mustard and our continuous focus on bringing new varieties in, is paying off, and this is going to be a sizable business in the next couple of years for us.

items.statement: Maize prices fell to Rs 1,200-1,300/quintal but recovered to Rs 1,800-1,900; ~Rs 2,000 is good for farmers.
items.quote: I do agree that the maize prices are down. In fact, it went down to as low as RS. 1,200 crores to RS. 1,250 crores, RS. 1,300 crores. But right now it's close RS. 1,800 to RS. 1,900.

items.statement: Gross margin to remain subdued for at least next couple of quarters due to MRP cuts and input inflation.
items.quote: Given the current geopolitical situation and resultant unpredictability in the forex and crude prices, coupled with increased competitive intensity, the gross margin is likely to remain subdued over the next couple of quarters at the minimum.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure in Dishwash and Liquid Detergent; gradual recovery expected as raw material prices ease.
items.quote: While near-term margin pressures persist, especially in Dishwash and Liquid Detergent segments due to reduced MRPs and input cost inflation, especially in LABSA and SLES, we expect gradual stability in raw material prices going forward.

items.statement: Dishwash portfolio price reduction of 8-9% taken due to competition.
items.quote: See, our pricing action, downward pricing revision at a portfolio level would be between 8% and 9% in Dishwash category.

items.statement: Volume-value gap expected to persist at 2-3% in near term.
items.quote: Amit, we mentioned this earlier also that in the near term, the volume value gap is likely to persist to the range of 2% to 3%.

items.statement: HI segment expected to turn profitable by end of FY27.
items.quote: And as indicated earlier, maybe by the end of FY '27, we are quite positive that we should be able to turn around this completely and we'll be out of woods.

items.statement: A&P spend to remain in 8-9% of revenue range over broader horizon.
items.quote: However, our A&P spend on a broader time horizon will remain in 8% to 9% range.

items.statement: Urban demand revival seen in Q3; sustainability to be watched over next few quarters.
items.quote: The good news is that in this quarter, we saw a good revival of demand in urban markets. It's too early to comment.

items.statement: Coil share in HI revenue reduced to one-third; focus on liquid vaporizers and new products.
items.quote: Now coiI stands at one-third of total HI revenue as we speak.

items.statement: Direct reach expanded to 14 lakh outlets this year from 13 lakh last year.
items.quote: This year, we will we are close to closing it at 14 lakh retail outlets, which is direct reach.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility and forex fluctuations remain watch points.
items.quote: Geopolitical volatility and forex fluctuations continue to remain watch points.

items.statement: Price increases taken in Post Wash where leaders; detergents remain competitive.
items.quote: And there, we are taking price increases as and when required. Only if material, raw materials and things go up, we are taking price increases.

items.statement: No margin guidance; will wait a few quarters for market stabilization.
items.quote: At this stage, we are watching the market and the external environment very carefully. We are not giving any guidance on the margin.

items.statement: Laundry business under Fabric Spa has 200+ outlets; no cash losses, working towards profitability.
items.quote: And under Fabric Spa brand, we have 200-plus outlets spread across a few states.

items.statement: Rural demand resilient for last 4-5 quarters; urban stress easing.
items.quote: See, overall, as we have been mentioning, the demand has been resilient as far as rural market is concerned for the last whatever, 4, 5 quarters.

items.statement: FY27 top line target of INR1,800 crores and EBITDA of INR300 crores on annualized basis after all machines come online.
items.value: INR1,800 crores top line, INR300 crores EBITDA
items.quote: we are targeting a top line of close to INR1,800 crores and a bottom line of -- or an EBITDA margin -- EBITDA level of close to INR300 crores going into the future.

items.statement: FY26 top line expected around INR1,100 crores with EBITDA margins in similar range.
items.quote: overall, we should touch a top line of about INR1,100 crores. And EBITDA margins, as you're already seeing, will be around that range.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 performance expected slightly better than Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Q4 is going to be slightly better than Q3.

items.statement: FY27 performance expected better than FY26, with improved EBITDA margins and overall economics.
items.quote: We are in for a better performance for the next year, '26-'27.

items.statement: PM2 upgrade costs INR45 crores, PM3 upgrade INR140 crores, part of INR735 crores total plan.
items.value: INR45 crores, INR140 crores, INR735 crores
items.quote: PM 2 upgrade is about INR45 crores and PM 3 upgrade will be about INR140 crores. And this is part of the overall plan of INR735 crores

items.statement: Tissue paper machine of 50 TPD planned, capex INR70-80 crores, implementation 16-18 months.
items.quote: the investment for this machine will be in the range of about INR70 crores to INR80 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin in Q4 FY26 expected to enhance by at least INR2,000 per ton, climbing to INR15,000-17,000 per ton.
items.value: INR2,000 per ton, INR15,000 to INR17,000 per ton
items.quote: This EBITDA margin in Q4 should be enhanced by about INR2,000 per ton at least. And going forward, it should climb to between about -- up to about INR15,000 to INR17,000 per ton.

items.statement: Price hike of INR2,000-4,000 per ton expected industry-wide, with INR2,000 already implemented and another INR2,000 expected by month-end.
items.quote: We could see a hike of between INR2,000 to INR4,000 per ton. And sort of -- and that would be an industry-wide phenomena

items.statement: Wheat straw prices increased by INR1,500 per ton, offset by lower wood chip prices of INR800 per ton.
items.value: INR1,500 per ton, INR800 per ton
items.quote: the increase in wheat straw prices of about INR1,500 per ton was offset by lower wood chip prices of around INR800 per ton of production

items.statement: Demand growing at 6% CAGR, with government focus on education supporting writing and printing paper demand.
items.quote: demand is growing at a good and gradual increment of about 6% CAGR.

items.statement: Low-priced imports from ASEAN and China pressuring realizations; safeguard measures and MIP being pursued.
items.quote: realizations face pressure due to the influx of low-priced imports, which has weighed on the industry margins.

items.statement: Peak long-term debt expected at INR750 crores, currently INR600-650 crores, with INR30 crores quarterly repayment.
items.value: INR750 crores, INR600 crores to INR650 crores
items.quote: peak debt, as you asked, it will be not more than INR750 crores for long-term loan. And as the repayment of, say, around INR30 crores per quarter will be repaid. So as of now, it is somewhere around INR600 crores to INR650 crores

items.statement: Launched Kuantum Kopio copier brand and Kuantum Pura with 65% agro pulp furnish.
items.quote: we have launched Kuantum Kopio, our new dedicated Copier brand available in 65, 70 and 75 GSM

items.statement: GST reduction on notebooks to 0% led to INR7,500 per ton impact, passed on to customers via price increase.
items.quote: the impact is close to about INR7,500 per ton. So, if anybody wants this kind of supply from us, the basic price we have enhanced by this same value

items.statement: Targets 1 million tonnes of ore raising in FY27.
items.quote: we are targeting 1 million tonnes of ore raising, that is 10 lakh tonnes in FY '27.

items.statement: Plans INR600 crores capex next year and INR400-500 crores the following year.
items.quote: it is like INR600 crores next year and another INR400 crores to INR500 crores the year following.

items.statement: Underground mining capex of INR1,000 crores to be spent over 4-5 years.
items.quote: On the mine side, we have said we have an overall capex of INR1,000 crores, but it will be spent out in next 4 to 5 years as we go for the developments.

items.statement: Expects similar EBITDA margins in Q4 FY26 as Q3, provided prices hold.
items.quote: Provided prices hold, which is what we expect it to be, we expect it to be sort of similar.

items.statement: Expects weighted average EBITDA cost for expanded output to reduce by INR1,500-2,000 per tonne.
items.quote: we expect our weighted average EBITDA cost for the expanded output to reduce by about INR1,500 to INR2,000 a tonne on account of logistics costs and all of that.

items.statement: Domestic ferrochrome prices at INR118,000-120,000 per tonne; Chinese prices at USD0.96-0.97 per pound.
items.quote: domestic prices are roughly in the INR118,000 to INR120,000 a tonne mark, and Chinese prices are around USD0.96 to USD0.97.

items.statement: Metallurgical coke prices may rise slightly from current ~USD250 per tonne.
items.quote: our current stock, what we are consuming is around the USD250 mark. And Suresh is a little aggressive when he looks at USD5. I would say that there might be a slight bit more upward bias in terms of costing for metallurgical coke.

items.statement: Sees structural demand-supply gap in ferrochrome persisting over next 1-2 years, supportive of prices.
items.quote: We do see a sort of a structural sort of gap between demand and supply persisting over the next 1 to 2 years, which should be supportive of prices.

items.statement: Plans to shift export-domestic mix from 90:10 to 60:40 over next 2 years.
items.quote: we expect to move from 90 -10, that is 90% exports and 10% domestic market at present with enhanced capacity over the next few years for it to be somewhere around 60-40.

items.statement: South African ferrochrome production revival could impact global prices, but sees it as complex zero-sum game.
items.quote: if Chinese output doesn’t come down and South Africa adds its capacity, then logically, ferrochrome prices will fall.

items.statement: Tata Steel acquisition funded entirely from internal accruals; no major debt drawdown expected.
items.quote: as far as our acquisition is concerned, which is at a base price of INR610 crores plus GST plus net working capital, that's going to be funded entirely out of internal accruals

items.statement: Ethanol project commissioning delayed to March 2026; revenue contribution from April 2026 (FY27).
items.quote: we expect to commission it in March 2026, that is next month. So, there is a slight delay because we were initially targeting the second half of February, but there's been a slight spillover on that, and we are expecting to commission it in March.

items.statement: KNR1 greenfield project on track; first furnace commissioning in June 2026, second shortly after.
items.quote: we expect to commission the first furnace in June 2026 and the second furnace shortly thereafter.

items.statement: Expects FY26 revenue to close between Rs. 1,300 crore and Rs. 1,400 crore.
items.quote: So, FY 2027, still pretty early to say for this year, for FY 2026 already for nine months our sales are around Rs. 1,100 crores, so we expect to close the year between Rs. 1,300 crores to Rs. 1,400 crores.

items.statement: Next year revenue expected around Rs. 1,600-1,800 crore; FY28 even better.
items.value: Rs. 1,600 crores, Rs. 1,700 crores, Rs. 1,800 crores
items.quote: And next year, we will come around Rs. 1,600 crores, Rs. 1,700 crores, Rs. 1,800 crores also, because just I told in the Mr. Gunit question also, that we are already in the same path where we are developing our new product.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target around 12%.
items.quote: Analyzed basis, we will be at around 12% or so. So that would be our EBITDA targets.

items.statement: Next year EBITDA margin minimum 16-17%, not 20%.
items.quote: Not 20%, but definitely our target is there, but I cannot say 20%. But definitely, it will be 16% to 17% will be minimum.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA similar to Q3, aim to avoid losses.
items.quote: So, EBITDA would be in similar lines like current quarter but it could be a little better, and we will try not to have losses in Q4.

items.statement: CAPEX remains on hold; will reconsider in 4-5 months.
items.quote: Yes, it is still on hold. We will think about it four, five months down the line, not now.

items.statement: No CAPEX now; existing capacity sufficient for next two years.
items.quote: So, for CAPEX, we are not doing anything as of now.

items.statement: Warrant conversion decision pending; may forfeit if not paid by May.
items.quote: So, as per the terms, the amount will get forfeited, so we do not want that situation to happen. But based on the market situation, we will take a call and discuss with the investors.

items.statement: El Nino risk possible; will prepare inventory with caution.
items.quote: So, yes, El Nino effect might be there, but it will show only in July-August, but before that we have to prepare ourselves with the inventory, which we will do, but we will go with a caution.

items.statement: Q4 rabi season lean; sales return expected 50-60% lower YoY.
items.quote: So, in Q4 the sales return that we had last year, we are seeing 50% to 60% or even less, it will not be that much.

items.statement: Focus on patented products; non-patent sales lower by 35-40%.
items.quote: So that we said was lower by 35% to 40%. Yes, we might have lost a little bit, but not on the patent portfolio but on the non-patent sales a little bit.

items.statement: Existing capacity can support Rs. 2,000+ crore revenue.
items.quote: So, based on our existing capacity, we can do Rs. 2,000-plus crore.

items.statement: Sales return reduced 40-45% in nine months; Q3 provision Rs. 70 crore vs actual Rs. 90 crore.
items.quote: If you see overall nine months to nine months, we have improved a lot, 40% to 45% sales return we have reduced. On specific question of Q3, we had provisioned around Rs. 70 crores, but returns what we got was around Rs. 90 crores.

items.statement: Maintains 15%+ revenue growth guidance, aspiration to exceed.
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance of 15%+. But as I said, our aspiration would be to do better than that. But as of now, the guidance stays the same.

items.statement: Aspires to 23-24%+ EBITDA margin in 3-4 years.
items.quote: So, our aspiration, of course, is to be 23% - 24% plus in the three-to-four-year period, and we are very confident of delivering that.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected INR 275-280 crore; FY27 10-12% higher.
items.quote: For capex this year, our expected closure is about INR 275 crore - INR 280 crore of capex and next year, probably about 10% - 12% higher than that.

items.statement: 15%+ growth split: 10% volume, 5% ARPP.
items.quote: So, our -- the breakup for the 15%+ is about 10% will come from volume growth and about 5% will come from ARPP growth.

items.statement: North Bangalore 120+ bed facility to start by end Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The North Bangalore facility with a planned capacity of over 120 beds is expected to commence operations by the end of Q4 FY '26, with clinician hiring largely completed.

items.statement: Expects ROCE to improve to 20% in 4-5 years.
items.quote: we are confident of delivering the ROCE margins that we have committed in our Investor Day deck of about 20% in the next four to five years.

items.statement: Expects 10% volume growth in South cluster in coming quarters.
items.quote: going forward, volume growth of about 10%, we are expecting from this market in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Medical tourism to increase from 3.5% to 7% in 4 years.
items.quote: Currently, it is about 3.5%, Rajat, and our endeavour is to take it to about 7% in the next four years.

items.statement: Rights issue to strengthen balance sheet; details after Board meet.
items.quote: we believe that an equity infusion at this stage will strengthen the company's balance sheet and the capital structure. And that is directionally why the rights issue is there.

items.statement: 80% of margin growth from existing centres, 10-12% brownfield, 5-6% greenfield.
items.quote: about 80% of our margin growth, in absolute terms is going to come from existing centres. About 10% - 12% is going to come from brownfield expansion in the cities that I mentioned and about 5% - 6% will come from greenfield expansion

items.statement: GST cut had marginal impact, offset by pricing and consumption initiatives.
items.quote: as far as GST is concerned, there was a marginal impact on the top line as well as margin and we were able to offset that by some initiatives that we took within the organization around pricing and consumption.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh strike impacted volumes for 20-25 days, now resolved.
items.quote: we lost about twenty-twenty five days of working, and that did have an impact on the November volumes as well. But now that growth is coming back to us.

items.statement: Q4 expected to be best quarter; North Bangalore impact from Q1.
items.quote: obviously, Q4 is trending better than Q3. And our hope is that it will be the best quarter for us this financial year. But the impact of North Bangalore, we will only be able to see in Q1 coming in

items.statement: Expects 20-25% topline growth in FY27 over FY26.
items.quote: Yes. I think it is achievable and internally when probably by next month when we are finalizing our budget for the next year internally with our teams I think that is something that should be minimum required.

items.statement: C&I business expected to cross or approach Rs.1000 crores next year.
items.quote: I think the C&I next year we should be looking at probably crossing let's say thousand crores in a way or coming close to that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 expected to be best quarter for metering supply and installation.
items.quote: We do expect Q4 to be probably the best quarter in the current year in terms of metering supply and installation also from the AMISPs.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue expected to show growth over Q4 FY25 (Rs.500 crores).
items.quote: I think we should see a growth from there. Now what growth, I cannot say that, but yes I think we are looking at it internally, we do have strong targets, our teams are working day and night to make sure that the best figures are there but yeah I think we should have a growth from there.

items.statement: Current order book over Rs.3000 crores, providing multi-year visibility.
items.quote: We currently have an order book of over 3,000 crores, which gives us clear multi-year visibility.

items.statement: Metering to remain ~55% and consumer ~45% of revenue over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: But on a steady basis I would see these to be maybe metering in the next 2-3 years remaining 55%, and consumer being 45%.

items.statement: Copper cost increases passed on to consumers with 2-3 week lag in wires and cables.
items.quote: So any increase in the cost is getting passed on to the consumer but with a lag. So the maximum impact would happen in the wire and cable where typically it takes two to three weeks to pass on the cost to the consumer.

items.statement: Six to seven price increases taken in last 9 months due to metal costs.
items.quote: But over the last couple of months, let's say if you look at the 9 months, there might have been at least six to seven price increases which the industry or even a company like us have affected on our consumers.

items.statement: Industry may implement at least 5 crore smart meters annually for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: I think that seems to be a possibility of having at least 5 cr meters being implemented.

items.statement: Water metering revenue expected to start in H2 next year after approvals.
items.quote: So in terms of revenue we should start seeing something probably in the second half of next year because there are approval processes and others, but we have already initiated those.

items.statement: Execution challenges with AMISPs and monsoon may persist but improving.
items.quote: The challenges in the last let's say 9 months or 12 months have emerged mainly, I believe so, from the execution part which are being faced by the AMISPs. So I think those are also getting addressed, although maybe like a monsoon or certain things which are out of control of everyone probably those challenges may remai

items.statement: Exploring entry into higher voltage cables (HT/EHV) over 3-5 years.
items.quote: It's a progression which typically for any good company would take 3 to 5 years to actually come out with those ranges. But yes we are actively looking at it and to come into the higher set of cables because our wire and cable over the last 3 years has seen very good growth.

items.statement: International smart meter business expected in 12 months after certifications.
items.quote: So maybe another 12 months from here as we get all the certifications in place, but eventually if we are able to crack even three-four countries the volumes can be big and the values are good, the realizations are pretty good and especially if you look at the European or the advanced middle east markets, the values can

items.statement: Spencer's expects mid-single-digit top-line growth in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Q4, I can give some guidance that on the Spencer's part of the business, we are looking at good growth. We will get to, I would say, mid-single-digit growth as far as Spencer's is concerned on top line.

items.statement: Spencer's aims for operational EBITDA breakeven in two quarters.
items.quote: we are quite confident that we are moving in the right direction towards a true operational EBITDA breakeven for Spencer's I would say, in two quarters from now.

items.statement: Offline business expected to break even at EBITDA level in FY27.
items.quote: we have a very good visibility and a path to breaking even at an EBITDA level in the offline business in FY '27.

items.statement: Membership program to reach 100,000 members by end of Q4 FY26.
items.quote: We are hoping to exit this year, which is at the end of Q4 with about 100,000 members for the membership program which is, I think, in 9 months is good progress.

items.statement: Membership base to double in the next fiscal year.
items.quote: And the intention is to see how we can double that in the year going forward.

items.statement: E-commerce business to exit FY26 with close to INR200 crores.
items.quote: We will exit this financial year with close to INR200 crores coming from our e-commerce business alone, phone deliveries extra.

items.statement: Out-of-store business to reach 20% of overall mix by early Q1 FY27.
items.quote: our out-of-store business, which is a combination of the phone delivery and the e-commerce business should be at around 20% of the overall mix. We are today at making progress at around 16-17%, and we expect to get to that level, if not at the end of Q4 by early quarter 1 of next year.

items.statement: Jiffy aims to increase orders to 300,000 per month from 240,000.
items.quote: We need to get to a level of close to 300,000 orders a month. We are currently at around 240,000.

items.statement: Gross margins to be maintained at Q3 levels, no further expansion planned.
items.quote: I don't foresee nor do I want to push further expansion in margins. What I want to push is continued growth.

items.statement: Nature's Basket margins to return to 29-30% after fixing supplier terms.
items.quote: the true margins of this business have to be what we have delivered in the past, in the region of 29-30%.

items.statement: No new store openings planned in Q4 and Q1, only relocations.
items.quote: we are not going to add on too many new stores at least in Q4 and Q1. We believe we have the playbook. We have the levers to drive growth from our base of stores which are currently there

items.statement: Online grocery trend to continue, more pronounced in metros and nuclear families.
items.quote: this whole thing on online consumer behaviour, as you guys know it better and as you guys are also consumers, it's not a fad. It is a trend. And I think it will only continue.

items.statement: Private label strong in staples, accounting for 35% of staples category.
items.quote: Close to 35% of our staples category is accounted for by private label.

items.statement: Board approved INR65 crore capex for 3 double-wall vacuum insulated steel flask lines in Rajasthan, 4 million units per year capacity.
items.quote: This project includes 3 double -wall production lines for vacuum ins ulated steel flasks, bottles and containers with an estimated capacity of close to 4 million units per year with an estimated capex of approximately INR65 crores.

items.statement: Two of three new steel flask lines to start commercial production by end of Q4 FY26 (March), third by end of Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Estimated commercial production from 2 of these lines is expected by the end of quarter 4 of this year, that is in March in the next month and from the third line by the end of quarter 1 of financial year '27, subject to receipt of necessary approvals.

items.statement: Investing INR75 crores in 20 MWp solar plant with battery storage, commissioning in Q4 FY26, to cover 65% of power needs.
items.quote: The company is further investing INR 75 crores towards setting up a 20 MWp ground-mounted solar plant with a battery energy storage system that will further reduce the overall power cost.

items.statement: Targets low-20s EBITDA margin in near future; would have been ~18% this year with hydra supply.
items.quote: So yes, like I said before, we should be in the low-20s in the very short foreseeable future. This year itse lf, while we have reported 16% we would have been closer to 18% or slightly more than 18% if we have supply of hydra.

items.statement: Expects hydra sales to return to at least last year's level in coming year, aided by own production and domestic sourcing.
items.quote: So, I do believe that between our own production as well as the domestic sourcing, we have a very good chance of going back to at least last year's level of hydra in the coming year.

items.statement: Targets 24% pre-tax ROCE across business, including new hydra plant, long-term.
items.quote: So obviously, our target would be that we should generate a ROCE of 24%. That's our target for -- across our business.

items.statement: Domestic sourcing for small kitchen appliances to reach 85% by end of coming year, up from ~60% now.
items.quote: Yes. I think we are now inching towards 60%. And I think by the end of the coming year, we'll be at 85%.

items.statement: Demand picked up in H2 across categories; glassware best, appliances and steel strong, opalware weak.
items.quote: So actually, demand, I think, which was a bit depressed in the first half of the year has definitely picked up in the second half of the year, okay? And this is across product categories.

items.statement: Plans brownfield glassware expansion by 50% at existing facility; announcement likely next quarter.
items.quote: No, brownfield. We have space in the existing facility to expand by 50%.

items.statement: Opalware furnace debottlenecking from 84 to 90 tons per day at next furnace rebuild next year, no material capex.
items.quote: But that will happen at the time of the next furnace reconstruction, which will happen next year -- yes, next year.

items.statement: Confident glassware margins will achieve or surpass opalware margins in next 2 years.
items.quote: And while they not had opalware margins yet, I still stand by my statement that in the next 2 years, we probably will achieve or surpass the opalware margins. I'm quite confident about that.

items.statement: FY27 capex not yet approved by Board; expects reasonable capex given growth opportunities.
items.quote: FY '27 capex has not been approved yet by the Board. So I would not like to take a stab at it. But it's -- we see many growth opportunities. So there will be reasonable capex in FY '27, I think.

items.statement: Reaffirms 4-year 10%+ revenue growth commitment; expects significant increase in guidance to be given at Q4 results.
items.quote: we expect to show significant increase in the guidance we have been giving over and above the 10% growth we have committed for 4 years.

items.statement: Maintains 10%+ constant currency revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin guidance for current financial year.
items.quote: delivering 10-plus percentage on revenue growth in constant currency and maintaining EBITDA margins in the 20 to 22% range. This is for the current financial year.

items.statement: Plans to grow AI/GenAI team to 1,000 employees by end of FY27.
items.quote: we plan to grow our AI/GenAI team to a 1,000 Happiest Minds by the end of FY'27 while maintaining financial discipline in the process.

items.statement: Pipeline showed significant increase, especially in larger deals with 3-4 year tenure.
items.quote: There was a significant increase in the pipeline. And the increase has been more in some of the larger deals. So , contrary to the point you made, we are actually seeing quite a few deals that are 3 to 4 years tenure.

items.statement: Expects BFSI and healthcare to drive Q4 growth; hi-tech and retail to stabilize.
items.quote: I think BFSI will continue to be a vertical that will drive our growth because we are expecting an uptick in Arttha license revenues.

items.statement: Expects edtech vertical to stabilize in FY27 with potential reversal of downward trend.
items.quote: I believe that in FY '27, we should see a reversal of the downward trend that we saw in the tech space.

items.statement: Gross margins have been improving over last two quarters; utilization improved to 82%.
items.quote: Utilizations have improved from marked 80% to 82%, and we kind of trying to push that as well.

items.statement: IP-led sales at 10.4% of revenue; subscription/SaaS offerings have higher gross margins.
items.quote: It's all of this is covered in the IP-led sales which is at about 10.4% as of end of quarter.

items.statement: DSO increased to 92 days; target to bring back to 85 days.
items.quote: DSO increased to 92 days from 87 in the previous quarter, and we remain focused on collections and billing discipline. The idea is to bring that back down to the 85 -day number

items.statement: Happiest Health IPO expected at least 6 years away.
items.quote: I would imagine IPO could be easily 6 years away.

items.statement: No plans for capital raise; debt is working capital with healthy current ratio and significant cash.
items.quote: Almost all our debt is working capital debt, Mr. Rakesh. And if you look at our current ratio, that's quite healthy. And we get -- we have a significant amount of cash on our balance sheet.

name: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd

items.statement: Thane and Mahadevapura to break even by end of Q1 FY27; Electronic City by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: But I think between Thane and Mahadevapuram in Bangalore and towards the end of Q1 next financial year, we should become EBITDA positive or EBITDA neutral. Electronic City might take a little longer by because we commissioned it only in the month of December. So I think by end of Q3, Electronic City also should turn EB

items.statement: FY27 capex expected INR500-600 crores; FY28 plan not yet finalized.
items.quote: '27, the full closure and capex will be another incremental INR500 crores to INR600 crores. And for '28, we have not yet put a plan together because there's no new hospitals that we're commissioning that.

items.statement: Kondapur new facility to grow 20-25% YoY; old hospital to shut in 6 months.
items.quote: In 6 months, once the new building is ready, we will shut down the old hospital. And I think 20% -- 20%, 25% year-on-year growth at the new Kondapur facility is something that we are extremely confident about.

items.statement: Nashik turned EBITDA positive in January; expects further improvement with CGHS/ECHS empanelment.
items.quote: Nashik yes, there is, it took us 13 months to achieve break even and in January we are EBITDA positive in Nashik, Rahul. We've achieved almost INR8.5 crores revenue and we turned EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Bangalore hospitals priced ~15% below competition; may rationalize in coming months.
items.quote: Vis-a-vis in respect to competition, we are slightly priced at least at least I would say that around 15% lower in the initial days. We may rationalize it in the coming few months, but yes, we will be slightly at least for some more time, will be slightly lower compared to competition.

items.statement: Telangana to reach 75-80% occupancy in 3-4 years; new Kondapur facility to drive volume growth.
items.quote: Telangana, we should get to 75%, 80%. There are little constraints in Telangana because some beds, we have now shut down because of renovation. Once those beds come into operation, which will happen end of next year, that should contribute to growth.

items.statement: Andhra volume dip due to Aarogyasri strike; January volumes recovered.
items.quote: As far as Andhra, in quarter 3, we had a strike with the state government. So we had not taken Aarogyasri scheme for almost a month, and that's why you see a significant dip in volume. But otherwise, January, things have bounced back and the revenues are as per how it was in Q2.

items.statement: Net debt INR2,850 crores; expected to moderate as capex peaks.
items.quote: Chirag, it is about INR2,850-odd crores at a consolidated level as on 31st of December '25.

items.statement: Kollam to break even in next 1-2 quarters; Kannur ramping well.
items.quote: Kollam is just 6, 7 months old. It should breakeven in the next 1, 2 quarter.

items.statement: Institutional revenue share to decline as expansion outside Telangana grows.
items.quote: Correct, from state government schemes.

items.statement: No incremental capex needed for new hospitals up to full capacity; only manpower addition.
items.quote: All the capex for all the 3 hospitals are fully done, there is no incremental capex that we'll have to incur for more beds up to each of their capacities.

items.statement: Insurance empanelment delays in new units; top 5 insurers partially done.
items.quote: There has been some progress in both units on insurance empanelments. But the top 5 companies that we wanted to do, out of which 2 are done, 3 more are to be done. We are almost in the last leg of closure on all 3 for both Nashik and Thane. It should be done by -- before the end of this quarter, quarter 4.

items.statement: Chennai hospital construction to complete in 2 years; agreement signed for 26-year lease.
items.quote: KIMS entered into an agreement with Andrea Saba for its land to construct and operate a hospital at Chennai for 26 years. The construction is expected to be completed within 2 years.

items.statement: Debt to moderate unless new large expansions announced.
items.quote: Correct. Unless we don't announce anything large, I think debt should moderate.

items.statement: Expects 15-18% overall revenue growth in FY27.
items.quote: Yes. As of now we still expect and on the basis of the forecast on this end we expect in between you know maybe 16 to, or rather 15 to 18% of overall growth.

items.statement: Expects 12-14% CAGR over next 3-5 years and plans to double revenue by 2030.
items.quote: But definitely the order book and the program tenure, what we have received we expect somewhere about, you know in between 12 to 14% CAGR growth on for the next three to five years.

items.statement: Monthly order book of Rs 95-105 crore for next three months.
items.quote: Order book as of now on a monthly basis, it is ranging somewhere about 95 to 105 crore for the next three months.

items.statement: Targeting order book of Rs 325-330 crore for Q1 FY27.
items.quote: But if you ask me Q1 what I am looking for, or rather on the basis of the forecast, what we are targeting is somewhere about 300 and you know 25 crore or something like that for the very first quarter.

items.statement: Net operating EBITDA margin expected to reach 22-22.5% at 68-70% utilization.
items.quote: And once I'll be having utilization up to, you know, 68, 70% or something like that, definitely this operating margin would touch maybe 22% or 22.5 even, we can achieve once we have that kind of scale of economy.

items.statement: Bearing rings net EBITDA margin 18-22%; auto components 20-25%.
items.value: 18-22% for bearing rings; 20-25% for auto components
items.quote: Traditionally or other bearing ring, if I figure it out, it would be somewhere about, you know one eight, 18% to 22% in some kind of net operating EBITDA, whereas auto components, it ranges in between 22 two zero, 20 to 25% of net EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Expects US market recovery from Q1 FY27 after tariff clarity.
items.quote: But we are very much positive from the first quarter of FY27 that now the things are, things would be on a very streamline and US would be on track because till now, for last six to eight months, customers are very much in the state of you know, the wait and watch kind of situation.

items.statement: European customers indicate increased sourcing from India post EU FTA.
items.quote: Coming to the other part Europe deal as you EUDIL definitely it is welcome and our customers have again starting reviving or rather revising their you know; certain calculations and they are in they have already indicated that they would like to source more from India.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 12 crore in H1 FY26 for furnaces and equipment.
items.quote: Operating cash flow we had for the first half it is almost 87 odd crore free cash flow what we have generated again within CAPEX of hardly 12 crore in terms of couple of furnaces and a small 4G client.

items.statement: New customer additions in Q3 FY26 are for auto components; one bearing ring customer to start by Feb end.
items.quote: What we have added in the you know, in this quarter, that both this customer are for auto components and maybe in this month, before end of February, one of the bearing ring customer would be started.

items.statement: US tariff rate uncertainty persists; awaiting final notification with HSN codes.
items.quote: So, now looking to the notification or rather the issued by the US government we are not sure whether this 25%, what it is applicable to us as of now, because we also got a feedback that it would be a zero also in certain auto components, it would be an 18% also on certain kind of this thing, or it may continue with th

items.statement: Expects to close FY26 with flat revenue around Rs 1150 crore.
items.quote: We expect, as I told you, that maybe we would be closing somewhere about you know, 1150 odd something top line in this year wherein I expect almost 200 odd crores, somewhere about 180 to 200 crore additional revenue from these new programs because something it has already been started.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 62-63% in 9M FY26; expected to reach 72-75% in FY27.
items.quote: We are almost 62, 63% utilization of my overall the same and I hope or rather we expect it would be somewhere about, you know crossing 72, in between 72 to 75% of utilization in next year.

items.statement: Plans to close ROR matter before March 2026.
items.quote: And we are going to, you know submit that we would like to close this matter maybe before March 26.

items.statement: BESS revenue expected Rs. 300-500 crores in FY27, ramping to Rs. 800-900 crores from 1 GWh in FY28.
items.quote: However, for this financial year, which is just a correction in the statement, it is expected to be in the range of within Rs. 300-Rs. 500 odd crores.

items.statement: BESS Phase-1 capex of Rs. 150 crores, funded via internal accruals, for 5 GWh plant operational H2 FY27.
items.quote: This expansion will involve additional capacity expenditure of approximately Rs. 150 crores in Phase-1, entirely funded through our internal accrual, and will establish an initial plant capacity of 5 gigawatts.

items.statement: Confident of exceeding FY26 revenue growth guidance of 10-12% CAGR.
items.quote: In FY '26, we remain confident of surpassing the earlier guidance of growing on 10%-12% CAGR basis, demonstrating shared commitment, resilience, and ambition to become a top-quality polymer compounder to the world from India.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 5,000 crores revenue by FY30, with 20-25% from exports.
items.quote: We remain strongly confident in exceeding our earlier FY '26 guidance, with our goal of reaching Rs. 5,000 crores in topline by FY '30, firmly on track.

items.statement: BESS ROCE expected 25-30% with 2-3 year payback.
items.quote: We expect that the payback will be in the range of 2-3 years of time for the CAPEX, whilst ROCE we are expecting in high double digits in the range of 25%-30%.

items.statement: Positive demand momentum expected to continue in upcoming quarters and fiscals.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate this positive demand momentum will continue in the upcoming quarters and fiscals also.

items.statement: Capacity addition of 30,000 MT (5,000 HFFR, 25,000 PVC) for Rs. 50 crores, total capacity 268,400 MT.
items.quote: We have commissioned an additional 30,000 metric tons per annum, comprising 5,000 metric tons dedicated to HFFR and 25,000 metric tons to PVC, thereby elevating our total installed capacity to 10,000 metric tons per annum for HFFR and 69,000 metric tons per annum for PVC.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton improved by Rs. 150-200 per quarter, average Rs. 15,500, positive trajectory expected.
items.quote: So we expect the average, which has reached to almost Rs. 15,500, which was our overall target between Rs. 1,500-Rs. 1,600 is there. And last quarter always remains comparatively better. So we see a positive trajectory for the last quarter also.

items.statement: BESS working capital intensive, targeting 60-75 days cycle initially.
