items.quote: We are looking towards 60-75 days at max to start with wherein we will be the suppliers to them and when we think of going to the next stage, when we will be tying up with the government agencies or supplying them directly, then probably this will change, but as of now to start with we are targeting a limited cycle.

items.statement: Export growth strong, US trade deal to boost XLPE exports.
items.quote: Notably, exports grew strongly to Rs. 196 crores, almost Rs. 200 crores, in quarter 3 of Financial Year 2026, which is 27% of our total revenue.

items.quote: So this fund is going to be released. This is how we can foresee and the project should move further now.

items.statement: Maintains FY26 revenue growth guidance of around 50% year-on-year.
items.quote: we are maintaining our financial year '26 revenue growth guidance of around 50% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% revenue CAGR over medium term.
items.quote: Over the medium term, we continue to target a 30% to 35% revenue on a CAGR basis.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA margin expected 25.5-26.0%.
items.quote: operating EBITDA margins for Quarter 4 of financial year '26 are expected in the range of 25.5% to 26.0%.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin expected 17.5-19.0%.
items.quote: PAT margins for financial year '26 are expected between 17.5% to 19.0%

items.statement: Pump and motor plant expansion: bulk ordering by Q4 FY26, completion by Q2 FY27.
items.quote: we expect to complete the bulk of ordering towards capacity expansion and automation of our pump and motor facility by Q4 FY '26, with the entire capex program scheduled for completion by Q2 FY '27.

items.statement: Solar module expansion: 1 GW by Q1 FY27, remaining 0.5 GW by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: we expect the first phase of expansion comprising 1 GW of solar capacity to be completed by Q1 FY '27. The remaining 0.5 GW expansion is planned to be completed by Q3 FY '27

items.statement: Current order book over 24,500 pumps; near-term pipeline exceeds 25,000 pumps.
items.quote: Our current order book stands at over 24,500 pumps, comprising direct PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM KUSUM, and export orders. Additionally, we have a strong near-term pipeline exceeding 25,000 pumps

items.statement: Cannot pass on commodity price increases in government tenders; rates fixed for about a year.
items.quote: definitely we cannot pass it on in any of the government tenders because the rate that we have taken on the day of the tender, after that, those rates are applicable more or less for a year until the tender is finished

items.statement: Neutralized 15-16% cost impact to only 1-1.25% margin impact via value engineering and supplier support.
items.quote: the impact which was of 15%-16%, we neutralized that and brought only 1%-1.25% to our balance sheet on the margins.

items.statement: PM KUSUM 2 expected end-March or early April 2026 with large quantum and modifications.
items.quote: I think we are expecting this PM KUSUM 2 at the end of March or early April.

items.statement: Receivables delayed from Maharashtra Magel Tyala scheme; 70-75% of total receivables from Maharashtra.
items.quote: major receivables are of Maharashtra; if we see around 70%-75% receivables in total receivables, so again they are of Maharashtra.

items.statement: Diversifying into PM Surya Ghar, exports, private solar pump market, and EPC for large rooftops.
items.quote: we have started our trials in connected lines like PM Surya Ghar, and we are strengthening its backward integration even more as much as we already have, so that in the coming time, we are also opening a new vertical which is of PM Surya Ghar.

items.statement: Market share in PM KUSUM 1 around 28% of total installations.
items.quote: our share would be around 28% total directly and indirectly.

items.statement: Expects ~30% annual topline growth, supported by signed pipeline.
items.quote: If we take this headroom, inbuilt headroom, it already provides a strong visibility of growth and should support the approximate 30% annual topline growth subject to ramp-up timelines.

items.statement: VAS revenue share to increase to 15% next financial year.
items.quote: However, the value-added stream scale, we see the contribution increasing to 15% in next financial year.

items.statement: VAS net margin expected around 15%.
items.quote: And a net margin of these services would be around about 15%.

items.statement: Corporate EBITDA margin to remain 20-21%, no major expansion foreseen.
items.quote: So yes, focus is on growth if I would say, but the margin would be a certain in the range of 20%-21% which we have already achieved by the operating leverage as we mentioned before.

items.statement: H1 capex ~INR180 crores; H2 similar, total ~INR360 crores.
items.quote: So it was -- H1 was around about, I would say, about INR180 crores. The H2, Adhidev would be something in the similar range.

items.statement: Over INR400 crores of IPO proceeds allocated to capex, on track.
items.quote: And that is where you see from the IPO proceeds that we raised, we have allocated more than INR400 crores towards the capex, and we are on track and using those funds.

items.statement: Signed pipeline of 3.26 million sq ft (72,000 seats) to operationalize in 18-24 months.
items.quote: So this leaves already a pipeline of 3.26 million square feet, which is approximately 72,000 seats, which is already signed and which is expected to become operational over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Annual addition of 1.5-2 million sq ft (33,000-44,000 seats) to continue.
items.quote: And we intend to continue to operate within the similar range going forward.

items.statement: Solar power achieves ~50% cost savings versus grid power.
items.quote: 50% power savings we are able to achieve, yes.

items.statement: GCCs contribute 56% of revenue; client mix stable.
items.quote: 56% revenue comes from Global Capability Centers.

items.statement: Client retention exceeds 95%; one-third of growth from existing clients.
items.quote: Client retention has been in excess of 95% typically.

items.statement: Brokerage payout stable at 2-2.1% of revenue.
items.quote: And our total brokerage payout is about 2% to 2.1% of our revenue.

name: Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Ltd

items.statement: Confident of achieving FY26 pre-sales guidance of INR1,100-1,300 crores; on track.
items.quote: Our pre-sales we have guided in the range of INR1,100 to INR1,300 crores, and we are on track to achieve that pre-sale number.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining PAT margins of 25-30% given project mix.
items.quote: Given this project mix, we are confident of sustaining PAT margins in the range of 25 to 30%.

items.statement: Expects to retain EBITDA margin of 35-40% going forward, at least next two-three years.
items.quote: But we are expecting to retain our EBITDA level in the range of 35% to 40% going forward.

items.statement: Lotus Trident commercial project launch expected in Q1 FY27 pending approvals.
items.quote: On Lotus Trident, our Greenfield commercial project, certain regulatory and statutory approvals are currently underway, and its launch is expected in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Q4 collection expected to be much higher than Q3; exact number not anticipated.
items.quote: But exact number can't be anticipated right now but we are very much sure that our Q4 number of collection would be much higher than what we have done in Q3.

items.statement: No debt or QIP needed for next two years; sufficient cash for about INR17,000 crores projects.
items.quote: But looking forward to next two years I don't think we require anything from both of these.

items.statement: Majority of IPO proceeds expected to be deployed by next one year.
items.quote: And whatever will be the cash balance, that will be the routine process and majority of the IPO proceed we will able to deploy that by next one year.

items.statement: Of 20 projects, 15 redevelopment, four joint development, one Greenfield own project.
items.quote: 15 redevelopment, four joint development and one Greenfield own project.

items.statement: Plans to propose dividend policy to board and general body in very near future.
items.quote: We are going to propose to our board and general body about the dividend. So we will have a dividend policy in very near future.

items.statement: Arcadian completion targeted next financial year; Amalfi mostly Q1 FY28.
items.quote: we are on target to complete Arcadian in next financial year and Amalfi in mostly Q1 of FY’28.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected around INR1,250 crores with EBITDA margin of 12.75%.
items.quote: We expect the topline to be around INR1,250 crores with EBITDA margin in the visibility of 12.75% supported by a strong Q4 across the domestic and export markets.

items.statement: FY27 growth expected in upper teens; more specific guidance by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: However, you can certainly expect strong higher-teen growth. This is indicative guidance for now, and we will provide more specific details by the end of Q4.

items.statement: Unbuilt export order book of INR280-300 crores at end FY26 to be built in FY27.
items.quote: We expect to carry an unbuilt export order book of approximately anywhere between INR280 and INR300 crores at the end of FY26 to be built in FY27 along with additional PEB and Proflex capacities that will be added available for a major part of the year.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR80 crores, including Sanand expansion and Phase 2.
items.quote: We expect the total capex to be in the range of about INR80 crores next year.

items.statement: Sanand 20,000-ton expansion to be operational by Q2 FY27; Cheyyar expansion by Q1-Q2 FY28.
items.quote: Sanand plant expansion is underway. We have already started doing all the work required and we are targeting to make it operationalized by Q2 of FY '27. Cheyyar plant expansion we will immediately take up thereafter so that it becomes operational in somewhere around Q1 or Q2 of FY '28.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book INR1,059 crores as of Dec 31, 2025, up 38% YoY.
items.quote: As of 31st December 2025, the unexecuted order book stood at INR1,059 crores, up by 38% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 order inflows INR480 crores, up 86% YoY.
items.quote: Order inflows during Q3 FY26 were particularly encouraging at INR480 crores, marking an 86% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target 12.75-13%; Q4 expected stronger with better margins.
items.quote: Overall, we remain confident of achieving margins in the range of 12.75% to 13%.

items.statement: FY27 margins around 13% or slightly higher as indicative benchmark.
items.quote: Based on the current scenario, margins of around 13% or slightly higher could be a reasonable benchmark for next year as well.

items.statement: US sectoral tariffs on steel remain at 50%, no change; reciprocal tariff reduction does not directly affect business.
items.quote: Where we fall is the sectoral tariff which is on iron, steel and copper, which is flat on the entire world whatever country is exporting into the US market. So that remains intact at 50%.

items.statement: Strong export demand from US and Canada; order inflow expected in current quarter and Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The size of projects may vary but we are quite confident about the order inflow that will be coming in in the current quarter as well as Q1 FY27, right?

items.statement: Railway RUB opportunity TAM 2-2.25 crore sqm; live inquiries 5-5.5 lakh sqm across zones.
items.quote: So total addressable market only for railways for this RUBs, the Vande Bharat depots, the line sheds, that we are seeing at between 2 crore square meters to around 2.25 crore square meter, which is a huge opportunity.

items.statement: Capacity constraints at Sanand limit ability to serve domestic and export simultaneously; balancing act.
items.quote: So if my export execution is higher then we will be compromising on the domestic output. So that's how that balance will always remain but it may keep shifting on a quarter on quarter basis because my capacity, additional capacity is not in place yet.

items.statement: No plans for QIP or additional capital; focused on IPO proceeds and internal accruals for capex.
items.quote: If I have to borrow, I have enough propensity to borrow but we'll not be thinking of any such thing like QIP etc.

items.statement: Second OTC product NutriRoz to launch this month; target 16 products by Dec 2026.
items.quote: In total, I have taken a target of 16 products within this year.

items.statement: Capex per bed is INR3-4 lakh; 100-bed hospital costs INR3-4 crore.
items.quote: Our capex is very clear in every call. We set up one bed for INR3 to INR4 lakh. If we have to open a 100-bed hospital, we open it in INR3 to INR4 crores.

items.statement: Target 7,000-10,000 beds in next 3-5 years; currently around 2,800 beds.
items.quote: I had said that in the next 3 to 5 years, we will reach 7,000 to 10,000 beds. Currently, we are around 2,800 beds.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 20-25% maintained; may exceed if possible.
items.quote: That is our margin; that is what should be maintained, and if it comes in higher, it's God's grace.

items.statement: Occupancy target 70-80% easily; will increase beds as occupancy grows.
items.quote: Sir, I am planning to reach 70%-80% occupancy very easily so that it maintains at 70%-80%.

items.statement: Finalized agreement with Entero; will reach 1 lakh medical stores in 15 days.
items.quote: as soon as we join with Entero, that number will straightaway reach 1 lakh, goods will start being sent to Entero in the next 15 days or so.

items.statement: Passed on entire GST cut to customers; example price reduced from INR960 to INR900.
items.quote: we passed on the entire GST cut to the customer. For example, if a product was priced at INR960 and the GST decreased, we made the price INR900.

items.statement: Wellness patients increased to 15% from 5% previous quarter.
items.quote: We have started getting 15% wellness patients, which was only 5% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Health Card to launch soon with referral bonus and points redeemable at INR1 each.
items.quote: We are soon going to launch the Jeena Sikho Health Card, which will give patients a sense of Swadeshi and Indianness.

items.statement: Two international day care centers operational; four being built in Dubai; started Kazakhstan and Nepal.
items.quote: We have made two international day care centers operational. One in Abu Dhabi in Khalifa City, and one in Khalidiya. Currently, four are being built in Dubai. And we have started Kazakhstan also. We started Nepal also.

items.statement: Tied up with three medical colleges; first started, others delayed to this month.
items.quote: We have tied up with only three medical colleges so far. The first one has started. And for the first one, the other two we deliberately delayed because the last quarter was a weak quarter.

items.statement: Diagnostics from Chandan deal at INR3 lakh per day; target INR10-15 crore turnover.
items.quote: My target is to increase turnover by INR10 to INR15 crores just from diagnostics.

items.statement: Planning super-specialty clinics; first 5-10 own, then decide on franchise.
items.quote: So first, we will do 5 to 10 ourselves, and after that, we will decide whether to do franchises or not.

items.statement: Reduced government business due to payment delays; recovered INR20-21 crores.
items.quote: We have greatly reduced the government business and focused primarily on recovery. So in the last few months, we have recovered approximately INR20 crores, INR21 crores.

items.statement: Current year profit expected at approximately INR225 crores plus; next target is INR1,000 crores in 3-4 years.
items.quote: Look sir, right now this year our profit will be approximately INR225 crores plus. You would have guessed. After this, my next target is straight INR1,000 crores. Now for that, if I have to work hard for 3-4 years, I am ready.

items.statement: Plans to make profit 4x to 5x from current level.
items.quote: So that's why I am saying that right now I am planning to make the profit 4x to 5x from here.

items.statement: Target of 7,000 to 10,000 beds; 7,000 beds would give 50% occupancy.
items.quote: We have to work simultaneously on beds plus products according to beds. We can't separate them from each other. Because the patient uses the product later. And products bring the patient. So I have clearly said that my target is 7,000 to 10,000 beds.

items.statement: Occupancy plan now and later is 70% to 80%; launching cheaper packages to boost occupancy.
items.quote: Sir, my plan for occupancy, now and later, is 70 % to 80%. So we are launching some cheaper packages too. For knee pain, back pain, heart. We will launch their packages, then our bed occupancy will increase.

items.statement: OTC revenue target of INR500 crores in two financial years, achievable easily.
items.quote: Omkar G.: Yes, yes, yes. So meaning , in two financial years, you will have INR500 crores OTC revenue. Correct? Manish Grover: Easily. Easily.

items.statement: 15 products identified; INR1,000 crores sale from 10 products would yield INR500 crores profit.
items.value: INR1,000 crores sale; INR500 crores profit
items.quote: So like th is, 12 to 15 products are there and there are 7,000 to 10,000 beds. If I give 7,000 beds, my 50% occupancy is done. And I get a sale of about INR1,000 crores from 10 products, so my INR500 crores profit is being made like this, sir, 12x.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing expected to increase margins.
items.quote: So with that our margin will also increase. Because manufacturing must be taking some margin, right? And quality will come more under control.

items.statement: Health insurance reimbursement for day care and medicines driving growth; insurance currently less than 25% of business.
items.quote: And right now we haven't even started , health insurance is less than 25% for us. Think how much percent it can grow now. So now our journey has started.

items.statement: Chandan partnership testing at INR3 lakhs per day, target INR5 lakhs per day; 34 centers to become 64.
items.value: INR3 lakhs per day; target INR5 lakhs per day
items.quote: Sir, I told you, right? We have reached 3 lakhs per day. 7 days ago we were at 2 lakhs per day. Day before yesterday we were at 3 lakhs per day. Soon we have made a target of 5 lakhs per day.

items.statement: No capex on Chandan partnership; Chandan invests all money and manpower, company gets percentage of collections.
items.quote: We don't have to do any capex on them. Not a single rupee. Capex is theirs. All money they are investing. Their headache, their job. All money, manpower is theirs. We just have to give them whatever collection happens a percentage of that they give to us.

items.statement: Reducing government business due to no margin; government turnover cut from INR118 crores to INR8 crores in quarter.
items.quote: Government business doesn't have margin and money doesn't come in government business, so we are reducing the government business. You look, in 2024 -'25 our total turnover from government business was INR118 croress. I have reduced it to INR8 croress in the quarter.

items.statement: Ayushman Yojana coverage for Ayurveda still pending; government keeps promising but no timeline.
items.quote: Sir, that is ongoing, and the Indian government keeps saying they are bringing it, bringing it, bringing it, that they will bring it in this budget; that's what they promised, but sir, it's the government, what can I say to them?

items.statement: New ESOP scheme with 3-year vesting: 20% year 1, 30% year 2, 50% year 3 to retain talent.
items.quote: Now we brought a new scheme, 3 -year one. First year 20% will reimburse. Second year 30%, third year 50%. Due to new ESOP scheme, good manpower has come to our company.

items.statement: Targets minimum 25% year-on-year growth in Q4 FY26, including acquisitions.
items.quote: I think 25% is the minimum that we are targeting for the Q4 Y-on-Y.

items.statement: Expects full-year FY26 sales to grow over FY25 despite Q1 fire loss.
items.quote: considering the loss of sales which has happened in quarter 1 of FY26, still we are hopeful that we will grow in terms of the sales as compared to the FY25 numbers.

items.statement: Aims to grow better than industry average over next 3 years.
items.quote: in the next 3 years, we are hopeful to do much better than the market growth.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of around 40% plus/minus 2-3% going forward.
items.quote: So we want to remain in the bracket of around 40% plus minus 2 %-3%.

items.statement: Expects to sustain 40%+ margins in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: I can't give a number, but hopefully we will be able to get good budgets. If you see the last 3-4 years, that is the figure that approximately we are working with.

items.statement: North India sales impacted by construction ban; 8-10% of expected North sales postponed to Q4.
items.quote: I can give you the broad range of close to 8% to 10% of the sales, which we generally expect from the North India has not given us the sales and this could be the postponement into the next quarter of FY26.

items.statement: Construction ban in North India lifted; business back to usual.
items.quote: Yes. I think like 2 weeks back, now there are no restrictions. And they had a GRAP 4 where the entire construction interior, exterior was at a hault. Now it has been lifted and the business is now as usual.

items.statement: Wall panels contributed ~66.5% of 9M FY26 revenue; laminates 26.9%.
items.quote: In nine months, FY26 decorative wall panels contributed around 66.5% of our revenue. Decorative laminates accounted for 26.9%, and the remaining portion came from al lied products such as interior films, adhesive, and other miscellaneous offerings, providing resilience and diversification to our business model.

items.statement: Plans to start Hues Ply Decor JV by Q1 next year with investment of INR2 crores initially, upper limit INR8-10 crores.
items.quote: So we plan to start this by Q1 next year. We have put a upper limit of around INR8 to INR10 crores, but I think it would be done lesser than that. Initially, it should be around, total investment should be around INR2 crores from the company side, plus minus 10%-15%.

items.statement: Targets 12-15% annual growth in channel partners.
items.quote: So our internal target is to grow at least 12% to 15% more channel partners every year.

items.statement: Warehouse utilization at 80%; expansion readily available.
items.quote: So around 80% is the utilization as of today and whenever we need more space, it is readily available.

items.statement: Plans to introduce 300-400 SKUs in Hues Ply Decor JV in next one year.
items.quote: So we have done a joint venture where we plan to do around 300, 400 SKUs in the next one year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 expected stronger revenue and margin expansion as assets absorbed.
items.quote: Q4 FY '26 is expected to see a stronger revenue momentum and a margin in expansions as assets are absorbed and company will be able to run more efficiently as measure of the fixed costs are already booked in the financials of the company.

items.statement: FY26 ethanol production revised to 36-37 crore liters due to delays.
items.quote: Due to which we are projecting a revised production of about 36 to 37 crore liters for the year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin projected at 20-22%.
items.quote: It is looking somewhere in the range of 20% to 22%. This is the projected EBITDA of about 20% to 22% that is what we are trying to achieve.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 capacity utilization projected at 90-95%.
items.quote: For Q4, we project at least about 90% to 95% between that number for capacity use.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capacity utilization projected at 80%.
items.quote: We are projecting a 80% capacity use for Q1 because all the capacity is in play.

items.statement: SAF project capex over INR2,000 crores, completion by July-Oct 2027.
items.quote: We have projected a capex of about INR2,000 -- upwards of INR2,000 crores to set up the plant.

items.statement: CBG capex: INR650 crores for GAIL JV, INR940-980 crores for Sumitomo JV.
items.quote: So gross it will be about around INR940 crores to INR980 crores. Give or take close to INR1000 crores for the Sumitomo JV and about INR600 crores for the -- INR650 crores for the GAIL JV.

items.statement: Contracted with Nayara and Jio-bp for ethanol supply.
items.quote: So we have contracted with Nayara and we have contracted with Jio-bp for ethanol blending with petrol.

items.statement: CBG business achieved 63% EBITDA margin and 43% PAT margin for 9M FY26.
items.quote: For the nine months ended December 31, 2025, the CBG business recorded an EBITDA margin of 63% and a PAT margin of 43%, reflecting the depth and robustness of our operating model.

items.statement: Ethanol realizations fixed: INR71 for maize, INR65 for syrup.
items.quote: For maize it is around INR71, for syrup it is INR65.

items.statement: SAF blending mandates: 1% by FY27, 2% by FY28, 5% by 2030.
items.quote: India's mandate is going to kick in from FY '27 onwards where 1% of blending is scheduled, 2% by '28 and 5% by 2030.

items.statement: Q4 DDGS revenue expected INR70-80 crores.
items.quote: And for the quarter to come we expect a revenue of somewhere about -- considering the production plan, should be upwards of about INR70 crores to INR80 crores for DDGS.

items.statement: SAF investment strategy based on offtake guarantees, not policy dependence.
items.quote: Our investment strategy is structured based on offtake guarantees before we commit on ground investments.

items.statement: Expects 8-10% sales growth for FY26, with solid order book for H1 2026.
items.quote: So, we are looking at anywhere between 8% to 10% growth in sales for this year definitely.

items.statement: Mahad drag on profitability expected to reduce progressively as utilization rises.
items.quote: Mahad being a greenfield facility in ramp-up continues to be a near-term drag on consolidated profitability, an effect we expect to reduce progressively as utilization rises and fixed costs get absorbed better, consistent with what we have discussed earlier in Q2.

items.statement: Without tariff uncertainty, nine-month sales would have been 6-9% higher.
items.quote: But I would have said that we would have very easily expected to have a 6% to 9% more sales in these nine months.

items.statement: Aroma chemical prices have bottomed out; 14% duty gap with China offers pricing hope.
items.quote: So, currently, in our industry, there is a 14% duty difference between the Chinese and the companies like mine.

items.statement: Mahad targets 30% domestic and 70% export split for 250 tonnes to reach profitability.
items.quote: Point number two is we are looking at a split of anywhere between 30% local and 70% exports in terms of the 250 tonnes that we have kind of earmarked for this particular plant, which will help us get into the profitable zone.

items.statement: Mahad running at 30-35% capacity; expects independence in next two quarters.
items.quote: So, in seven months, we are already seeing that the plant is running at anywhere between 30% to 35% of its capacity.

items.statement: Camphor imports from China and GST evasion harming profitability; no anti-dumping progress.
items.quote: Today the situation is like whatever camphor is manufactured in India, the capacity has increased a lot, and demand has grown that much and because of that there is an impact on the profitability.

items.statement: Specialty aroma ingredients industry continues to grow but is crowded.
items.quote: I mean, just to answer briefly, the specialty aroma ingredients business continues to grow, looks strong, but is also crowded.

items.statement: FMCG segment strong but camphor profitability under pressure.
items.quote: We all have to also be mindful that the FMCG part of our business is in camphor, which as a product is very much under pressure in terms of the profitability.

items.statement: No current plans for JVs; open to future opportunities based on merit.
items.quote: If there are any opportunities that come in the future, we will definitely explore them based on the merit.

items.statement: Strong R&D pipeline for new products; will launch when opportunities arise.
items.quote: So, we have a very strong pipeline, which we normally do not talk about. As and when the opportunities come, we will be in a position to, A - launch them commercially and B – inform you guys.

items.statement: World's only US FDA approved camphor manufacturer, plays large global role in pain management.
items.quote: We are the world's, to the best of my knowledge, we are the world's, and I stand corrected, we are the world's only US FDA approved camphor manufacturer, point number one.

items.statement: Fiber draw capacity to reach 8 million km by end of Q1 next fiscal; preform plant to be commissioned this fiscal.
items.quote: We expect to have a fiber draw capacity of about 8 million kilometers by end of Q1 in the coming fiscal.

items.statement: OFC business total revenue potential of INR 600-700 crores in a full year with added capacity.
items.quote: I think with the additional capacity that we have put up, total revenues from this can go to about anywhere between INR 600 crores to INR 700 crores in a full year.

items.statement: OFC EBIT margins could recover to 8-9% from current ~2.5% as utilization rises.
items.quote: It's only in the last three years or so, that number has fallen to the levels they are now 2.5% or so, there is a potential that it can go to about 8%- 9%.

items.statement: Sustainable Cables segment margin seen at 11-12%; currently slightly below that level.
items.quote: But I think what should be sustainable would be between 11% and 12%. We are slightly behind that at this point in time.

items.statement: Nine-month capex of INR 146 crores in line with beginning-of-year projections.
items.quote: In the quarter, we spent about INR 36 crores and for nine months, it is INR 146 crores in line with the projections that we had made in the beginning of the year

items.statement: Of INR 300 crores capital WIP, ~INR 220-230 crores preform to be capitalized next month; fiber draw towers later.
items.quote: when that is done, out of the INR 300 crores, about INR 230 crores or INR 220 crores, somewhere around that will get capitalized

items.statement: Took 5 price corrections last quarter totaling ~12% selling price increase; two more changes this quarter.
items.quote: Last quarter, we took 5, with an overall correction of about 12% in the selling prices. This quarter, between January and today, we have already done two changes.

items.statement: Fiber prices hardening from under $3 to ~$5 per month; shortage in preform and fiber.
items.quote: from an average of about slightly under $3, which was prevailing during quarter 3, the prices currently as on date, are closer to $5 a month

items.statement: Wires and Cables volume up over 25-26% in the quarter, led by auto cables at 42%.
items.quote: Overall, Wires and Cables, the volume increase was more than 25% - 26%.

items.statement: Solar cables running at 80-85% of capacity built last year.
items.quote: Big new entrant for us during the quarter was Solar Cables, we are currently hitting close to 80%-85% of our capacity that we built up last year

items.statement: New entrants Birla and Adani into wires and cables will intensify competition; Birla production likely next year.
items.quote: But yes, there will be competition to a large extent on the wire space, but we do believe that there is sufficient space for players to coexist.

items.statement: Agricultural applications underperformed due to off season and pricing issues.
items.quote: What didn't do so well was the Agricultural Applications. A, it was off season, and there were pricing issues, so the overall numbers on the Agricultural side was a little lower than the previous years.

items.statement: Provision of INR 6 crores for gratuity due to new labor code effective November 21.
items.quote: we have reassessed the obligations towards gratuity and have taken a provision of INR 6 crores, which has been booked in this current quarter.

items.statement: Channel inventory higher than it should be due to commodity price increases pushing volumes.
items.quote: I believe so, yes, the channel inventory would have been higher than it should, I believe yes.

items.statement: Aims to grow DC refrigerator market share modestly, about 20-30 bps per year.
items.quote: Modest increases, maybe 20 bps, maybe 30 bps a year, we will see.

items.statement: Plans to grow top-load washer share modestly using mid-to-top-end product portfolio.
items.quote: And so, I expect to see us use this top-end to mid-end of the product portfolio to grow our shares. Again, modest basis points over the next five years.

items.statement: Sees significant opportunity to increase frost-free refrigerator share from mid-double digits.
items.quote: Frost-free, we are in the mid-double digits. And I think there is opportunity to take that up further, more in line with our DC or our top load kind of washing machine shares.

items.statement: Front-load washing machines have huge growth opportunity; current share below 5%.
items.quote: We have very low market shares; still less than 5% volume market share for us. And if you see the rest of our washing machines, they are somewhere between 15% and 19%. So, huge opportunity.

items.statement: Air conditioners will be a revenue driver, not profit driver, due to lower industry margins.
items.quote: So, the portfolio position for it will be revenue driver, not so much a profit driver, because the margins in an air conditioner typically for the industry are lower than the margins for refrigerators and washers.

items.statement: Intends to keep growing gross margin to fund higher ROI reinvestments.
items.quote: But the intent really is that more often than not to keep growing the gross margin, as that will help fuel any plans that we have to reinvest on higher ROI ideas.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin improved 320 bps from FY23 to 9M FY26 via P4G program.
items.quote: We, from fiscal year 2023 to the nine months in fiscal year 2026, we had a standalone gross margin improvement of 320 basis points.

items.statement: 9M FY26 gross margin improved 62 bps YoY despite RMI and forex headwinds.
items.quote: Given the headwinds on RMI, given the headwinds on FOREX, etc., as a result of all the P4G and the cost reduction programs, we have seen an offset impact of all the RMI and FX and delivered a gross margin improvement of 62 basis points versus last year.

items.statement: P4G cost productivity offset price index maintenance actions during Q3.
items.quote: And the team did a great job in managing the cost productivity, and as a result of which, we were able to offset a lot of price indices maintenance actions, which we needed to do during the quarter.

items.statement: Q3 saw low-single-digit industry growth driven by Diwali festival demand.
items.quote: In this quarter, we saw a low-single-digit industry growth, basically driven by the festival demand, we had Diwali falling within this quarter and that is where we saw a little bit of pickup of demand and that also helped the revenue.

items.statement: 9M revenue declined 1% due to weak summer season impacting Q1.
items.quote: On a nine-months basis, we delivered a top line of Rs.5,853 crores. That was a marginal decline of 1% versus last year. The decline in revenue was mainly on account of weak industry.

items.statement: Premium and high-margin portfolio expansion helped drive EBITDA improvement.
items.quote: And see, the expansion of our premium and high margin portfolio also helped in driving our EBITDA improvement.

items.statement: Air conditioner category risks inventory buildup if season is weak.
items.quote: It can be a category in which if the season does not come through well, you could be sitting on tons and tons of inventory.

items.statement: Revenue growth could accelerate to early double-digit over five years if market grows ahead of GDP.
items.quote: If the market were to grow slightly ahead of GDP, then I do not see why the high single-digit cannot become an early double-digit kind of growth number over a five-year period.

items.statement: Profitability will grow modestly, not breakthrough, due to heavy competition and regulatory costs.
items.quote: I do feel that profitability will also grow, but it will grow modestly. I do not think you will have breakthrough growths in profitability.

items.statement: FY27 will be structurally most challenging for profit due to regulatory changes and transition costs.
items.quote: I think of all the years I have been in, this would be probably from a profit point of view, structurally the most challenging year, because you have entire refrigerators and air conditioners all going up in regulation in the same year, plus the year in this full financial year which we are moving to a completely indep

items.statement: After transition year, strong margin improvement should continue.
items.quote: And after the year of transition, I think you will end up for me in a situation where we should be able to continue a strong progress basically in terms of margin improvement.

items.statement: No price increase announced yet; monitoring market for dynamic decisions.
items.quote: We are not right now talking about any price increase, etc., or communicating what we have done in the market because we are waiting and watching to see what happens in the market.

items.statement: Elica may trade off 200 bps PBT margin for strong double-digit revenue growth.
items.quote: The really interesting question for us would be what is the trade-off between that PBT margin or maybe a couple of hundred basis points lower and the revenue.

items.statement: Regulatory costs from BEE energy rating changes will impact entire industry in 2026.
items.quote: There is a significant regulatory impact that will happen in calendar year 2026 because of the refrigerators and air conditioners.

items.statement: Future ESOPs will be based solely on India performance, not Whirlpool Corporation.
items.quote: Any ESOP plans that we give to our people going forward, will be based on India performance and India performance alone.

items.statement: Commits to quarterly earnings calls going forward.
items.quote: Yes, I do commit on this call that we will have the calls every quarter.

items.statement: Evaluating capex for new projects and cost-reduction investments with short paybacks.
items.quote: Secondly, there is CAPEX for new projects that we can do. Thirdly, we could be looking at what is interesting in the market. Decisions, for example, a three-year payback or a two-year payback or a four-year payback on something that can reduce the cost of P&L on a going basis is much lower.

items.statement: Freight costs are comparable when adjusted for product mix; no disadvantage seen.
items.quote: We have benchmarked our freight costs versus the entire industry. We do not believe that we are sitting on any comparative disadvantage.

items.statement: Refrigerator penetration at 36-37%, expected to head towards 65-70% over 20 years.
items.quote: Very frankly, we should be at least heading towards the next 20-years towards 65-70% penetration.

items.statement: E-commerce and quick commerce salience to move to early teens or twins by FY27.
items.quote: I think this certainly will move very quickly maybe to the early teens or twins, right, is how we see this going forward in FY '27.

items.statement: No forward-looking margin guidance; will balance margins while increasing brand investments.
items.quote: So Mihir, we know that the margins that we've had are very good and a lot of factors are at the moment favorable. So you likely said that the commodity prices are stable and maybe on the lower side. So while we won't want to make any future forward-looking commitments.

items.statement: Most price points to return to round INR5 and INR10 by end of quarter, passing full GST benefit to consumers.
items.quote: I think as we speak, a lot of these regional players and national players are going back to INR5 and INR10. And I think by end of this quarter, most of the price points would be the round price point, passing the entire benefit to consumer.

items.statement: Britannia fully implemented GST reduction, giving extra grammage at INR5 and INR10 price points.
items.quote: So the option was that you can reduce the price point to INR4.5 and INR9. So for a very short interim period to manage the packaging material, we did that, but we were first off the block moving to INR10 and INR5 with more biscuits.

items.statement: November-December sales growth ~12%, half from volume and half from higher realizations due to GST.
items.quote: So Harit, like I said, the 12% is equally divided between volume growth and the growth that we are realizing because of higher NSC realization as a result of rate reduction. It's about half-half.

items.statement: Regional competition exists beyond East; will fight with focused resources and brand investment.
items.quote: In terms of regional competition, yes, I'm aware that in the past, we have talked about regional competition in the East. The truth is that there are pockets of regional competition in regions apart from East also.

items.statement: GST transition causing market flux; some competitors yet to move to INR5/INR10, impacting volumes asymmetrically.
items.quote: But at the moment, the market is still in a bit of flux because all companies have not fully moved towards the INR10, INR5 price point and 2 price points on the packaging still exists, which is a bit confusing.

items.statement: Loss of state fiscal incentives INR65 crores in Q3, offset by INR48 crores Labor Code provision.
items.quote: Yes. So you're right, the incentive that we got from the state of Bihar is something that accrued in this quarter and therefore is very specific to this quarter. However, having said that, we also have, as you may have seen, provided for the Labor Code impact in this quarter to the tune of INR48 crores. So in some sens

items.statement: In discussions with state governments to convert lost incentives into capital subsidy or extend period.
items.quote: We already have or in discussions with the state government authorities for providing us an alternate ways of providing the incentive that was intended originally. We're talking about converting this possibly into a capital subsidy or of extending the period of incentive or any other form that would be appropriate unde

items.statement: Adjacencies (cake, rusk, croissant, wafers) growing double digits, 3x e-commerce traction vs biscuits.
items.quote: What is interesting is that all these 4 categories, cake, rusk, croissant and wafers are growing in double digits. And we can also see that the traction that they're getting in e-commerce is a lot more. They are literally about 3x of biscuits.

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities to build composite portfolio; not everything can be built organically.
items.quote: And I gave an example, but we also believe where we have not taken off the blocks is that there are maybe attractive opportunities on the inorganic side and Britannia would be justifiably evaluating them. So the idea is going ahead that how do you really make a composite portfolio and everything cannot be built from or

items.statement: New CMO to oversee brand Britannia across verticals including adjacencies to drive synergies.
items.quote: So at the moment, what I can share with you is that one of the changes that we are bringing on is that the CMO is going to be responsible for brand Britannia under all the verticals, which also includes adjacencies, which basically, for us is croissant, rusk and cake.

items.statement: Cheese business slow; new head appointed, focus on innovation and modern trade to revive.
items.quote: So yes, like you said, cheese has been a slow starter for us. And we acknowledge that. But let me tell you some of the things that we are doing to be able to correct that. As you would have noticed in the month of December, we also now have a new head for our dairy business, who also is involved to head what we have is

items.statement: Board approved brownfield expansion at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu, raising annual capacity to 2 million units from 1.4 million.
items.quote: For this expansion, we will invest an estimate of almost INR 958 crores over a period of 2 years, reaching the target capacity by FY 27-28.

items.statement: Q4 growth momentum expected to continue on better inquiries, conversions and bookings.
items.quote: So in Q4, I'm expecting the growth momentum to continue. Inquiries are better. Conversions are better, bookings are good.

items.statement: Industry to grow high single digit next year; Royal Enfield to outgrow the market.
items.quote: I think the whole industry is looking at high single digit, that's sort of the growth. And the premium segment will grow. We will continue to outgrow the market.

items.statement: January blended model price increase of about 0.5% on select models.
items.quote: I think I would say a blended model price increase of about 0.5%.

items.statement: April and July price increases on select models contributed 140 bps, offsetting cost inflation.
items.quote: But all of this has been offset by about 140 basis points, which is on account of price increases that we've taken in April as well as July on select models case-by-case basis.

items.statement: Commodity pressure expected to persist for some more time, partly offset by value engineering pipeline.
items.quote: But there will be a bit of a pressure on the commodity for some more time. That's for sure. But we also have a value engineering pipeline, which is kicking in continuously.

items.statement: OBD2B norms added 100 bps to cost; commodity inflation net 70 bps offset by 20 bps value engineering.
items.quote: We've got 100 basis points on account of increase in cost due to OBD2B norms. We've also had a 70 basis points, which is a net impact of commodity inflation, which is offset by around 20 basis points, which is on account of value engineering, etc.

items.statement: 350cc demand continues post-GST; 450cc and 650cc recovering, with 650cc faster.
items.quote: So there is a demand for the 350cc, which is continuing.

items.statement: Domestic model mix improved gross margin by about 0.6%.
items.quote: overall improvement in GC due to domestic model mix is about 0.6%.

items.statement: US tariff at 18% post trade deal; steel/aluminum tariff clarity awaited, weighted average tariff 41-42%.
items.quote: With the latest trade deal, which has been done, the rate is 18%. However, there is a steel and aluminum tariff, that, there is no clarity as of now.

items.statement: EMEA duty currently about 6%; clarity sought, expected to go off, improving European market access.
items.quote: As far as EMEA is concerned, currently, we are at almost about 6% duty structure. Once again, clarity is being sought. Mostly that will also go off.

items.statement: One module of about INR 100-odd crores invested to add capacity for Q1.
items.quote: we also have gone ahead with one module for about INR 100-odd crores, which we have invested to come out with some capacity additional requirement for the Q1 itself.

items.statement: 450cc and 650cc capacity sufficient; debottlenecking and automation to cater next year's growth.
items.quote: So for 450cc and 650cc, there is a capacity which is built, which is good enough because currently, the utilization is slightly lower.

items.statement: Operating leverage, fiscal discipline, model mix and VA/VE drove profitability improvement.
items.quote: So primarily number one is operating leverage, as Vidhya was mentioning and fiscal discipline on the expenses, in fact, even the marketing expenses, we have done ahead planning for this season, which has also helped us in looking at a unit benefit.

items.statement: Board cleared INR958 crores capex to expand capacity from 1.45 million to 2 million motorcycles over 8 quarters.
items.quote: The board has cleared the investment of about INR958 crores.

items.statement: 2 million capacity to be fully available by beginning of fiscal year 2029.
items.quote: And basically, the whole 2 million capacity will be available to us in the beginning of fiscal year '29.

items.statement: Value engineering benefit of about 0.2%, difficult to quantify timing across quarters.
items.quote: as we said, we've talked about 0.2%.

items.statement: Price increases taken last year in April and July totaled about 140 basis points across models.
items.quote: we've talked about 140 basis points that you see both across models, yeah.

items.statement: INR100 crores debottlenecking capex to raise capacity from 1.2 million to 1.45 million, starting in 1-1.5 months.
items.quote: And about INR100 crores, which was actually cleared by the Board about 2 months back, which we said was the first quarter, which will start kicking in.

items.statement: Demand holding up well; urban, rural and semi-urban markets all growing; inquiries strong.
items.quote: So Pramod, currently, the demand is holding up. There's a good inquiry.

items.statement: All 350cc models growing equally; Hunter age profile dropped to 23-24 years, now 40% of buyers.
items.quote: It has come to almost 40% of the buyers who are buying Hunter.

items.statement: 650cc recovering faster than 450cc post-GST; 450cc recovery slower, more activation needed.
items.quote: 650 has shown the recovery much higher than the 450.

items.statement: Precious metal costs expected to go slightly higher; company hedging and prebuying for next 4 quarters.
items.quote: we are expecting that to go slightly higher, but we are protecting so that it is not hitting us as a headwind.

items.statement: International markets cautiously optimistic; Europe/UK a calibration year due to OBD2B pre-registration discounts.
items.quote: So maybe in the coming year, as I mentioned, calibration and grow. That's what is for the international market.

items.statement: Flying Flea electric: C6 launch next quarter, S6 around EICMA time; cautious category build.
items.quote: That you will see it in the next quarter time window. And S6 will come during the course of the year around the EICMA time.

items.statement: VECV producing 10,000+ vehicles per month, at 80-90% utilization; may add Bhopal capacity next year if growth continues.
items.quote: Currently, we are producing 10,000 vehicles per month, 10,000 plus. So we are almost at 80%, 90%.

items.statement: VECV exports strong in Middle East, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Africa; Q4 exports likely better.
items.quote: And going forward, Q4 also is likely to be better as far as exports are concerned.

items.statement: Expansion of 15,000 tons on track, completion by early 2028.
items.quote: Construction activity of our recently announced expansion by a further 15,000 tons is progressing as per schedule, and we stand by our earlier target of completing this by early 2028

items.statement: Composite scheme expected to be approved by NCLT by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We anticipate that this entire scheme will be approved by NCLT by Q1 FY27.

items.statement: 50-60% of next year's volumes already contracted; pricing similar to recent quarters.
items.quote: at least 50%-60% of whatever volume that we are going to sell in the next year, we have settled everything for the 50%-60% kind of a number.

items.statement: No price uptick expected for next two quarters; similar pricing.
items.quote: for the next two quarters, you can just assume a similar price. Do not expect any uptick in that.

items.statement: EAF transition to generate incremental graphite electrode demand of ~200,000 tons by 2030 ex-China.
items.quote: this transition is expected to generate incremental graphite electrode demand of approximately 200,000 tons by 2030, excluding China

items.statement: 20 million tons new EAF capacity added in 2024-25; 60 million tons expected 2026-28; 30 million tons 2029-30.
items.quote: about 20 million tons of new Greenfield electric arc furnace capacities have already been added in the calendar years 2024 and 2025, and we believe another 60 million tons will be added between calendar years 2026 to 2028

items.statement: Product mix ~70-75% ultra high power (UHP) electrodes.
items.quote: It is more or less in the region of 70%-75% ultra high power.

items.statement: 18% US tariff will hit profit but not significant; company will absorb cost to retain customers.
items.quote: with 18%, of course, it will hit the profit, but it is not going to be significant.

items.statement: Chinese UHP electrode supply not a major threat due to quality gaps; demand growth to absorb capacity.
items.quote: we are not as much worried about the impact of their UHP on us, because we can also see the commensurate demand coming.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by operating leverage, not raw material cost reduction.
items.quote: what you see improvement in margins is basically coming from our operating levels, nothing else.

items.statement: Peak utilization may reach 94-95% subject to product mix.
items.quote: probably 94, 95 might be, in real working conditions, that is I think, but we have to try, we are already at our 90-level.

items.statement: HEG Greentech will have negligible debt post demerger; project-level debt later.
items.quote: post the demerger, which will be done in by Q1 FY27, the debt will be negligible there.

items.statement: Anode business power cost below Rs.5/unit for 5 years from operations start.
items.quote: our power prices will remain significantly probably lower than Rs.5 for at least five years from today.

items.statement: HEG Greentech revenue meaningful from Q1 FY28; peak from FY29.
items.quote: You will see meaningful revenue from energy storage business and our IPP business including revenue from BESS, which we have already won, and in which we have been declared as L1 bidder, from, say, the Q1 of FY28.

items.statement: Margins should normalize progressively in FY27 as client negotiations conclude to recover tariff-related support.
items.quote: I think progressively going into the next year, margin should normalize.

items.statement: Capex for new product verticals will be within annual maintenance capex buckets; no additional capex.
items.quote: Our capex will not be altered any capexes on account of new product verticals will be within our annual maintenance capex buckets.

items.statement: Bath business expected to see more buoyancy; bedding growth to be more muted.
items.quote: We see more buoyancy in our bath business, going forward. Our bedding business, while it will see growth, but the growth would be a little more muted

items.statement: U.S. revenue share to fall below 50% over next 18-24 months; India and EMEA to drive growth.
items.quote: U.S. will substantially -- will come down substantially below the 50% mark over the next 18 to 24 months is what we believe, if not earlier.

items.statement: India market targeted to reach INR400-500 crores in next 2 years, part of INR800-1000 crores over 4-5 years.
items.quote: I think India should become approximately INR400 crores to INR500 crores market in the next, I would say, 2 years.

items.statement: Price revisions with U.S. clients to be negotiated, not automatic; effective for new orders, not current shipments.
items.quote: our price revision will need to be discussed and will be for orders that are over and above what's currently in the system, most probably, but this has to be negotiated.

items.statement: U.S. cotton not cheaper than Indian cotton; no cost advantage, sourcing based on product positioning.
items.quote: the U.S. cotton to the best of my knowledge is definitely not cheaper than Indian cotton for the varietals that we use in our industry or at least as far as Himatsingka is concerned.

items.statement: Raw material mix to shift towards Indian content as new verticals added, but varies by client requirements.
items.quote: our raw material mix will shift more -- more and more in favor of Indian raw material content. But again, that could vary depending on client requirements.

items.statement: Non-U.S. jurisdictions like India and EMEA to substantially increase revenue contribution over next 2 fiscals.
items.quote: over the next 2 fiscals, we would like to substantially correct our U.S. exposure, and diversify our exposure. And a lot of that will be taken up by India and the EMEA region

items.statement: No COCO strategy for India; focus on MBO, large format stores, e-commerce, and asset-light models.
items.quote: We're not adopting a COCO strategy because of underlying challenges in the home textile category.

items.statement: Reiterates FY26 revenue growth guidance of 20% with gradual margin improvement.
items.quote: For FY26, we reiterate our guidance of 20% revenue growth with a gradual margin improvement as operating leverage plays out and higher margin segments like switchgear scales up.

items.statement: Expects blended EBITDA margin of 9.5-10% for FY27.
items.quote: Blended EBITDA margins, I think we are, we should be able to do close to around 9.5%, 10% for FY27.

items.statement: Wires and cables EBITDA margin to improve by 1.5-2% to ~6.5% over 1.5 years.
items.period: next one and a half years
items.quote: I think we will be able to improve this by around 1.5% or 2% over the next one and a half years.

items.statement: Implementing major price hike in February and March due to silver price surge.
items.quote: So we are going in for a price increase in the month of February and March.

items.statement: Silver and copper price increases impacted margins by ~200 bps.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also witnessed an unprecedented increase in key input costs, particularly silver and copper, which had a marginal impact on the margins to the extent of approximately two hundred basis points (2%).

items.statement: U.S. tariff reduction restores export competitiveness; renewed inquiries from U.S. customers.
items.quote: That overhang is now substantially lifted, and we are already seeing renewed inquiry levels from U.S. based customers.

items.statement: Industrial switchgear market growing at 7-9% CAGR; EV charging market projected $1.6-1.9B by 2030.
items.quote: Our core switchgear market continues to grow at 7% to 9% CAGR. India has crossed 50% non-fossil fuel installed capacity, and EV charging market is projected to reach $1.6 billion to $1.9 billion by 2030.

items.statement: Growth driven by industrial switchgear, especially transformers and control gears.
items.quote: The major growth for us is now coming from the industrial switchgear market, particularly the transformers and the control gears that we are making.

items.statement: Smart meter order delays due to stringent eligibility criteria and aggressive pricing; no guidance provided.
items.quote: While we are yet to secure a large-scale order, this is primarily due to industry factors such as stringent eligibility criteria linked to the past execution, scale, evolving tender conditions, and also aggressive pricing dynamics.

items.statement: Bengaluru energy saving project to start generating revenues from September 2026.
items.quote: The project execution is going on as expected, and we will start to see revenues coming in from September 2026.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia subsidiary to start commercial production from June 2026.
items.quote: Salzer Saudi Arabia Limited, our 100% subsidiary in Saudi Arabia, where we have started to install machinery, and we are expecting to start commercial production from June 2026.

items.statement: Temperature sensor product targeting commercial supplies by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: On the temperature sensor product, which is currently under validation with two – tire-2 automotive OEMs, we are targeting commercial supplies by Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Debt to remain stable in FY27; reduction expected once smart meter business normalizes.
items.quote: Next financial year, we will remain stable at this level, I think so. But once we start seeing the normal business continuing, then we will start reducing it.

items.statement: Global PV production projected to grow to about 93 million units in FY27 from about 91 million in FY26.
items.quote: The latest global PV production outlook remains encouraging with FY'27 production projected to grow approximately around 93 million units, up from around 91 million units expected in FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected within guidance of INR 6,000 crores plus 10%.
items.quote: So earlier this year, we gave guidance of around INR 6,000 crores plus 10%. We believe our exit number would be well within this guidance.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance to be given at March year-end call.
items.quote: As far as next year is concerned, allow us a quarter. During the March year -end call, we'll probably give you update on the next year's capex outflow.

items.statement: INR 1,594 crores reinvested into the business for capex in Q3.
items.quote: In addition to delivering strong financial performance, we continue to maintain disciplined capital allocation with approximately INR 1,594 crores being reinvested into the business for capex.

items.statement: 12 Greenfield plants under development in emerging markets; majority on stream by H2 FY27.
items.quote: We currently have 12 Greenfield plants under development, all across emerging markets to support future growth in both automotive and non -automotive segments.

items.statement: Consumer electronics capacity to double by Q3 FY27 with third plant starting operations.
items.quote: The third plant is expected to commence operations in the third quarter of FY '27. We are very excited about this. It will double up the current capacity and enable vertical integration to enhance operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Consumer electronics to reach annual capacity of about 16 million units by end of FY26.
items.quote: The consumer electronics business is ramping up as planned with 2 operational plants on track to achieve an annual capacity of approximately 16 million units by end of the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Emerging businesses growing over 50%, with consumer electronics up 75% QoQ and aerospace up over 40% YoY.
items.quote: Siddhartha, as you know, our emerging business has registered a fair amount of growth, is more than 50%.

items.statement: Modules and polymer margin expansion mostly from operational improvements and Europe restructuring; more to come.
items.quote: Most of the expansion in the margin that you're seeing over there is definitely due to operational improvements.

items.statement: Integrated assemblies margin improvement expected to continue with focused execution.
items.quote: So hopefully, this continues, not hopefully, I'm sure it will continue with the focused efforts.

items.statement: Nexans Autoelectric wiring harness acquisition expected to complete by end of H1 FY26.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also signed an agreement to acquire 100% of the wiring harness business of Nexans Autoelectric, which will provide SAMIL a scalable platform for PV and CV growth globally.

items.statement: Yutaka Giken acquisition expected to close in first half of FY26; tender offer commenced.
items.quote: The earlier announced acquisition of Yutaka Giken in Japan is expected to close in the first half of FY '26 and our tender offer to Yutaka's public shareholding, which is about 30%, has already commenced on the 9th Feb.

items.statement: Net leverage at 1.1x, within stated financial policy.
items.quote: Our leverage ratio remains comfortable at 1.1x net debt to LTM EBITDA, providing us with the financial strength and flexibility to pursue our 2030 targets.

items.statement: Q4 expected to be even better than Q3, with copper scenarios playing out and customer money received.
items.quote: So , we are 1 quarter down, and we feel the thing is going to be even better in the fourth quarter, because I think most of our copper scenarios will play out.

items.statement: Targets 50% top-line growth for FY26, revenue 625-650 crores.
items.quote: We continue to maintain our target of 50 percent growth in top line over the last year, which comes to around revenue of 625 to 650 crores.

items.statement: Expects FY26 EBITDA margin of 22-23%.
items.quote: The current margin profile looks quite sustainable, and we expect to close the year with EBITDA offering 22 to 23 percent.

items.statement: Targets FY27 revenue of 800 crores, then 1000 crores.
items.quote: In the past, we have mentioned that next year we are targeting a top line of 800 crores and subsequently we would like to be a 1000 crore company.

items.statement: Expansions at Saravalli and M.E Energy Pune to complete in 6-8 months.
items.quote: Furthermore, we have commenced the expansion of Kilburn factory at Saravalli, which is expected to complete in the next six to eight months. Also, we have commenced Phase 2 expansion at M.E Energy at Pune.

items.statement: Order backlog 495 crores; received 70 crores orders/LOIs since Jan 1.

items.statement: U.S. consumer demand remains robust; no signs of weakness seen.
items.quote: I think just our sort of understanding or reading is that it's relatively stable and U.S. consum er demand remains robust. We are not seeing any signs of weakness.

items.statement: Continued shift towards lab-grown diamonds; trend clear and will accelerate.
items.quote: I think we continue to see a shift towards lab-grown diamonds. I think that the trend is very clear, and it will continue to accelerate.

items.statement: May exit certain low-ROCE, consignment-heavy B2B customers to improve cash conversion.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth guidance for FY27 is 8-9%.
items.quote: On a standalone basis, we should be able to grow 8% - 9% in terms of revenue.

items.quote: our Board has yesterday approved a further investment of INR218 crores for further enhancing the capacity of the Machine Building Division for presses as well as certain industrial machinery.

items.statement: Ongoing Machine Building expansion to complete by July 2026, adding INR225 crores annual revenue.
items.quote: This ongoing expansion is expected to be completed by July 2026. And when completed, it can give an additional annual revenue of INR225 crores.

items.statement: Board approved INR22.6 crores for new machining facility for iron castings, adding INR20 crores annual value addition.
items.quote: our Board has approved an investment proposal of INR22.6 crores for setting up a new machining facility for our Iron castings business. This can yield an additional value addition of about INR20 crores per annum.

items.quote: The proposed investment of INR87 crores has now been revised to INR110 crores. The first phase of this facility is expected to be completed by March 2027 and the second phase by March 2028.

items.quote: The orders in hand as on 31st December 2025 on a consolidated basis are INR8,709 crores against INR7,334 crores as on 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin of 8-9% is fair to expect for core business.
items.quote: No, I think what you're saying 8%- 9% is a fair, fair thing to expect.

items.quote: So as of now, we are not seeing too much adverse impact on our costing. But if commodity prices were to rise any further, significantly rise any further, it might have happen.

items.statement: Overall demand trend encouraging, inquiry position robust, export inquiries picked up.
items.quote: The overall demand trend continues to be encouraging, and the inquiry position continues to be robust. Export inquiries have also picked up.

items.statement: Confident in 5-7% LFL growth despite high base; no headwinds seen.

items.quote: Yes, definitely, we are already on the job, and we expect to increase the turnover by at least 25% to 30% in next financial year. From INR200 crores, we wish to go to INR250 crores, INR260 crores.

items.statement: Cotton yarn prices increased INR20-25 in last 45 days; no pricing pressure, prices rising.

items.statement: Cotton yarn spreads currently around INR130 vs INR113 in Q3; expected INR20 higher than last quarter.
items.quote: Right now, I think the spreads, which were -- at cotton yarn spreads, which were at about INR112, are now around INR130 or so.

items.statement: EU-India FTA game changer; duties for India to go from 9-12% to 0%, while competing LDC countries phase out to 8%.
items.quote: And with EU, of course, there is a substantial change in the duties because right now, most of our competing countries are paying 0% duty. And we were paying 12% -- 9% to 12% right now. And once this deal is formalized in the next 6 to 8 months, we are going to come back to 0% -- we are going to be also at 0%.

items.statement: Sharp demand from China for cotton yarns after long time; Bangladesh consistent; India-US deal unlocked additional demand.
items.quote: As the new year started, we have witnessed a sharp demand from China for cotton yarns after a long time. Bangladesh has been pretty consistent and resilient for us in spite of all the uncertainties in the market before the impending elections.

items.statement: Cotton prices are the only headwind; hope US cotton gets duty-free access once deal signed.
items.quote: Cotton prices are the only headwind left in the system to make us the most competitive textile nation in the world. There's a ray of hope that U.S. cotton would be given a duty-free access once the deal is signed.

items.statement: Fire accident at Bathinda plant; financial impact INR1.5 crores to bottom line.

items.statement: Industry consolidation: 5-6 million spindles shut down in India; more consolidation expected.

items.statement: MedTech revenue could reach INR1,000 crores in 3-5 years with 20-25% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: So in the next 3 to 5 years, revenue could be around INR1,000 crores and EBITDA would be around, say, 20%, 22%, 25% would take higher.

items.statement: Occlutech expected to achieve 10% EBITDA by FY27, rising to 23-24% in 3 years.
items.quote: And our estimate is to have 10% EBITDA by FY '27, which will take us to around 23% to 24% in 3 years' time.

items.quote: Yes, probably around INR600 crores, we are estimating in the calendar year '26. And then subsequently, we will grow that number up to INR780 crores in -- yes, approximately 14% CAGR about -- for the next 5 years.

items.statement: MedTech will require INR200-300 crores additional investment over 3-4 years, mostly already done.
items.quote: So, I think, more or less, maybe overall medtech .will take INR200 crores to INR300 crores more of investment in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.quote: So the initial investment will be of around INR1,100 crores.

items.statement: Occlutech gross margin currently ~73%, with potential for improvement via operating leverage and cost optimization.
items.quote: Yes. So, first of all, the gross margi n of the company is as of now close to 73%.

items.quote: But as of now, the way it looks like, it looks like overall close to, say, INR80 crores to INR100 crores impact, but some of this would get -- should get nullified by some of the market pricing because even our trade generic business, we have a big portfolio on that front.

items.statement: Domestic business expected to grow 100-150 bps above IPM, with IPM growth recovering.
items.quote: I have always maintained that we will continue to grow at 100 to 150 basis points more than the IPM growth.

items.statement: Trade generic business expected to return to high single-digit to early double-digit growth from next year.
items.quote: I think we will be back to our high single-digit to early double-digit kind of growth even in generic business from next year.

items.quote: But if you don't consider the additional portfolio, which we are going to launch or you don't consider LA, which is a big opportunity, the payback is around 10 years on this asset.

items.statement: CBG blending currently below 1% of volumes, minimal impact.

items.quote: We look at the cash flows around May when we announce our final results. That is the time we can take a call based upon the liquidity and the discussions that will happen internally at the Board level.

items.statement: Interest rate reduction to 9.65% for fund-based limits, full impact in FY27 finance cost.
items.quote: The latest sanction from the Lead Bank of Consortium sees a fund-based limit interest rate at 9.65% per annum and further reduction in non-fund-based limits.

items.value: INR18 crores to INR20 crores per month

items.quote: We have lost 1 month, we have lost INR100 crores at least.

items.quote: So, whatever business we have lost, thanks to the downgrade, that will be reclaimed over a period of something like 3 to 5 years.

items.quote: Looking ahead, driven by strong growth momentum and portfolio of high-value margin-accretive products, we expect FY '27 full year EBITDA margins to be in double-digit number.
