items.statement: Leverage to reach peer levels of 3.5x-5x with growth; no equity needed.
items.quote: I think if you look at most of peers in the industry are operating somewhere between 3.5x to 5x, right? So that's really been where most of our peers are.

items.statement: One more state to be added for Micro LAP business in next 6 months.
items.quote: I think it's fair to say that in the next 6 months, we would like to add one more state for our MLAP business.

items.statement: All-in yield fell to ~17.25% from 18-18.25% due to prime segment; NIM broadly stable.
items.quote: So all-in yield, which used to be about 18% to 18.25%, right, that has come to about 17.25%. But our NIM has broadly remained same because our own cost of fund has come down.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost 9.1% vs book cost 10.3%; convergence expected to save interest cost.
items.quote: So I mean, you would see there is a gap between our incremental cost of borrowing, which is at about 9.1% versus our cost of borrowing in the book, that is 10.3%

items.statement: Strong disbursement momentum expected in Q4; 20% QoQ growth maintained.
items.quote: So a lot of these actions that we're taking are towards maintaining this growth momentum of 20% that we saw in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Prime segment added, expanding addressable market with lower yields and credit costs.
items.quote: We've added prime segment, which we're not serving earlier, thereby expanding our addressable market. The yields and credit cost on loans to this segment would be lower.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR8,100 crores, PAT margin 4.25% plus, volume ~750 kg average.
items.quote: And the revenue guidance we have given INR8,100 crores for the next year and 750 kg on an average, we are expecting next year.

items.statement: FY30 revenue target INR18,000-19,000 crores, PAT margin 5.2% plus, OCF to PAT ~20%.
items.quote: To summarize, we are looking at revenue of INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores, PAT of 5.2% plus, OCF to PAT of close to 20% and achieving net debt-free position by 2030.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 8.27% in 9M FY26 from 5.97% in FY24, up 230 bps.
items.quote: In the current year-to-date, our consolidated gross margin stood at 8.27% versus 5.97% in FY '24, means an increase of 230 bps.

items.statement: Interest cost currently ~1.2% of sales, expected to reduce to virtually zero with deleveraging.
items.quote: As cash flow strengthens and debt is repaid, interest cost currently at close to 1.2% of sales will reduce to virtually zero.

items.statement: 9-month capex around INR35-40 crores; annual factory capex ~INR50 crores.
items.quote: So around INR35 crores - INR40 crores.

items.statement: Advanced gold business 12% of volume; making charges INR11 crores in Q3.
items.quote: So 12% was from advanced gold in this quarter and value, maybe you can calculate.

items.statement: Value-added products now >50% of revenue vs 4-5% three years ago; 18kT share 20% in Dec quarter.
items.quote: Value-added products now contributes more than 50% of the revenue compared to just 4% to 5%, 3 years ago.

items.statement: Gold price rise 60-70% in a year; shift to lighter caratage; demand resilient for lightweight jewelry.
items.quote: So you can say gold prices have risen by, I think, 60%-70% in a year.

items.statement: Fully back-to-back hedged; no direct impact from gold price movements.
items.quote: We are fully back-to-back hedged, so price movements do not directly benefit us.

items.statement: Gold price volatility can soften demand and strain unorganized players, but organized players gain advantage.
items.quote: However, when gold prices rise sharply, end demand tends to soften and unorganized manufacturers struggle with the additional working capital requirement.

items.statement: No equity dilution or fund raise planned; growth funded by internal accruals.
items.quote: So we are all nicely funded, and we are guiding for cash flow. So we are not planning for any dilution at this point of time.

items.statement: Promoters to take zero salary from FY27, compensation via dividends only.
items.quote: As promoter, we have agreed for Zero salary compensation model from FY'27. We will follow dividend-only compensation.

items.statement: Global audit firm to be appointed from April 1, 2026.
items.quote: From 1st April, 2026, global audit firm will be put in place, kudos to Siddharth for leading this change.

items.statement: Residential vertical EBITDA breakeven by FY27; AGEasy breakeven by Q4 FY27; consolidated profitability by FY28.
items.quote: move towards breakeven in residents vertical by end of FY '27.Focus on increasing Care Home occupancy, scale AGEasy to reach eventually a potential breakeven by FY '27 last quarter with consolidated profitability expected by FY '28

items.statement: Plan to raise INR200-250 crores in next 6-9 months for growth.
items.quote: We will raise funds about INR200-250 crores. In what shape and form and structure, we will decide, but that much fundraise we will do in the next 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Total investment in AGEasy by March 2026 about INR180 crores; additional INR40-50 crores needed.
items.quote: by the end of this year, which is March '26, about total INR180 crores would have been invested in AGEasy so far

items.statement: Committed to 1.5 million sq ft; 1.04 million locked in, seeking 0.5 million more in Chandigarh, Bengaluru, Chennai.
items.quote: we are aggressively pursuing to make our commitment of 1.5 Mn come true. For this year, 1.04 Mn is already locked in. We are looking for 0.5 Mn more.

items.statement: AGEasy steady-state EBITDA margin 15-20% at INR500 crores top line; ROCE >30%.
items.quote: Eventually steady state EBITDA margins would be somewhere around 15% to 20% at the top line of INR500 crores.

items.statement: Care Homes contribution margin target 30% at 70% occupancy.
items.quote: it should trend to 30% for Care Homes, which are trending towards 7 to 8 quarters or 70% occupancy.

items.statement: AGEasy organic to performance marketing mix to shift from 20:80 to 40:60 next year.
items.quote: the mix today of organic to performance is approximately 20 to 80, 20 is organic and 80 is performance driven. Next year, this ratio will move towards 40-60.

items.statement: Care Home occupancy improved from 25% in Q2 to 27% in Q3 FY26; targeting 50% before expanding beds.
items.quote: Our occupancy also has improved sequentially from 25% in Q2 FY '26 to 27% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Noida sales price moved up significantly; Phase 2 launch expected to yield better profit.
items.quote: the sales price has moved up significantly. So as and when we get the approval and launch Phase 2, then we'll have a nice decent profit more than what we expected.

items.statement: Flipkart technical glitch impacted AGEasy; largely solved, pending inwarding expected in Feb-Mar.
items.quote: there was a technical glitch in one of the marketplaces channel, Flipkart particularly.

items.statement: Noida Phase 1 OC expected in next couple of months; then Phase 2 approval to be pursued.
items.quote: we're hoping in the next couple of months, we'll get the OC clarified, and then we'll start pushing hard for the Phase 2 approval.

items.statement: Noida Phase 1 pending collections ~INR150 crores; DM fee ~INR15 crores to be received.
items.quote: once the OC will come, the collections of approximately INR150 crores odd will be pending against which we will be getting a INR15 crore fee straight as a DM fee.

items.statement: Residential 360 collections lumpy in FY27, steady from FY28.
items.quote: 360 lumpy would only be for '26-'27, just to correct you. After that, it is pretty much in shape.

items.statement: Care Home bed expansion paused; decision mid-year after seeing 50% occupancy.
items.quote: we will take a call midyear around September, October, once we see that at least half the beds move towards breakeven.

items.statement: CMCD INR1,000 crore revenue target delayed by a few quarters, now expected by FY28.
items.quote: we are still comfortable -- while there is a delay by a few quarters, in terms of our ramp-up to the INR1,000 crores, we don't see any significant issues and realizing that by FY '27-'28

items.statement: R32 first full year revenue expected around INR600 crores.
items.quote: The first full year, we should have around INR550 c rores -- INR600 crores, roughly around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Suspension PVC expected to break even at PBT level in February and March.
items.quote: Suspension PVC by February and March, yes. The answer is yes.

items.statement: Caustic soda production to normalize by March 2026.
items.quote: We expect the production to normali ze by March 2026 in 2 months from now.

items.statement: MPB-3 Phase 3 completion and pilot commissioning targeted in Q4 current year.
items.quote: MPB-3 Phase 3 is expected to be completed in Q4 of the current year with pilot commissioning also targeted for Q4 of this year, following which, production is expected to ramp up gradually.

items.statement: Civil works for MPB-4 targeted for completion in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Civil works for MPB-4 are targeted for completion in Q1 of FY '27.

items.statement: R32 capacity expansion of 14 KTPA underway; commercial sales to start post swing plant commissioning by end of this quarter.
items.quote: On our refrigerant gas project, the R32 capacity e xpansion of 14 KTPA is underway, including 2 new R32 plants of 10 KTPA and 2 KTPA capacity, respectively, and conversion of the existing R22 capacity into a swing plant at Mettur. Commercial sales are expected to start post the swing plant commissioning by the end of t

items.statement: Suspension PVC breakeven contribution margin is INR11,000-12,000 per ton.
items.quote: That generally varies between somewhere around INR11,000 to INR12,000 per ton.

items.statement: Paste PVC price increase of INR2,000 per ton rolled out recently.
items.quote: But I think in Paste PVC, the price increase has on ly been -- we've just rolled out one price increase of around INR2,000 very recently.

items.statement: Chinese export tax rebate withdrawal of 13% or $70-80 per ton effective April 2026 expected to reduce Chinese export price advantage.
items.quote: This rebate, which amounted to 13% of the export pr ice or roughly around $ 70 to $ 80 per metric ton, has been a significant factor supporting Chinese exports to India.

items.statement: Suspension PVC demand expected to recover, ending year flat or slightly higher than last year.
items.quote: Therefore, for the year as a whole, I believe that we would make up this very small negat ive in the first 9 months and we'll end up either at the same level as last year or maybe slightly more than that.

items.statement: Paste PVC demand strong with 8% increase in first 9 months and continued pull in January and February.
items.quote: As far as Paste PVC is concerned, actually, the de mand has been very strong. There has been an 8% increase in the first 9 months of the year on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Possible surge in Chinese PVC imports in March before export tax rebate withdrawal, but manageable given strong demand.
items.quote: So there could still be some increase in quantities coming in, in March, but we believe that it is manageable especially given the fact that the demand has come back strongly.

items.statement: No equity fundraising plans currently; debt fundraising ongoing as per plan.
items.quote: As for equity raising is concerned, w e don't have any plans as of now. I can't comment about the next 2 years. But we don't have any plans as of now.

items.statement: Next year store openings: not less than 20, up to 25-30.
items.quote: Next year I am saying not less than 20 but up to 25 to 30.

items.statement: COGS expected at 53-55%, PAT margin 20-22%.
items.quote: On the COGS side, you can expect COGS to the level of 53% to 55% and PAT margin somewhere between 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Capex per store: INR25-30 lakh for silver, INR50-60 lakh with diamond, INR1 crore for own store.
items.quote: if it is a only for fashion jewellery of the silver, then capex is required INR25 to INR30 lakh. If it is including diamond, then capex is required around INR50 to INR60 lakh.

items.statement: Diamond share to rise to 45%, silver to 55% by H1 next year.
items.quote: I am expecting it to become almost 45% of the diamond and 55% of silver by H1 of next year.

items.statement: Margins likely to improve due to indigenous manufacturing and silver price savings.
items.quote: So margins are likely to improve.

items.statement: No dilution or debt needed for at least 18 months; treasury of INR70 crores sufficient for 25 EBOs.
items.quote: No, as I said in coming at least 18 months' period, I am not requiring any dilution or any debt for funding the expansion either FOCO model, FOFO model, company-owned or third-party franchise.

items.statement: Same-store growth expected not less than 25% on average.
items.quote: But yes if you go on average out the SSG will not be less than 25%.

items.statement: Main board listing expected by September 2026 after FY26 results.
items.quote: So we can get listed in main board after the declaration of result for 31st March and it is on the track, we are preparing for that and you will get it to see if everything goes correct through the regulators and everything by September '26, you will see ourselves on the main board.

items.statement: AI impact on jobs may affect consumer sentiment but not drastically reduce buying power.
items.quote: But I don't think that it will reduce the consumer's buying power drastically, because nothing like this is going to happen that today 2 crores are employed and suddenly AI came so only 50 lakh remained employed 1.5 crores will remain unemployed.

items.statement: 9-carat gold jewellery sold 1 kg gross weight since launch.
items.quote: And I can tell you, 1 kilo on gross weight basis we have already sold 9 carat jewellery.

items.statement: Reva Diamond Jewellery IPO opens Feb 24, listing tentatively March 4.
items.quote: So it is already on public domain that issue is opening on 24th of February and tentative listing date is 4th of March.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA to be largely in line with last year with only marginal growth.
items.quote: Looking ahead for the full year FY '26, we expect EBITDA to be largely in line with last year with only marginal growth.

items.statement: Confident of meeting CDMO revenue guidance for FY26, but exceeding target now difficult.
items.quote: We are confident of meeting our CDMO revenue guidance for FY '26. However, exceeding that target, which was earlier a possibility, now looks difficult due to certain project deliveries getting pushed by a few months.

items.statement: Atali project total outlay INR450 crores; INR300 crores capitalized, balance to complete in next couple of months.
items.quote: No. So we have done the capitalization of around INR300 crores and the total project outlay is around INR450 crores. So that balance, certain second phase is getting completed. And we will have that completion happening in next couple of months.

items.statement: Xanthine expansion project approved at around INR150 crores for both sites.
items.quote: Xanthine in total, the project that we have approved is around INR150 crores, with both the sites together.

items.statement: At least one new block at Atali next year; not a large capex.
items.quote: Yes, yes, we will have at least one block coming up in Atali in next year. So we will get that capex approval going forward.

items.statement: API business to see new launches in 2026; FY27 to be better year overall.
items.quote: In 2026, we have a few launches like Apixaban and a few other anticancer products that are getting launched in 2026. So with those launches, we will see 2026 to be a better year -- 2026-'27 to be a better year overall in terms of API.

items.statement: CDMO growth guidance for FY27 to be provided after budgeting exercise in March; good growth expected.
items.quote: I think we will be able to give that guidance of CDMO/CMO growth post our budgeting exercise, which we will do in next month. But we are looking at good growth.

items.statement: Net debt to equity expected around 0.3-0.35 by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: I think we should look at net debt to equity of around 0.3 -- between 0.3 and 0.35, depending upon how Q4 goes.

items.statement: CDMO working with 21 customers, 59 active projects, 40 commercial.
items.quote: We are working with 21 customers and the number of active projects are 59, out of which 40 projects are in the commercial stage and 19 are under various stages of development, both at customer end.

items.statement: INR49 crores of goods in transit not booked as sales in Q3; expected to be booked in Q4.
items.quote: Apart from Q3 reported sales, another INR49 crores worth of goods were in transit as of 31st December '25. These goods could not be booked as sales due to accounting norms.

items.statement: Plans to launch INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV in Noida in Q4 FY26, targeting overall presales guidance.
items.quote: Max Estates is now planning launches, aggregating about INR4,000 crores GDV in Noida, comprising of Max One in Sector 16B and a project in Sector 105 in Noida targeted for Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Expects FY27 collections of INR2,800-3,000 crores from existing and new sales.
items.quote: No. It will come -- it will more range close to in the range of INR2,800 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Aims to add 1-2 million sq ft residential and 1-1.5 million sq ft commercial annually, deploying INR1,000 crores.
items.value: 1 million to 2 million square feet residential; 1 million to 1.5 million square feet commercial; INR1,000 crores
items.quote: we are planning to acquire in the range of 1 million to 2 million square feet of residential every year and close to 1 million to 1.5 million square feet of commercial every year to augment our portfolio. In terms of GDV, what we expect is to deploy a capital of close to INR1,000 crores across the residential and comme

items.statement: Incurred INR350 crores on projects and INR450 crores on land acquisition in Q3.
items.quote: what we have incurred in the current quarter is a number in and around INR350 crores on the project. In addition, in the current quarter, we also paid out for the new acquisition, which we did on the Golf Course Extension Road, which had an outlay of close to INR450 crores.

items.statement: Pre-leased 200,000 sq ft at Max District for INR270 crores over 9 years, 35% premium to market.
items.quote: signing of an LOI for a long-term lease, pre-leasing 200,000 square feet at Max District, Sector 65, in Gurugram, securing gross rentals of over INR270 crores over the lease period. The transaction has been concluded 2.5 years ahead of the project completion and at a 35% premium to the prevailing micro market rentals.

items.statement: Operating margin exceeds 25% in Q3 FY26 after adjusting for marketing expenses.
items.quote: If we adjust for that, we would be looking at an operating margin in excess of 25%.

items.statement: Estate 28 margins 40-45%; Estate 360 and 361 margins 22-25%.
items.quote: in the case of Estate 28, we would be having margins in the range of 40% to 45%, which is an outright asset. And in the case of Estate 360 and 361, which are in the nature of joint development agreement, we will have margins of 22%, 25%.

items.statement: Average price realization at Estate 361 is INR22,000 per sq ft, premium to micro market and Estate 360.
items.quote: average price realization in this development currently stands at INR22,000 a square foot, reflecting a significant premium to the prevailing micro market as well as to our previous launch project Estate 360

items.statement: Focus on premium residential (INR6-14 crores) and senior living segments in NCR.
items.quote: we are both in the premium segment and also in the senior living segment. And they straddle the range of the entire premium category upwards of INR6 crores, INR7 crores up till about INR12 crores, INR13 crores, INR14 crores.

items.statement: Delhi land pooling approvals pending; hopeful to progress in coming year.
items.quote: So far, there is no incremental progress based on what we had last reported, but we continue to work for the approvals and are very hopeful that in the coming year or so we should be able to move the needle on the approval process.

items.statement: No incremental debt taken in Q3; net debt INR414 crores as of Dec 2025.
items.quote: incremental debt has not been taken during the period. The only regular construction finance debts have been taken.

items.statement: Commercial portfolio annuity rental potential over INR700 crores annually.
items.quote: commercial portfolio is poised for an annuity rental income potential of more than INR700 crores annually on a 100% basis across delivered and under-construction assets over the next few years.

items.statement: Revenue run rate to remain INR 220-250 crores per quarter for next 2 quarters, then rise to INR 270-280 crores after ASK full rollout.
items.quote: So, what we are talking is our revenue run rate which is currently between INR 220 to 250 crores per quarter. It is likely to remain at least for next 2 quarters. Then after 2 quarters, once we have completed ASK full rollout, we will add another INR 40 to 50 crores in a quarter/quarterly run rate.

items.statement: New businesses to contribute 25% of revenues in next 2-3 years, up from 11-12% currently.
items.quote: Our new businesses in the next 2 to 3 years will contribute about 25% to revenues. We are already at 11% to 12% in this year. So , from 11% to 12% to 25% in next 2 to 3 years, we are aspiring for that kind of growth in new businesses.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to expand by 300-400 basis points over next couple of years.
items.quote: So, EBITDA, we are already at 19%, if you see. So , there will be an expansion of 300 to 400 basis points, which is what we said last time also in next couple of years once we start growing our revenues at this stage.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands at over INR 1,600 crores, nearly twice annual revenue.
items.quote: The unexecuted order book stands at over INR 1,600 crores, nearly twice our annual revenue.

items.statement: Aadhaar Seva Kendra project to add INR 200 crores annual revenue once 190 centres fully rolled out by September.
items.quote: Once that is implemented on a full-scale basis, we'll have about INR 200 crores revenue increase on a year-on-year basis on an annual basis.

items.statement: Won INR 25 crores Ethiopian agricultural DPI mandate, spread over 2-3 years.
items.quote: We won a strategic national level mandate valued at INR 25 crores to implement the digital public infrastructure for the Ethiopian agricultural ecosystem.

items.statement: Existing businesses (Tax, CRA, identity) to grow at 8-10% average rate.
items.quote: What we are saying is our existing businesses, which is Tax, CRA and foundational identity businesses continues to grow at an average rate of 8% to 10%.

items.statement: CRA business growth normalized at 12-14% excluding pricing impact; stabilization expected in one more quarter.
items.quote: About 12% to 14% growth, I would say, if we remove the impact of the pricing.

items.statement: New businesses contributed 11% of operating revenue in 9MFY26 vs 4% in FY25.
items.quote: In the first nine months of FY26, they contributed in double digits, 11% of operating revenue compared to 4% in FY25.

items.statement: Senior management exits due to retirement and restructuring; no further large-scale changes expected.
items.quote: The complete restructuring has been carried out. We have strong leaders in place, and there should not be any sort of changes or restructuring after this.

items.statement: No plan for buyback; cash to fund working capital for large RFP projects and inorganic opportunities.
items.quote: No. So, as of now, there is no thought process or there is no plan of buyback, but we would definitely consider and put...

items.statement: Depreciation run rate to remain 4.5-5.5% of revenue.
items.quote: So, the run rate for depreciation will increase. Right now, we are at about 4.5% on revenue. So, it will remain between 4.5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Cloud business strategy to be clear in next 1-2 quarters; considering sovereign cloud and partnerships.
items.quote: So right now, we are in a strategic phase for this business. But having said that, I think in the next 1 or 2 quarters, we should be clear about these businesses.

items.statement: Other income normally steady at INR 15-16 crores per quarter.
items.quote: Otherwise, normally, other income is steady at INR 15 to16 crores level.

items.statement: New business peak annual revenue of INR800 crores to start from FY27, scaling over 2-3 years.
items.quote: We have visibility of new and incremental peak annual business of approximately INR800 crores, expected to commence from FY '27 onwards, which will scale up over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected INR400-500 crores; FY27 capex ~INR400 crores excluding solar, ~INR480 crores including solar.
items.quote: we expected our total capex for FY '26 to be in the range of INR400 crores to INR500 crores

items.statement: EBITDA margin target range 29-31% over medium term; near-term range 28-32%.
items.quote: Our focus remains on maintaining EBITDA margins within a sustained range between 29% to 31% over the medium term.

items.statement: Heavy engineering signed orders ~INR180 crores; 80-85% of INR800 crores to be delivered in next 2 years.
items.quote: on the heavy engineering, particularly on the large crank shaft family, we have close to INR180 crores of signed orders right now.

items.statement: New INR800 crores business mix: 24% PV, 27% CV, 44% industrial, 4% farm equipment.
items.quote: So it is roughly around 24% coming from passenger vehicle, 27% coming from commercial vehicle, 44% from industrial and 4% from farm equipment.

items.statement: Export percentage to improve meaningfully from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: And we expect export percentage to improve meaningfully from second quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Steel is pass-through for ~85% of business with 1-month lag domestic, 1-quarter lag export; scrap not pass-through.
items.quote: steel is a pass-through in most of the cases, you can say almost 85% of the business, steel is a pass-through, but there is a lag of 1 month. And in export, there is a lag of 1 quarter. But scrap is not a pass-through.

items.statement: Alloy steel prices expected to increase by INR3-4 per kg, settlement pending.
items.quote: It could be in a range of INR3 to INR4 a kg. But it all depends on the primary steel producers and Tata Motors to settle it.

items.statement: Machining capacity increased to 68,000 MT in Q3 FY26; new 10,000 ton press in Q4 FY26, 4,000 ton press in H1 FY27.
items.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, H1 FY27
items.value: 68,000 MT machining; 10,000 ton press; 4,000 ton press
items.quote: We increased our machining capacity to 68,000 MT, an addition of 9,800 MT in quarter 3 FY '26. This expansion is in anticipation of the upcoming demand. Further, we will strengthen our forging capacities by commissioning a new 10,000 ton press in quarter 4 FY '26 and the 4,000 ton press in H1 FY '27.

items.statement: FY27 forging capacity to reach 150,000 tons, machining 82,000 tons; FY28 forging 180,000 tons, machining 90,000 tons.
items.quote: So FY '27, we'll be looking at forging capacity of 150,000 tons and the machining capacity is around 82,000 tons.

items.statement: Solar project to reduce power cost by INR25-30 crores per annum, operational from Q3 FY27.
items.quote: we expect to reduce our power cost by INR25 crores to INR30 crores per annum, which is a substantial cost reduction that we'll be seeing on our power grid on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Domestic CV and farm business grew 22% in value; CV export degrew 10-12%; PV grew 37% YoY.
items.quote: roughly 55% of our revenue comes from domestic CV and domestic farm business. So where in terms of value, we have grown by almost 22%, you can see on an average in terms of value.

items.statement: U.S. tariff clarity pending; duty may be 0% or 18% under Section 232, paid by customers.
items.quote: So it is still not clear. See, in most of the cases, the duty is paid by our customers. So we have not kept it in our scope.

items.statement: U.S. revenue share to increase from 7-8% to 15-16% in 2-3 years.
items.quote: So Mitul, so right now, we are around 7% to 8% on direct and indirect business to U.S. This will definitely inch up to 15% to 16% going forward.

items.statement: Advertising and branding spend to increase to 8-10% of revenue for next year, impacting short-term profitability.
items.quote: The advertising and branding spend for 9 months FY '26 stood at approximately 5% of the revenue, and we intend to increase this to 8% to 10% of revenue for the next year, even if it has a short-term impact on profitability.

items.statement: Revenue for FY26 expected to be 5-6% lower than last year.
items.quote: But by the end of the year, we might be 5% to 6% lower than last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to reach around 25% by end of Q4 FY26.
items.quote: By the end of the year, this should -- EBITDA should come to around 25%-odd by end of Q4.

items.statement: For next couple of years, advertising spend to be 8-10% of revenue.
items.quote: So for the next couple of years, for sure, we are going to be spending 8% to 10 %-odd of our revenue.

items.statement: Growth expected to start from next year onwards, with full recovery after a couple of years.
items.quote: So certainly, we should start seeing gr owth from next year onwards. But after the next couple of years, we'll definitely be back on track.

items.statement: Demand expected to pick up from spring/summer '26 onwards.
items.quote: We are hoping that the demand should pick up from spring/summer '26 onwards.

items.statement: Merchandise improvements expected to pay dividends from spring/summer '26.
items.quote: However, the improvements and changes that we have made in the merchandise, et cetera, hopefully from spring/summer '26, they should start paying dividends.

items.statement: For FY26, net store count to be minus 10, ending at around 431 stores.
items.quote: So for the year FY '26, we would be at minus 10, which is 431-odd stores.

items.statement: Next year, plan to close 20-25 stores and open 25-30 stores, focusing on quality over scale.
items.quote: And going forward, in the next year, we intend to close about 20, 25- odd stores and open 25 to 30- odd stores. We are not going to chase scale. We're going to chase quality for the next year.
