items.statement: No big capex planned before demerger; any capex only after demerger completion
items.quote: Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger.

items.statement: Raised INR467 cr via preferential allotment in Nov'25; prepaid INR582 cr debt in Q3; plan INR75-100 cr more in Q4 and INR100-150 cr in Apr'26
items.quote: Company has raised INR467 crores in November through preferential allotment through the promoters, their friends and relatives. We have utilized the entire INR467 crores for the prepayment of the existing debt.

items.statement: Swapped INR130 cr high-cost debt saving 125-150 bps; further swaps underway
items.quote: We are also in the process of swapping the high-cost debt to the low-cost debt in which we have recently swapped, about INR130 crores debt, which will save us about 125 basis points to 150 basis points.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals pipeline strong with customers like BSF, Dove, L'Oreal; end segments: crop protection, personal care, paper, oilfield, flavours/fragrances
items.quote: We are working with some very strong names right from BSF, Dove to many others internationally as well as within the country. Our end segments include crop protection, carbon smart products, personal care, crop protection, paper, oilfield and we are looking at new areas like flavour and fragrances.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma under pressure from feedstock cost volatility and weak Western markets; nicotine sales restarted, Gloriosa seed supply stabilizing, new branded products (Gingeren, asparagine) launched, US office established
items.quote: Thiocolchicoside the raw material feedstock, which is Gloriosa seed is now being stabilized, and the new crop is coming. So we don't foresee any problem in getting the material, and we are expecting a better price in the international market also. And the nicotine sales, which was earlier under stress, now it has been

items.statement: Aims to double revenue in 3-4 years, requiring ~15% CAGR; currently at 10% growth.
items.quote: Doubling the business will require a CAGR of close to 15%. We are currently sitting at about 10% growth.

items.statement: Expects to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.
items.quote: So you should see scaled expansion of our margin getting to double-digits within next 2 to 3 years, I would say.

items.statement: Growth mix to be two-thirds volume and one-third value in short term, moving to 50-50 longer term.
items.quote: So I will say, two-third to come from volume and 1/3 to come from value expansion in the mix.

items.statement: Expects olive oil commodity prices to remain stable, turning Italian business value positive.
items.quote: We do expect the commodity prices to remain stable in this. And hence, we also expect our growth momentum on this business to continue and turn value positive in the period ahead.

items.statement: RTE small packs (INR10) are 70% of business; large packs 30%, mix to shift towards large packs gradually.
items.quote: We have about small pack, INR10 business, which will be about 70% of the business and 30% would be on the large pack business.

items.statement: Acknowledges new competition in popcorn from Marico's 4700 BC, but sees it spurring category growth.
items.quote: So I would also see competition also to help us drive penetration on this category.

items.statement: Promoter increased stake by 4.99% from Del Monte Pacific; further 5% to be acquired next fiscal.
items.quote: Del Monte Pacific was the shareholder, which has exited or, let's say, reduced their shareholding from 15% to 10% and that shareholding has been increased by promoters.

items.statement: Focus investments on four key categories: popcorn, Italian, culinary, and peanut butter.
items.quote: Our biggest bet is popcorn business and the entire ACT II franchise. Our second biggest bet would be Italian franchise, which is sitting under Del Monte portfolio because that's where the premiumness and the entire value of that Del Monte brand sits in a big way.

items.statement: E-commerce growing at 39% YTD, quick commerce at 50%, driving overall growth.
items.quote: On e-commerce business, if you look at YTD basis, we are growing at about 39%.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion of 230 bps YTD, 330 bps in Q3, driven by foods business.
items.quote: At a quarter 3 level, that number is close to 330 basis points.

items.statement: Innovation contributes INR55 crores sales, ~5% of total, from 70+ new products launched.
items.quote: We have launched 70 -plus new products across the franchise of ACT II, Sundrop and Del Monte. And within -- if I -- and our metrics says anything which is launched in the last 24 months, we are seeing our innovations a re today contributing close to about INR55 crores of our sales, which is close to 5% of our sales.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 24-25% despite product competition
items.quote: We still believe that we would be good for looking at 24% - 25% next year.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 R&D spend expected at 7.5-8.5% of sales
items.quote: For the full year, as indicated, we expect R&D to be around 7.5% - 8.5%.

items.statement: FY27 R&D spend expected to remain at 7.5-8.5% of sales
items.quote: I think 7.5% - 8.5% is a good number to look at this stage.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 effective tax rate expected at 21-22%
items.quote: For the full year, we expect ETR to be about 21% - 22%.

items.statement: India formulations business to outperform IPM by 1.2-1.3x
items.quote: We remain confident that our India formulations business will continue to outperform IPM by 1.2 - 1.3 times.

items.statement: India Rx business to grow double-digit (20-30% ahead of market) for next couple of years
items.quote: So, I think 20% - 30% ahead of the market is what we would see ourselves at. The market is growing strong, so double-digit growth is assured.

items.statement: US injectables portfolio to ramp to $100M+ in next 3 years with biosimilars adding to it
items.quote: We really see the injectables portfolio ramping up in the next three years to USD 100 million plus with tens of millions of dollars in individual products and then biosimilars adding to it.

items.statement: Pegfilgrastim biosimilar approved for US, launch expected in Q4 FY26 with meaningful revenue from FY27
items.quote: We would launch this quarter, but you'll start seeing numbers really in the next fiscal year.

items.statement: First 505(b)(2) product launch planned in FY27, ramping over next couple of years
items.quote: In fiscal year FY27, we will start our first 505(b)(2), and that's going to ramp up in the next couple of years as a material contributor as well.

items.statement: Xywav (exclusive FTF) launch targeted for FY29
items.quote: The launch date is FY29, if I'm not mistaken.

items.statement: Semaglutide injectable India launch imminent (day one), targeting INR 50-60 crore in year one
items.quote: I think the internal modelling that we have at this point of time seems to suggest that this will be a INR 1,500 crore odd opportunity in the first year, and we talked about maybe doing INR 50 - 60 crores something like that in the first year.

items.statement: Tolvaptan competition expected staggered (Apotex IP hurdles, Teva unknown, others Nov'26/27 stay dates)
items.quote: We don't have any intelligence on Teva's approval and then we know that other competitors have November'26, 30 months stay date and into '27. So we think that it, if competition comes in it's likely going to be staggered.

items.statement: FY27 steel pipe volume guidance of 11 lakh tonnes, ~17-18% growth.
items.quote: next year we have a minimum budget of 11, 00,000 tonnes for FY 2026 and we will have a growth of approximately 17% - 18% in that also.

items.statement: FY27 steel division EBITDA per tonne minimum Rs 5,000, total EBITDA Rs 540-550 crores.
items.quote: our EBITDA per tonne will be a minimum of Rs 5,000 per ton in FY 2026 next year and we will generate an EBITDA of Rs 540 crores – Rs. 550 crores in the Steel division alone.

items.statement: FY27 lighting revenue ~Rs 2,100 crores, 15% growth; EBITDA Rs 200 crores.
items.quote: next year, we are assuming a growth of 15% and our overall turnover will be around Rs 2,100 croress. And in the Lighting division alone, we will also touch the figures of an EBITDA of Rs 200 croress.

items.statement: FY27 overall EBITDA target Rs 750 crores.
items.quote: we will have an EBITDA of Rs 750 crores in next year i.e. FY 2027.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 overall EBITDA expected Rs 200-210 crores including lighting and steel.
items.quote: in Q4, our EBITDA will be around Rs . 200 crores – Rs. 210 crores including Lighting and Steel division together.

items.statement: FY26 steel pipe volume expected 9.35-9.40 lakh tonnes; Q4 2.90-3.00 lakh tonnes.
items.quote: we will do around 2,90,000 tonnes - 3,00,000 tonnes in Q4. And I think we will close at 9,35,000 tonnes - 9,40,000 tonnes in the whole year.

items.statement: FY26 overall EBITDA expected Rs 585-590 crores.
items.quote: this year also we will do EBITDA of Rs. 585 crores – Rs. 590 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Capex of ~Rs 250 crores in existing plants; work orders for Rs 100 crores to be issued soon.
items.quote: we already have our internal projects worth Rs 160 crores and we are going to issue a work order of about Rs 100 crores within the next week or 10 days. So, we have a CAPEX of around Rs 250 crores in the existing plants.

items.statement: Steel division order book ~Rs 500 crores; lighting order book ~Rs 150 crores.
items.quote: the order book stood at approximately Rs 500 crores for Steel division and almost Rs 150 crores for Lighting, led by Spiral P ipes, Export and Domestic API orders.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 steel EBITDA per tonne expected Rs 5,600-5,700 due to stock gain.
items.quote: the stock gain in Q4 will impact our EBITDA will be around Rs. 5,600 - Rs. 5,700 per tonne.

items.statement: API demand expected to recover from Q1 FY27; ONGC ERW approval a big opportunity.
items.quote: hopefully from Q1, next year, the API demand will also come because it is natural - API’s demand will come because almo st 35 years have been completed for the life of those pipes.

items.statement: EU CBAM and quotas may reduce exports to Europe by 10,000-12,000 tonnes annually, to be compensated by Middle East and Africa.
items.quote: annually, there will be a disadvantage of around 10,000 tonnes to 12,000 tonnes but we will compensate it with other Middle East and African countries.

items.statement: Wire capacity being increased due to strong demand; additional Rs 10-12 crores spent on publicity in Q3.
items.quote: we are increasing the capacity in that also. After watching us, some of our peers in the Lighting vertical have also launched the Wire business. The acceptance is very good in the country. And to improve the visibility, we have spent an additional Rs 10 crores -12 crores in this particular quarter, for publicity.

items.statement: Management will consider buyback and demerger suggestions in Board.
items.quote: you said it well about buyback, and we will definately place your suggestion in the Board.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 7.4% in Q3 FY26 expected to be sustained in current and next quarter; volume improvement expected in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in this quarter and next quarter should be maintained in the similar range.

items.statement: Revenue target of ~₹5,000 Cr for FY27 (vs ₹3,412 Cr 9M FY26 annualized), implying ~10% growth
items.quote: Of course, we will come to the level of around ₹5,000 Cr hopefully next financial year 2026-2027.

items.statement: Knitted fabric expansion of ₹92 Cr progressing in phases, fully operational by H1 FY27; capacity up 20% from 750 to 900 MT/month
items.quote: The knitted fabric expansion that we discussed last time involving a capital expenditure of ₹92 Cr is progressing in a phased manner, and we are expecting this to be fully operational in FY 2027 first half.

items.statement: LNJ GreenPET project cost ₹427 Cr (70:30 debt-equity), targeting ₹475-500 Cr revenue at full utilization over 2-3 years
items.quote: The funding is perceived to be at 70:30 level. So, we have a project cost of ₹427 Cr. Out of that, approximately ₹300 Cr is likely to be funded through debt, and the balance ₹127 Cr is to be funded as a form of internal accruals or equity.

items.statement: Printed knit lines (120 MT/month) added via BAKPL acquisition (₹54 Cr) to access 30-35% fashion-intensive market (kids/women/loungewear)
items.quote: A key highlight of this expansion is the introduction of printed knit product lines, enabling RSWM to enter a fashion-intensive segment. The current account for approximately 30% to 35% of knitted fabric market, which includes kids wear, women's wear, loungewear.

items.statement: Power cost savings ₹1-1.5/unit via 9.6 MW behind-meter solar (₹22-25 Cr capex) and 60 MW group captive RTC with Adani (₹60 Cr equity, 26% stake)
items.quote: If you look at per unit savings would be varying from ₹1 to ₹1.5 per unit and thereby impacting our overall consumption per kg, giving benefit to us.

items.statement: Mixed demand in Q3; volume moderation in knit, denim, mélange, cotton yarn due to US tariffs; expecting volume recovery in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The volume should look better in the first quarter next year.

items.statement: Bangladesh yarn import policy uncertainty impacting near/medium term; long-term risk if India doesn't build garmenting capacity
items.quote: The uncertainty or the difficulties in that market are definitely impacting us in the shorter run for sure and medium run more likely.

items.statement: Working capital cost <9% via vendor discounting platform; no equity raise planned for GreenPET (70:30 debt-equity from internal accruals)
items.quote: So, if you talk about overall cost of working capital, it comes less than 9%.

items.statement: EU FTA (effective Jan 2026) and UK FTA (2-3 quarters) to eliminate 8-12% duty disadvantage vs Bangladesh/Vietnam; industry CAGR 8-10%, India share potential $35-40B from $8B
items.quote: Now with this FTA with the EU, which is likely to be reality next January, and this U.K. FTA which is in discussion and also maybe through in just two, three quarters, we will have the level playing field.

items.statement: Management sees start of new CV replacement cycle triggered by GST rationalization, with bulk buyers now projecting purchases for 3-4 quarters ahead and freight rates rising alongside demand.
items.quote: So we are, at this point in time, very confident that this could be a start of a new replacement cycle in the CV industry.

items.statement: Industry expected to stay strong in FY27 with phenomenal growth in H1 (April-October) on low base, though H2 will face high base effect from strong Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Overall, we still believe that the industry is going to stay strong next year.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin at 13.3%, up 50bps YoY; material cost at 72.2% of revenue, up 70bps YoY and 100bps QoQ due to adverse mix and non-ferrous commodity inflation.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 13.3%, higher by 50 basis points against Q3 of last year.

items.statement: Commodity headwind of ~50bps in Q3 from PGM, copper, aluminium; management targeting >60bps price recovery via discount reductions, with some success in January.
items.quote: It was roughly 50 basis points, Gunjan. In the Q3, we suffered 50 basis points because of this increase. And we are trying to recover it from the customer by way of increasing the prices by about 60, more than 60 basis points, including the margins.

items.statement: ICV share surged to ~30% in Nov-Dec (vs normal 22-24%) due to retail-led demand; expected to normalize to 23-24% as bulk buyers return, improving mix.
items.quote: Going forward, it has to come down to 23%, 24%. Now whether it takes 1 month or 2 months, 3 months, hard to say.

items.statement: Q3 capex INR186 cr; 9M capex INR844 cr; no major capacity expansion needed for FY27, only INR50-100 cr for niche bottlenecks.
items.quote: There may be one or two areas which where we may have to invest, let us say, INR50 crores to INR100 crores kind of amount, but those would be limited to only one or two areas.

items.statement: Switch India order book at 1,350 units; defense order book and tender pipeline remains strong.
items.quote: Current order book stands at 1,350 units.

items.statement: OHM Global has INR300 cr invested and INR300 cr earmarked; beyond INR600 cr, external fundraising will be explored.
items.quote: We have already invested INR300 crores in OHM. We have also earmarked another INR300 crores for OHM as and when needed. And like we have, I think, told you before, beyond this INR600 crores, we will be open at looking at other fundraising options.

items.statement: Dedicated Freight Corridor JNPT extension delayed; management expects minimal impact on tractor-trailer volumes over next 2-3 years, with positive offset from ICV/LCV last-mile demand.
items.quote: Even on the tractor trailer side, it will be very minimal over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Net cash position strengthened to INR2,619 cr at end-Q3, up >INR1,660 cr YoY; staff cost reduced ~INR20 cr in Q3 due to variable pay adjustment.
items.quote: We had net cash of INR2,619 crores at the end of the quarter, an increase of more than INR1,660 crores on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Management will share FY27 outlook in May; no specific number given now.
items.quote: outlook we'll share like we normally do in May and will not give a specific number on outlook

items.statement: Auto capacity to add 5-6k units/month by Jul-Aug FY27 via de-bottlenecking; another 3k EV capacity from 9S launch; FY27 ICE capacity up 7-8k from Chakan IQ platform; Nagpur greenfield adds 8-10k in CY28 ramping to 500k.
items.quote: we'll probably add this year 5 to 6,000 by July-August in ICE over what we have right now. Another 3 odd in EVs , so 7 to 8. F Y27 we would add in ICE another 7 ,000 to 8,000 at least

items.statement: 7XO has very strong order pipeline with waiting periods; 70%+ bookings for top two variants (X7L skew higher than expected).
items.quote: 7XOs got very good response, very strong order pipeline . And as some of you did mention, customers, we're back into this waiting period thing

items.statement: Auto standalone margin 10.4% (excl. contract mfg); EV business made Rs 175 cr end-to-end EBITDA in Q3 (MEAL EBITDA Rs 149 cr + M&M Rs 27 cr).
items.quote: Auto standalone without contract manufacturing is 10.4%

items.statement: 1% price hike taken in Jan to offset commodity inflation; hedging covers portion but not steel; precious metals inflation structural, iron-related supply issues may ease.
items.quote: there is a 1% price increase to take care of what is going to be the future impact of this commodity inflation

items.statement: Commercial segments (LCV, tractors, CVs) see fundamental demand shift from GST cut (10% price drop, 4-5% operator profit improvement); SUV demand momentum continues post-festive; sub-10L products very strong.
items.quote: we believe this is a fundamental shift and this will lead to a cycle of increased demand and it's not a one or two month thing

items.statement: 7XO variant mix skewed 70%+ to top two variants (X7L); 9S driving North India EV adoption; 3XO, Bolero, Bolero Neo (sub-10L) seeing robust growth.
items.quote: Big skew again to the top end, in spite of very attractive lower end versions ; almost 70% plus is the top two versions

items.statement: Memory chip shortage is a cross-portfolio supply chain risk (not EV-specific); covered short-term but risk could be severe; EV supply chain otherwise seamless.
items.quote: memory chip is something which is a watch out across the portfolio right now. That's the new rare, rare earth, let's call it that

items.statement: Mahindra Finance pivoted to growth after 3-year asset quality/controls/tech focus; GS3 <4%, ROA ~1.9%, targeting 2.4-2.5% via cross-sell; strong new management team.
items.quote: Mahindra Finance has announced in its analyst call two weeks ago that it will now pivot to growth

items.statement: Tech Mahindra on track for FY27 target of 15% EBIT margin; internal delivery org transition centralized and working well.
items.quote: It is on track to deliver what it has to in its first phase which ends by F27 and it has to get to a 15% EBIT margin

items.statement: Last Mile Mobility IPO planned next year to unlock value, not for monetization; business competing fiercely and doing well.
items.quote: we would look at an IPO next year and that is more around where the business is, where its trajectory is

items.statement: EU FTA benefits: 2.5x quota at 0% tax for exports to Europe; lower component import duties (e.g., electronics screens from 16.5%); US FTA minimal auto impact.
items.quote: we can send our cars to Europe at 2.5 times the quota that they have there, which is a great quota from our standpoint at 0% tax

items.statement: Tractor industry grew ~24% in FY26 (vs 11-12% expected); Maharashtra subsidy added ~35k units (one-time); reservoir levels, rural spending, terms of trade supportive for FY27.
items.quote: this year is going to end at 24% growth, which no one expected, right

items.statement: Farm subsidiaries impairments (Japan restructuring, Turkey hyperinflation) taken in operating profit; trailing costs to continue this year, trajectory improvement H2 FY27.
items.quote: there will be trailing costs and then there will be losses till the time the complete restructuring has been completed. So, at least for this year, don't expect any dramatic changes

items.statement: Expects 30% year-on-year growth in Q4 FY26 and maintains this into next year.
items.quote: And we expect a growth of 30% year-on-year, and we continue to maintain that going into the next year as well.

items.statement: Margins to improve in Q4, further in Q1, with real upside from Q2 when copper conductor factory is in full swing.
items.period: Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27
items.quote: No, it should be better. In fact, it will be better for Q4. And be even better than Q4, which will be in Q1. But the real upside will come from Q2 onwards and the CTC factory will be in full swing.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 approximately INR60 crores cash flow-wise.
items.quote: Approximately cash flow-wise around approximately INR60 crores.

items.statement: Order book at INR1,103 crores as of December 31, 2025; expects ramp-up over next two quarters.
items.quote: Our order book remains high at INR1,103 crores as of December 31, 2025, reflecting sustained demand momentum across our key product lines.

items.statement: Propulsion system initial orders on hand valued at about INR50 crores, expecting more orders.
items.quote: Valued about roughly about INR50 crores. We have the initial orders on hand. And as I said, we are expecting a few more orders to come in.

items.statement: Indian Railways plans to manufacture 1,700 electric locomotives next year; tenders to start coming out now.
items.quote: So Indian Railways plans to manufacture 1,700 electric locomotives in the next year. And all of those tenders will start coming out now.

items.statement: BeLink subsidiary will continue to be loss-making for next few quarters until turnaround.
items.quote: It is loss-making, it will continue to be loss-making until, for the next few quarters until we can turn that around.

items.statement: May consider fundraise later as company grows, but not sure yet.
items.quote: But as we grow bigger and as we address more opportunities, maybe later on down the line, we might consider a fundraise. We're not sure yet.

items.statement: Board approved bonus issue in ratio 1:1, subject to approvals.
items.quote: The company is delighted to inform its shareholders that the Board of Directors has approved the issue of bonus shares in the ratio of 1:1, subject to the necessary statutory and shareholder approval.

items.statement: Propulsion system trials commenced at Western Railway; expected to complete in three to four months.
items.quote: The trials of our propulsion systems have officially commenced at Western Railway. And ideally, it should be completed within three to four months.

items.statement: Board approved investment of INR90 lakh in Coincade Studios via equity shares subscription.
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved an investment of INR90 lakh in Coincade Studios Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Hind Rectifiers Limited, to subscription of its equity shares.

items.statement: About 40 products under development in R&D, rolled out continuously.
items.quote: Yes. So, there are about 40 products which are under development in R&D. These include completely new products, upgrades, improvements, engineering and these products are rolled out continuously.

items.statement: Expects higher growth in Q4 FY26 vs Q3 FY26; targeting double-digit revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: We are seeing this momentum to be even stronger in quarter 4 and expect a higher growth in quarter 4.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 at 16.8%-17.5%
items.quote: So -- but in the longer -- next year, we can say it's approximately 16.8% to 17.5% is my number.

items.statement: Secured new orders worth INR1,000 crores over next 5 years, including INR700 crores export orders and INR100 crores for EV cars
items.quote: We secured new orders worth INR1,000 crores to be executed over the next five years, of which nearly INR700 crores are export orders, including large orders from very large OEMs, and about INR100 crores of these orders are for electric vehicle cars.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR165 crores for FY27 funded through internal accruals and borrowings
items.quote: We are looking to have a planned capex of about INR165 crores for the year '27, funded through internal accruals and borrowings.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 18%, up 60 bps YoY, among highest in industry
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q3 of FY '26 stood at 18%, up by 60 basis points, among the highest margins in the industry.

items.statement: Heat Shields growing strongly; Chassis, Rubber, Forging and Heat Shield expected to outgrow Gaskets over next 5 years
items.quote: I think chassis, rubber, forging, and heat shield from the Gasket division.

items.statement: Internal target of 10-15% YoY growth in absolute EBITDA and gross profit, not public guidance
items.quote: We are internally looking at anywhere between 10% to 15% growth on EBITDA as well as gross margin on a minimum basis on a year-on-year basis. That's the internal targets that we have, but that's not a guidance, please.

items.statement: Pricing is pure pass-through of raw material costs with no structural impact on absolute gross margins
items.quote: As highlighted earlier, our pricing continues to remain a pure pass-through of raw material movements with no structural impact on absolute gross margins.

items.statement: Q4 and Q1 historically best quarters; January-February 2026 in line with seasonal strength
items.quote: In terms of the local demand, Q4 and Q1 is supposed to be the best that happens historically, and we are in line with that as we actually have seen in the month of January and February.

items.statement: Spray drying running at 100% capacity, expanding by 120 MT/year; Vankal vegetable processing at 65-70% utilization, snacks line at full capacity with 3 shifts
items.quote: For the spray drying is a 100% capacity we are using and we are as mentioned in the investor note, we have expanding our capacity by 120 metric ton in a year. Construction is already started and likely to complete in another 9 months period.

items.statement: No significant capex expected this year; will assess operational investment needs during the year.
items.quote: Although I don't see any significant capex for this year. But we'll see. And if the opportunity comes, we'll do either organic or inorganic investment.

items.statement: ECB first tranche prepaid in September; second tranche due June 2027.
items.quote: the first tranche was due for replacement -- repayment in December 2025. However, this was prepaid in September already. And I think that's where the confusion is coming from. So second one is due for June '27, right?

items.statement: Blueloop asset utilization holding steady at 25-30%; customer trials and prototyping ongoing.
items.quote: Having said that, we have been holding steady on the asset utilization. At the moment, we are still looking at 25%, 30%, which is not bad.

items.statement: US accounts for only 1% of sales; trade deal upside limited.
items.quote: our total impact is only 1% of our sales. So if we say our INR2,400 crores top line, only 1% of that business is through U.S.

items.statement: Renewable electricity project progressing; energy generation expected in Q2 this year.
items.quote: We have a renewable electricity project undergoing at the moment, which is progressing steadily, and we hope that we have the energy generation from this project in the second quarter of this year.

items.statement: Operational and go-to-market changes are sustainable, not one-time; no one-offs this year.
items.quote: We had a significant one-off last year, as I mentioned earlier, but not this year.

items.statement: Three strategic priorities: profitable growth, capital discipline, and accountability.
items.quote: Number one is profitable growth. Number two is capital discipline. So it's good to grow, but we have to -- also have to make sure that we are disciplined in how and where we spend the money. And very third thing which I have been working on in the last few months that I have been associated with the company is on the a

items.statement: No royalty paid to parent; service charges are common and benefit from global scale.
items.quote: Actually, we do not pay any royalty. So it's zero. I think that is very clear, right?

items.statement: Regional/smaller FMCG customers growing faster than larger FMCG players.
items.quote: some of these larger FMCG players are actually growing a little slower than what we see from the regional customers. So smaller brands, they are probably doing much better in terms of growth than the larger brands, right?

items.statement: Capacity sufficient for next few years after prior optimization; efficiency creates room to grow.
items.quote: we also did optimization exercise a couple of years ago, and we are pretty certain that for the next few years, we'll be okay in terms of capacity utilization.

items.statement: Focus is organic growth; open to opportunities but no M&A commitment now.
items.quote: At this moment, our focus is organic, and that's what we are focusing on. If some opportunities come, we'll never say no. But at the moment, that's not our focus.

items.statement: Headwinds include regulations, taxation, government policies, labour codes, and changing customer packaging requirements.
items.quote: I guess the headwinds are always around regulations or political environment, taxation, government policies, labour codes, all that kind of stuff, which are not under control.

items.statement: Labour code impact expected not significant due to proactive actions on employee liabilities.
items.quote: we actually took some proactive actions in recent past particularly in relation to employee liabilities. So we expect not a very significant impact to our business moving forward.

items.statement: Surplus cash in bank deposits and mutual funds yielded over 6% average during the year.
items.quote: Surplus cash was deployed into bank deposits and mutual funds, generating an average yield which exceeded 6% during the year.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected similar to last year or slightly higher; EBITDA margin should see improvement for full year
items.quote: Our FY26 revenue, we are looking at a similar level as last year or slightly higher. I cannot give an exact guidance. EBITDA margin, we should see some improvement for overall financial year basis.

items.statement: FY26 capex budget Rs 25 crore; 60% allocated to driveline and axle growth areas, 40% to engine; Rs 18 crore spent in 9M FY26
items.quote: 60% of our CapEx allocation is to future growth areas, that is driveline and actual products. So, I'm talking about our 25 crore FY26 CapEx budget. So, 60% of that has been allocated to future growth areas and the remaining 40% is for the engine

items.statement: New business order book Rs 162 crore: Rs 107 crore connecting rods, Rs 45 crore driveline, Rs 10 crore axle
items.quote: Around 107 crores of new business is from connecting rods, which is our core business. But the new growth areas contribute significantly to the new business order book which implies 45 crores from driveline and 10 crores of new business in the axle segment.

items.statement: Price improvements negotiated on old products without revision for years; positive confirmations from supportive customers
items.quote: We have been negotiating prices with customers and for many old products which did not have a price revision for many years and we have got positive confirmations from many of the customers who are very supportive and understand the business in our industry.

items.statement: Both debt and equity funding options in parallel for capex; timing differs, keeping both open
items.quote: Our funding plan is also aligned to this CapEx strategy and we have both debt and equity options in the works in parallel. The timing of both would be slightly different and therefore, we are keeping both options open.

items.statement: Target to productionize Rs 30 crore of new business in FY26; ~Rs 20 crore done in 9M FY26
items.quote: Our aim is to productionize at least 30 crores of this new business in FY26. Already, a good amount has been has been launched earlier this year, as well as in last quarter and around 30 crores, we are looking at productionizing this year

items.statement: Employee cost at 21-22% of revenue; focus on productivity improvement and technology to reduce percentage over time
items.quote: We are completely conscious of the high employee cost percentage right now and our focus is on improving productivity, reducing manual work in all the operations, improving staff productivity as well through technology and better training.

items.statement: India-EU FTA effective Jan 2027; positive for exports, already seeing interest from European OEMs; US FTA also advantageous
items.quote: With the free trade agreement in Europe, of course, there is some fine tuning and finalisation of the fine print, so to speak and the exact agreement will take effect from January 2027, if I'm not mistaken. That's when the real benefits will start kicking in

items.statement: Capacity utilisation improved in Q3 but margin expansion driven by mix and efficiency, not volume; significant operating leverage headroom remains
items.quote: Utilizations have definitely improved in Q3. However, the margin expansion has been driven more by business mix, discipline and operational efficiency rather than pure volume absorption and we are not yet operating at peak capacity.

items.statement: Guides FY27 PAT of INR200-220 crores, ~1.4x growth over FY26 expected.
items.quote: For FY '27, we are guiding a profit after tax range of INR200 crores to INR220 crores, representing approximately 1.4x growth over FY '26 expected.

items.statement: Expects FY27 earnings split: H1 43-48%, H2 52-57%.
items.quote: We also expect the earnings profile of FY '27 to remain balanced with H1 contributing approximately 43% to 48% of full year profit and H2 contributing to remaining 52% to 57%, broadly in line with our historical seasonality across certain categories while maintaining overall earnings stability.

items.statement: Board authorized INR50 crores greenfield HPC project.
items.quote: As the first project of this new phase, the Board has authorized a greenfield HPC, Home & Personal Care, project with an investment of INR50 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex over INR750 crores, >60% of opening gross block.
items.quote: During FY '26, the company undertook a cumulative capital expenditure of over INR750 crores, representing more than 60% of the opening gross block at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Internal minimum return threshold of 18% ROCE for all new projects.
items.quote: All new projects are evaluated against the internal minimum return threshold of 18% ROCE.

items.statement: GST reduction causes duty inversion, increasing working capital; may shift to conversion model.
items.quote: In some of these categories, we are seeing a duty inversion, which will lead to an increase in the company working capital requirement.

items.statement: May transition to conversion-based model, reducing reported revenue but not absolute profitability.
items.quote: If implemented in select cases, revenue occurring to the company would be only to the extent of the conversion cost as opposed to the cost of the entire finished goods.

items.statement: Optimistic GST cut in bottled water, ice cream, foods will boost consumption and demand.
items.quote: We are optimistic that the reduction of GST in categories like bottled water, ice cream and foods, etcetera, will lead to the meaningful increase in the consumption and create new demand for the capacities.

items.statement: Beverage capacity to exceed 250,000 kL by end of FY26.
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform that at the end of this financial year, our total beverage capacity across the country will be more than 250,000 kL.

items.statement: Duty inversion from GST cut may increase working capital; mitigation via customer discussions.
items.quote: This duty inversion needs to be addressed. Like we've mentioned a bunch of times, we are reasonably disciplined in terms of our working capital investments.

items.statement: Aims for 20% annual growth, comfortable with 1:1 debt-equity for capex.
items.quote: I think I can go out on a limb and say that if you just look at our operating cash flows and if you look at levering it up 1:1, like Mayank said, we should be able to grow at about 20-odd percent per year just on the basis of that.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at 0.77x, within comfort threshold.
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, cash and cash equivalents stood at INR151 crores, and the net debt to equity was at a comfortable level of 0.77x, well within our internal comfort threshold.

items.statement: FY26 PAT estimated INR140-145 crores.
items.quote: From FY '21 to '26, the company has delivered a steady and consistent increase in profitability with profit after tax rising from INR34 crores in FY '21 to an estimated of INR140 crores to INR145 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Data center opportunity still at RFP stage, partnered with physical setup firm for large data center.
items.quote: We are still in the discussion stage, we are not at a proposal stage yet. We are responding to RFPs and we are going and presenting.

items.statement: Cannot quantify AI-driven margin expansion; most efficiency gains passed on to customers.
items.quote: So, we cannot at this point say, okay, hey, because we are using AI, our margins are going to increase by X amount of points, which is something that we cannot do at this point.

items.statement: AI delivers 20-30% efficiency gains on measurable outcome-based projects.
items.quote: But anyway, so the one where we can very clearly measure it is this outcome based projects, where we are seeing depending on the technology kind of project, is it a new one, is it an old one that you are upgrading to a new project where you a re seeing between 20% to 30% efficien cy gains.

items.statement: AI skills premium rates expected to last only about a year before competition erodes advantage.
items.quote: So, like back in the day, there were the B lockchain and NFT technologies. So, we could command slightly incur rates, right. So, we would have $10 or a $15 upside on the rate.

items.statement: Majority of customers currently refuse AI use in their contracts, especially in the US.
items.quote: Okay, majority of our customers are telling us we cannot use AI, Pratik. The reason for that is t hat they are still not ready for AI.

items.statement: Non-AI T&M contract pricing unchanged; customer dictates named resources and outcomes.
items.quote: No, it has been the same. There is no change on that, right? That is not changing on the non-AI contract.

items.statement: Expects leaner teams but volumes may increase, potentially growing from 300 to 400-500 customers.
items.quote: I am just picking discussions that as w e have 300 customers today that could go to 400 or 500 customers, or it could be some people are talking about an order of magnitude too, right?

items.statement: Kumori acquisition deepens ServiceNow partnership, enabling global outreach and expected revenue growth.
items.quote: What Kumori has given us is a ready-made partnership with deeper expertise. And now using Ke llton's sales arm and the global reach, we will be able to get a lot more customers as well as interactions when we are going with ServiceNow.

items.statement: Management dismisses SaaS apocalypse fears; sees minimal impact on Kellton's outcome-based model.
items.quote: So, we do not see a huge impac t either way. Yes, the way we operate will change, efficiencies will improve, but beyond that, I think that was just a market reaction.

items.statement: Legacy modernization project of 4 million lines of code would have been 3-4x cost without AI.
items.quote: And even if he did, it would Page 7 of 10 have been at least 3x to 4x of that value.

items.statement: Achieved Microsoft solution partner designation across data/AI, digital/app innovation, and infrastructure.
items.quote: We have a chieved the Microsoft solution partner designation across three areas; data and AI, digital and app innovation, and infrastructure as well.

items.statement: Won 11 new clients including global tech giant, heavy engineering, food services, telecom, healthcare, and UN agency.
items.quote: We have about 11 clients, but I will quickly go through some of them so that you sort of get a little bit of color on these client wins.

items.statement: Expects FY27 guidance to be better than current FY26 guidance of 7-9% revenue growth.
items.quote: So we should expect that our guidance for FY27 will be better than what we have projected currently for '26.

items.statement: Confident of improved top-line in FY2026, sticking to target.
items.quote: I once again like to reiterate and stick to our target of -- our target and are confident of an improved result in top-line of FY 2026.

items.statement: Plans additional capex of ~INR10 crores in FY26, including 1 MW rooftop solar.
items.quote: we plan to close FY 2025 with an additional Capex of around INR10 crores, including a rooftop solar installation of approximately 1 megawatt or less

items.statement: Cumulative capex of INR27 crores incurred over last three quarters.
items.quote: Over the last three quarters, we have incurred a cumulative Capex of INR27 crores in our factory

items.statement: Order backlog stood at ~INR586 crores as of December 2025.
items.quote: As on December 2025, we have order backlogs stood at approximately INR586 crores and we recorded order inflows of about INR222 crores.

items.statement: Machine tool division order backlog ~INR142 crores, 24% of total.
items.quote: total order backlog for this division now reaching about INR142 crores as of December 2025, accounting for almost 24% of the company's overall backlog order position.

items.statement: Margins to improve substantially as in-house manufacturing increases from capex.
items.quote: It should improve. It should improve substantially, because the more we manufacture in-house, our margins automatically improve.

items.statement: Expects only marginal margin improvement, not dramatic; volume growth is key.
items.quote: So I would say that don't expect dramatic change in margins. There'll be marginal improvement in margin, but it will not be dramatic. What change will take place is more volume.

items.statement: Textile industry extremely bullish post Indo-US trade agreement at 18% duty.
items.quote: going forward, the textile industry is extremely bullish because at 18% duty, we would be amongst the lowest tariff for textiles into the U.S.

items.statement: Machine tool manufacturing to see robust growth over next 3-4 years.
items.quote: So next three, four years would be a robust growth as far as the machine tool manufacturing is concerned.

items.statement: Focus on non-textile business for textile engineering; may get breakthrough order this year.
items.quote: Our focus is on the non-textile business as well to grow. And hopefully this financial year we may get a breakthrough order.

items.statement: Bangladesh LC issues impacting exports; hope resolution post elections.
items.quote: while we have very good order inflow from Bangladesh, the problem today is of getting the LCs from Bangladesh, which hopefully will get resolved with the election that is taking place currently in Bangladesh.

items.statement: India domestic revenue expected to grow low double digits if global disruptions don't occur
items.quote: I think India will be low double digit is something that we are reasonably confident on, right?

items.statement: Europe targeting profitability in FY27 after restructuring costs end in FY26
items.quote: Next year, our cost structures in Europe will be a lot lower than what they have been this year. So, our goal is not break even. Our goal is to get to profitability, right?

items.statement: US distribution operations (Pattons, Michigan Air) expected to improve in Q4 FY26 vs Q3
items.quote: I am confident that Q4 will be better than Q3. I don't want to make any commitments in terms of specific numbers, but definitely it will be better than Q3

items.statement: Tariff impact on EBITDA margins (~1% in Q3) to taper down from Q1 FY27 as high-cost inventory bleeds out
items.quote: It won't be higher, but it will progressively taper down. I don't expect it to reduce significantly in Q4, but Q1 of next year we see that there will be a reduction

items.statement: US prices increased 6-7% to offset 50% tariff; selling prices not reduced despite tariff dropping to ~18%
items.quote: We have been able to more than recover the tariff impact now, depending on where the tariff is going to land, that difference is going to be pure margin for us in the future

items.statement: New campus investment of 500-600 crore over 5 years; 2 plants under construction, one operational by March-April
items.quote: Progressively, we are moving each line there now that is a 500 to 600 crore investment that we hope to invest over the next 5 years now

items.statement: Annual maintenance capex ~50 crore; capacity for FY27-28 in place by end of FY26
items.quote: our own regular annual capex is roughly in the neighbourhood of about 50 crores that takes care of what I talked about that investment in capacity one year in advance

items.statement: Low-cost screw compressor range (30-40% cheaper) launch may slip to Q2 FY27 from Q1; products ready, validation ongoing
items.quote: if our current compressor is selling at 100, these machines are sold at probably around 60 or 70, right? So, I would say somewhere between 30 to 40% low

items.statement: Green shoots across all Indian industrial sectors; steel, automotive optimistic, cement muted but expected to recover
items.quote: steel is looking optimistic, automotive is looking optimistic. So these I think it is across the board Ravi. I won't pinpoint to any one sector that's standing out today

items.statement: Chinese imports ~25-30% of Indian market volume; ELGI launching competitive low-cost range with quality/service differentiation
items.quote: the Chinese imports are close to, in our estimate, 25 to 30% of the market right in volume terms, not in value

items.statement: Raw material prices (copper, aluminium, steel) rising; evaluating if permanent or temporary; ready to absorb or pass on as market allows
items.quote: We are evaluating this carefully, but we are ready to absorb these. To the extent that is required in the market, we are willing to pass it on

items.statement: Inventory at 6 months (excessive); target 3-3.5 months; new planning system implemented Aug-Sep 2024 in final validation
items.quote: 6 months is excessive inventory, right? When you have a lead time of shipment of about two and a half months, your inventory should be only about three – three and a half months

items.statement: Demand=Match stabilizer launched Oct 2024; 150 units in field; 6-17% energy efficiency gain; standard fitment in India; realizing better prices
items.quote: The response from customers has been just outstanding, right? So, the efficiency, energy efficiency has been anywhere from 6 to 17%

items.statement: Vacuum business ahead of budget; medical, furniture, chemical sectors key; 30-40% overlap with compressor applications; not in ultra-high vacuum for semiconductors
items.quote: Vacuum is ahead of our budget, so I don't want to give numbers in terms of we are growing more than what we plan to grow

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins above 30% near term and progressing towards 40% long term
items.quote: We are confident of sustaining EBITDA margins above 30% and progressing towards our long-term benchmark of 40%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 31.5% (up from 22.8% YoY); PAT margin 28.5%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at Rs. 12.09 crores, up 6.5% year-on-year and 55.9% quarter-on-quarter, with margins expanding to 31.5%.

items.statement: Greenfield project in Madhapur progressing through land conversion and design stages; evaluating brownfield opportunities in Hyderabad and leisure destinations
items.quote: Beyond these upgrades, our Greenfield project on Madhapur is progressing through land conversion and design stages, while we continue to evaluate downfield opportunities in Hyderabad and leisure destinations across India.

items.statement: Renovation-related inventory constraints temporarily impacted 9M FY26 revenue (-2.7% YoY); phased refurbishment planned to protect revenues
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, revenue was Rs. 94.5 crores compared to Rs. 97.1 crores last year, reflecting a 2.7% decline due to renovation-related disruptions.

items.statement: Finance costs declined to Rs 1.15 cr from Rs 1.61 cr YoY reflecting improved debt servicing and balance sheet discipline
items.quote: Finance costs declined to Rs. 1.15 crores from Rs. 1.61crores reflecting improved debt servicing and balance sheet discipline.

items.statement: Pharma double-digit growth delayed to FY27; Crop flat YoY for FY26 unchanged
items.quote: The Pharma has got delayed by a quarter or so because of the U.S. FDA impact. What we anticipated to happen towards the end of H1 only started in Q3. And so we are off by about a quarter. We will have some growth, but we don't expect the double-digit growth in pharma. It will start from next year. It's got delayed to n

items.statement: Worst behind; FY27 budgets being finalized, no formal guidance yet
items.quote: Well, our budgets are currently being finalized as we speak this month. So it's not appropriate for me to give any forward guidance. But I think the statement that we made over the last 3 years, yes, there have been some challenges for various reasons. And I think the worst is definitely behind us, I can confidently sa

items.statement: FY26 capex reduced to INR 150 cr from INR 200 cr guided; INR 100 cr spent in 9M, INR 40-50 cr in Q4
items.quote: Yes. So capex, in the beginning of the year, we said we will do a capex of about INR200 crores, but I think we've been very conservative this year, and we've cut it down to INR 150 crores overall capex compared to INR 200 crores is what we had guided at the beginning of the year. So this year, we'll end the year at abo

items.statement: US FDA remediation substantially complete; 6-week updates given (last Feb 9); warning letter period ends in ~2 weeks; reinspection timing uncertain
items.quote: We have given our remediation plan to U.S. FDA. We don't give them a monthly update, but we are giving an update once in 6 weeks. The last 2 updates were given on December 16 and as recent as this Monday, which is February 9. Now after completion of the warning letter, which will be of 6 months, which will just get ove

items.statement: Aims for 25-30% top-line growth next year, reaching INR225-240 crores, including Beryl.
items.quote: So from INR180 crores to 225 million, that's about 225, 230. We are looking at a 25%, 30% top line growth with the reduction of employee costs in the mechanical division.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% CAGR top-line growth over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: And your question about 3 to 5 years, we'll continue to grow at the rate of at least 20%, 25% CAGR on the top line.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to cross 20% overall, with potential to reach 25%.
items.quote: So going forward, we are very confident that the EBITDA margins and the top line revenue growth will be definitely somewhere in -- I mean, the top line growth should be in the region of 25% to 35% and EBITDA should at least cross 20% overall.

items.statement: Beryl's EBITDA margin can improve to 30-35% within a year via outsourcing to India.
items.quote: Beryl has last year, 8% to 10% EBITDA. That EBITDA margin can shoot up to 30%, 35% within a year's time once half of their work is outsourced to our Indian office.

items.statement: Building own campus in Nashik to save INR2-2.5 crores annual rental.
items.quote: That will considerably save our rental costs, which are running almost INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores per annum.

items.statement: Mandate to place 30 people on-site in next 3 months for MES.
items.quote: We have a mandate to place 30 people in the next 3 months.

items.statement: Civil engineering to see at least 20% growth next financial year.
items.quote: So I'm very confident that Civil will see at least a 20% growth in the next financial year.

items.statement: Poles and towers revenue to cross $1-1.2 million next year from $400-500k.
items.quote: Now we are looking at next year, it may cross $1 million or $1.2 million, which is a good jump in terms of MES revenues.

items.statement: Data centers to add $2-2.5M civil and $0.7-1M mechanical revenue, ~20-25% of turnover.
items.quote: So all put together, probably about $2 million, $2.5 million from civil side and about $0.7 million to $1 million in mechanical side we'll be able to add to that. That is almost like 20%, 25% of the INR150 crores turnover what we are hovering around.

items.statement: Reducing automotive team from 160 to 60, retraining for poles and towers.
items.quote: So the team size from 160, we are dropping it down almost to 60 in due course of time.

items.statement: High-rise design pricing at $80-100 per hour; Beryl charges $60-80 per hour.
items.quote: For high-rise buildings, the pricing typically is about $80 to $100 for designing hours.

items.statement: MES losses to be pruned, adding INR6-7 crores to bottom line.
items.quote: And MES might stay where it is, but its losses will be pruned out completely. So which will be almost adding INR6 crores to INR7 crores to the overall bottom line by pruning down the losses which that division has been incurring.

items.statement: Beryl CEO to buy $0.5 million shares, holding for minimum 3 years.
items.quote: Mr. Leo Cannyn will be buying about $0.5 million worth of shares and the demat process is just getting completed. And then the shares may be issued in the next couple of months.

items.statement: No buyback considered; cash reserved for acquisitions and Nashik campus.
items.quote: And buyback is an idea we are not yet considered because we are keeping this cash and funds for further acquisitions or even constructing our own campus in Nashik

items.statement: Management confident Q4 will be good and hopes to reach INR 1,500 crore revenue for FY26
items.quote: Because the performance is almost the same which happened in the preceding quarter so I am confident the last quarter will be definitely good and let's hope we once again reach the INR 1,500 crore.

items.statement: Q3 margins expected to be sustainable in Q4 if performance continues
items.quote: They should. If the performance is going the same way, the profitability is the same way so hopefully they will be good.

items.statement: Domestic Basmati prices rose 4-20% across varieties from October to December 2025
items.quote: Its price was INR 6,400 at the end of October, which at the end of December is INR 7,300 — INR 6,400 per quintal, we calculate in quintal in our business, in domestic market and in December, it was INR 7,300 and this is around 15% increase.

items.statement: Top 6 country export volumes more than doubled from ~15,500 to ~34,600 metric tons in Q3
items.quote: Quantity wise, 15,493 metric tons has gone to 34,578 tons, top 6 countries. So, it is more than - 100%, more than 15,000, it's very high.

items.statement: Potential capex of INR 5-10 crore for auto packing machines and production upgrades
items.quote: INR 5 crore, INR 7 crore, INR 5 crores, INR 10 crores. Not huge, not huge.

items.quote: Maharani revenue is around 8%, 9%.

items.quote: it was quite a big obstacle, 25% to 50% kind of a joke, but thank God, the effort of our government, particularly Modiji, it has been brought down to 19% now, 19%.

items.statement: New product 'Teasan' (rice tea) developed, passed government lab tests, human trials ongoing, planning domestic and international launch
items.quote: We have come out with a -- we are coming with a brand Teasan, T-E-A-S-A-N. That is tea made from rice, which has ingredients like cardamom, three flavours we have made already.

items.statement: Bank borrowing seasonal; HDFC limit INR 300 crore with only INR 2 crore drawn; PNB INR 50 crore at 6.60%
items.quote: You will be happy to know the company limit with HDFC bank is INR 300 crore and my availment as on the date is INR 2 crore.

items.statement: Expects double-digit top-line growth in the next financial year based on order wins and pipeline.
items.quote: I think for the next few quarters, as we start the next fiscal year, definitely I've been challenging teams.

items.quote: Revenue mix has to change for us. That's the goal, though, definitely. That's the goalpost.

items.statement: Plans to hold an Investor Day in the current financial year after scheduling constraints.
items.quote: But we definitely plan to hold it in the financial year and we will definitely share details in due course.

items.statement: Plans tuck-in acquisitions using surplus cash for technology or market access, not top-line growth.
items.quote: So, we will look at some tuck-in acquisitions. But the point is that if you make a smaller tuck-in acquisition, it's unlikely to give you the top line, right.

items.statement: Middle East subsidiary recapitalization to support working capital; revenue impact expected in 4-5 quarters.
items.quote: So, from an order booking side, I can just say the -- it can take another, let's say, four to five quarters and the real business will start flowing into that, and it will obviously result into the top line growth eventually after a few more quarters.

items.statement: FraudZap revenue to be recognized straight-line over contract duration, faster than traditional products.
items.quote: In terms of FraudZap, at least the first one, and I can only meaningfully speak about the one that we have closed, that's more of straight line.

items.statement: Traditional RAFM/BA revenue: 30% over four quarters for implementation and license, then subscription revenue.
items.quote: So, RAFM and BA is typically -- 30% of our revenue comes over four quarters, so which is primarily implementation and license revenue.

items.statement: FraudZap targets aggressive sales, with roadshows and sales targets set.
items.quote: Sales guys have been given way more aggressive target than you are even telling me it’s 20.

items.statement: Exploring integration of PrivaSapien product with Subex stack, but no open lead yet.
items.quote: So PrivaSapien, we have been talking to them for a while. This is something that the PrivaSapien itself has become a little bit more India focused, actually, because of the DPDP Act.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target about Rs. 2,300 crores with no incremental capex.
items.quote: For FY26, we remain on track to deliver a top line of about Rs. 2,300 crores, driven entirely by optimization and high utilization of existing capacities with no incremental capex planned.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin expected 9-10%; ethanol segment 10-11%.
items.quote: EBITDA margins are expected to be in the 9% to 10% range at the consolidated level, with the ethanol segment delivering 10% to 11% operational margins.

items.statement: FY27 revenue aspiration Rs. 2,600-2,800 crores at 80-90% utilization.
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we aspire to achieve Rs. 2,600 crores to Rs. 2,800 crores in revenue, assuming 80% to 90% utilization across all divisions.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expected 9-10%.
items.quote: Consolidated margins, we are expecting in the range of 9% to 10%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target Rs. 2,600-2,800 crores at 80-85% utilization.
items.quote: That will be at about 80%-85% capacity utilization. items.statement: No fresh capex until FY27; new capex planned for FY28.
items.quote: Until FY27, we are actually fully focused on improving our cash flow, giving out good results quarter-on-quarter, and improving the cash flows and reducing the working capital utilization. Any fresh capex will come in FY28.

items.statement: Ethanol orders ~Rs. 1,200 crores (17 crore litres) for ESY 25-26; capacity 26 crore litres.
items.quote: We currently have orders of approximately Rs. 1,200 crores translating into 17 crores litres for ESY 25 and 26. Our total ethanol production capacity stands at 26 crores litres per annum.

items.quote: So current maize prices are varying between Rs. 18 to Rs. 21 across India. In our Madhya Pradesh plant, the current maize price is at about Rs. 18 to Rs. 19, and in Assam plant it is about Rs. 20 to Rs. 21.

items.statement: Expect full distillery capacity utilization in FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain constructively optimistic and expect to achieve full utilization of our distillery capacity in FY26 and FY27.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: ethanol Rs. 1,400-1,500 cr, grain Rs. 800 cr, rest mineral.
