items.statement: Grain processing faces headwinds from starch overcapacity; margins under pressure.
items.quote: The grain processing segment continues to face headwinds due to industry-wide overcapacity in starch. As a result, starch prices remain under pressure.

items.statement: Working capital borrowing cost reduced to 7.25%; debt-equity ratio 0.6.
items.quote: Working capital borrowing is around 7.5% from three banks from where we have inducted our working capital requirement. And now over the last two months, it's further reduced to 7.25% working capital interest, i.e., ROI which we are borrowing from the banks.

items.statement: Received Rs. 21.8 crores PLI from MPIDC; PLI factored into Q3 EBITDA.
items.quote: Before moving to the outlook, I would like to highlight that the company has received a total amount of Rs. 21.8 crores from MPIDC towards state and industry promotion incentives related to our Madhya Pradesh operations.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 biosimilars EBITDA margin guided at mid-20s; Q3 margin of 28% driven by high-margin market prioritization
items.quote: So, we believe that this has gone as we had projected. And on a full year basis, we'll of course be in the mid-20s on our margins as well.

items.statement: Group capex moderated from ~$275M/year to <$225M; further moderation expected as Malaysia capacity build-up completes, shifting to maintenance capex
items.quote: At a group level, we were tracking roughly $275 million plus, Neha, if you recollect, of capex every year. That has moderated to less than $225 million.

items.statement: Biocon Biologics insulin drug product capacity doubling coming online in FY27; drug substance expansion 1-1.5 years later
items.quote: The drug product capacity comes online in the coming fiscal year, so we expect to double our capacity. So that investment is clearly behind us.

items.statement: Biosimilars Q3 EBITDA margin 28% (up from mid-20s guidance) due to North America mix shift to 46-47% from ~40% and operating leverage
items.quote: This quarter, it's beyond 46%, 47%. And that's the reason we have been able to get both higher gross margin and EBITDA as a percentage terms.

items.statement: Insulin demand robust globally; Biocon doubling drug product capacity in FY27 to meet growing demand as innovators focus on GLP-1s
items.quote: We do not expect that the insulin demand globally will reduce. And we expect us to be a very, very significant player in the insulin space.

items.statement: Four biosimilar molecules crossed $200M annualized revenue in FY25: trastuzumab, pegfilgrastim, insulin franchise (glargine), adalimumab
items.quote: The four molecules we have named last year, so I think trastuzumab, pegfilgrastim, insulin franchise, including glargine and adalimumab.

items.statement: CRDMO (Syngene) Q3 revenue down 3% YoY due to one customer challenge; pressure transient, medium-to-long-term trajectory intact
items.quote: As has already been disclosed, the business has been impacted by challenges faced due to one customer. While this pressure will take some time to fully ease, it is transient.

items.statement: Two QIPs raised nearly $1B, fully retiring structured debt from Viatris acquisition; annualized interest savings ~INR 300 crore from FY27
items.quote: Over the past year, we proactively addressed acquisition-related leverage through 2 successive QIPs cumulatively raising nearly $1 billion.

items.statement: No specific quantitative guidance given for FY27 biosimilars growth or margins; management indicates growth trajectory improving with new launches
items.quote: We've refrained from giving specific guidance for the future. We did say that we will have the mid-20s for the current financial year.

items.statement: Acquired full global rights to Hulio (adalimumab) from FKB; tech transfer initiated in phases across device, drug product, drug substance
items.quote: We have secured full and exclusive global rights for Hulio®, which is our very successful biosimilar adalimumab, from Fujifilm Kyowa Kirin Biologics Company Limited.

items.statement: Generics growth driven by liraglutide EU launches (Zentiva + direct); US filing under review, Latin America filings progressing
items.quote: The growth was driven primarily by liraglutide launch in European markets, which was through our partner Zentiva as well as direct to market.

items.statement: Semaglutide Canada approval delayed; Health Canada yet to approve any generic GLP-1; Biocon expects progress by next calendar year
items.quote: We have not seen a single generic GLP being approved, including liraglutide, which has not been approved by Health Canada.

items.statement: Syngene extended BMS partnership through 2035, broadening scope across discovery, development, manufacturing, clinical trials
items.quote: Syngene extended its longstanding partnership with Bristol-Myers Squibb, or BMS, which runs through 2035, broadening the scope of its integrated services.

items.statement: Net debt to bondholders/banks in narrow range $1.1-1.2B; all structured debt retired; finance costs down >INR 62 crore sequentially in Q3
items.quote: The net debt that we owe to the bondholders and the banks, it shifts in a narrow range of $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion.

items.statement: Committed to achieving Gaana breakeven in the next few quarters, with possible month or two delay.
items.quote: We remain committed to get Gaana breakeven in the few quarters going forward.

items.statement: Believes there is a path to Gaana profitability in the next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: So, but having said that, we remain committed. We believe next 2, 3 quarters, we have a path to profitability on that, 1 or month here and there, but we should be there.

items.statement: FY27 Gaana spend will shift to marketing for subscriber growth at CM3 level, not CM1.
items.quote: Yes. So, it will be more on marketing to drive subscriber growth. As we breakeven in 2.5, 3 quarters, the nature of spend will be largely towards marketing, which will be on the CM3 level and not on the CM1 levels.

items.statement: Share of Gaana subscribers on new pricing rose to 66% from 54% last quarter.
items.quote: Last quarter, I had said about 54%. This now it's about 66%.

items.statement: Non-FCT gross margin was 27.2% and EBITDA margin 18.5% this quarter.
items.quote: So, the gross margins this quarter has been around 27.2%.

items.statement: Radio ad rates remained broadly flat; festive shift pressured pricing slightly.
items.quote: More or less remained in the same bag. But as I said, there is a festive shift. So, there was some bit of drop in the inventory levels, and that could have put pressure on the pricing, but more or less in the flattish range ma'am.

items.statement: Radio pricing still down 25-30% versus pre-COVID levels.
items.quote: It's still a drop. As I said, in the last previous meetings also, it's almost about down 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Ad demand showing early signs of stabilization but advertisers remain cautious; management stays cautious.
items.quote: While the demand has now started to show early signs of stabilizing, advertisers remain cautious, which has kept pressure on all traditional mediums, including radio.

items.statement: Some recovery in ad revenue seen, partly base effect; not very bullish, remains cautious.
items.quote: Yes. So, there is some bit of recovery. We're seeing that not major. I would not say we are very bullish on that. There is some bit of recovery, some base effect coming in, some sentiments improving.

items.statement: Radio now 51% of overall business; non-radio (digital and solutions) 49%.
items.quote: So, our overall business, radio now contributes to about 51%. The non-radio business is 49%.

items.statement: Digital revenue reached INR30.8 crores, close to 50% of radio revenues, up from 27% YoY.
items.quote: Revenues from digital business reached INR30.8 crores, contributing close to 50% of our radio revenues, up sharply from 27% in the same quarter last year, underscoring the rapid expansion of this vertical.

items.statement: YTD digital investment was INR29 crores, down 22% year-on-year.
items.quote: Total investment in digital business during the current year at YTD level stood at INR29 crores, reflecting a significant 22% decline compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Will not cut subscription prices despite competitor tactical offers; sees price headroom to increase.
items.quote: So, we are very clear that we don't reduce the price. We came under a little pressure. Our marketing spends went up, but we remain focused of getting at the right price.

items.statement: Competitive price cuts and rising performance-marketing costs across the subscription ecosystem may delay breakeven.
items.quote: Yes, a month or 2 months here and there can happen because that may be competitive pressure or the marketing budgets taking a toll because the marketing budgets on digital spends is not just about your music competitors.

items.statement: Management guides 15-20% revenue growth for next 12-24 months, with 4-wheeler contribution on top of this organic rate
items.quote: Over the next 12 to 24 months, we continue to guide with our initial guidance, just 15% to 20% growth. We have kind of always outperformed the industry. So we will strive to do the same.

items.statement: Targets sustaining 14%+ EBITDA margin going forward despite planned INR200 cr capex over next 2 years
items.quote: Even with that, we believe that we should be at these margins, or at least 14% plus is what we are targeting.

items.statement: FY26 capex target INR100 cr; next 24 months capex ~INR200 cr total for existing and 4-wheeler projects
items.quote: This year will be INR100 crores for FY '26. And for the next 2 years, we think it could be upwards of INR200 crores, around INR200-odd crores.

items.statement: Electronic content per vehicle increasing 30-80% on existing LED lighting base; in-house SMT/EMS and new EMC/EMI lab enhancing capabilities
items.quote: It is totally dependent on product-wise. It is very difficult to say percentage, but it always varies from 30% to 80%.

items.statement: 2-wheeler industry production grew 15% YoY to 6.8M units in Q3; 9M production at 19.6M units, on track to exceed FY19 peak of 24.5M
items.quote: Total 2-wheeler production grew by 15% year-on-year to 6.8 million units in the quarter. For the first 9 months, industry production is already at 19.6 million units.

items.statement: Input cost increases passed on to customers on rolling basis, sometimes with a lag; escalations received in Q3 boosted margins
items.quote: Nothing specific. And if it does, as we mentioned, it is kind of passed on. It sometimes comes with a lag. But otherwise, all the input costs are passed on, on a rolling basis.

items.statement: Targets 15% net margin in scaffolding segment next year, with revenue growth, barring major geopolitical disturbances.
items.quote: I think with our product mix, with our strategy, we should be able to have growth in revenue as well as deliver a 15% net margin.

items.statement: Expects engineering services segment to grow 25% YoY with stable 15% margins.
items.quote: So with the growth of 25% year-on-year that we expect, we should be operating at about 15%.

items.statement: Scaffolding and formwork segment expected to cross INR2,000 crores revenue in next 3 years.
items.quote: I think next 3 years, we continue to be quite bullish that the Scaffolding and Formwork segment will cross revenue of INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Drum closure volumes in China to increase 10-15% in FY27.
items.quote: I think going into FY '27, we should be able to average maybe a 10% to 15% increase in this volume and the capacity is available.

items.statement: Formwork revenue for full year expected around INR900 crores.
items.quote: But I think for the entire year, we should be on track to do INR900 crores or maybe close to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Scaffolding and formwork segment revenue for full year expected close to INR1,400 crores.
items.quote: We should be looking at close to INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Plans to add Phase 2 extrusion plant and increase Mach One capacity towards end of 2026-27.
items.quote: We do plan to add Phase 2 probably sometime towards the later part of '26, '27, where we will put up another extrusion plant and further increase in Mach One capacity.

items.statement: Formwork order book around 350,000 to 400,000 square meters.
items.quote: Our order book is around close to 350,000 to 400,000.

items.statement: Scaffolding segment margins dropped due to volume decline; expects recovery to 15%.
items.quote: Our target is always 15%. We budget at 15%, and that's what we operate at. So I think we are very optimistic and we are positive that we should get to that level.

items.statement: Aluminium formwork pricing linked to NALCO, no absorption of aluminium price fluctuations.
items.quote: We don't absorb any fluctuations. Once the engineering is completed, the price gets frozen.

items.statement: US scaffolding demand picked up from November; December and January sales back to 2024 levels.
items.quote: December, we were back to our original sales levels. And January also, we are close to that.

items.statement: Potential tariff interpretation change could maintain 50% tariff on full product value.
items.quote: If they go with the latter then we may continue to pay the same tax.

items.statement: Focus on higher-margin orders in formwork due to increased competition.
items.quote: We are being quite choosy, picky and we are focusing on taking the right margin orders as compared to any order.

items.statement: No immediate plans for stock split or bonus; buybacks and dividends used for shareholder returns.
items.quote: But splitting of the shares so far is not with the Board. Maybe in future appropriate time, the Board may consider that. But as of now, there is no such proposal.

name: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 20% on total sales; PAT margin 12.7%; retrospective price adjustments in Q3 cause seasonal margin expansion
items.quote: The company delivered strong operating performance in Q3 FY '25-'26, achieving an EBITDA margin of 20% on total sales and profit before tax before exceptional items stood at INR 194.5 crores.

items.statement: Retrospective price adjustments from April-September collected in December drive seasonal Q3 margin improvement; price increases effective 1st April but POs issued in Nov/Dec
items.quote: price increases happen with effect from 1st April, but the effect is given via POs in December, November or December. That is the reason why in December results, there would be an impact of retrospective price increases from April to September.

items.statement: CV >6 tonne segment grew 20.6% in Q3 FY26; company outperformed market by 7.5% with 28.1% sales growth driven by EV buses, ESC penetration, new exhaust brake variant
items.quote: During Q3, FY '25-'26, CV more than 6 tonne production recorded a growth of 20.6%, while our overall sales rose by 28.1%. The strong performance enabled us to outperform the market by 7.5%.

items.statement: ADAS regulation effective 2027; ESC pricing INR 20,000-25,000; ADAS pricing expectation halved to ~INR 20,000-22,500 from earlier INR 40,000-45,000 due to competitive pressure
items.quote: On the ESC, we would be at around INR 20,000 to INR 25,000 as we had indicated earlier. On the ADAS, the earlier indication of INR 40,000 to INR 45,000 was the number we had indicated during our earlier discussions. However, based on the latest outlook and the feedback from customers, their expectation is somewhere hal

items.statement: 10,500 e-bus order concluded in Nov-Dec 2025; PM-eBus Sewa and STU tenders driving EV bus growth; potential 17,000 e-buses in 2 years plausible subject to charging infrastructure
items.quote: most recently, I think the 10,500 buses order was also concluded in the month of November, December, which is going to add a real fill to several OEMs who are into bus manufacturing.

items.statement: ADAS/ESC capex currently limited to application engineering and test track capabilities; further localization investment when volumes pick up post-2027 regulation
items.quote: At this moment, we are only enabling our capabilities from an application engineering perspective. So, that's more from a test track related capability requirement only, yes.

items.statement: Export of goods declined 10.9% YoY in Q3 FY26 due to US volume reduction; EU grew 9%, US vehicle production fell 28%; FDA agreement and potential US tariff reduction expected to support recovery
items.quote: In Q3 financial year 2025, '26, our export performance declined by 10.9% compared to the same period last year. Primarily due to volume reduction from the U.S. market.

items.statement: Aftermarket sales INR 158 crores in Q3 FY26, up 19.2% YoY driven by retrofit demand (INR 4.1 crores from PSU oil/gas), BS-VI replacement, mining, and 7 new service centers
items.quote: In Q3 FY '25-'26, our aftermarket sales reached INR 158 crores, reflecting a strong 19.2% growth over the INR 132 crores recorded in the same quarter in last financial year.

items.statement: Export services grew 11.1% YoY in Q3 FY26 driven by engineering services to global centers; India strengthening as strategic engineering hub for ZF Group
items.quote: Export of services grew by a robust 11.1% in Q3 FY 2025, '26 compared to the corresponding quarter last year. This growth was driven by a sustained increase in engineering activities delivered from India to global centers.

items.statement: ADAS competition from passenger car players offering lower pricing; proof-of-concept trials ongoing; ZF emphasizing testing capability and field data algorithms as USP
items.quote: there are discussions going on in the market with regards to other players who have offered products at a lower pricing than what is currently being offered by ZF. And as a result of that, there are several discussions and ongoing proof-of-concept related topics that are undertaken with each OEM.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue mix: OEM INR 520 crores, Aftermarket INR 157 crores, Exports INR 259 crores, Service income INR 125 crores
items.quote: OEM was about INR 520 crores, aftermarket INR 157 crores and exports INR 259 crores, with service income being about INR 125.

items.statement: NRL expansion to reach 50% utilization (4 MMT throughput) by Q4 FY27, 100% by Q2 FY28; petchem commissioning by end FY28, full capacity by Q2 FY29
items.value: 4 MMT throughput FY27; 9 MMT capacity FY28
items.quote: So, to summarize, in Q4 of FY '27, we will be at 50% daily capacity utilization and going up to 100% by Q2 of FY '28 and petchem will start by close of FY '28 and we will be achieving its full capacity by, say, Q2 of FY '29.

items.statement: Oil India standalone capex FY26 INR8,800 cr (will exceed); FY27 around INR9,200 cr+; NRL capex INR6,000 cr YTD, INR8,000 cr FY26E, total project INR45,000 cr
items.quote: The number that we have indicated for '25-'26 is INR8,800 crores, but given the numbers that we have seen yesterday as part of our Q3, it would be increasing.

items.statement: Duliajan-Numaligarh pipeline expansion to 2.5 MMSCMD mechanically complete, commissioning by April 2026; Paradip-NRL crude pipeline 92% lowering done, commissioning Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Duliajan-Numaligarh pipeline expansion from 1 million to 2.5 million has already achieved mechanical completion on 15 November, and we expect to commission the expanded pipeline by April 2026.

items.statement: NRL Q3 GRM $16.27/bbl (up 54% QoQ) driven by high diesel cracks (65-70% yield) and 100%+ utilization; standalone EBITDA margin 33.96%
items.quote: The gross refinery margin, excluding excise duty is $16.27 per barrel, which is up by 54% vis-a-vis Q2 of the current year.

items.statement: Contract costs surged 70% YoY/QoQ due to deeper wells (5,500m+), more rigs, higher workovers, seismic; current run-rate seen as baseline for onshore/shallow water
items.quote: This month, we have already drilled the equivalent number of drilling that we had done last year. And this is just 62. We are going to drill another 12 to 15 wells. So, this is the additional cost which is coming on the way.

items.statement: Gas sales impacted by temporary shutdowns at Namrup Power Plant and BVFCL; shutdowns lifted, production and sales recovering in Q4
items.quote: The gas sales have experienced minimum de-growth driven by reduced offtake from major customers such as Namrup Power Plant, BVFCL, which has resulted in the temporary shutdown of their units. These shutdowns have now been lifted and the gas production and sales are well beyond recovery during the quarter of '25-'26.

items.statement: Drilled 51 wells in 9M FY26 (65% of annual target); targeting 75+ wells FY26 (highest ever), 100 wells FY27; Rajasthan output now 1,000 bpd
items.quote: This year, by this time, we have already completed 62 wells. Of course, this has got a mix of exploratory and development wells, but we are going to close the year by a number which will be the highest ever in the history of Oil India Limited, that will be 75-plus wells.

items.statement: Gas evacuation constrained pending feeder line govt authorization (18 months post-approval); Andaman exploration carries dry-well write-off risk; Russian dividends ($300M) stuck in Moscow SBI account
items.quote: The dividends are in safe account of Oil India Limited and the account lies with CIBL branch that is SBI branch in Moscow. So, it is in our account. The range, the order of magnitude of retained money in Moscow branch is about $300 million.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend INR7/share (total INR10.5/share FY26 YTD); 9M consolidated revenue INR27,037 cr, EBITDA INR9,299 cr, PAT INR5,126 cr
items.quote: We are pleased to inform you that the company has declared a dividend of INR7 per fully paid equity shares during our period closing of 31st of December 2025.

items.statement: FY27 likely muted; expects FY28 to be very strong with revenue doubling toward prior INR8,000-10,000 crore target
items.quote: I believe FY27 is likely to remain muted. While the disruption has eased significantly, we do not expect it to be fully resolved.

items.statement: Wheelset business at full production has annual revenue potential of INR2,000-2,500 crore
items.quote: Regarding wheelsets, as I mentioned earlier, at full production, this business has a revenue potential of approximately INR 2,000 crore to INR 2,500 crore annually.

items.statement: EV mobility targeting INR200 crore revenue by FY27, led by battery storage growing ~100% month-on-month
items.quote: And that is why we are very bullish on the revenue targets of INR200 crore, which we have set.

items.statement: Odisha greenfield integrated wheelsets plant progressing; production expected to commence by year-end
items.quote: The facility is expected to commence production by year -end, which will materially enhance wheelset availability and support higher throughput across our wagon and component businesses.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR5,041 crore as of Dec 31, 2025, diversified across wagons, wheelsets, braking and containers
items.quote: As of 31st December 2025, the consolidated order book stood at INR5,041 crore, covering diversified products across wagons, wheelsets, braking systems and containers, reinforcing sustained customer confidence and demand strengths across both public and private sector clients.

items.statement: About 8,000 wagons pending, roughly 70% from private customers
items.quote: It's close to about 8,000 wagons which we have pending right now.

items.statement: Private wagon demand robust across steel, cement, container and auto; expects strong traction in CY2026 and 2027
items.quote: We are very confident on that segment, and we expect a lot of traction in that segment in calendar year 2026 and 2027, both years, we expect very strong traction.

items.statement: Railway Ministry procurement estimate ~32,000 wagons; tender timing uncertain but expected during the year
items.quote: If you look at the Indian Railways budget, they have mentioned around 32,000 wagons. We expect this to materialise at some point during the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin sustained ~13% vs ~14% last year; expects margins to improve
items.quote: Last year I think we were around 14% and this year we are maintaining close to about 13%. So that is not a very big differential given the disruption which we have faced. So EBITDA margins will improve

items.statement: Private order book ~70% of mix, balance Indian Railways
items.quote: So the mix right now, I think our private order book is about 70% and the balance is the Indian Railways order book.

items.statement: Entering passenger rolling stock as OEM in 2026; non-wagon business to grow over next 2-3 years
items.quote: See, this year itself in 2026, we will be entering the passenger rolling stock business and in the next few months, you will get to hear our announcements coming on that, our partnerships.

items.statement: Wheelset supply disruption to persist next two-three quarters until new capacity comes online
items.quote: So till that capacity doesn't come, this disruption will remain. So next two or three quarters we expect that the disruption will continue.

items.statement: EU CBAM carbon border mechanism could be a trade barrier for unprepared companies; Jupiter already working on compliance
items.quote: I think in Europe, the biggest challenge in the Indian industry is going to face on the CBAM and which, I think, unless people are already up preparing themselves and gearing themselves up, Europe is going to be a major challenge.

items.statement: Tatravagonka converted warrants; 28,72,340 equity shares allotted after INR101.25 crore balance subscription; promoter stake rose to 68.31%
items.quote: Additionally, on December 19, 2025 Jupiter Wagons Limited allotted 28,72,340 equity shares pursuant to the conversion of warrants by Tatravagonka upon receipt of the balance subscription amount of INR101.25 crore.

items.statement: Target to become a $2 billion consolidated company (ex-Arka) by FY30 with margin improvement driven by advanced products, aftermarket and exports
items.quote: We stated a 5-year strategy, which is to be a $2 billion company by fiscal year '30. And we've also said that we hope to continue to improve margins over that time because our focus areas continue to be Advanced products, Aftermarket and Exports where these typically are the margin levers in our industry.

items.statement: INR700 crores capex plan underway to ramp up operations
items.quote: As we have mentioned earlier, there is INR700 crores of capex that we are deploying into ramping up our operations. A lot of that work is currently ongoing.

items.statement: Nuclear segment order book of INR798 crores basic value with 2-year execution timeline
items.quote: So the overall order value that we have spoken about earlier is INR798 crores in basic value. We have time lines of 2 years from now.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 12.2% in Q3 FY26 from 10.3% in Q3 FY25; gross margin flat at 35%
items.quote: EBITDA margin at 12.2% for Q3 FY '26 versus 10.3% for Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Gross margin flat at 35% but expected to improve as HHP proportion increases
items.quote: Right now, our gross margin is flat at 35% margin. But in future, as you see more sales from HHP, definitely, the gross margin should improve.

items.statement: Commodity price increases being managed; gross margin held flat at 35% through appropriate actions
items.quote: We are keeping a close watch on that. And if you look at our gross margin, that has remained flat. So we are taking the appropriate action on those commodity price increase.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margins of 12-15% and expects similar growth trajectory to continue
items.quote: we are targeting EBITDA margins between 12% to 15% at any point of time. So, we will maintain that. Obviously, as we scale, there is potential for these margins to improve.

items.statement: Q4 demand outlook positive with Eid and Gudi Padwa sales in March as defining month
items.quote: Quarter 4 again remains a generally upbeat quarter from a demand point of view. We do see good demand overall. Again, month-three, where we have our Eid and Gudi Padwa sale happening, that would be the defining month for us.

items.statement: Core winter wear (sweaters, sweatshirts, jackets) contributed 15-20% of Q3 revenue, peaking at 35% in December
items.quote: When we look at pure new winter wear products, which is largely sweaters, sweatshirts, jackets, these products have contributed somewhere close to about 15% to 20% during this particular quarter, and in the month of December, it was as high as 35%.

items.statement: Bhiwandi warehouse fire caused Rs 21.85 cr inventory loss; fully insured with Rs 31.22 lakh net P&L impact
items.quote: the carrying value of the inventory at our warehouse in Bhiwandi has been disclosed in the notes to account at Rs.21.85 crores approximately.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 11.92%, 9M EBITDA margin 12.65%; PAT margins 7.54% and 7.4% respectively
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 11.92%. Profit after tax stood at INR5 crores, an increase of 67% year-on-year, and PAT margins stood at 7.54%.

items.statement: Online apparel market growing 25-35%; mass premium to premium segment (Rs 750-2,000) expected to outpace baseline growth
items.quote: Generally, online apparel in major marketplaces is experiencing a 25% to 35% kind of growth even right now. We believe that there will be outside growth that there would be in the more premium or mass premium segments.

items.statement: Receivable days expected to settle around 60 days long-term as contracts transition to direct B2C model
items.quote: So, we believe that long-term receivable days would settle at somewhere around 60-days. And this is under current accounting practices.

items.statement: Own brand Thomas Scott grew 91% YoY to Rs 27 cr; licensed brands up 18% to Rs 34 cr; contract manufacturing up 113% to Rs 5 cr
items.quote: our own brand, Thomas Scott, recorded revenues of INR27 crores, marking a 91% year-on-year growth, reflecting the rising strength of our own direct-to-consumer franchise and sharper assortment planning.

items.statement: Fire incident may have cost 15-20% additional revenue in Q3; estimated steady-state revenue Rs 75-80 cr vs actual Rs 66 cr
items.quote: purely based on my judgment, we believe that 15% to 20% additional revenue could have been expected in this particular quarter.

items.statement: No new store expansion planned; focus remains on e-commerce depth and width; 6 Bangalore stores too early to evaluate
items.quote: currently, we continue to be focused on getting greater depth within e-commerce online or greater width within e-commerce online. And that focus continues to remain.

items.statement: Thomas Scott average selling prices: denims ~Rs 1,200, trousers ~Rs 1,200, shirts Rs 800-1,000; high MRP-high discount strategy for marketplace visibility
items.quote: our Denims typically have an average selling price of close to actually Rs.1,200, our trousers are close to again Rs.1,200, shirts are between Rs.800 to 1,000.

items.statement: Menswear trends long-cycle; only 2-3% of 2-3 year old bestsellers de-trended; growth driven by color extensions on proven styles
items.quote: even today, amongst the bestseller products that we created, say, two or three years back out, maybe just 2% or 3% of those products have actually gone into a de-trend bucket.

items.statement: Inventory turns managed via high-width low-depth model: 100-120 units per style test launch, 180-240 day clearance cycle for tail inventory
items.quote: a combination of these factors allow us to clear most of the inventory within a 180-to-40-day kind of period.

items.statement: Solar pump order book stands at 1,500 pumps with 60% executed; rooftop segment has no sizable order book due to fast churn
items.quote: As on date, we have total order wins of 1,500 out of which, as I said already, 60% is already executed. Also, there is further new orders expected in the coming months in that segment.

items.statement: Ahmedabad plant capex of INR 10 crore, 50% incurred, balance in current quarter; no other sizable capex planned
items.quote: The expected capex amount for this plant is INR10 crores. So, almost 50% of it is already incurred and the 50% is of, the balance 50% would be incurred in the current quarter. Apart from that, going forward, there is no sizable capex planned at the moment.

items.statement: Expects to sustain current quarter EBITDA margin of 12.68% in coming quarters; Ahmedabad plant to add ~1.5 pp to micro-irrigation margin over 1-2 years
items.quote: We are expecting that the margins which we have seen in the current quarter, we will be able to sustain that in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Ahmedabad plant in-house components (5-10% of system value) to improve micro-irrigation operating margin by ~1.5 percentage points within 1-2 years
items.quote: We are expecting a margin improvement of around 1.5 percentage for the micro-irrigation business because of the new product capacity that will be setting up at the Ahmedabad plant.

items.statement: Government budget continuity for PM KUSUM (INR 5,000 cr) and PM Surya Ghar supports demand growth in solar pumps and rooftop segments
items.quote: The budget for PM KUSUM has been kept at the similar level. And also for the rooftop business, there is continued support under PM Surya Ghar project as well. So, for these two segments where we are operating, we see that the demand will continue to increase in the next year as well.

items.statement: GST reduced from 12% to 5% on micro-irrigation and solar products, improving affordability and expected to boost demand
items.quote: The government has recently announced the reduction in GST from 12% to 5% on both micro-irrigation and the solar products. So, this further improves the affordability of our products and hence, we also see that there will be a demand improvement in both the segments going forward.

items.statement: Solar EPC mix to rise from 10% to 50% of revenue in 3 years driven by solar pumps; micro-irrigation to grow 25% CAGR
items.quote: We are targeting after 3 years, the mix of business will be 50-50. Right now, the business mix which is at 90-10, that mix would come to 50-50 over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Solar rooftop margins under pressure (high single digits) due to high competition; solar pump margins vary by tender but generally higher
items.quote: Generally, for the rooftop segment, the operating margins are in high single digits. So, if you compare both the segments, solar water pumps, the margins are higher. Whereas in the solar rooftop, the market is competitive. And obviously, because of that, the margins remain under pressure.

items.statement: Expect to arrest sales decline in coming quarter and then focus on profitability augmentation after 40% decline in H1 and 14-15% decline in Q3
items.quote: We have experienced close to 40% decline in the first half. We are bringing it down to about 14%, 15% in quarter 3. And we believe we are now heading towards a quarter wherein we should arrest any decline and thereafter, look at profitability augmentation.

items.statement: Knit Gallery factory targeting 40-50% growth next year with minimal capex, leveraging PDS processes and India FTA benefits
items.quote: We are looking at a 50% growth next year in this factory. We believe that is pretty much doable. And one really does not need to do any significant capex.

items.statement: U.S. direct business targeting first profitable quarter in Q4 FY26 with $1M+ profit, though full year still in loss
items.quote: We are looking at, hopefully, fingers crossed, making money first time in our U.S. business in quarter 4. The business internally is targeting $1 million plus of profit.

items.statement: Order book growth currently at 6-7% vs 14-15% mid-year, but customer dialogues indicate double-digit growth visibility for next year
items.quote: On the order book, what was in the mid of the year, a 14%, 15% growth in the order book, it actually right now a 6%, 7% growth in the order book.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 236 bps YoY in Q3 and 45 bps in 9M; targeting sustainable 50 bps YoY improvement through procurement efficiencies and mix
items.quote: Gross margin expanded 236 basis points year-over-year in Q3 and 45 basis points in the 9-month period. This is driven by procurement efficiencies, mix and cost discipline.

items.statement: Manufacturing business now profitable at 3.5-4% PBT margin with potential to scale up; Knit Gallery at 4-5% PBT margin currently
items.quote: The business is profitable, making closer to 3.5% to 4% margin, and we believe there is potential to scale up to next level.

items.statement: No significant capex needed for Knit Gallery 40-50% growth; growth to come from operational efficiencies and PDS process integration
items.quote: We believe that is pretty much doable. And one really does not need to do any significant capex. There is inherent potential built in by bringing in PDS-established process systems from Bangladesh factories into Knit Gallery.

items.statement: Global apparel demand remains restrained and value-led; retailers operating with shorter order visibility and tight inventory control
items.quote: The global apparel environment is continuing to be very, very restrained and measured. Consumer demand across U.S. and Europe is still value-led. In fact, in value led as well, customers are restraining spending for now.

items.statement: U.S. tariff increases causing 5-10% price increases in market, leading to reduction in quantity and demand in U.S.
items.quote: With the U.S. tariffs, what we've been speaking to the customers, there has been a 5% to 10% price increase in the market, which has led to some reduction in quantity and demand, what they are buying.

items.statement: Customer credit risk remains key concern; Gerry Weber bankruptcy and Matalan restructuring impacted revenue but payments secured via risk framework
items.quote: The only risk we face in the system, not only us, but every company in our industry faces is the creditworthiness of the customers, certain customers. So Gerry Weber if you look at, unfortunately, the retailer went bankrupt.

items.statement: $15M (~₹140-150 cr) of sales deferred in Q3 from top 10 verticals due to customer inventory caution; orders intact but shipment timing delayed
items.quote: In our top 10 large verticals, if I have to broadly recall, approximately $15 million, that's almost like ₹140 crores, ₹150 crores of sales that got pushed out.

items.statement: Net debt reduced sharply to ₹70 cr from ₹374 cr in Mar'25 despite ₹98 cr Knit Gallery acquisition debt; net working capital at 7 days, operating cash flow ₹644 cr in 9M
items.quote: Net debt reduced sharply to around ₹70 crores as of December from ₹374 crores in March '25, despite the addition of debt of ₹98 crores from Knit Gallery acquisition.

items.statement: Closing order book as of 31st December 2025 stands at INR999 crores, excluding mobility and product services which add INR125-150 crores annual revenue.
items.quote: During the quarter, we booked new orders totaling to INR170 crores, excluding mobility and product services, taking our closing order book as on 31st December to a healthy INR999 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 23.48% in Q3 FY26, up 452 bps YoY; management expects margins to remain stable and sustainably improve quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: If you see the presentation also, we have seen the EBITDA margins growing steadily quarter-on-quarter for the last 8 quarters. So from a base level of 17% every quarter we have seen increase, and we have reached at 23.4%.

items.statement: Invested INR24 crores in technology innovations and business development in Q3 FY26, of which INR16 crores was expensed to P&L; focus on U.S. expansion and AI/ML product development.
items.quote: During the quarter, we invested INR24 crores in technology innovations and business development, specifically aimed at expanding our presence in the U.S. and other territories. Out of this investment, INR16 crores was charged to our profit/loss account.

items.statement: Demand remains strong with new orders of INR170 crores in Q3 FY26; robust pipeline for FY27 despite election-related delays in government tendering.
items.quote: Demand for our offerings remains strong. During the quarter, we booked new orders totaling to INR170 crores, excluding mobility and product services, taking our closing order book as on 31st December to a healthy INR999 crores.

items.statement: Geospatial & Engineering Services grew 122% YoY to INR109 crores in Q3; Technology Solutions declined 3% YoY to INR61 crores; 9M both segments grew ~78% YoY.
items.quote: For the quarter under review, our Geospatial and Engineering Services revenue increased by 122% year-on-year to INR109 crores, while on the Technology Solutions side, revenue declined moderately by 3% to around INR61 crores.

items.statement: Order inflow delayed due to back-to-back Model Code of Conduct in Maharashtra causing 4-month standstill in government tender decisions; pipeline remains intact but may slip to Q1 FY27.
items.quote: There has been a code of conduct, which we didn't anticipate back-to-back, 2 code of conduct has come and it's almost lost over 4 months of operation. So government was standstill on taking decisions and coming out with tenders.

items.statement: Working capital cycle stable at 160-162 days; Q3 collections of INR170 crores matched revenue; target to reduce to 125 days by Q4 FY26 as government disbursements accelerate.
items.quote: We have maintained discipline of working capital with our net working capital cycle in the range of 160 to 162 days. ... During the quarter, our collections were INR170 crores, which is equivalent to operational revenue.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisition due diligence nearly complete; compliance delays pushing closure to Q4 FY26; focused on synergistic targets in geospatial/engineering domains.
items.quote: The due diligence process is also almost over. There has been a slight delay from the compliance side because we are evaluating all the aspects. So I think we are not able to give you the answer right now. Hopefully, by quarter end -- quarter 4 end, you will have a little more clarity.

items.statement: Strategic MOUs signed with Tech Mahindra (global BD, telecom, utilities, Europe, Middle East) and Aetosky (AI/image interpretation, Middle East/Far East presence) to expand service offerings and geographies.
items.quote: We have entered into MOU with Tech Mahindra and Aetosky, which adds to the long list of strategic and OEM partnerships. We are working towards building more such strategic partnership in the coming times.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission scheme runs until 2028; existing orders under execution and pipeline pursued; some delays but opportunities remain visible.
items.quote: JJM mission is -- scheme is on until 2028, and we already have a few orders which are being executed. And some of the orders in pipeline is also pursued in respect of the JJM orders.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 gross margin declined to 31.9% from 35.7% YoY due to sulphur price surge from $284 to $560/ton; management expects normalization in Q4
items.quote: Look sir at this moment what I am understanding based upon your question and the data you provided, is that this margin dip that is visible, this is mainly due to the increase into the raw material prices. That too also specifically due to the sulphur. Sulphur is a very important ingredient in our whole chain of the ra

items.statement: Chemical segment volumes up 75.6% YoY and 54% QoQ to 26,595 MT; fertilizer volumes down 23.7% YoY and 26.3% QoQ to 53,444 MT due to sulphur cost pressure and seasonal winter slowdown
items.quote: In the chemical segment, revenue was Rs. 156 crores, a growth of 38.1% year-on-year basis and 18.2% quarter-on-quarter, driven by the improved volumes and strong demand. Sales volume for the segment was 26,595 metric tons, marking an increase of 75.6% year-on-year and 54% sequentially.

items.statement: New Dyes plant at Unit 5 (reactive & acid dyes) and NPK/phosphoric/sulphuric acid complex at Unit 6 to diversify product portfolio; targeting 60-65% utilization initially
items.quote: Sir we are waiting for two units which are awaiting for additional electricity requirement by the company. And in that there is one additional of this complex unit which is NPKs and phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid and one more unit at Unit 5 which is a Dyes plant.

items.statement: Bangladesh political instability temporarily reducing textile demand (~7-8% of revenue); management expects recovery post-elections (March 2026); Dyecol Bangladesh subsidiary not yet operational
items.quote: Sir in Bangladesh apart from textile, no other big economy, textile is a very big part of Bangladesh's economy. You know without this textile Bangladesh economy is difficult to run. Though there is a political instability in Bangladesh, I can understand whatever the news articles we are reading in the various print med

items.statement: China cancelling VAT refund on dye exports making Chinese products non-competitive; India becoming net exporter of H-Acid/Vinyl Sulphone to China; management sees net positive for Indian dye industry
items.quote: Sir if you pick up the data from last June , July 2025 till today, if you look at the data, five-six years ago, H-Acid, Vinyl Sulphone used to be imported in India. Now sir if I am not wrong, as far as my data is correct, from last June July till today at least 7 to 8 thousand tons of H-Acid has been exported.

items.statement: Solar capacity expanding from 9.8 MW DC to 20.6 MW DC under open access to enhance energy self-reliance and reduce carbon emissions
items.quote: the company currently operates 9.8 megawatt DC solar plant with the capacity being expanded through two additional installations. Upon completion, the total solar will reach to 20.6 megawatt DC under open access scheme.

items.statement: New labour code impact to be quantified in Q4 FY26 after actuarial valuation for gratuity
items.quote: Sir the impact of the labour code we will identify in Q4, which we had discussed with our statutory auditor and also discussed regarding gratuity valuation. So the full picture of that will be clear in Q4 sir.

items.statement: Historical PAT margin low of 5.5% two years ago; current 8% level; management sees capability to reach 10-11% over time
items.quote: Sir two years ago we went down till 5.5% but that was a different global situation and today we have reached to a level of 8%. In my opinion we still have a capacity and capability of going to around 10% to 11% in times to come.

items.statement: Targets 30% sustained annual revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 20%+ under 50-plus compounding strategy
items.quote: Our long-term operating philosophy is anchored on what we call the 50-plus compounding strategy, which focuses on targeting over 30% sustained revenue growth annually alongside a structured EBITDA margin profile of around 20% and above.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.2%, PAT margin 13.8%; 9M FY26 EBITDA margin 20.5%, PAT margin 13.4%
items.quote: I'm happy to announce in Q3, we delivered revenue of INR 5,512 Lakhs Our EBITDA is INR 1,225 Lakhs giving an EBITDA margin of 22.2%. Our PAT stands at INR761 lakhs, a PAT margin of 13.8%.

items.statement: Revenue per outcome increased from INR 45.89 in Q2 to INR 47.45 in Q3 driven by AI optimization, premium video mix, and global expansion
items.quote: One of the key metrics for our business is the linked outcomes. It's revenue per outcome, which moved from INR45.89 to INR47.45.

items.statement: Outcome-linked revenue rose to 92% in Q3 from 90% in Q2; premium video formats (CTV, streaming) driving mix shift
items.quote: In the previous quarter, I said about 90% of the revenue was outcome-linked and I'm happy to say that today this is about 92% of our Q3.

items.statement: Q3 revenue grew 67% YoY to INR 55.12 Cr driven by Quick Commerce, BFSI, Fintech, Travel, Retail, Consumer Goods; RMG contribution dropped to -1.4% in Q3
items.quote: We concluded Q3 of FY 2026 with consolidated revenue of INR55.12 crores compared to INR32.97 crores in Q3 of FY '25, reflecting a strong year-on-year growth of 67.2%.

items.statement: Raised INR 50 Cr (of approved INR 100 Cr) at INR 1,088/share for AI stack, global expansion, and selective M&A over 12-18 months
items.quote: The Board has proceeded with initial allotment of INR50 crores and which is adequately supporting our near and mid-term objectives. Now the usage of this funds are largely for our platform enhancement, our AI stack that we are building, our global expansion.

items.statement: International revenue contribution 10.5% of 9M FY26; UK subsidiary now generating revenue; expanding into LatAm (Argentina, Chile, Brazil, Mexico), ASEAN, and UK
items.quote: Our global expansion continues to strengthen geographical diversification with international markets contributing today 10.5% of 9 months FY '26 revenue.

items.statement: Real Money Gaming segment banned in India; contributed 6.2% of 9M revenue but -1.4% in Q3; business diversified across digital-native categories
items.quote: For the first 9 months in this year, this segment, especially RMG, contributed 6.2% of our total revenue. In Q3, specifically, this contribution is turned down almost roughly, which is negative of 1.4%.

items.statement: Transitioning from AI-powered to AI-driven automation; model training time reduced from 10-12 hours to 1 hour; response time 12-15ms vs industry 50ms+
items.quote: Our deep neural network and models are now trained on over 50 terabytes of large-scale behaviour and contextual data sets in nearly 1 hour. This is compared to 10 to 12 hours previously.

items.statement: No immediate fund raise needed for next 12-18 months; may consider after 18-30 months if required for new division
items.quote: So yes, we do not envision any sudden need of funds in the next 12 to 18 months. Business is dynamic. We are growing. If there are a need of funds maybe after 18 months or 24 months or 30 months, we might look into it.

items.statement: Management maintains conservative guidance philosophy; comfortable overachieving current targets with buffers for unforeseen circumstances
items.quote: If you have seen my BSE guidances from 2016 onwards, every single guidance has been conservative because I do not believe in just giving a number and then if I overachieve that number, I'm comfortable.

items.statement: New-age business revenue targets for FY26: Gx ~INR60 cr, Pet Care ~INR42 cr, Nutritional ~INR26 cr; targeting INR550-580 cr total revenue
items.quote: This year at year-end closing, we are pegged to do somewhere around INR60 crores of our Gx business, around INR42 crores of our pet care business, around INR26 crores of our nutritional business. And that gives us a head -- runway to reach around INR600 crores and we are comfortable -- and around INR550 crores, INR570

items.statement: New-age business growing 20-25% YoY; target 51% revenue share by 2029-30; mobility segment growing 25-30% YoY
items.quote: By 2029, 2030, 51% of the business should be from the new-age business. That's what we are targeting. We are growing because they are smaller numbers right now, 20%, 25% growth in each of the divisions year-on-year.

items.statement: PAT margin sustainable at 5-6% currently; expects further jump in profits over next 6-7 quarters as high-margin new-age brands (50-70% gross margin) achieve cost efficiencies
items.quote: See, anything over 5%, 6% is a great margin at the rate that we are growing because our top line is growing, our margins are also growing. Margin growth, you will see a sudden increase after a few quarters once the cost efficiencies of the new-age brands start kicking in because they are intrinsically higher gross marg

items.statement: Expanding production capacities at current plants and added 37 partner manufacturing facilities; fundraise proceeds deployed in Q3 for working capital
items.quote: We are right now also increasing our production capacities at our current plants, and we have also added new partner facilities where we ourselves manufacture across various locations. So we have around 37 of those.

items.statement: No impact from India-US/EU trade deals as company focuses on manufacturing in India for India; no US/EU sales planned
items.quote: There will be no effect. We don't sell any products to U.S. and neither do we sell any products to Europe, neither do we intend to sell any products to U.S.

items.statement: Pet biscuits production started in Q3 FY26; revenues to reflect from Q3 and Q4 FY26; mobility products expanding to 4-5 new states covering 60% of India
items.quote: The pet biscuits line is doing phenomenally well. The revenues and numbers right now, we are adding more and more divisions right now and products. We started production in the second quarter of -- actually third quarter of this year, so this quarter.

items.statement: Finance costs increased due to working capital needs, bank changes, and machinery loans; expected to decline over next 2-3 quarters as fundraise proceeds deployed and internal cash flows improve
items.quote: Any growing company and rapidly expanding company has -- always requires working capital. So certain things, plus we had changed our banks also. And we have taken new machinery loans also. So those all add up to the finance cost part of it. This will decline over the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: New-age business manufacturing to become increasingly asset-light; will leverage partner cost efficiencies for mobility, pet care, herbal, nutraceutical products
items.quote: So of course, the new things that we are going to start is going to be asset-light. It suits our things also. We don't want to start manufacturing everything we sell. We want to use someone else's cost efficiencies, which have been achieved and use those to penetrate further into the markets that we already have.

items.statement: Seasonality: Q4 strongest, Q1 weakest due to distributor purchase targets and schemes; seasonality to normalize over 5-6 years as new-age ethical/OTC marketing grows
items.quote: If you see our numbers, if you see our business from 1995 onwards, our last quarter is always higher. It's a part of the business that we are in. And when you have a higher number, you have to give schemes, you have to give discounts, month-end schemes, year-end closing schemes.

items.statement: Revenue potential of INR1,500 crores by FY28 at ~40% Pakhajan utilization with 17-19% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we expect to scale of our revenue in FY '28 to approximately INR1,500 crores at around 40% utilization of available space at the Pakhajan facility

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected to close around INR800 crores
items.quote: We will do somewhere -- we should close somewhere about INR800 crores.

items.statement: Strategic MNC project capex INR85-90 crores fully customer-funded, INR19.9 cr advance received, equipment delivery Q2 FY27, commercialization Q1 FY28
items.quote: The estimated cost of the project is approximately INR85 crores to INR90 crores, which will be fully funded by customer. And we have already received an advance of INR19.9 crores. Equipment deliveries are expected to begin in Q2 FY '27 with commercialization targeted for Q1 FY '28.

items.statement: INR25.9 crores deployed for two manufacturing lines, trial runs March 2026, commercial production Q1 FY27
items.quote: we have deployed INR25.9 crores towards two manufacturing lines focused on high visibility product categories with sustained demand. Trial runs for these lines are expected to begin in March '26 and commercial production is planned for Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Industrial segment 85-90% of sales, targeting 90-95% in 2 years; consumer segment flat to declining
items.quote: Right now, we are about 85% to 90% industrial, will eventually go to 90% to 95% in the next 2 years' time. That's what we expect because consumer will remain flat or will have a degrowth, further degrowth.

items.statement: Long-term contracts target 60-70% of sales at full utilization vs 30% spot
items.quote: It will be 60% to 70% long-term contract, 30% will be spot.

items.statement: Gross margin compression 80% due to product mix change, 20% due to volume discounts to bulk buyers
items.quote: Well, it's more from a product mix. And I will say 80% from product mix and 20% from discount. There is a bulk buyer.

items.statement: Domestic demand improving in industrial and consumer segments; aggressive pricing strategy driving volume growth in India
items.quote: demand in India, we've seen it's been improving day by day, not only in industrial, but also somewhat into the consumer segment, too. So that is helping us to continue the growth in volume.

items.statement: EU-GMP remediation audit expected in Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026); NIP/OTF revenue ramp from regulated markets seen in Q4 FY27
items.quote: We believe April, May or June would be – the next quarter would be – we would have a specific date, where we would be told when the authorities will visit to actually inspect.

items.statement: ROW and emerging markets formulation business targeting ~20% growth, driven by new markets and NIP/OTF traction
items.quote: We are looking at about 20% growth in ROW markets.

items.statement: Export revenue INR 906 mn in Q3 FY26, up 23.2% YoY, contributing 88% of operating income
items.quote: Export business increased significantly in Q3 FY26 to INR 906 million, an increase of 23.2% YoY, contributing 88% to the total operating income.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 13.4% vs 13.8% in Q2; nine-month margin pressured by higher operating expenses and regulatory investments
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at approximately INR 145 million translating into a margin of around 13.4% compared to 13.8% in the previous quarter

items.statement: Margin normalization expected after EU-GMP clearance and regulated-market NIP/OTF sales ramp (high-margin products)
items.quote: The entry into Europe and the regulated market is one more inflection point where you will see the market improving over what we have been delivering very fast on QoQ basis.

items.statement: NIP and OTF revenue INR 132 mn (12.2% of operating income) in Q3 FY26; growing in ROW/emerging markets despite EU-GMP hold
items.quote: Revenue contributed from NIP and OTF stood at INR 132 million representing 12.2% of operating income.

items.statement: EU-GMP non-compliance delaying regulated-market NIP/OTF launches; site transfers (3-4 products) underway as contingency
items.quote: We have transferred one product, and are in the process of transferring two more products to alternate sites, thereby derisking the entire NIP business timeline regardless of this inspection.

items.statement: ~10% of INR 35 cr preferential issue proceeds allocated to CAPA remediation; company well within budget
items.quote: Yeah, so out of the funding what we are taking, around INR 35 crores, around 10% we have allocated for the CAPA.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 gross margin expanded 91 bps YoY to 36.5%; 9M FY26 gross margin up 72 bps to 35.5%
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter increased by 4.6% year-on-year to INR142 crores. Gross profit margin expanded by 91 basis points to 36.5%

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin stable at 10.0%; 9M FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 41 bps to 11.3%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR39 crores and remained largely stable year-on-year with margin at 10.0%.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 14-15% over next couple of years; FY27 expected to be better than FY26
items.quote: Over time, I think in our industry, the segment where we operate, it would be very -- it would be nice to say or the sustainable level of EBITDA that we look forward to is somewhere between 14% to 15%.

items.statement: No major capex commitment in near term; focus on enhancing free cash flow and reducing debt
items.quote: With no major capex commitment in the near term, the focus remains on enhancing free cash flow and further reducing debt.

items.statement: Force NXT premium brand grew 26.5% YoY in value and 48.1% in volume in Q3; 9M value growth 16.7%, volume 27.1%
items.quote: Force NXT continued its strong momentum, registering a year-on-year value growth of 26.5% and volume growth of 48.1% in quarter 3 FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 volumes grew 2.4% YoY; 9M volumes grew 8.5%; demand conditions remained steady
items.quote: During quarter 3 FY '26, total volumes grew by 2.4%, while for the 9 months ended FY '26, volume growth stood at healthy 8.5%.

items.statement: Competitive intensity easing but still present; expected to settle in 2-3 months; deep discounting by competitors at 4-5% vs Dollar's 1-1.5%
items.quote: No. So, it's not like what we saw 9 months back, but it's easing out, but it's still there. So -- which is causing a bit of a problem.

items.statement: Lakshya distribution project contributing 32% of 9M revenue, up 1% YoY; completed states showing double-digit growth (Haryana 11%, Odisha 24%, AP 20%)
items.quote: In Lakshya project, our contribution coming in from Lakshya project has been 32% this 9 months ended, if we look at the 9 months ended figure, which is up 1% from last year.

items.statement: Rainwear subsidiary Dollar Garment targets 12-15% growth in FY26 to ~INR42 crores; aims to cross INR100 crores revenue within 2 years; segment EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: This year, we're hopeful that we have the growth of around 12% to 15% in the overall segment. And already we completed the INR15 crores in the quarter 1. So, balance we cover in this quarter. Other than this, we have the target that within 2 years, we reach -- we cross the 3-digit in our revenue in this segment.

items.statement: Modern trade, e-commerce, quick-commerce channels grew 36% value and 38.9% volume in 9M; contributed 11.6% of 9M revenue
items.quote: For the 9 months ended FY '26, these channels recorded strong value growth of 36% and volume growth of 38.9%, contributing 11.6% to overall revenue.

items.statement: Expects to close NGC contract (~₹33,000 cr) by end of FY26 (March 2026) and reach order book of ~₹50,000 cr by FY26 end.
items.quote: we are confident of this contract getting concluded during the current financial year, which means next month we intend closing this contract , signing the contract with the Indian Navy. They have also indicated that the approval process is well on track which means we are hopeful and confident of ending the current fi

items.statement: Targets FY27 order book of ~₹70,000 cr assuming P-17 Bravo win as L2 yard (~₹30,000 cr share).
items.quote: if things go on well , we would like to look at ending FY '2 7 with an order book plus around ₹70,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book at ₹18,482 cr as of Dec 31, 2025 (42 platforms across 10 projects), down from ₹20,000+ cr due to faster execution.
items.quote: Our order book position as of 31st December is ₹18,482 crores. And interestingly, this is the first time we are dipping below ₹20,000, which is good news for you, which means our execution rate has picked up.

items.statement: Defense pipeline: 7 projects with AON worth ~₹1,55,000 cr (incl. P-17 Bravo ₹70,000 cr, LPD ₹35,000 cr, MCMV ₹32,000 cr); expects RFPs from April 2026.
items.quote: for the projects where AON has already been accorded and where we expect the RFPs to come out from now, which means something could come out in the next month onwards for the next 12 months is approximately ₹1,55,000 crores.

items.statement: NGC revenue accrual starts Q4 FY28 (2 years post-contract); FY28 growth cushioned by spares (10-15% of project cost) and research vessel/MPV deliveries.
items.quote: the revenue accrual will commence two years down the line, which means if FY '26 end we are concluding the contract, FY '28 end, that means the 4th Quarter of FY '28 we can expect revenue accrual.

items.statement: Govt shipbuilding schemes total ₹69,725 cr: SFA ₹24,736 cr (15-30% subsidy), Credit Note ₹4,001 cr, Maritime Development Fund ₹25,000 cr (brownfield subsidy + interest subvention), Clusters ₹19,989 cr (up to 50% greenfield subsidy).

items.statement: Swamy & Sons revenue ~INR200 crores, margins higher than current.

items.statement: Capex to continue at ~1.1% of revenue for new projects.

items.statement: GFS faces pricing pressure and macro headwinds.

items.statement: New business wins to maintain healthy margins, no dilution.

items.statement: Swamy & Sons acquisition expected to close in Q4.
items.quote: In terms of what is the outlook for FY '27, the transaction is still not closed. I think probably we are expecting to close this in Q4.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue to touch 800 crores, up from around 670 crores this year.
items.quote: In 27 we will touch 800 crores, this year we will be around 670 crores but next year we will touch 800 crores .

items.statement: Expects 11-12% EBITDA margin from June quarter.
items.quote: Sir I am hoping in June quarter we will be a able to see 11-12%

items.statement: Only maintenance and balanced capex of 10-20 crore for FY27.
items.quote: Beyond this, we expect only maintenance and balanced capex of around 10 to 20 crore for FY27.

items.statement: Capacity utilization expected to improve to 75% next financial year.
items.quote: Capacity utilization during the quarter stood at 67%, and we expect this to steadily improve to 75% for the next financial year.

items.statement: Solar project to reduce power cost by about 15 crore annually once fully operational.
items.quote: Once fully operational over the next 3 -4 weeks, the project is expected to reduce power cost by approximately 15 crore annually.

items.statement: Recycling plant to reduce raw material cost by 10% annually.
items.quote: The recycling plant is expected to further reduce our raw material cost requirement by 10% annually, supporting margin expansion going forward.

items.statement: Expects 8-10% volume growth in the quarter.
items.quote: I think 8-10% growth will be seen in the quarter.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased by 8 rupees per kg for both polymer and steel.

items.statement: Expects 5 crore benefit from inventory due to price increase.
items.quote: You will see a 5 crore benefit now.

items.statement: Wada plant subsidy of around 3 crore annually to be recognized after March.
items.quote: The annual profit of around 3 crores is the subsidy, we will consider it.

items.statement: Demand is good and prices are going up, right opportunity to scale up production.
items.quote: The demand is good, prices are going up. So this is the right opportunity to scale up the production and capacity utilization.

items.statement: IBC growth higher, MS drum decreased; will grab IBC growth first.
items.quote: In this quarter also, IBC growth is 8% higher. MS drum has decreased but IBC growth is higher.

items.statement: Export demand not yet seen but expected to come.
items.quote: Now the demand should come, everyone has heard about the export. The demand has not been seen yet, but it seems that the demand will come.

items.statement: Interest cost to decrease as repayment has started.
items.quote: Interest cost will decrease, repayment has started.

items.statement: FY26 PAT expected above 15%, EBITDA 22-23%.
items.quote: For FY26, we expect it to be above 15%. That is PAT. EBITDA in excess of 22-23%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 will be better than Q3 FY26; Q1 FY27 will outpace previous year.
items.quote: Q4, we will get better. And Q1 of the next fiscal year, we will overtake it, definitely from the previous year.

items.statement: FY27 will be better than FY25.
items.quote: Yes, FY27 would be better than FY25.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book around Rs.2,200 crores as of now.
items.quote: Unexecuted order book is around Rs.2,200 crores as of now.

items.statement: Expect order book to increase to around Rs.3,000 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: So, in Q1 we will definitely have the order book of around Rs.3,000 crores because Rs.2,200 crores, and in this quarter, we can exhaust it by Rs.200 crores almost, and of course we can have Rs.3,000 crores in Q1 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Expect order inflows of about Rs.1,000 crores in next three to four months.
items.quote: So, we are expecting it to enhance in next three, four months by about Rs.1,000 crores.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline around Rs.4,000 crores.
items.quote: Around Rs.4,000 crores.

items.statement: PAT may remain around 15% average for this year due to competition.
items.quote: So, it may remain around 15% as an average for this year.

items.statement: Next year PAT expected 17-18% as historical.
items.quote: And otherwise, for the next thing, we will remain about 17%-18% of the PAT as we have done in the history of the 10-11 years of the company's history.

items.statement: No plans to expand borrowings; current facilities sufficient.
items.quote: No plans on expanding in our borrowings. The facilities that we have are sufficient for execution of our projects.

items.statement: Promoter loan reduced to Rs.140 crores; plan to reduce to Rs.100 crores by FY26 end and settle next FY.
items.period: this financial year, next financial year
items.quote: We have reduced it to Rs.140 crores. We have repaid about Rs.70 crores of the principal amount along with interest. And we are planning to reduce the principal amount to less than Rs.100 crores by the end of this financial year and repay the whole amount in the next financial year.

items.statement: Uttarakhand rainfall and disasters caused delays; Q3 affected.
items.quote: Due to unexpectedly heavy rainfall and the landslides and natural disasters that took place in that state in the Q2, we expected it to recover by Q3, but the disaster management taken up by government that took some time more than what we expected and we could not execute or book revenue in that state.

items.statement: Flex sheet and paper plant output 800-900 tons, may reach 1,100+ tons next FY.
items.quote: But till now, I think that plant is producing about 800-900 tons of output. And it can reach an output of about 1,100-plus tons in the coming financial year.

items.quote: we are not only eyeing Tritium's EBITDA breakeven later part of FY27, but also now continuously strengthening revenues in EBITDA from current quarter Q4 FY26 onwards

items.quote: Pune has grown by almost 250-odd-percent compared to last year. Hyderabad has grown by almost 30%, 35% and Chennai has grown by about 35%.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents around INR120 crores plus on books.
items.quote: So currently, we have around INR120 crores plus in as a cash and cash equivalent in our books.

items.statement: Asset-light model to continue; selectively deploy owned fleet.
items.quote: So Yes, we will our philosophy and model is asset-light and we intend to keep it that way only.

items.quote: We are investing INR7 to INR10 crores in FY '26 to build an integrated and intelligent technology backbone with SAP ERP expected to go live within s ix months.

items.quote: Quite similar. INR1 crores asset and INR1 crores inventory, around INR2 crores.

items.quote: currently from a quarter which is INR 20-21, I would say we should be in good pace to have close to INR24 for the Q4 and then moving forward with that.

items.statement: Export order margins range from 7% to 18%.

items.quote: Q4 definitely we are looking forward for growth as well, and we are in the mid of Q4, so I think the growth will be there.

items.quote: During 9M FY26, AGPL achieved gross sales of INR 54 crores, reflecting encouraging market acceptance and effective execution of our distribution strategy.

items.quote: On the weather side, El Nino is expected to run neutral through winters, reducing tail risk from extreme anomalies.

items.quote: EBITDA increased 98.7% year -on-year to INR144.6 crores, with margin improving by 391 basis points to 12.6%, primarily due to favorable product and brand mix, higher localization, and strong operating leverage.

items.statement: Market growth expected at 15-20% YoY; pent-up demand may not materialize due to supply chain constraints
items.quote: Lately, due to the supply chain challenges and the cost rise, we have internally mitigated that maybe the pent -up will not happen and it'll just remain at the 1 5-20% slab and that kind of growth will happen.

items.quote: We are placing forward orders up to even three quarters in advance and in some cases even doing pre-payments to lock the chipsets, thereby securing supplies and maintaining market share growth trajectory.

items.statement: Chinese players excluded by trusted supply chain policy; CP PLUS has 90%+ models ER/STQC certified; new entrants delayed by component shortages
items.quote: As per the policy, the government has smartly done a trusted supply chain clause and those kind of things, so they don't qualify into these.

items.quote: These next -generation offerings, powered by Qualcomm's edge AI hardware and CP PLUS extensive market reach and product ecosystem, are expected to be commercially available in the H1 of coming year.

items.statement: FY27 growth expected to be better than historical levels.

items.statement: Bamboo business to contribute 20% of overall revenue in three years.

items.statement: CPG channel correction to conclude in Q4; stronger operating model expected from Q1 FY27
items.quote: This correction which we've taken, and the strengthening of the incumbent business model should conclude in Q4. And I think we should be back at a better clip in Q1 with a more efficient operating model from the staples perspective.

items.statement: New food FMCG categories to be announced in May 2026 earnings call
items.quote: We will also announce in Q1 the newer categories we wish to enter in the food FMCG space. This is a body of work, which is being done currently with some industry experts. And when we meet in May, we will give you a clear picture as to which categories beyond staples and sweeteners, we will enter in the food FMCG space

items.statement: Refinery expects lower white premium environment to continue for next 2 quarters
items.quote: So, we expect this tightness or the lower white premium environment to continue at least for the next 2 quarters going forward.

items.statement: Energy efficiency projects implemented end of last year reducing refinery costs to $41/MT sustainably
items.quote: The costs have come down during the current year mainly on account of energy efficiency projects that are implemented over end of last year giving results. So, we expect we should be able to sustain these cost levels going forward.

items.statement: No export quota utilized yet; 1.5 MMT export quota allocated for SY25-26
items.quote: the export quota, which has been given at 1.5 MMT

items.statement: Sugar segment EBITDA improved despite higher FRP and input costs due to efficiency gains
items.quote: certainly, from an EBITDA delivery, we have fared better. This is obviously despite FRP increases and increases in other input costs and this has rarely been driven by efficiency and cost work, which the business has done over the last year.

items.statement: Cane landed cost increased to INR4,122/MT from INR3,899/MT YoY due to FRP hike
items.quote: The cane landed cost is at INR4,122, this is due to the impact of the FRP as against INR3,899 per MT of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: El Nino signs from August-September may impact rainfall distribution and reservoir levels
items.quote: IMD has warned that there are some El Nino signs from August to September, and this may impact some of the rainfall distribution and reservoir levels later on in the year.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to sell 15 lakh Coromandel shares (0.51%); no timeline for execution
items.quote: it's an enabling resolution, which the Board has taken. So, we will determine at the right time basis any appropriate use of funds, which we may have, we will determine at that point in time.

items.statement: Expects casting volume growth of 15-16% including Punjab foundry in FY26, targeting 185,000-190,000 tons next year
items.quote: We should be going up very substantially and which I say that it should be around 15% to 16% growth, including the Punjab foundry. And subsequently, then we look forward at least going to 185,000, 190,000 tons next year.

items.statement: Pig iron margin improvement expected in Q4 FY26 due to price increases of INR 4,000/ton in North and INR 3,000/ton in South/West from January
items.quote: From January, there are price increases which have come into pig iron market. Northern India, almost like INR 4,000 per ton of pig iron, which is like around 10%.
