items.statement: Steel plant at Koppal to be ordered by March 31, 2026 with 2-year commissioning timeline
items.quote: Everything is ready. We have to sign off and order the equipment. So I think before end of this 31st March, we will take that step so that 2 years, we should commission steel plant.

items.statement: Second foundry line at Solapur targeting July 2026 commissioning
items.quote: July commissioning is still possible. I look forward to that.

items.statement: ONGC order for heavy tubes to deliver volumetric and value growth in Q4 FY26 and beyond
items.quote: First of all, the large volume is ONGC, I agree with you. And see, these are heavy tubes, and we will get both volumetric as well as the business in terms of value also it comes into the growth.

items.statement: Pig iron EBITDA margin around 9-10% in Q3 FY26 before price hikes
items.quote: I think we are around 9% to 10% EBITDA in pig iron.

items.statement: Coking coal covered for 3-4 months from January, providing temporary margin buffer against rising input costs
items.quote: I only say that at least for a short period, we should enjoy that, because I have a coverage of coking coal for 3, 4 months.

items.statement: Casting demand remains very strong across tractors, automotive, commercial vehicles and earthmoving equipment
items.quote: Demand for casting continues to be very strong from all the sectors, tractors, automotive, commercial vehicles as well as the earthmoving equipment.

items.statement: Punjab foundry (Oliver) to be merged into KFIL by end of FY26, contributing ~15,000 tons in FY26
items.quote: By end of this year, we are looking forward to merge the Punjab foundry into KFIL, Oliver into KFIL, and we are in the process to merge it. That foundry this year will produce and sell close to 15,000 tons, and that is not reflecting here.

items.statement: Tube sales target of 220,000 tons in FY27 from ~195,000 tons in FY26, with expander mill planned for >230,000 tons capacity
items.quote: We should be very close to 2 lakh tons this year and do maybe 10% more in the next year. And we expect that current installed whatever equipment are there, we should be able to go up to 2,30,000. And we are planning for an expander mill so that beyond 230,000, we get the benefit of the new mill.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 NBM guidance of 24-25% with stronger sales outcomes
items.quote: We continue to reinforce our guidance, which we had set out at the start of the year that -- which is for FY '26, the NBMs will land in the range of 24% to 25%, along with now stronger sales outcome that we are experiencing.

items.statement: GST impact ~350bps on margins; mitigated ~1/3 in Q3, ~70-80% in run-rate; confident of full mitigation over few quarters
items.quote: As we had guided earlier, in the first half call, the gross impact on margins is close to around 350 basis points due to GST, though through a series of cost actions, commercial conversations, product mix tweaks, we have been able to mitigate almost one-third of this impact in quarter 3 FY '26. And more importantly, in

items.statement: Q3 APE mix: Par 20%, Non-par savings 18%, Protection 15%, Annuity 10%, ULIP 38%; 9M mix: Par 16%, Annuity 9%, Non-par savings 24%, Protection 14%, ULIP 37%
items.quote: Due to all these actions, our Q3 APE product mix stood at approximately par at 20%, non -par savings at 18%, protection at 15%, annuity at 10% and ULIP at 38%, all this reflecting a balanced and resilient portfolio aligned with the long-term value creation objectives.

items.statement: Protection franchise strong: Retail protection +99% in Q3 (pure protection +95%, riders +100%); Group credit protection +45%
items.quote: During Q3, our protection franchise delivered strong growth supported by GST -related tailwinds and a targeted execution approach. items.statement: Annuity business grew 141% in Q3 and 107% in 9M FY26; broad-based across retail (>100%) and group (~40%)
items.quote: Our annuity business also reported healthy momentum, growing 141% in Q3 FY '26 and by 107% during 9 months FY '26. This performance was driven by consistent execution across both retail and corporate annuity pools as well as growing customer demand for guaranteed retirement income solutions.

items.statement: January sales grew 29% YoY with proprietary and partnership channels growing equally; Axis Bank contributed significantly
items.quote: Before we move ahead, happy to note that our growth trajectory continues in the month of January as well. Our sales grew by 29% at a company level with proprietary and partnership channels growing at equal growth rate with a very significant contribution coming from a leading bank partner, Axis Bank.

items.statement: Oil palm plantation expansion target of 40,000 hectares in FY27 (20,000 ha in Northeast, 20,000 ha in South India)
items.quote: This year, our target is that we should do close to 40,000 additional hectares, which is a mix of 20,000 in the northeastern part of the country and 20,000 in the South India.

items.statement: Brand ambassador contracts active: Dhoni extended 2 years; Shilpa Shetty, Tiger Shroff, Tamannaah Bhatia, Shahid Kapoor contracts continuing
items.quote: Mr. Dhoni is signed up for an additional 2 years. The contract for Mrs. Shilpa Shetty continues and likewise, both for Tiger Shroff and Tamanna Bhatia and similarly for Mr. Shahid Kapoor that also continues.

items.statement: Novelis FY26 exit cost savings run rate target raised to $150 million
items.quote: Back in April 2025, we had set an FY 26 exit savings run rate target of $75 million, which we raised last quarter to $125 million. With another quarter of solid execution behind us, that run rate is now $150 million as we accelerate all cost efficiency initiatives.

items.statement: Novelis 3-year goal to permanently reduce cost structure by $300 million by FY28 exit
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain committed to our 3-year goal of permanently reducing our cost structure by $300 million by FY '28 exit.

items.statement: India Aluminum Upstream Q4 cost expected to be ~1% higher driven by CP Coke prices
items.quote: Yes, I think that we are expecting 4th Quarter cost to be about 1% higher, largely driven by CP Coke. CP Coke prices, which goes into making the anode, has sharply risen due to what is happening, I think, in the demand and supply in China.

items.statement: India Copper Q4 EBITDA guidance of INR 600 crore comfortable
items.quote: In fact, we are predicting Q4 will be an extremely strong quarter for copper. The demand is very strong, and the EBITDA guidance of INR 600 crore is completely comfortable in Q4.

items.statement: India alumina sales for Q4 expected around 170-180 Kt
items.quote: Alumina sales for the 4th Quarter should be around 170 Kt to 180 KT. We did 160 in Q3.

items.statement: India CAPEX target for FY26 ~INR 10,000 crore including Bandha mine; FY27 similar range INR 10,000-12,000 crore
items.quote: So, this year, our target is about, we will be finishing the year at around INR 8,000 crores, and you need to add to that the INR 2,000 crores we paid to get the Bandha Mine. So, roughly this year will be INR 10,000 crores, and next year we also will be in the same range, about INR 10,000 crores to INR 12,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt to EBITDA target maintained around 2x
items.quote: we remain committed to maintain our net leverage around 2x at the consolidated level.

items.statement: AV Minerals raised $800M at SOFR+105bps (5-year tenure); $750M infused into Novelis Dec 2025; additional $200M upsized Feb 2026 also for Novelis equity
items.quote: During the quarter, Hindalco's wholly-owned subsidiary, AV Minerals, raised $800 million at SOFR plus 105 basis points. items.quote: Our quarterly EBITDA was up 14% year-on-year at INR 4,832 crore, backed by our resilient performance across the value chain, fully aligned with our philosophy of operational excellence by design. items.statement: Expect FY26 volume growth of 3-4% despite H1 decline of 5%
items.quote: Based on our quarter 3 performance and the current trends, we expect to end financial year '26 with a volume growth of 3% to 4% in spite of a minus 5% degrowth in H1 FY '26 on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in FY27 driven by trade agreements and domestic buoyancy
items.quote: Looking ahead, as we look to build our domestic volumes and continue our growth momentum, we expect the trade agreements with the U.S. and EU to provide a fillip for better overall volume growth in FY 27.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin improvement of ~150 bps annually over next 2-4 years
items.quote: We are looking that with all the initiatives over the next 2 to 3, 4 years, we expect at least on an annual basis, an improvement of 150 basis points plus or minus on an annual basis.

items.statement: TDQ antioxidant plant at Dahej ahead of schedule; production trials planned H1 CY26
items.quote: Our TDQ antioxidant investment at Dahej, is coming along well. And we expect to be ahead of our original schedule with production trials planned during the first half of the calendar year.

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew high single-digit in Q3 FY26 driven by GST 2.0 demand improvement
items.quote: The domestic volumes witnessed a high single-digit growth, driven largely by the improved demand due to GST 2.0.

items.statement: Export volumes at ~50% of pre-tariff run-rate in Q3; expect recovery in 2-3 months
items.quote: Roughly about 50% of that, yes.

items.statement: New products pipeline expected to contribute 10-12% of current volumes over time, ramping from FY28-29
items.quote: Eventually, surely, we expect these products should give us at least about 10% to 12% compared to current volumes, at least.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.5%, up from 8.2% in 9M FY26; cost savings of Rs.23 cr in 9M from working capital and utility efficiency
items.quote: The operating EBITDA for Q3 FY '26 stood at Rs.27 crores as against Rs.22 crores recorded in Q2 FY '26. The EBITDA margin stood at 8.5% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Antidumping investigations initiated on key products (China, EU, US, Korea, Thailand); final findings expected in 1.5-2 months
items.quote: Seeing merit in our submissions, the authorities have initiated detailed investigations, and we expect the outcome of these proceedings in the coming months.

items.statement: Aniline raw material costs rising gradually since start of year; expect to pass through price increases
items.quote: Yes, so we are looking at so that we will be able to pass on because it is an overall gradual increase that's been happening since the beginning of this year.

items.statement: Imports stable at current levels; not expected to increase significantly further
items.quote: Imports coming in, so it has kind of been at a certain level in the last few quarters. I don't expect that it should now significantly increase from here on.

items.statement: Latex capacity utilization at ~60% in 9M FY26; export growth in FY27 includes moderate latex recovery
items.quote: I think in the 9 months, we are looking at, it's about 60%.

items.statement: India-EU FTA expected to benefit raw material imports from Europe, though current import volume from Europe not sizable
items.quote: Yes, yes. There are some raw materials, which there will be a benefit once the FTA comes into play.

items.statement: February expected to be a very strong month for hospitality; outlook positive with events and luxury demand
items.quote: February is a time, and all indications are that February will be a very strong month for us, as I would imagine it would be for the industry.

items.statement: Like-for-like revenue growth in Q3 was 14% excluding closed hotels and lounge business
items.quote: On a Y-o-Y basis, taking all the impacts which we had on account of The Oberoi Grand, of course for The Oberoi Grand there is hardly any impact, OAS, Mumbai and the other things, including the Wildflower Hall, we have grown 14% in Q3, as against the 9% growth, what you saw earlier.

items.statement: Development pipeline of 30 hotels with ~2,450 keys to be added over next 3-4 years
items.quote: As of the current quarter, we have a healthy pipeline of 30 hotels with approx. 2450 keys which we are going to add in next three to four years' time.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 6-7% vs 9% revenue growth due to faster OFS growth diluting margins; standalone EBITDA grew 8% vs 12% revenue
items.quote: EBITDA grew at 6%, it was lower than the revenue growth due to change in the business mix mainly on account of OFS growth which grew much more faster.

items.statement: Segment mix plateaued; direct booking growth flattened; OFS growing faster than hotel revenue changing business mix
items.quote: We have seen growth of direct segment over the last few years, but that has plateaued now and the percentage mix or the segment mix remains same in current year versus last year.

items.statement: Flight disruptions in December caused 26% higher cancellations; pollution warnings impacting North India travel; wage code one-time Rs 30 cr hit
items.quote: In December, occupancy was lower for the same reason which was mentioned earlier. The first two weeks December we saw a higher impact of cancellations on account of the flight disruptions we saw in the Indian aviation space.

items.statement: Surplus funds increased from operational profits and Mashobra settlement (Rs 115 cr); cash reserves support organic/inorganic expansion
items.quote: Increase of surplus funds in the last qtr due to operational profits over last quarters. Also, we got one time cash increase, from Mashobra settlement which was in the range of INR 115 crores adding to our cash position.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 2,500 crore; FY26 capex expected at INR 1,200-1,300 crore including INR 100 crore remaining spend
items.quote: INR 2,500 crore is for FY27, not FY26. FY26 is already underway, that would involve spending of around INR 100 crore, bringing the total to approximately INR 1,200–1,300 crore.

items.statement: Pipeline of ~15 new products in R&D/pilot stages across mining chemicals, flame retardants, personal care, flavors & fragrances, polymer applications; commercialization staggered over next several months
items.quote: At the moment, we have a pipeline of about 15 products at various stages between R&D, piloting and awaiting customer feedback with regards to samples. items.statement: Nitric acid integration benefits to reflect from Q4 FY26 as 100% self-consumption achieved from mid-December 2025; Q3 margins hit by spot purchases during commissioning gap
items.quote: We commissioned the nitric acid plant in the middle of December 2025. This quarter and next quarter will be the first period where we would have pretty much 100% consumption of nitric acid.

items.statement: Chinese overcapacity remains significant risk affecting ~30-40% of products; Chinese government deflation control measures underway; European phenol capacity shutdowns ongoing
items.quote: It doesn't change the fact that there is a significant Chinese overcapacity. And this will affect a couple of products. I don't anticipate that it affects every single one of our products, maybe many of our products, 60%, 70% of our products are not as directly affected by Chinese oversupply.

items.statement: Management expects full-year FY26 revenue of ~INR 1,500 crores, implying ~INR 450 crores net revenue in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Looking at the scenario right now, I think we would reach close to about INR 1,500 crores by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: UP greenfield Phase 1 (INR 370 crores) on track for June 2026 completion; Phase 2 (INR 200 crores) ~1 year later; financial closure achieved for both phases
items.quote: Phase 1 investment is about INR 370 crores. Phase 2 is INR 200 crores. Phase 2 will happen approximately one year after Phase 1.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh tender decision expected this weekend; if approved, supplies could start in Q4 FY26, else meaningful contribution from FY27
items.quote: If they act soon, then we'll be able to supply this quarter itself. Otherwise, for next year, it will be a good revenue for us.

items.quote: We expect that there should be a revival in the gross margins in Q4 because the season has started.

items.statement: No price hike planned for Q4; focus on volume growth; excise policy allows only annual price revisions limiting cost pass-through
items.quote: No, there is no plan to take any price increase. If there is an opportunity that is presenting to us, then we'll look at it.

items.statement: IMFL volumes up 46% YoY in Q3 (5 lakh cases) and 55% in 9M (13.1 lakh cases); premiumization strategy gaining traction; Hunter share fell due to cold in MP/Delhi
items.quote: Our IMFL segment saw a strong 46% increase, contributing 5 lakh cases. Despite the overall volume pressures, our IMFL brands continued to show positive momentum.

items.statement: Bhopal plant license suspended; petition heard in MP High Court, order reserved, decision expected within days; plant currently closed, no fresh production or sales possible in MP
items.quote: We have made the required submissions in the MP High Court, and we expect a judgment on the issue in the next 2 to 3 days.

items.statement: Promoters to raise stake to 51% in short-to-medium term (2-3 years) via preferential issues as capital needed or open market purchases
items.quote: I think the time frame for increasing it to 51% is short to medium term, maybe in the next 2 to 3 years. And the increase is going to come through preferential issues as and when the capital is required in the company or from open market purchases.

items.statement: Q3 plant utilizations: Bhopal 56%, Woodpecker (Odisha) 42%, Odisha plant 36%; ample capacity at existing plants plus new UP capacity coming
items.quote: Sir, Q3, we operated the Bhopal plant at 56%, Woodpecker at 42% and Odisha plant at about 36%.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable PAT margin target of 7% within 2-3 years, up from current 4%
items.quote: our long-term sustainable PAT margin is at 7% levels and we're quite confident we'll achieve that in the next, within the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Double-digit sales growth targeted, with 15% as internal target
items.quote: I will say double-digit sales growth. 15, we can definitely say is one of the targets we have in mind, but double-digit sales growth will come in too.

items.quote: The boilers division saw a very strong increase in our order backlog to INR123 crores this quarter.

items.quote: Our Q3 PAT margins were at 3.56%. After including the one-time events, we would have been at 4%.

items.quote: Our revenue and profit trajectory continues to shift towards higher-margin businesses, and this positive trajectory will continue to grow our PAT at double-digit rates.

items.quote: As of right now, we are at about 60% capacity utilization. We'll get to, we'll get to 70% by the end of this quarter.

items.quote: The monthly run rate right now compared to what it was 2 months ago, 3 months ago is higher by double-digit numbers. You can say north of 20% higher. So it's, it's growing and growing quickly. PEB India.

items.statement: PEB India growth vectors: process engineering, automotive, high-rise buildings (up to G+16); US PEB mix geared to warehouse and data centers; boiler order book INR 123 cr (blended 6-month execution)
items.quote: We are primarily seeing it in the process engineering space, the automotive space and the high-rise building space. Those are the three growth vectors where we've received significant order inflows.

items.quote: We have solved the labor problem. We've solved it late last quarter. To the impact, the positive impact from that would not have been seen in the full quarter. items.quote: The order backlog is projected to more than double in the next few weeks. So that I can tell you.

items.statement: Peak combined India+US PEB/structural capacity at 80% utilization could yield INR 200-220 cr/month revenue
items.quote: If you were to combine India and the US both for PEB and structural, at peak capacity let's say 80% I think is fair. I don't think we should go much higher than that. We will absolutely be able to hit a revenue number closer to INR200 crores to INR220 crores per month.

items.quote: Give us a quarter or max two quarters on this. We're getting our ducks lined up on this. items.statement: Targeting net margin increase from ~3.5% to 5%
items.quote: Our net margin after tax is approximately 3.5% presently and we are targeting to increase it to 5%.

items.statement: Planning capacity expansion of 30-40% by adding machinery
items.quote: And after that, we can expand our capacity by at least 30% to 40%.

items.statement: Upgrading machinery next quarter to increase efficiency and production
items.quote: So that is what we are planning to do the next quarter, by upgrading our machineries.

items.statement: Current margins sustainable; focus on value-added products to improve margins
items.quote: The current margins are sustainable and we are keen to increase our current margins.

items.statement: Renewable energy expansion to reduce power cost by at least 25%
items.quote: This will help to reduce our power cost overall by at least 25%.

items.statement: Optimizing interest cost via reserves and negotiating supplier credit terms
items.quote: Second, our one of the major cost factor is the interest cost, which we are already optimizing by adding our reserves and we are negotiating, from our suppliers' financial terms by increasing the credit limit they provide us.

items.statement: Demand constantly increasing in Indian and international markets; exports to diversify
items.quote: Yes, the demand is constantly increasing in the Indian market as well as the international market.

items.statement: Expect 10-20% rise in industry exports due to trade deals with EU and US
items.quote: We expect the rise of at least 10% to 20% in the current exports due to these trade deals, going overall the whole industry.

items.statement: Capacity utilization over 95% currently; has been above 95% for last few quarters
items.quote: Current capacity utilization is over 95%.

items.statement: Direct exports challenging as B2B; benefits from trade deals indirect via customer demand
items.quote: We are a B2B company, so our direct exports to these countries will be difficult. But yes, due to this trade deal, our customers would have requirement of exports and indirectly, we would have good requirements.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10-15% and bottom line growth of 15-20%
items.quote: So in the coming year, we expect minimum 10% to 15% growth in the top line and 15% to 20% in the bottom line.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue expected at INR600 crores with EBITDA margin around 11%
items.quote: Yes, yes, sure. We expect INR600 crores revenue in the fourth quarter. And margin will also be increased.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve by 1-2% in Q4 FY26 from current levels
items.quote: But we hope we will increase, I guess, the EBITDA margin increased by 1% to 2% in the coming quarter.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR150-200 crores, similar to FY26 levels
items.quote: the capex regularly we are doing is approximately INR150 crores to INR200 crores. So I think for FY '27, we will also be doing the same level of the capex

items.statement: FY26 capex likely INR130-135 crores vs budgeted INR150 crores, 60% for growth
items.quote: total capex for FY '26 is something around INR150 crores. we are into the last quarter, so maybe a little less to that INR150 crores we budgeted. But I think we are in the last quarter. items.statement: EBITDA margin target revised to 11-12% for FY26 from earlier 13-15% due to fuel cost
items.quote: Initially we said that we will try to reach to around 14% to 15% , after that we said we will be reaching to around 13%. But I think now we are just understanding that we will be reaching something 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin upside of 10-15% from current profile with mix improvement
items.quote: Margin, I think CFO already discussed about this for the next year, around 10% to 15% upside from the current margin profile.

items.statement: Target ibuprofen:non-ibuprofen 50:50 by FY27, long-term 25:75
items.quote: we are targeting to further have 50-50 ratio for the '27 from ibuprofen and non-ibuprofen. This is what we are discussing, and we are very hopeful that we may cross it or to reach very near to this.

items.statement: Rice husk fuel costs remain elevated at 450-500 MT/day consumption, impacting margins
items.quote: Our current consumption of rice husk is somewhere around maybe 450 to 500 metric tons per day.

items.statement: Ethyl acetate and paracetamol pricing stable Q-on-Q, volumes increasing

items.statement: Q4 revenue expected at 90-95% of Q3 level; hyperlocal grows in Q4 due to Valentine's Day
items.quote: Net -net, at a business level, we expect anywhere between 90% to 95% of the revenues coming in Q4 versus Q3.

items.statement: Reaffirmed sustained double-digit revenue growth guidance with EBITDA growth slightly ahead of revenue
items.quote: Our long-term guidance remains unchanged, which is double-digit revenue growth. We've delivered it now consistently for the last few quarters. And we are confident that we will continue to deliver to our strategy.

items.statement: Expects Europe margins to return to mid-teen levels in coming quarters
items.quote: We are confident that going forward, Europe will operate at mid-teen margins.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 20.1%, down 20 bps YoY but within target range; expects gradual improvement through scale benefits
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 20.1%, 20 basis points lower than last year but firmly within our target operating range.

items.statement: Thailand plant commercialized in November 2025; depreciation growth to remain lower than revenue growth
items.quote: We commercialized our Thailand plant in this quarter itself, Quarter 3.

items.statement: 50% of business on pass-through basis; strengthened proactive pricing processes to protect margins from commodity cycles
items.quote: We are mostly on a pass-through basis. And hence, 50% of our business is on pass-through basis. Balance 50% is negotiated when the prices go up.

items.statement: Seeing early recovery signs in oral care in AMESA; B&C demand strong across all regions with multiple quarters of 20%+ growth
items.quote: We are seeing early recovery signs in oral care. Obviously, you will see it will take some time for it to fully recover. But definitely, this quarter has been better and we feel that momentum will start turning and become positive.

items.statement: Europe impacted by adverse customer mix, short-term operational issues (higher write-offs, outsourcing, production issues) and seasonal Q3 slowness
items.quote: Our challenges were adverse customer mix. In addition to that, we were impacted by short-term operational challenges, which are in the nature of higher write-off, higher outsourcing and some production issues as well.

items.statement: Strong pipeline in Thailand built over past year; organic entry model with sales team on ground
items.quote: We have a really strong and healthy pipeline. We will execute against that over a period of time because Thailand has been operational in this quarter for less than 4 weeks.

items.statement: Net debt increase due to dividend payout and accelerated capex phasing; expects correction on full-year basis
items.quote: This is just phasing. So, in this quarter, we do a dividend payout. And we have some accelerated CAPEX spending. This is a timing impact and should get corrected on a full year basis.

items.statement: Actively pursuing M&A for new geographies or capabilities; no concrete deals to announce
items.quote: We continue to actively pursue M&A opportunities. When we look at M&A, we use two criteria to look at targets. One is anything which takes us to a new geography or indeed helps us build new capabilities.

items.statement: Targets continued ROCE improvement year-on-year; prioritizes growth over other metrics
items.quote: Our ROCE this year has gone up. It is at 18.7%. It has gone up by 200 basis points. And we will continue to target to improve our ROCE year-on-year as we go forward.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue guidance to INR6,325-6,375 crore from INR6,750-7,000 crore due to supply chain delays
items.quote: Owing to such delays in execution time line, our orders, which is supposed to be executed in this quarter has flown to subsequent quarters. Therefore, we have revised revenue guidance from the expected range of INR6,750 crore to INR7,000 crore to now INR6,325 crore to INR6,375 crore.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA guidance revised to INR555-575 crore and PAT to INR220-230 crore
items.value: EBITDA INR555-575 crore, PAT INR220-230 crore
items.quote: The revision in revenue reflects EBITDA of INR555 crore to INR575 crore and a PAT of INR220 crore to INR230 crore in FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 order booking guidance maintained at ~$1 billion; Q4 expected to book $300-350 million
items.quote: The company continues to maintain strong order momentum and remains confident of achieving its FY '26 order booking guidance of approximately $1 billion, thereby entering FY '27 with a strong traction.

items.statement: Q3 order bookings of $232 million; total backlog at $601 million as of Dec 2025
items.quote: As highlighted by Sanjeev earlier, the company continued to witness strong order momentum during Q3 with order bookings of $232 million. The total order backlog stands at $601 million as of December 2025.

items.statement: Acquisition of 2S Inovações Tecnológicas for ~INR275 crore upfront plus earnouts; expected to add INR500 crore revenue in FY27
items.quote: We will be paying close to around INR275 crore at closing, and this is subject to some working capital adjustments. And then there is the additional deferred payments, including earnouts linked to the performance, which we will pay over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Targeting 10% EBITDA margin for FY27; current run-rate ~8.9-9%
items.quote: So we continue to hold on to our margin guidance. Our goal is to move to 10%. We are at 9-ish, 8.9%, 9%. So I think this acquisition or otherwise as well, at scale, we believe will be margin accretive.

items.statement: Industry-wide supply chain constraints (fiber, cables, GPUs, power) delaying data center project execution; revenue shifted to FY27
items.quote: The data center ecosystem is currently witnessing heightened industry activity, which has resulted in shortages across several critical inputs, including optical fibers, cables, GPUs, racks, etcetera, power infrastructure and funding access.

items.statement: $40-45 million revenue deferred from FY26 to FY27 due to customer delays and supply chain constraints
items.quote: Approximately $40 million to $45 million relates to revenue that was initially expected to be recognized in FY '26, but has shifted due to temporary customer level delays and supply chain constraints. As these challenges gradually normalize and execution progresses, this revenue is expected to flow in FY '27.

items.statement: Project order book grew $37 million QoQ to $195 million in Q3, driven by data center segment
items.quote: The project order book witnessed a robust growth, reflecting an upside of $37 million, at $195 million in Q3 FY '26 compared to $158 million in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Targeting 30-35% CAGR including inorganic to reach $2 billion revenue by FY30
items.quote: So we're targeting a CAGR of 30%, 35%, including inorganic to be able to get to our goal of $2 billion, right? So that's what we're looking at.

items.statement: Expecting quarterly order booking run-rate of $300-350 million from FY27 onwards
items.quote: Our goal next year moving into should be upward of $300 million, $350 million every quarter going forward. We are currently at $230 million, $250 million.

items.statement: 2S acquisition funded through mix of internal accruals and debt; target ROE/ROCE 25-30%
items.quote: And then this acquisition of INR275 crore, what we have to pay we will be funding it through internal accruals, mix of internal accruals and debt. And we have already told earlier also that we believe in putting our capital prudently. Our ROE and ROCE, we want to be 25% to 30% type of range.

items.statement: Exceptional items (rent restructuring, severance) expected to continue for 2-3 more quarters in FY27
items.quote: I think that at least another two quarters in FY '27, we should have these exceptional items. But the exceptional expenses should a little bit go down because we continue to pivot and, let's say, identify the opportunities to sever the people wherever we think that it is not required.

items.statement: Expect FY27 top-line growth to be better than FY26; H2 FY26 better than H1 FY26
items.quote: we expect growth in financial year'27 to be better than financial year'26

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin to stay around guided 22-23% range (ex-Ice Cream)
items.quote: we expect consolidated EBITDA margin to stay around the guided range

items.statement: Expect low single-digit price increases over FY26 due to stable-to-inflationary commodity trends
items.quote: overall, for the year, if you look at it, we do expect a low single- digit price increases over the year

items.statement: Underlying volume growth of 4% in Q3 FY26, highest in 12 quarters; broad-based across categories
items.quote: Our UVG for the quarter is the highest UVG that we have recorded in the last 12 quarters

items.statement: Quick commerce now 3% of business, doubling quarter-on-quarter; service levels up 1,400 bps, lead time down 20%
items.quote: it is now 3% of our business, growing almost 100% quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Minimalist and OZiva combined ARR of Rs 1,100 cr; Minimalist expanded to 25,000+ offline stores from 3,000 at acquisition
items.quote: Between these two brands, we have now built an ARR of Rs. 1,100 crores business

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of remaining 49% stake in OZiva for Rs 824 cr; divesting minority stake in Nutritionab for Rs 307 cr
items.quote: the Board of Directors has approved the acquisition of remaining 49% stake in OZiva at an investment of Rs, 824 crores

items.statement: Investing in dedicated quick commerce organisation, bespoke supply chain, tech and digital marketing capabilities
items.quote: we are stepping up investments not just in people dedicated to the channel, but also in bespoke supply chain, tech and digital marketing capability

items.statement: Input cost volatility persists: rupee depreciation pressures imported materials; palm oil inflationary long-term; non-feedstock commodities and sulfuric acid inflating
items.quote: depreciating rupee increased cost pressure on imported materials, while commodity trends remain divergent

items.statement: Organisational restructuring: Business Unit Heads now report directly to CEO; Chief Marketing Officers appointed per BU; India-focused R&D design & deploy organisation created
items.quote: All Business Unit Heads will now directly report to me instead of the earlier dual-reporting structure

items.statement: Ice Cream demerger completed; KWIL listing on 16 Feb 2026; demerger adds ~50 bps to EBITDA margin
items.quote: you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points

items.statement: Expect Q4 sugar crushing of ~90 lakh quintals at 100% capacity utilization over 90-91 days
items.quote: Given that 67 lakh crushing is already there in Q3 and 90 days even if we operate 91 days if we operate our sugar mill properly and use 100% capacity. So another 90 million tons of -- 90 lakh quintals of crushing should be available with us.

items.statement: Zuari Infra World achieved Gross Development Value of INR 3,100 crores; targeting INR 10,000 crores GDV in current financial year
items.quote: Our target itself has been we had set ourselves an internal target to do DM projects for at least INR10,000 crores in the current financial year itself. And when you see that those, if we achieve those targets, so even considering the 10% of DM fee which you just stated, it becomes a meaningful size.

items.statement: Simon India executing orders worth ~INR 100 crores; completed INR 55.5 crore evaporator project for PPL
items.quote: Simon India, which is our engineering and construction company, commissioned the fifth evaporator project for PPL in this quarter. The value, contract value for this project was INR55.5 crores. It has now got orders of about INR100 crores that it is executing for various clients.

items.statement: SPE division maintains 8-10% EBITDA margins; standalone Q3 EBITDA INR 36.3 crores vs INR 37.7 crores YoY
items.quote: SPE remains you can say a very, it's a core business for Zuari Industries and it gives at almost 8% to 10% EBITDA margins for us.

items.statement: Ethanol prices stagnant despite 16.7% increase in cane SAP; industry representations made to government for price revision
items.quote: Given that there is almost 16.7% increase in FR in SAP of sugar cane prices this year, the industry in particular was expecting that the government is going to increase the prices of ethanol, which has not happened so far, although multiple representations have been made to the ministry.

items.statement: No sugar glut expected; India sugar production estimated at 34.4M tons, diversion 3.4M tons, exports 1.5M tons, leaving ~29M tons availability vs 28-29M tons consumption
items.quote: I believe Indian sugar industry is very much well placed. We don't see a sugar glut in India, which is going to have any negative impact on sugar prices. I think it is my estimates say that sugar production is estimated at some 34.4 lakh million tons and diversion is around 3.4 million tons.

items.statement: Ethanol industry overcapacity concern; government paused blending at 20%, impacting demand outlook
items.quote: The overall macroeconomic situation in ethanol market remains a concern. As some of you may have noted, there seems to be significant overcapacity in the ethanol industry and I think a resolution must be found out to deal with it.

items.statement: Zuari Envien Bioenergy plant commissioned 1 Jan 2026; locked 20,000 KL ethanol contracts through October; 50% capacity tied to institutional buyers
items.quote: We have locked in about 20,000 kilo liter of contracts, which will take us through October and then hopefully we will have the next round of OMC tenders which will give us the revenues in the coming financial year.

items.statement: External debt (excl. working capital) reduced to INR 1,848 crores from INR 1,863 crores QoQ; deleveraging via Dubai and associate inflows in FY27
items.quote: Excluding working capital, the gross external debt of the company and its subsidiaries was INR1,848 crores, which was a shade lower than INR1,863 crores for the previous quarter.

items.statement: No IPO planned for Zuari Infraworld; focus on Dubai project completion and fund repatriation
items.quote: The first question about the IPO of Zuari Infra World. I just want to place on record that there is no such proposal on the table. We are not contemplating any IPO of Zuari Infraworld.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth in FY26 and FY27 with improving earnings quality and sustained margin strength
items.quote: Collectively these levers give us confidence in delivering double digit revenue growth in FY'26 and FY'27 with improving quality of earnings and sustained margin strength.

items.statement: Guides 12-14% consolidated revenue growth for Q4 FY26
items.quote: I would say 12% to 14% in Q4 as a topline growth is realistic.

items.statement: Expects management fee income to grow in high teens in FY27 driven by 60+ openings
items.quote: Management fee income is set to grow in the high teens driven by 60 plus openings. Yes, ladies and gentlemen, 60 plus openings in FY '27 and sustained asset light expansion on what we call a capital light model.

items.statement: Expects new business verticals (Ginger, Qmin, amã, Tree of Life) to deliver 25%+ revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: Ginger and our new business verticals are expected to deliver 25 % plus revenue growth supported by integration benefits and scale efficiencies.

items.statement: Expects Atmantan to generate ~INR 100 crores revenue in FY27 with margins north of 40-45%
items.quote: This property and this brand is projected to generate revenue of approximately INR 100 crores in FY '27 with strong margin characteristics aligned to the premium wellness positioning.

items.statement: Expects ANK and Pride acquisitions to contribute INR 250-300 crores to consolidated topline in FY26-27
items.quote: These transactions strengthen our presence in high growth segments including mid-scale, experiential leisure and holistic wellness while further expanding our portfolio, scale and geographic footprint. Importantly, these acquisitions are expected to contribute meaningfully in the range of INR 250 crores to INR 300 cror

items.statement: Pipeline of 30,200 keys under development (almost equal to 32,300 operational keys); 80% managed, 94% capital light
items.quote: Importantly, this translates as I mentioned previously to 32,300 operational keys and an almost equal amount of 30,200 keys under development which is an industry leading pipeline that provides strong multi-year growth visibility.

items.statement: Q3 RevPAR growth 9% driven by 7% ARR growth; expects 8.5-10% RevPAR growth going forward
items.quote: The majority of the growth is coming driven by average room rate which if we take everything together comes to 7% which accounts for the 9% RevPAR growth.

items.statement: Sees structural demand tailwinds from rising incomes, infrastructure, MICE, weddings, spiritual tourism, premiumization; supply additions measured in key micro markets
items.quote: Because India's travel and tourism ecosystem continues to deepen driven by rising disposable incomes, infrastructure investments, MICE demand, weddings, spiritual tourism and premiumization of experiences. On the supply side additions remain measured in several key micro markets and this is ultimately supporting the Re

items.statement: Taj Bandstand project timeline uncertain due to 164m tall building with construction in water; climate and other factors beyond control may affect completion
items.quote: It is very difficult to say that today because we are building a 164-meter tall building and a part of the construction is in water. You know, there are things that happen in terms of climate and other things which are beyond anybody's reasonable control.

items.statement: Expect business EBITDA of EUR 9-10 million for Q4 FY26; long-term target EUR 90-100 million EBITDA in 3-4 years
items.quote: we expect a EUR 9 million to EUR 10 million of a business EBITDA

items.statement: Frankfurt plant rightsizing completed; production transferred to India; no major manufacturing footprint changes planned
items.quote: Frankfurt was to be rightsized, which has been done. And that production is already transferred into India. We don't see any need to further -- I mean, there will be tactical but no major product changes in manufacturing

items.statement: Benzene price increases well covered; minimal impact on merged entity due to diversified portfolio; no Q4 margin pressure expected
items.quote: we do see increases. But I think we are well covered on the raw materials, and we should not see any impact on Q4. Secondly, with our larger portfolio, our dependency, the impact which could have, especially if you refer to benzene would be quite miniscule

items.statement: No order backlog cited; confidence based on customer purchase commitments after destocking completion
items.quote: Our confidence on the demand is, as I mentioned, the customers promised that they would start buying after January, and we are seeing that already in January and early February

items.statement: No refinancing plans mentioned; current borrowing cost 5.75-6%; higher reported finance cost due to IndAS lease accounting and acquisition fair valuation
items.quote: we are in the range of 5.75% to 6% as our interest cost. Balance effect is because of the IndAS accounting on the lease and the other fair valuation of the acquisition

items.statement: FY27 combined business volume growth guided at high-single to low-double digit, followed by low-double digit for next couple of years
items.quote: For FY27, we expect a high-single digit to low-double digit volume growth for the combined business, which will be followed by low-double digit volume growth over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins to expand 150-250 bps over next 24-36 months for combined business
items.quote: In terms of margins, we expect the consolidated EBITDA margins to expand by 150 - 250 bps for the combined business over the next 24 - 36 months.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio expected below 1.0x by FY29
items.quote: As highlighted earlier as well, we expect the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio going down below 1.0x by FY29.

items.statement: Imperial Blue to see low to mid-single digit volume degrowth in FY26 vs FY25 due to pre-acquisition performance
items.quote: Despite a strong start for IB under TI ownership, the brand will witness a low to mid-single digit volume degrowth in FY26 as compared to FY25 on account of tepid performance in the 8 months preceding the acquisition.

items.statement: Imperial Blue expected high-single digit volume growth in Q4 FY26 despite integration
items.quote: Even amidst integration exercise, we expect to register a high-single digit volume growth for IB in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Ex-IB NSR expanded from Rs 1,161 to Rs 1,209 per case YoY in Q3
items.quote: And even ex-IB NSR has expanded from Rs. 1,161 per case in Q3 of FY25 to Rs. 1,209 in this quarter.

items.statement: Prag bottling unit expansion to be commissioned in Q4 FY26, ~Rs 10 crore remaining investment
items.quote: On CAPEX related to our Prag bottling unit, we are expecting the expanded facility to be commissioned in the 4th quarter of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Raised Rs 2,093 crore via preferential issue; promoter warrants to convert in upcoming fiscal year
items.quote: During the year, we have received Rs. 2,093 crore as a part of the preferential issue. This includes proceeds received in the current quarter upon initiation of warrant conversion by all public investors. Warrants held by the promoter group will be converted during the upcoming fiscal year.

items.statement: Took Rs 2,100 crore debt from banks/NBFCs with 2-year principal moratorium, 6-year tenure, ballooning repayment
items.quote: On the debt side, we have taken on debt to the tune of Rs. 2,100 crore from banks and NBFCs. The loan is subject to principal moratorium for the first 2 years of the 6 years tenure, followed by a ballooning repayment structure with majority principal only due in the last year.

items.statement: Maharashtra Made Liquor segment doing 5-6 lakh cases/month, still evolving; prestige category de-grown ~25%
items.quote: MML is doing anywhere between 5 - 6 lakh cases per month. Right now, not really sure whether this is the peak or there is still growth to come, it is still pretty evolving in terms of nascency in terms of the segment.

items.statement: Telangana government receivables overdue a concern; actively engaging with authorities for clearance
items.quote: Of course, it has been a matter of concern in terms of the increased receivables, which we are having from the government. But as a company and as part of larger industry associations, we are actively in touch with the government authorities to expeditiously clear this overdue.

items.statement: Launched Seven Islands Pure Malt whisky in Maharashtra, Puducherry and export markets; organically launching more whisky brands in promising segments
items.quote: Organically, we will launch certain whisky brands in segments which we see as promising over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Imperial Blue acquisition completed Nov 30, 2025 for Rs 3,442 crore plus EUR 28m deferred to FY30; achieved 1.8M cases in Dec, 32% market share in South
items.quote: We completed the acquisition of Imperial Blue on 30th November 2025. As disclosed to the exchanges, the consideration paid to Pernod Ricard was Rs. 3,442 crore, of which Rs. 182 crore was towards closing adjustments, primarily relating to inventory taken over by us and prepaid expenses. There is another EUR 28 million

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth in coming quarters from enhanced capacity utilization
items.quote: The Company expects double-digit revenue growth in coming quarters due to enhanced utilization of recently added capacity.

items.statement: US tariff reduction to improve profitability from Q1 FY27 after higher duty inventory exhausted
items.quote: Recently announced reduction in the USA tariff will lead to improved profitability from the USA operations starting from Q1, FY27 once the higher duty paid inventory is exhausted.

items.statement: Capex cycle largely complete; focus on sweating ₹1,100+ Cr strategic capex, no major capex planned for 3 years
items.quote: Capex cycle of the Company is largely complete. Now the focus will be on sweating strategic capex done in recent years amounting to more than ₹1,100 Cr.

items.statement: BOPET gross margin Rs 12/kg in Q3 FY26 vs Rs 6/kg in Q2 FY26 and Rs 21/kg in Q3 FY25
items.quote: BOPET Films gross margins have been running at Rs 12/- per kg during December'25 quarter vs Rs 6/- per kg in September'25 quarter and Rs 21/- per kg in December'24 quarter.

items.statement: BOPP margins improving from December; January margins better than December
items.quote: The BOPP margins have also improved. We started improving from December and right now, January margins are even better than December margins.

items.statement: Better demand scenario expected in Q4 FY26 after seasonal Q3 weakness
items.quote: We see better demand scenario in Q4.

items.statement: Specialty volume share to dip from 70% in FY25 to ~50% in FY27 with new capacity, target to return to 70% in couple of years
items.quote: Our Specialty as a percentage to our total sales volume is estimated to come down temporarily from 70% in FY25 to about 50% in FY27 once new capacities are at full utilization. Our target will be to take this number to about 70% in a couple of years.

items.statement: Specialty chemical subsidiary sales Rs 52 Cr with 25% EBITDA in Q3 FY26; 3 new products to commercialize
items.quote: The Specialty Chemical subsidiary has continued to achieve traction and posted sales of Rs 52 crores with 25% EBITDA in Q3, FY26.

items.statement: US anti-dumping duty caused ~Rs 8 Cr incremental impact in Q3 FY26; full year impact ~Rs 50 Cr; growth curtailed
items.quote: On a full year basis, it was expected to give an Rs.50 crores impact on our P&L. More than that, all our new growth has curtailed because of this anti-dumping duty.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 1,215 Cr at Dec 2025; target Rs 200-250 Cr annual reduction (15-18% per year) over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We expect between Rs. 200 crores, Rs. 250 crores each year reduction, which translates to 15% to 18% of the reduction in the net debt position each year.

items.statement: Rigid packaging (Cosmo Plastech) reached EBITDA breakeven in Dec 2025 at ~70% utilization
items.quote: Cosmo Plastech (which is our Rigid packaging business vertical) has reached EBITDA breakeven in Dec 2025. The business has reached close to 70% capacity utilization in Q3.

items.statement: First international shipment of $20,000 sample order to Richardson Electronics completed; volume orders expected after evaluation
items.quote: Last quarter, we did our first international shipment to a very reputed global dealer and there was a sample order of $20,000. Once that is evaluated, we expect volume orders from Richardson Electronics which is the one of the largest and the most reputed distributor.

items.statement: NSE listing targeted for completion by March 31, 2026
items.quote: NSE is equal priority and that's our next action to finish it by March 31st or as soon as we possibly can.

items.statement: Expects INR300 crore revenue growth in FY27 from non-16,500 ton machinery, with 16,500 ton press adding minimal revenue initially
items.quote: We expect company to grow by at least INR300 crores in FY '27 from where we close out FY '26. So that growth will be largely out of the non-16,500 ton machinery.

items.statement: Targets INR55 crore interest cost in FY27, down from INR80 crore run rate in FY26, via interest rate swaps and rate negotiations
items.quote: We expect our interest rate to come down to the region of INR55 crores for the next year. Or slightly lower, but our target is, we are very sure that we will bring it down to INR 55 crores in the next year. From around a run rate of INR 80 crores this year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 56.34% in 9M FY26 vs 53.57% in 9M FY25; expects EBITDA and PAT margins to improve in FY27
items.quote: In fact, the gross margin went up by 3%. In fact, in FY '26, that is I'm talking about Q3 -- up to Q3 FY '26, it is at 56%, 56.34% as against 53.57% in the corresponding quarter, Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Machining mix at 53% in 9M FY26 (down from 58% in FY25); expects machining mix to rise as almost all new orders are for machining
items.quote: Machining mix will go up. Almost all new orders are only for machining. Almost. Most new orders are for machining.

items.statement: US tariff on steel/aluminum imports expected between 18-25% (Section 232); company prepared for either outcome
items.quote: They are also expecting it to be between 18% to 25%. If it is 18%, then we stand at an advantage to competition. If it is 25%, we are ready for it.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR 100 crore, similar to FY26
items.quote: It should be along the similar lines of this year, about INR100 odd crore.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 100-150 crore added to gross block of over INR 1,100 crore
items.quote: An additional INR100-odd will be added on top.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth low double-digit for Q3 and 9M FY26
items.quote: So there is a low double-digit growth in the domestic volume.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 240 bps to 17.2% driven by better gross margins and product mix
items.quote: EBITDA increasing by about 15% year-on-year to INR 81 crore and margins expanding to 17.2%, reflecting an improvement of over 240 basis points.

items.statement: Domestic ASP flattish; cigarette tax hike impact on volumes uncertain
items.quote: I would say, flattish.

items.statement: Gravure cylinder facility commissioned at Silvassa for backward integration
items.quote: I would also like to highlight the commissioning of our gravure cylinder manufacturing facility at Silvassa, established under our wholly owned subsidiary, Accura Technik Private Limited.

items.statement: MIP on paperboard does not affect export competitiveness due to advance license route
items.quote: Yes, MIP is only applicable if the material is meant for domestic use. If you are exporting, then you can import in advance license and then re-export, there is no problem.

items.statement: Chennai plant utilization below 50%, expected to improve in coming quarters
items.quote: Chennai utilization is less than 50% right now but we are expecting some good improvement in coming quarters.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 70-75%; flexible packaging higher
items.quote: Overall about 70%-75%, I would say.

items.statement: Tobacco tax hike negative for sentiment but volume impact uncertain due to inelastic demand
items.quote: So definitely it is a negative sentiment for the domestic cigarette business. However, being a very inelastic consumption kind of item, so I am not sure, what at the end of the day the volume impact is going to be.

items.statement: Creative Electronics packaging plans underway but management staying cautious on disclosure
items.quote: So we have a lot of plans and things in motion but in the past also I have sounded too upbeat and then investors were disappointed. So then this time we would rather just keep it to ourselves until something actually happens.

items.statement: Historical capex turnover ratio ~1.5x; adding ~INR 150 crore to top-line annually
items.quote: We are adding about INR150 crore, I think, to the top-line year-on-year.

items.statement: No margin expansion budgeted from Chennai ramp-up or gravure cylinder facility
items.quote: We do not budget for it.

items.statement: FY26 presales target of INR 2,000 crores surpassed driven by Ashiana Aaroham launch
items.quote: We have surpassed our FY '26 presales target of INR2,000 crores, driven by strong booking conversions in Ashiana Aaroham project in Gurugram, which contributed around INR767 crores in sales on launch.

items.statement: Cumulative sale value of projects under development/delivered FY25-26 ~INR 7,200 crores; FY26-29 pipeline ~INR 6,840 crores
items.quote: If I look at the total sale value of the projects under development and which has been delivered between FY '25 and '26, it's close to about INR7,200 crores already. INR6,840 crores for the ones getting delivered between FY '26 and '29.

items.statement: Underwriting target 30% gross margin; first projects in new markets typically lower margin
items.quote: All the underwriting that we do is on 30% gross profit margin. But in all first projects in every location, there have been some negative surprises that were not captured into except for Amodh in Pune.

items.statement: Senior living floor price ~INR 7,000/sqft; high end INR 10,000+/sqft; Aaroham at INR 15,200/sqft
items.quote: I think in general, the floor price in senior living now is getting closer to INR7,000 a square foot for us. And the higher end going INR10,000 and plus as well, we're looking at higher end.

items.statement: Senior living growing at 25%+ CAGR over last 5-6 years; less cyclical than regular housing
items.quote: Over the last 5, 6 years, I think more than 25% CAGR in senior living. We were earlier struggling to get volumes, to get pricing. And that has started changing for the company over the last 5, 6 years.

items.statement: Strategic pivot to senior living portfolio across micro-markets; multiple ticket sizes in MMR (Talegaon, Karjat, Panvel)
items.quote: Our strategy overall right now is to have a portfolio of senior living projects in any micro market we are in. So we are considering Mumbai, Pune to be one micro market where we want to have multiple ticket sizes.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; healthy pre-tax operating cash flow of INR 179 crores in Q3
items.quote: The company posted pre-tax operating cash flow at INR179.05 crores during the quarter. Cash flow continues to be healthy, driven by better sales and collections.

items.statement: Partnered with Epoch Elder Care for assisted living in Bhiwadi on management fee model; pilot project
items.quote: We have given it to them. This is first one is a pilot. If it goes well, we'll probably end up giving more of these facilities to Epoch to manage.

items.statement: Active land acquisition discussions in Jaipur, Bhiwadi, Jamshedpur, and Bombay-Pune corridor
items.quote: We are in conversations in Jaipur, we are in conversation in Bhiwadi. We are in conversations in Jamshedpur. So there are a few going on. There is one conversation outside of Pune on, again, the Bombay-Pune access.

items.statement: Expects 10-12% domestic revenue growth in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Without global, that we are expecting in this quarter , you are talking about the quarter 4. So approximately, we can say 10% to 12% further improvement in the quarter 4.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 12.5-13% in Q4 FY26 and 12-12.5% for full FY26
items.quote: In quarter 4 we are also expecting between 12.5% to 13% margins, so then overall at least around 12% to 12.5% margins we will close for this full year.

items.statement: Order book of ~Rs 9,100 crore to be executed by FY29, implying exit revenue ~Rs 3,500 crore
items.quote: supported by the healthy order book of approximately Rs. 9,100 crore, strong customer relationships and disciplined execution.

items.statement: Rs 850-900 crore of order book utilized so far; new wins add Rs 300-350 crore by FY29
items.quote: And maybe till quarter 2, maybe in the last quarter, we have spent approximately Rs. 700 crore we have utilized. And this quarter also around Rs. 150 crore utilization has happened. So overall, around, we can say, Rs. 850 crore to Rs. 900 crore we have utilized out of this order book.

items.statement: Metal price increase added Rs 6-7 crore cost (~0.6-0.7% gross margin impact) in Q3
items.quote: So, in 1.67%, if you see the metal prices have started going up. So, around Rs. 6 crore to Rs. 7 crore additional cost has happened. Maybe it is being paid by the customer, but it is sitting in the revenues as well as 100% as a cost.

items.statement: Global markets muted: North America -2% YoY, UK -19% YoY in Q3; cyberattack at UK OEM disrupted supplies for 5 weeks
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, the global automotive industry witnessed moderate de -growth of around 1% on a year -on-year basis. Within this, the market in North America was lower by 2% year-on-year and U.K. was lower by 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: EcoVadis 'Committed' certification places company in top 35% globally for ESG
items.quote: Alicon Castalloy has been awarded a committed certification by EcoVadis. This rating places Alicon among the top 35% of companies globally assessed by EcoVadis and reflects our solid commitment to corporate social responsibilities across key pillars.

items.statement: Management aims to reach as close to full-year FY26 revenue guidance as possible, with Q4 expected to be the highest revenue quarter ever.
items.quote: We aim to reach as close to our revenue guidance given for the full year FY '26.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately INR 2,100 crores, diversified across multiple states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana.
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong diversified order book of approximately INR 2,100 crores with healthy representation across multiple states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana.

items.statement: Q3 margins pressured by 4% lower realizations in Magel Tyala orders, ~2% raw material cost increase, one-time INR 4.4 cr labor code cost, and higher mix of low-HP pumps; management expects improvement as mix shifts to higher-HP pumps and ex
items.quote: Margins during the quarter were also impacted by several factors. These included lower realizations of around 4% in Magel Tyala orders, a continued increase of around 2% in raw material prices such as copper, steel, and solar panels, and higher employee costs.

items.statement: Raw material prices (copper, steel, solar panels) increased ~2% in Q3; dollar volatility impacts input costs; DCR panel prices decreased slightly recently.
items.quote: a continued increase of around 2% in raw material prices such as copper, steel, and solar panels

items.statement: Export retail business grew 25% YoY in 9M FY26; cash sales (non-KUSUM) grew 68% YoY to INR 66.6 crores in 9M FY26; Maharashtra tender of 100,000 pumps expected; Karnataka order execution aligned with payment milestones.
items.quote: Our export business remained resilient, performing well during the quarter, with the retail business reporting 25% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: Q3 margin decline driven by higher share of low-margin 3HP/5HP Magel Tyala pumps; margin improvement expected as execution shifts to higher-HP (7.5HP/10HP) pumps in other states and Karnataka.
items.quote: Because of the product mix you are seeing this. But currently, we have the order from South, which is on a good margin. The other 10HP and 7.5HP products that go to other states also have a good margin.

items.statement: Management paused INR 200 crore of Maharashtra orders in Q3 to protect balance sheet; will maintain disciplined execution tied to payment visibility in Karnataka and other states; willing to forgo orders if payment risk is high.
items.quote: During Q3, we consciously moderated execution, especially in Maharashtra, to address elevated receivable levels and protect balance sheet strength. As part of this approach, we temporarily paused execution of orders of approximately INR200 crores.

items.statement: Planning minimum debt of INR 400-500 crores for the INR 1,200 crore solar plant investment (cell + module capacity).
items.quote: Because the INR1200 crores investment to be made to install the solar plant, in that we are planning a minimum debt of around INR400 crores to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Targeting INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY28 driven by pump leadership, backward integration, rooftop solar, EV, and export expansion.
items.quote: In FY 28, we will see ourselves doing a revenue of INR5,000 crores. For this, we have planned all the capex, moved towards backward integration, new diversification, and will move forward in the export market.

items.statement: Export margins are ~10% higher than domestic; backward integration of solar module/cell capacity (operational by April 2027) expected to improve margins by ~3% and release ~50% of working capital tied to panel procurement.
items.quote: Absolutely. That's why the investment has been done so that our margin increases by approximately 3%. And more than that, the thing is that we will be able to supply on time.

items.statement: Revenue book at INR2,389 crores and order pipeline at INR3,083 crores as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: As on December 31, 2025, our revenue book stood at approximately INR2,389 crores, providing strong revenue visibility. In addition, we maintain a robust order pipeline of approximately INR3,083 crores

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% from 10.7% in 9M FY26, driven by better solution mix and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA grew 49% year-on-year to INR41 crores and EBITDA margins improved to 11.9%.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given per company policy; focus on improving product mix and annuity revenue to sustain margin expansion
items.quote: So, we are not giving any revenue guidance. As per policy, we are not giving revenue guidance there. However, we believe that our continued focus is to ensure that we improve the product mix and have more revenue and annuity-based engagements and service engagements, which will improve the margin profile.

items.statement: Capex for As-a-Service deals funded via internal accruals and long-term leases aligned with revenue streams; balance sheet supported by banking relationships
items.quote: We are funding these through multiple avenues. One is obviously through some of the internal accruals that we have with us. We are also utilizing certain lease options, so we are procuring devices on a long-term lease which collaborates with the revenue which is being generated from these devices.

items.statement: Data center and cloud contribution grew from 14% to 37% of revenue; managed services and annuity revenue at 21% and expected to grow significantly
items.quote: The contribution from data center and cloud has been steadily growing. Over the years, it has moved from 14% to 37% as we are today. With that and with the other annuity-based projects and the As-a-Service business that we are getting, we are looking to improve the profitability as we move along.

items.statement: Strong demand across data center modernization, cloud adoption, cybersecurity, and digital workplace driven by AI workloads, automation, and data localization
items.quote: Demand remains strong across our core offerings, led by data center modernization, cloud adoption, cybersecurity initiatives and digital workplace transformations. Data center and cloud solutions continue to be our primary growth engine, supported by AI workloads, automation and data localization requirements

items.statement: Input cost pressures mitigated via back-to-back OEM pricing agreements and productivity initiatives; no material margin impact seen
items.quote: We actively manage input costs and currently do not see material pressures that would impact margins. And this is due to our strong OEM partnerships where we have tied up with them for all these projects there.

items.statement: Geographic expansion phased: India primary focus, then APAC/Southeast Asia, then Middle East and Europe via partnerships and GITA membership
items.quote: In the near term, we are focusing on India, because the India growth story is not only intact but is very, very strong there. So definitely that's our primary goal. Having said that, we also are looking, we will look at APAC, particularly Southeast Asia as our next growth there

items.statement: RBI enterprise application platform order of INR250 crores is software and services only with no hardware component
items.quote: The order from RBI is for setting up an enterprise application platform. It is only application platform setups there along with implementation and services there. So, it is on the entire application software and the services and implementation there. There is no hardware as part of the order.

items.statement: 35% of revenue from global clients including Facebook, Uber, Amazon, S&P, Google; BFSI largest segment with ICICI Bank as key account
items.quote: If you see nearly 35% of our revenues, come from global customers. So, we have a suite of all the large global accounts like Facebook, Uber, then Amazon, S&P, Google, all of these are our customers, S&P Gartner.

items.statement: No seasonality in order intake; public sector budget cycles no longer concentrated in specific quarters
items.quote: So, erstwhile, there used to be something where banks and some public sector companies used to have budgets to finish off in a particular quarter of the year there. But now there is nothing like that. So it is, there is no seasonality or any particular quarter which is heavy.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 revenue target of INR 1,150 crores (~10% growth) and order inflow guidance of INR 1,300-1,400 crores
items.quote: From a near-term perspective, we reaffirm our growth targets for FY '26, comprising approximately 10% growth in top line with a healthy PBT level and order inflows in the range of INR1,300 crores to INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Guided FY27 revenue growth around 15% and order book of INR 1,500+ crores with healthy bottom line
items.quote: Further, as previously guided, we are on track to deliver revenue growth around 15% for FY '27 and an order book of around INR1,500 plus crores with a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: Long-term outlook: expects faster growth from FY28-29 onwards; 4-year target of INR 8,000-10,000 crores new orders and INR 7,500+ crores concurrent sales
items.quote: MV Reddy and SG Reddy are very confident of giving us a number of around INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores worth of new order booking and concurrent sales happening to the tune of about INR7,500 crores plus over the next 4 years themselves.

items.statement: Standalone order book at INR 2,226 crores as of Dec 2025; includes INR 1,477 crores from defence PSUs/DRDO, INR 249 crores space, INR 369 crores metrology/hydrology, INR 130 crores exports
items.quote: Our stand-alone order book has crossed the INR 2,000 crores mark and stands at INR 2,226 crores, as of December 2025, providing strong visibility for the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 order inflow of INR 476 crores; price negotiations concluded for INR 550-600 crores contracts likely to convert to firm orders by end of Q4
items.quote: We have also concluded price negotiations for the contracts worth of approximately INR550 crores to INR600 crores, which are likely to convert into firm orders by end of this quarter.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow guidance narrowed to INR 1,400-1,450 crores; FY27 visibility for INR 1,500-1,600 crores order booking
items.quote: For the next year, for FY '27, we have a clear visibility to book order close to INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores around that.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 30.9% (best ever) driven by favourable revenue mix and strong execution; 9M margin at 25%
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, the company delivered its best ever performance, supported by margin improvement, primarily due to favourable revenue mix and strong order execution.

items.statement: Shifted away from low-margin BTP export business to high-margin design-led exports and deemed exports; domestic mix driving margin expansion
items.quote: As been mentioned in last few earnings calls, we are slowly moving -- moved away from the BTP business. Now more or less, except serving our joint venture, where, in fact, we have a fairly reasonable good margin.

items.statement: No equity capital raise needed for working capital; bank financing sufficient; working capital borrowings will grow with top line
items.quote: I don't think we have to raise any equity capital as such to meet these working capital requirements. I'm sure that the bankers and other stakeholders will be more than happy to support the company.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility: Q4 FY26 expects INR 450 crores defence orders, INR 120 crores metrology; FY27 expects QRSAM, EW production orders (Nayan, Medhas, Samudrika, Dharashakti), exports INR 100-125 crores, metrology INR 50 crores
items.quote: For the next year, for FY '27, we have a clear visibility to book order close to INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores around that. And in that majority programs, which, as I mentioned, like orders will come from public sector customers like BEL, where the programs, which they are expecting orders for the first quarter li
