items.quote: Post receiving -- actually, it's not that we redrawn the implement execution. See, what will happen is in the majority of the development contracts, sometimes like after the receipt of the order during PDR, that is design review stage, there are many issues will get sorted out by the user or customer.

items.statement: Advances cover ~25% of gross receivables (Dec 2025); development orders get 20-25% advance, exports 30%, production orders nil; net receivables manageable
items.quote: Advances for customers accounted for nearly 25% of the gross receivables. So our net receivables are accordingly reduced.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR500 crores
items.quote: Next '27-'28 what the guidance we have given, INR500 crores we should be able to do.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected around INR420 crores
items.quote: Yeah, we are expecting that only. Around INR420 crores top line we are expecting from this year.

items.statement: 47 hotels in pipeline expected to open over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We are expecting next one to one and a half year we think that all hotels should come up.

items.statement: Four revenue-sharing hotels to add ~INR100 crores top line
items.quote: Roughly INR100-odd crores, yes.

items.statement: Target of 8 ICONIQA hotels by 2030 via lease and management mix
items.quote: So we've said we do 8 by 2030, and I think that's the target.

items.statement: No large capex planned; maintaining asset-light strategy
items.quote: No, no, we are maintaining cash asset light strategy, we continue to do that.

items.statement: Managed hotel fees ~INR45 crores in FY26 with 47-48% EBITDA conversion
items.quote: Current financial, we are looking at a top line from managed business of roughly around INR45 crores, out of which almost 47%, 48% flows down to the bottom line.

items.statement: Managed hotel fees projected ~INR55-58 crores in FY27 with 47-48% EBITDA conversion
items.quote: Next year projection roughly around INR55 crores, INR 58 crores of top line in the managed business and around 47%, 48% of the bottom line.

items.statement: ICONIQA Mumbai occupancy above 70% and growing
items.quote: It's doing a good occupancy, above 70, around 70 plus percentage and it will grow in time to come.

items.statement: ICONIQA Mumbai Q4 revenue expected INR23-24 crores
items.quote: Roughly INR23 crores, INR24 crores in this quarter we should get from ICONIQA.

items.statement: ICONIQA Mumbai peak quarterly revenue expected ~INR28 crores in FY27
items.quote: We should be somewhere around INR28 crores. We should be able to do.

items.statement: IndAS 116 lease accounting adds ~INR12 crores notional charge per quarter for ICONIQA
items.quote: Notional, IndAS effect, which has come almost INR13 crores, we have taken INR12 crores, we have taken the hit in this quarter.

items.statement: Subsidiary sale proceeds ~45% received; balance by April 2026; post-tax ~sub-INR30 crores
items.quote: Two tranches of money has already come, almost 40%, 45% money has already come into our account. Balance will come in March and April. So by April end, the entire transaction will get closed.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio revised up to 65% of PAT from 39% last year; second interim dividend of Rs 2.40/share approved
items.quote: The dividend payout ratio has been revised to up to 65% of PAT, continuing our track record of progressively improving shareholder distributions, with last year's payout at 39% . The Board has also appro ved a second interim dividend of Rs. 2.40 per share for the year.

items.statement: Standalone operating margin 39% in Q3 FY26; recruitment standalone margin 59% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Operating profits at a standalone level grew by 13% YOY to Rs. 297 crores, and the operating margins stood at 39%.

items.statement: Recruitment operating margin improved to 59% in Q3 FY26 from 56% in Q2 and 53% in Q1; excluding JobHai margins ~62%
items.quote: Therefore, the operating margins, which saw some moderation in Q1 to 53%, improved by 330 basis points to 56% in Q2 and further improved by 350 basis points to over 59% in Q3 . Excluding JobHai, the recruitment margins were around 62% in the third quarter.

items.statement: AI-Rex agentic AI platform serving 100+ clients, 20,000 mandates closed; early adoption phase, monetization strategy not finalized
items.quote: We are seeing encouraging traction in AI-Rex, our agentic AI-led workflow automation platform. It is already serving 100+ clients and has closed 20,000 job mandates, significantly reducing candidate sourcing time .

items.statement: Continuing investment in JobHai (~Rs50 cr/year loss), AI capabilities, and marketing; headcount not growing significantly
items.quote: There are some investments which we need to make, like we are losing approximately Rs. 50 crores a year in our JobHai business, which is our blue-collar business. That's a business we are building for the future. We will continue to invest in this business for the next few years.

items.statement: Shiksha domestic traffic sharply dropped due to AI impact; pivoting to counselling/services model; study abroad soft in US/Canada, diversifying to UK/UAE/Europe
items.quote: The AI related impact is now very visible in the Shiksha domestic business and has led to a sharp drop in traffic . This will also impact billing growth over time. The business is strengthening its domestic counselling capabilities to drive higher conversions from client responses to student applications to mitigate th

items.statement: Blended pricing increases historically 5-6% per annum; harder to push in lukewarm market; premium hiring growth could lift blended ARPU
items.quote: Over a period of time, if you take a longer period, then price increases tend to be in the range of 5-6% per annum.

items.statement: Cost optimization initiatives delivered 30-40% of targeted benefits with further improvement expected
items.quote: Our cost optimization initiatives, employee cost rationalization and operational efficiency measures have delivered around 30% to 40% of the targeted benefits so far, with the further improvement expected over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Home textile business to grow from 7-8% to 20% of total top line, doubling the business
items.quote: We want to build it to 20% of our total volume -- total top line. So we are going to double the business in home textiles.

items.statement: Home textile order visibility healthy through Q1 FY27, approximately 120 days visibility
items.quote: When I say the order book, there is a visibility of FY Q1, which means I have a reasonably long order book, which is close to about 120 days.

items.statement: India-US FTA benefits expected to materialize in about 2 quarters as spring/summer orders already placed
items.quote: the real effect of this will only be seen in about 2 quarters because you see the placement of the orders which had to happen, if you were to look at from the customer side for the spring/summer has already been done.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.2%, down 170 bps sequentially due to volume softness and one-time labour code costs; expect operating leverage as volumes normalize
items.quote: Total EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 133.7 crores, down approximately 170 basis points sequentially and 780 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: AI-driven delivery yielding 15-20% margin improvement in onshore locations (US/Canada/UK) and ~10% offshore
items.quote: In delivery locations that are onshore such as the US, Canada, and the UK, particularly in the US and Canada, we have seen margin improvements in the range of 15% to 20%. For offshore delivery, the margin improvement is currently around 10%.

items.statement: Added 21 new logos in Digital Operations & Technology Services in Q3 FY26, strongest signing quarter; wins expected to support FY27 growth as they scale over ~1 year
items.quote: In Q3, we added 21 new logos in Digital Operations and Technology Services, making it one of our strongest quarters for new signings. These wins are expected to support growth in the next fiscal year as they move from the early stages to scaled delivery.

items.statement: Digital & Media services at 45% of revenue; management targets incremental 5-10% mix shift toward Digital over time driven by AI differentiation and new logo scaling
items.quote: Today, Media and Digital together contribute about 45% of our revenue. Based on the traction we are seeing from the new logos and the pipeline, we believe this mix can progressively improve, with Digital driving an incremental 5% to 10% shift over time.

items.statement: Macro remains subdued with elongated decision cycles for large deals; PoCs moving to pilots, expect conversion to enterprise implementations over coming year
items.quote: On the market environment, what we are seeing remains consistent with the signals from many enterprises, a subdued macro backdrop and elongated decision cycles, especially for larger deals. We are seeing a number of proof-of-concept engagements move into pilot stages, with clients testing the waters, and we believe the

items.statement: Interaction Intelligence priced per call minute (transaction volume); outcome-based pricing discussed but early adoption; AMLens sold as process-led service not pure SaaS
items.quote: For example, with Interaction Intelligence, pricing is currently linked to transaction volumes— in this case, the number of call minutes processed through the platform. We are seeing traction, but it is still at an early stage.

items.statement: One-time Rs 4.5 cr impact from new India labour codes in Q3; ongoing impact expected limited with no change to long-term margin/growth outlook
items.quote: We recorded a one-time impact of Rs. 4.5 crores during the quarter arising from the implementation of India's new labour codes. This reflects statutory employee benefit adjustments and has been presented as an exceptional item in the financial statements. We expect the ongoing impact to be limited, with no change to ou

items.statement: Priority is margin expansion over top-line acceleration; no specific FY27 revenue guidance given; expect gradual improvement in growth and margins as AI solutions commercialize and volumes normalize
items.quote: Given this operating context, our near-term priority is clear: margin expansion over top-line acceleration. We are driving this through productivity, delivery rigor, disciplined cost management, and the internal application of automation to enhance transparency and agility.

items.statement: Net treasury balance Rs 5,227 cr (gross treasury Rs 6,429 cr vs debt Rs 1,202 cr); strong balance sheet funding growth internally
items.quote: The gross treasury balance was approximately Rs. 6,429 crores against debt of Rs. 1,202 crores, resulting in a net treasury balance of Rs. 5,227 crores.

items.statement: Broadband KPIs improving: 101-200 Mbps segment grew from 6% to 9% of mix (Q3 FY25 to Q3 FY26); franchisee 90-day churn reduced; bulk bandwidth cost 35% of revenue vs industry 38-40%
items.quote: If you compare the customer mix between Q3 FY25 and Q3 FY26, you will see a clear migration from lower-bandwidth plans to higher-bandwidth packs. The 10-30 Mbps segment has reduced from 28% to 21%, while the 101-200 Mbps segment has increased from about 6% to 9%.

items.statement: Enterprise revenue share rising: organic+enterprise now 46% of Digital Media revenue (enterprise alone 14%), reducing strategic alliance dependence
items.quote: In terms of revenue mix, we had indicated our intent to reduce dependence on strategic alliance partners and increase the share of organic enterprise revenue. Today, 46% of our revenue comes from organic and enterprise business, with enterprise alone contributing about 14%.

items.statement: HGS Agent X platform: 15-module framework, 21 AI assistants supporting 4.5M voice minutes and 3M digital minutes; positioned as default delivery platform for new CX opportunities
items.quote: The platform is now structured as a 15-module framework, with 21 AI assistants already supporting 4.5 million minutes of voice interactions and close to 3 million minutes of digital interactions.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue expected over INR 5,000 crore, implying over 35% YoY growth
items.quote: For FY '26, we expect to achieve a consolidated revenue of over INR 5,000 crore, translating to over 35% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue expected to grow around 75% over FY26 with EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: For FY '27, we expect our consolidated revenue to grow by around 75% over FY '26 with EBITDA margin of 20%-22%.

items.statement: Inox Wind net cash position maintained at end of H1 FY26 and continuing
items.quote: At the end of H1, we were net cash and we still continue to be a net cash company.

items.statement: Per megawatt realization varies quarterly due to changing scope mix (turnkey vs equipment supply); no specific per MW guidance given
items.quote: It is very hard to give because keeping in view the different scope, different components, supply and so on and so forth. So there has been no guidance, no specific per megawatt realization we are giving in terms of.

items.statement: Inox Clean Energy plans 3 GW hybrid renewable IPP projects annually, providing recurring order visibility for Inox Wind and portfolio addition for Inox Green
items.quote: Inox Clean has ambitious plan to set up 3 GW of Hybrid Renewable IPP projects annually which provides large recurring annual order visibility for IWL, Inox Wind Limited and strong portfolio addition for Inox Green.

items.statement: Targets 7% PAT margin by FY28 on consolidated basis
items.quote: So we are aiming for a PAT of 7% by the FY 28.

items.statement: Expects FY26 PAT margin of 5.8-5.85% with slight EBITDA improvement in Q4
items.quote: And accordingly, we are anticipating a PAT of 5.8%, 5.85% at which we will be closing the FY 26.

items.statement: FMCG segment EBITDA margin improved to 7.64% in Q3 from 7.2% in Q2; textile improved to 18.94% from 18.51%
items.quote: Same way for the FMCG segment, for Q2 the EBITDA margin percentage was 7.2%, whereas for Quarter 3 it is 7.64%. So standalone or segment-wise the EBITDA margin had improved during the quarter.

items.statement: Major capex completed; only minor technological upgrades planned for textile and FMCG, no concrete FY27 capacity addition plan
items.quote: So in the coming years, the capacity increase will be taking place basis the need and demand from the customer side. So as of now we don't have any concrete plan for capacity addition in FY2027.

items.statement: Expects FMCG capacity utilization to rise from 40-45% currently to >85% by end of Q4 FY26

items.quote: Out of total FMCG, I think around 50% is contributed by soap noodles.

items.quote: The expectation for next financial year is to stabilise the total investment with more or less € 25-30 million.

items.statement: India order wins in 9M FY26: ₹1,282.8 crore/year (₹1,265.5 crore new); 4W/non-auto wins ₹530 crore; Q3 alone ₹354 crore new (₹163 crore 4W/non-auto)

items.quote: With peak annual business value of ₹ 388 crores per annum for this plant, where the SOP for both UK and the U.S. OEMs will start by Q2 of the next financial year, with peak sales expected in the FY 29.

items.statement: Solar damper business won ₹250 crore across two clients; Sanand plant SOP April 2026; US client execution mid FY27
items.quote: The total business won till date for solar dampers and actuators across both the 2 clients stands at ₹ 250 crores.

items.quote: we've changed our policy from the WDV method to the SLM method.

items.quote: However, as a management from a gross margin perspective, we are very confident that we'll be able to achieve 65% plus of gross margin as we have informed earlier as well.

items.statement: Store expansion to normalize from next 2-3 quarters after strategic consolidation phase
items.quote: We feel that the store expansion should start normalizing from next 2, 3 quarters.

items.statement: 9M FY26 gross margin at 66%, EBITDA margin at 44%, PAT margin at 25.2%
items.quote: The Company continued to report healthy gross margin of around 66% along with healthy EBITDA margin of around 44%.

items.quote: In 90% of our products, GST rates have increased from 12% to 18%. However, following a balanced approach from a consumer lens and consumer perspective, we have not increased MRP of all the products.

items.statement: COCO store pilot (INR 11 cr capex) performing decently; future expansion to remain franchise-led
items.quote: As we mentioned in our earlier call, we had converted some franchisee store to COCO store to do some experimentation and to try new things to see what is the outcome of that.

items.statement: December 2025 had only 3 wedding days vs 6 last year; January 2026 had zero wedding days vs 11 last year, significantly impacting Q3
items.quote: This year, there were no weddings in January at all, no single date of weddings vis-a-vis last year, there were 11 wedding dates in January.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month cash conversion ratio at 95% (operating cash flow to PAT excluding finance income)
items.quote: During the trailing 12 period December '25, the Company reported strong and healthy cash conversion ratio of 95%.

items.statement: Net GST rate after input credits estimated in high single digits
items.quote: Broadly, at a net level, I would tell you that it would be net of everything, it would be in the range of high single digit, I would say.

items.statement: Lease renegotiation ongoing as normal process where market opportunities exist
items.quote: We do renegotiate lease rental wherever we feel that there's an opportunity considering the overall market situation. We always do that as a normal process.

items.statement: Inventory turns improved due to supply chain and demand planning efficiencies

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue expected to grow around 75% over FY26 with EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: For FY '27, we expect our consolidated revenue to grow by around 75% over FY '26 with EBITDA margin of 20%-22%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 40-45% organic domestic; long-term target $1B revenue with 14-15% adjusted EBITDA margin in 5-7 years
items.quote: See, the guidance that we have given of 40% to 45% growth for this year is all organic, all domestic. This doesn't include the growth that we are seeing in our acquisitions like Greenedge

items.statement: FY26 cash breakeven expected; FY27 operating cash flow turning positive
items.quote: On working capital, we are well on track and as guided, we will see breakeven for FY '26 and OCF turning positive in FY '27.

items.statement: ESOP charge for next year expected in range of INR 3-4 crores
items.quote: We expect that ESOP charge for the next year to be in the range of INR 3 crores to INR 4 crores.

items.statement: Incentive cost as % of program fees to stabilize at ~50% in 5 years from current ~67%
items.quote: And we estimate the steady state in about 5 years would be in the range of about 50% there or thereabouts as a percentage of program fees.

items.quote: To accelerate our revenue uptick and as we had mentioned in our last con call to reach our target of INR 500 crores for this segment within the next 4 to 5 years, we have earmarked a primary capital infusion of about INR 100-plus crores.

items.quote: Fueled by these partners and clients, 86400 is seeing a massive surge in its revenue from INR 17 crores in FY '24 to have already surpassed INR 50 crores in YTD FY '26, and we are hoping that they would cross about INR 65-odd crores this year.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned; INR 445 crores cash sufficient for accretive acquisitions

items.statement: Dice acquisition on cusp of closure; other term sheets under evaluation
items.quote: So as we mentioned, Dice, we are on the cusp of closure. So we should be closing that transaction very soon. And other term sheets, et cetera, we will let you know as things play out

items.quote: Some of the ORCs have started to kick in this quarter, this quarter as in Q3, overriding commissions that we get for hitting thresholds with the merchant brands. And some of them will come in, in the next quarter.

items.quote: FY '27, at least whatever we are targeting, around 18% to 20% growth, will continue, and we have various opportunities we are looking ahead. And we'd definitely meet that target of around 18% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Fast-moving products (disposable cylinders, Cryoseal, liquid cylinders, vaporizers, fuel tanks) contribute 30-40% of revenue; balance from long-cycle projects

items.quote: We'll try to -- order book of around 100,000 and sale of around 60,000 to 70,000, we will try to achieve in Q4 because it's continuously working now.

items.statement: 9M FY26 capex INR165 cr; Q3 FY26 capex INR57 cr; FY27 capex expected in line with past trends
items.quote: So the total capital expenditure that the company has made till now is INR165 crores for the 9 months. Around INR57 crores for this quarter.

items.quote: In Q4 as well, we see a double-digit volume growth. So this, as of now, looks sustainable in the near term, at least.

items.quote: If you even look at the gross margins, something in this business, we were operating at a 25% gross margins, which we, we have expanded to 35-odd percent in this quarter.

items.statement: Expect price adjustments and operating leverage from volume growth to aid profitability from FY27
items.quote: Along with the operating leverage coming from the volume growth, we also anticipate some price adjustments, which will further aid the profitability from FY ‘27.

items.quote: There are no surprises left on that until and unless there is very significant change in steel prices, which is very difficult for me to comment at this stage, but I don't see any short-term, play coming out in commodity prices, particularly steel.

items.quote: That is correct. In fact, it is the government and I can only say this that it is the state government of which we have already spoken about.

items.quote: It's just tactical decisions. That was predominantly for the non-SLCM portfolio. We are seeing what is the right calibration, and it's a delay of few months, if at all we call it a delay.

items.quote: India continues to require significant infrastructure development, which is reflected in the approximately 11% increase in budget allocation for government capital expenditure to about INR 12.2 lakh crores for FY ‘27.

items.quote: the expectation on passenger traffic growth generally is the 7% to 9% range is what you generally hear , over the next decade or so of travel. So, you may have some years a little bit less, some years a bit more. I think that's generally been the callout

items.quote: For TFS operated airports, passenger traffic increased by 1.6% year -on-year in Q3, reflecting an improvement compared to the nearly 1% year-on-year decline seen in Q2.

items.quote: It will take us another quarter or so to fully institutionalize service.

items.statement: Volumes improved 2X-3X in markets where service challenges were more deeply solved.
items.quote: we see volumes have improved almost 2X-3X in some markets wherever we have more meaningfully solved service challenges.

items.statement: Cell technology roadmap: 4680 to 4600 to 46120 over next 12-24 months, improving energy density and fast charging.
items.quote: in the next 12 to 24 months, 4680 goes to 4600 goes to 46120. Each next generation of cell actually gets us more energy density and more fast charging performance.

items.statement: Gigafactory scaling from 2.5 GWh to 6 GWh installed capacity by March 2026.
items.quote: We are currently at 2.5 gigawatt hour install capacity, scaling to 6 gigawatt hour by March 2026.

items.statement: No further gigafactory expansion expected beyond current roadmap; PLI 20 GWh allocation under discussion with government.
items.quote: for our business priorities, we don't expect any more gigafactory expansion as far as the current roadmap goes.

items.statement: 6 GWh capacity yields ~5 GWh, sufficient for ~1.2 million products across auto and Shakti.
items.quote: 5 gigawatt hour, if each product takes 3.5-4 kilowatt hour, that's about 1.2 million products.

items.statement: Next leg of EV growth requires educating follower customers; company to take meaningful marketing steps soon.
items.quote: this next level of a customer, which is a follower customer, needs more education and marketing of that. And you'll see the company, you'll see us do some meaningful steps in that direction very soon.

items.statement: Full-year guidance remains firm and consistent despite US duty announcement.
items.quote: our guidance which we have given at the start of the year, reaffirmed in quarter three earning call, remains firm and consistent.

items.statement: US module capacity to expand from 2.6 GW to 4.2 GW by mid-calendar year.
items.quote: our estimation is that all the two capacities acquired as well as under construction should be operational by mid of this current calendar year.

items.statement: Order book grew from ~₹40,000 crore to ~₹60,000 crore, net of dispatches.
items.quote: When we started this year our order book was in the range of 40,000 crore s plus cumulative order book. As we as we did our last earning call, it was in the range of 60,000 crore.

items.statement: No margin impact expected from US duty; contracts allow cost pass-through if needed.
items.quote: we really don't foresee any impact on the margins as far as this duty announcement is concerned, because of the same reasons that we have supply chain available from the countries wherein the impact shall not come across at all.

items.statement: US module prices currently $0.30-0.31; order book secured at $0.35-0.38, providing headroom.
items.quote: currently the price is in the range of $0.30, $0.31. We have a great leg space even for the further price impact in the US which will not impact at all the economics for the developers.

items.statement: US annual module demand expected at 70-80 GW, with pipeline of 180-200 GW over 2-3 years.
items.quote: broadly this 70, 80 gigawatt of overall co nsumption every year leads to a demand outlook of 180 to 200 gigawatt over next two, three years of time in US.

items.statement: 70% of revenue from premium segments: retail, overseas, and EPC/O&M services.
items.quote: around 70% of our revenues are coming from these three markets which are high premium and market which have clear cut entry barrier.

items.statement: Ongoing investigation on Chinese cell usage; provision already made for potential financial impact.
items.quote: proactively basis the discussions and advice of our councils, we have already done provision in the last quarter itself on the potential financial impacts.

items.statement: Oman polysilicon facility at pilot stage; commercial production expected in 2-3 months.
items.quote: the factory is already at the pilot stage and pilot production is already ongoing. Commercial production generally takes two to three months of time for such kind of capacities.

items.statement: US manufacturing run rate to increase as new capacity ramps up.
items.quote: as the new capacity keep coming up, I think the manufacturing in US is bound to increase from the numbers that we have seen in the previous quarters.

items.statement: Overseas revenue to remain 30-35% of total, with export-heavy order book over 3-4 years.
items.quote: on a revenue conversion basis, the overall overseas revenue generally comes around 30% to 35%, which is the number this year you could see even the last year also the number was below 30%.

items.statement: Plans to add 300-400 customers in 2-3 years, reaching 500+ customer base.
items.quote: we have a plan of adding another 300, 400 customers in 2-3 years

items.statement: Expects significant revenue from US subsidiary in next financial year.
items.quote: in this financial… next financial year, we should have a significant revenue from there also.

items.statement: Won 95 Cr 5-year healthcare KPO contract in Asia Pacific.
items.quote: one of the largest deals which we did in Asia Pacific was a 95 Cr contract. This was, again, a healthcare service provider, a KPO, wherein we had a 5-year deal

items.statement: Healthcare vertical has 200-250 Cr worth of contracts from 2-3 customers.
items.quote: among these two, three customers, we have more than 200-250 CR worth of contract.

items.statement: International customers have better margins; international revenue share increased to 28% in 9M FY26 from 25% last year.
items.quote: Which is a good sign, because international customers have better margins.

items.statement: IP will provide recurring revenue and better margins and profitability.
items.quote: this IP will give us a very sustenance and average recurring revenue, and also better margins and profitability.

items.statement: Sees significant opportunity in AI-as-a-service and CX-as-a-service market, 15 billion+ and growing.
items.quote: So, we see a significant opportunity. It's a 15 billion+ market, which is going to grow year on year.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute 85-87% of revenue, indicating concentration risk.
items.quote: And top 10 customers has been contributing close to 85-87% of revenue.

items.statement: Plans to establish global NOC in Noida and customer experience center in Chennai.
items.quote: we plan to establish our global NOC here in Noida. This will be shared across the globe, so, my CTO, Gopi, has a vision, then how we can set up a bigger NOC in Noida, and we will have a customer experience center based out of Chennai.

items.statement: Expects 25-30% revenue growth and 50-60% PAT growth in Q4 FY26 vs Q4 FY25
items.quote: See, revenue growth, we are expecting around 25 -30%, and PAT would be in the range of 50-60%.

items.statement: Total order book Rs 348 Cr, healthcare segment contributes Rs 210-220 Cr including IKS Health Rs 130 Cr and BLS Rs 95 Cr
items.quote: Okay, so let me tell yo u that out of 348Cr order book which we are talking, around close to 220Cr is from healthcare. So, 210 to 220Cr would be from healthcare.

items.statement: Order book growing 30-40% YoY, expects much higher growth with international expansion
items.quote: See, order book is increasing 30-40% year-on-year. We see much more increase as we expand more in international geography.

items.statement: ARR grew from Rs 20 Cr (3 years ago) to Rs 60 Cr (last year), targeting Rs 100-110 Cr this year
items.quote: Just to give you a figure, our AR R, our annual recu rring revenue was close to 20 Cr, 3 years back. It increased to 60 Cr last year, and this year, we will be closing around 100, 110 Cr.

items.statement: IP launch accelerated to 6-7 months from 1 year, revenue expected from Q3 FY27
items.quote: Q3 onw ards, you can expect, Akshayji. So, with some of these AI tools, we have expedited the process, and with some partnership also.

items.statement: International revenue mix improved to 28% (9M FY26) from 25% (FY25), targeting significant revenue from US, UK, Singapore, Australia this year
items.quote: But if you see 9 months that this proposition has changed, when it's 72% domestic and 28% international, Which is a good sign, because international customers have better margins.

items.statement: Aims to acquire 500-600 customers in next 3 years via IP and partnerships, key partnerships to be announced soon for global revenue
items.quote: Our motto is very clear. We want to acquire 500- 600 customers in the next 3 years of time, and that may happen both through ou r IP, as well as adding more partnership.

items.statement: Healthcare order book includes 5-year contracts with top-up potential, AI expected to significantly expand addressable opportunities in patient data analytics
items.quote: Now, these healthcare customers, while we have 5 -year contract, there is a huge potential of other oppo rtunities also from the service provider.
